title: Wiring Regulations (18th Edition)
subtitle: Twenty-five Wiring Regulations practice mocks
description: A comprehensive 18th Edition exam set with twenty-five full mocks covering BS 7671 scope, parts, definitions, protection, selection and erection, inspection and testing, special locations and appendices.
format: Twenty-five rotating 59-60-question practice mocks. Exam format: 120 minutes, open book. Pass at 60%+.

questions.prompt: BS7671 applies to the design, erection and verification of which of the following?

options.B: Equipment on board ships covered by BS 8450

questions.explanation: BS 7671 covers the design, erection and verification of many fixed electrical installations, including caravan parks and similar sites. Ships, mines/quarries and railway traction equipment are separate exclusions or specialist systems.

questions.prompt: With regard to additions and alterations to installations, which of the following needs to be considered?

options.C: Rating and condition of existing equipment

questions.explanation: Before altering an installation, the existing equipment must be suitable for the changed load and safety requirements. Its rating and condition determine whether the alteration can be made without making the installation unsafe.

questions.prompt: Ideally a characteristic of supply that should be allowed for before an installation design can begin is

options.A: Amount of socket outlets to be installed
options.B: Nature of current AC or DC
options.C: Proximity of persons to supply intake
options.D: The nature of installation of the distribution cabling

questions.explanation: The designer needs to know the nature of the supply before choosing equipment and protective measures. AC or DC supply affects device selection, fault behavior and cable calculations.

questions.prompt: It is recommended that every installation is subject to Periodic Inspection in accordance with Chapter
questions.explanation: Chapter 65 covers periodic inspection and testing of existing installations. It is the part used to decide how an installation is periodically assessed and reported on after it is in service.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would describe someone with enough technical knowledge or practical experience appropriate to the work undertaken and to be capable of avoiding electrical danger, risk or hazards?
questions.explanation: A skilled person (electrically) has the technical knowledge or practical experience needed to recognize and avoid electrical danger. The wording is more specific than a general competent or instructed person.

questions.prompt: A current passing through the body of a person or livestock such as to cause electric shock and likely to cause dangerous effects would be?
questions.explanation: Shock current is current passing through a person or livestock and capable of causing electric shock or dangerous physiological effects. Earth fault, leakage and short-circuit currents describe different fault or circuit conditions.

questions.prompt: Which earthing arrangement has only one point directly earthed at the source?
questions.explanation: In a TT system the source has a point directly earthed, while the installation uses its own earth electrode for exposed-conductive-parts. That distinguishes it from TN systems that use a supplier protective conductor.

questions.prompt: Which of the following characteristics will be considered in relation to continuity of service?

options.B: Selection of the protective device in order to achieve selectivity
options.C: Size and future proofing of containment system

questions.explanation: Continuity of service is improved when protective devices are selected for selectivity, so only the faulty circuit disconnects. This avoids unnecessarily losing healthy parts of the installation.

questions.prompt: Every installation shall be divided into circuits as necessary, in order to

options.A: Meet the needs of clients with disabilities
options.B: Mitigate the effects of earth faults
options.C: Prevent the de-energization of a circuit intended to be isolated
options.D: Reduce the possibility of unwanted RCD tripping due to excessive protective conductor currents not due to a fault

questions.explanation: Dividing an installation into circuits can reduce unwanted RCD tripping caused by normal protective conductor currents rather than faults. Keeping circuits separated limits inconvenience and improves reliability.

questions.prompt: With regard to electromagnetic compatibility, what shall meet the appropriate EMC compatibility requirements?
questions.explanation: EMC requirements apply to electrical equipment generally, because any item can emit disturbance or be affected by disturbance. The aim is for equipment to operate together without harmful interference.

questions.prompt: Which of the following comprises of having a protective conductor that is the metallic covering of the cable supplying the installation or a separate conductor?
questions.explanation: TN-S uses a separate protective conductor from the source, often the metallic sheath or covering of the supply cable or a separate conductor. Neutral and protective functions remain separate in the installation.

questions.prompt: The following is not recognised as a source of supply for safety services

options.A: Generator sets independent of the normal supply

questions.explanation: A safety service source has to be a defined standby or independent source such as storage batteries, primary cells or an independent generator set. A generic generator is not the listed source category used by the regulations.

questions.prompt: Chapter 41 specifies essential requirements regarding protection against electric shock. What else does it deal with?

options.B: Selection and erection of wiring systems
options.C: The application and coordination of installation protection with regard to external influences

questions.explanation: Chapter 41 is not only a list of shock-protection methods; it also coordinates those methods with the installation conditions. External influences matter because they can change how protection must be applied.

questions.prompt: To provide additional protection for automatic disconnection of supplies, RCDs may be used provided their residual current values are rated at no more than
questions.explanation: A 30 mA RCD is the usual upper limit for additional protection against electric shock. Higher residual-current ratings may provide other protection, but they do not give the same additional personal protection.

questions.prompt: In each installation main protective bonding conductors shall be provided to which of the following?

options.C: Metal pipes that enter a building that have an insulated section at the point of entry

questions.explanation: Main protective bonding connects extraneous-conductive-parts such as exposed metallic structural parts to the main earthing terminal. This keeps accessible metalwork at substantially the same potential during faults.

questions.prompt: The following would be classed as a potential source of electromagnetic disturbance within an installation.
questions.explanation: Power distribution busbars can carry high currents and create electromagnetic fields that disturb nearby circuits. Their routing and separation therefore matter when assessing electromagnetic disturbance.

questions.prompt: To meet 5 second disconnection what is the maximum permissible value of Zs for a 30A BS 3036 fuse?
questions.explanation: The listed Zs value is the maximum loop impedance that will allow enough fault current for a 30 A BS 3036 fuse to disconnect within 5 seconds. If Zs is higher, the fuse may not clear the fault quickly enough.

questions.prompt: As a protective measure, the use of obstacles and placing out of reach shall only be used in installations restricted to
questions.explanation: Obstacles and placing out of reach do not remove the electrical hazard; they rely on controlled access and informed behavior. That is why they are restricted to areas under skilled-person control.

questions.prompt: In order to meet basic protection requirements, horizontal top surfaces of enclosures that are accessible shall be protected to
questions.explanation: Accessible horizontal top surfaces need IP4X protection because objects or fingers may approach from above. IP2X is a lower basic barrier level and is not enough for that surface.

questions.prompt: What must be carried out when RCDs are not installed protecting socket outlet circuits in installations other than dwellings?

options.B: An as fitted drawing detailing those sockets not protected
options.C: Creation of a documented risk assessment explaining and justifying why RCD is not installed
options.D: Retention of a disclaimer from the client or designer

questions.explanation: Where the normal RCD requirement for socket-outlets is omitted in non-domestic premises, the omission has to be justified. A documented risk assessment records why the socket is not expected to need that additional protection.

questions.prompt: What should be carried out in determining if protection against atmospheric transient voltages is necessary?

options.B: A calculation to determine maximum fault currents generated

questions.explanation: A calculated risk level assessment is used to decide whether protection against atmospheric transient overvoltages is required. It weighs the likelihood and consequence of surge damage rather than relying on guesswork.

questions.prompt: When it comes to isolation and switching, in general the PEN conductor shall not be isolated or switched in
questions.explanation: A PEN conductor combines neutral and protective functions, so opening it can remove the earth reference and leave exposed metalwork dangerous. That is why PEN conductors are generally not isolated or switched in TN-C and TN-C-S systems.

questions.prompt: Emergency switching shall be provided where a risk of electric shock is involved and shall

options.A: Be readily accessible to all persons
options.D: Have to be reset by manual operation

questions.explanation: Emergency switching must remove the dangerous supply quickly, so it disconnects all live conductors. Earthing conductors are not switched because they are needed for safety.

questions.prompt: In busbar installations, where the equipment is rated at 200A per phase or more, the earthing busbar must have a CSA of at least,
questions.explanation: A large busbar installation needs a substantial earthing busbar so it can carry fault current safely. For equipment rated 200 A per phase or more, the minimum cross-sectional area in the question is 50 mm2.

questions.prompt: One of the main recommended methods of reducing EMI in installations is to use

options.A: A bypass conductor for screen reinforcement

questions.explanation: A bypass conductor used with a cable screen lowers the impedance of the screen path and helps control electromagnetic interference. It is a targeted EMC measure, unlike simply oversizing live conductors.

questions.prompt: The use of AFDD (ARC fault detection devices) to BS EN 62606 are recommended to provide additional protection against fire in AC circuits, where could devices be used?

options.A: Electric fences covered by BS EN 60335-2-76

questions.explanation: AFDDs detect arc faults that may not operate ordinary overcurrent protection but can start fires. Locations with combustible construction materials are therefore a logical place for this additional fire-protection measure.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum disconnection time for a 230 volt AC TT system? a- 0.4 seconds
questions.explanation: In a TT system the protective conductor relies on an earth electrode rather than a low-impedance metallic path back to source, so disconnection is by RCD and must be fast. For a 230 V final circuit the limit is 0.2 seconds, half the 0.4 s allowed on TN systems.

questions.prompt: With regard to electrical connections, every connection shall be accessible for inspection and testing purposes except in the case of the following example

options.A: A compound filled or encapsulated joint
options.B: A connection made in roof spaces or ceilings
options.D: A joint designed to be installed in lightning protection systems

questions.explanation: Most connections must be accessible so they can be inspected, tested and maintained. A compound-filled or encapsulated joint is an exception because it is sealed and intended not to be opened for normal inspection.

questions.prompt: Where a PEN conductor is installed it should be identified by the use of the following coloured marks

options.A: Blue throughout it's length with green and yellow at the terminations
options.C: Green and yellow throughout it's length

questions.explanation: A PEN conductor has both neutral and protective functions, so its identification has to show both. Blue throughout with green-yellow marking at the ends indicates the combined neutral/protective role.

questions.prompt: Omission of identification by colour or marking on conductors is permitted where

options.A: Numbers are used as an alternative
options.B: SWA is used as a protective conductor
options.C: Three core cables are used in switching arrangements
options.D: Two wire DC power circuits are used

questions.explanation: Where steel wire armour is used as the protective conductor, its construction and connection identify the protective function. That is why separate colour marking can be omitted in that particular case.

questions.prompt: What is the derating factor for a cable installed within 200 mm of thermal insulation?
questions.explanation: Thermal insulation prevents heat escaping from a cable, so the cable cannot carry as much current. The 0.63 factor reduces the current-carrying capacity for the stated 200 mm insulation condition.

questions.prompt: With regard to selection of electrical connections, which of the following is appropriate?

options.C: The cross sectional area of the conductor

questions.explanation: A connection must suit the conductor being terminated, especially its cross-sectional area. If the terminal is not suitable for the conductor size, it may overheat or fail mechanically.

questions.prompt: When a generator set is used as a safety source, it must comply with
questions.explanation: A generating set serving as a safety source must meet the recognised standard for such generating sets, so the protective supply is reliable when the normal supply fails. A fuse standard or vague local recommendation cannot govern the machine itself.

questions.prompt: Two or more circuits are allowed in the same conduit, ducting or trunking system provided the requirements of?

options.B: The appropriate calculations have been carried out
options.C: The containment is fixed and supported adequately
options.D: They are of the same type of insulation

questions.explanation: Section 528 deals with proximity and mutual effects between wiring systems and other services. Multiple circuits can share containment only when those requirements, such as segregation and interference control, are satisfied.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would meet the requirements for wiring systems to be supported so that they will not collapse in the event of a fire?
questions.explanation: Cable supports must continue to support wiring in a fire so falling cables do not create danger or block escape routes. Steel or copper clips are suitable because they do not fail like plastic fixings in heat.

questions.prompt: With regard to corrosive or polluting substances, one method of mitigating the effects in an installation would be to

options.C: Use protective tapes, paints or grease

questions.explanation: Corrosive or polluting substances attack conductors, terminals and containment. Protective tapes, paints or grease provide a barrier and help maintain the integrity of the installation.

questions.prompt: Emergency lighting systems shall comply with
questions.explanation: BS EN 1838 is the standard for emergency lighting applications. Fire alarm standards or local client criteria do not replace the emergency-lighting performance standard.

questions.prompt: An installation consists of groups of luminaires wired between the line conductors on a polyphase system with a common neutral. What needs to form a part of that installation?

options.A: A linked disconnector for all line conductors
options.B: A risk assessment to be carried out and archived

questions.explanation: With groups of luminaires connected between different line conductors and a common neutral, isolation has to remove all associated line conductors together. A linked disconnector prevents one part remaining live while another is being worked on.

questions.prompt: In relation to wiring systems of luminaires and lighting installations, which of the following is not an appropriate fixed wiring connection method?

options.A: A batten lampholder to BS EN 60598
options.D: An installation coupler to BS EN 61535

questions.explanation: A general-purpose connector is not a recognised fixed-wiring termination for luminaires. Ceiling roses, batten lampholders and installation couplers are purpose-made for permanent lighting connections, whereas an ordinary connector is intended for other or temporary uses.

questions.prompt: Earthing conductors that are made of steel are to be buried and are protected against mechanical damage and are corrosion can be of a minimum c.s.a. of
questions.explanation: A buried steel earthing conductor needs enough cross-sectional area to withstand fault current and environmental stress. Where it is protected against mechanical damage and corrosion, the minimum in the question is 10 mm2.

questions.prompt: Every firefighter's switch shall

options.A: Be easily visible, accessible and labelled accordingly
options.B: Be no more than 1.75m off the floor level
options.D: Comply with Part M building regulations

questions.explanation: A firefighter's switch has to be found and operated quickly in an emergency. Clear visibility, accessibility and labelling are therefore central requirements.

questions.prompt: Whilst carrying out inspection as part of initial verification of an installation, which of the following should not be checked?

options.C: Presence of diagrams, instructions and similar information
options.D: Selection and installation of suitable STDs where required

questions.explanation: Erection methods, identification of conductors, and the presence of diagrams and instructions are all defined visual inspection items for initial verification. The surge protective device option is the outlier here, making it the one not checked in this list.

questions.prompt: Where an installation does not include a new circuit or a replacement consumer unit/ distribution board has not been installed, what type of certificate should be issued to the client or person ordering the work?
questions.explanation: A Minor Electrical Installation Works Certificate is used for small additions or alterations that do not include a new circuit or replacement distribution board. New circuits require fuller electrical installation certification.

questions.prompt: What should be carried out before a measurement of earth fault loop impedance is taken?

options.A: A discussion with the client on suitable alternatives
options.B: A high current test of any extraneous metalwork

questions.explanation: Before measuring earth fault loop impedance, continuity of the protective conductor path should already be verified. The loop test depends on that path being intact.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum value acceptable of insulation resistance on a SELV system?
questions.explanation: SELV circuits use a lower insulation-resistance threshold than low-voltage circuits. For the SELV case in the question, 0.5 Mohm is the minimum acceptable value.

questions.prompt: On construction sites, selection and erection of equipment shall meet the standards layed down in
questions.explanation: Construction-site distribution assemblies are covered by the construction-site assembly standard BS EN 61439-4. The on-site guide may help with application, but it is not the product standard named here.

questions.prompt: To avoid ingress of water and when involved in installation of electrical charging installations, all equipment shall be to a minimum of
questions.explanation: EV charging equipment is exposed to outdoor and washing conditions, so it needs protection against water ingress. IPX4 gives protection against splashing water from any direction.

questions.prompt: In embedded heating systems, what is the minimum distance that heating elements should be installed in air from ignitable structures in order to meet Chapter 42 requirements?
questions.explanation: Heating elements near ignitable structures need spacing so heat cannot build up and ignite surrounding material. For the embedded heating case in the prompt, the minimum air distance is 10 mm.

questions.prompt: Which of the following types of cables could be installed to compensate for movement on a floating landing stage of an inland navigation vessel?

options.A: Armoured cable with thermoplastic or elastomeric covering
options.D: SY cable with butyl rubber sheathing

questions.explanation: A floating landing stage moves, so the cable must tolerate movement while retaining mechanical protection. An armoured cable with a thermoplastic or elastomeric covering is suited to that duty.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum rated residual current value for an RCD used to protect a cable that supplies the power to a temporary structure on an exhibition, show or stand?
questions.explanation: The RCD protecting the cable supplying a temporary exhibition structure is limited to 300 mA for fire protection. Lower ratings may be used for personal protection on final circuits, but this question is about the supply cable.

questions.prompt: For showers without a basin, what is the height of zone 0?
questions.explanation: For a shower without a basin, zone 0 is the shallow area at floor level that can contain water. The height used in the question is 0.1 m.

questions.prompt: Submerged luminaires installed in swimming pools should meet the requirements of
questions.explanation: Submerged pool luminaires must meet the luminaire safety standard, BS EN 60598, with the relevant pool-use requirements. A general IP code alone is not the product standard.

questions.prompt: What is particular about a FELV system in a medical location?

options.A: Associated enclosures should be non conductive
options.B: It should be fused on the supply side
options.C: It should be tested in accordance with Chapter 6
options.D: It should not be relied upon for protection against shock

questions.explanation: FELV does not provide the same shock-protection assurance as SELV or PELV. In a medical location it must not be relied upon as the protective measure against electric shock.

questions.prompt: On a construction site, which of the following is true with regard to wiring systems used?

options.A: Cables installed over roadways should be installed to a minimum height of 8 meters
options.B: Cables installed should be steel wire armoured
options.C: Cables should be installed within a duct or containment system
options.D: Cables should not be installed across a road unless adequate mechanical protection is provided

questions.explanation: Construction-site wiring is exposed to traffic and impact, especially where it crosses roads. It should not cross a road unless adequate mechanical protection is provided.

questions.prompt: Socket outlets installed in agricultural environments should

options.A: Be protected by a 300 mA RCD

questions.explanation: Agricultural socket-outlets need robust industrial-type plugs and sockets suitable for the environment. BS EN 60309-1 is the relevant standard in the answer options.

questions.prompt: Good design should consider energy efficiency within an installation. Which of the following should be taken into account?

options.A: Costs incurred by the installation team
options.C: Reduction of energy losses within the installation
options.D: Type of insulation used on cabling

questions.explanation: Energy-efficient design is concerned with reducing losses inside the installation, for example through cable sizing, layout and equipment choices. Installation-team cost or insulation type alone is not the energy-efficiency criterion.

questions.prompt: The maximum floor area served by a 20A radial power circuit wired with a 2.5mm conductor should be no more than
questions.explanation: The standard final-circuit guidance for a 20 A radial using 2.5 mm2 conductors limits the served floor area to 50 m2. The limit keeps load and voltage-drop assumptions within the circuit design.

questions.prompt: What value of current would it typically require to disconnect a 6A Type B circuit breaker to BS60898 in 0.1 of a second?
questions.explanation: A Type B circuit breaker trips magnetically at about 3 to 5 times its rated current. For a 6 A device, 5 times rating is 30 A, which is the typical current for very fast operation.

questions.prompt: The current carrying capacity for a 2.5 mm², 70 degree C rated thermoplastic sheathed twin and earth flat cable installed within a stud wall to method 103 would be
questions.explanation: Installation method 103 places the cable in a thermally restrictive wall condition, so the current-carrying capacity is reduced. For 2.5 mm2 70 C flat twin-and-earth in that method, the table value is 13.5 A.

questions.prompt: With regard to voltage drop within a consumer's installation, what is the maximum value allowed for a 230 volt lighting circuit on a typical public supply network?
questions.explanation: Lighting circuits on a typical public low-voltage supply are limited to 3 percent voltage drop. Three percent of 230 V is 6.9 V.

questions.prompt: BS 7671:2018 applies to electrical installations in
questions.explanation: BS 7671 applies to fixed electrical installations in many ordinary premises, including public premises. Aircraft, ships and mines/quarries are outside its normal scope or covered by specialist requirements.

questions.prompt: Protection against direct contact may be provided by
questions.explanation: Protection against direct contact means preventing contact with live parts in normal service. In BS 7671 language, that is basic protection.

questions.prompt: The selection of protective equipment would NOT include consideration of the effects of
questions.explanation: Protective equipment is selected for technical safety effects such as overcurrent, earth fault current and undervoltage. Equipment cost may affect purchasing, but it is not one of the protective-performance effects.

questions.prompt: The interval between initial verification and the first periodic inspection of an installation is determined by
questions.explanation: The designer sets the recommended interval to the first periodic inspection because they assess the installation type, use and external influences at design stage. The interval is then recorded for the person ordering the work.

questions.prompt: A cable support consisting of a series of transverse supporting elements rigidly fixed to main longitudinal supporting members is
questions.explanation: A cable ladder is made from transverse rungs fixed to longitudinal side members. That construction distinguishes it from tray, trunking or ducting.

questions.prompt: The magnitude of current to be carried by a circuit in normal service is
questions.explanation: Design current is the current a circuit is intended to carry in normal service. Overload and short-circuit currents are abnormal conditions.

questions.prompt: Protection against electric shock under single fault conditions is
questions.explanation: Fault protection is the BS 7671 term for protection under single-fault conditions, such as a live conductor touching exposed metalwork. Basic protection is different because it prevents contact during normal, fault-free use.

questions.prompt: When assessing the maximum demand of an installation account may be taken of
questions.explanation: Diversity recognizes that not all connected loads operate at full power at the same time. Taking diversity into account gives a realistic maximum-demand assessment.

questions.prompt: Every installation shall be divided into circuits in order to

options.D: To meet the requirements of the NICEIC

questions.explanation: Dividing circuits can help limit electromagnetic interference by separating affected loads and wiring routes. Circuit division is therefore not only about convenience or cost.

questions.prompt: Electrical equipment in, for example, kiosks or shops within shops need to be assessed with regards to
questions.explanation: Equipment installed in small units such as kiosks or shops-within-shops must be compatible with the supply and nearby equipment. Compatibility avoids harmful effects such as interference, voltage disturbance or unsuitable loading.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT recognised as a source for a safety service.
questions.explanation: A safety service must keep operating when the normal supply is lost, so it needs an independent or standby source. The normal DNO supply is not itself a safety-service source.

questions.prompt: An assessment for continuity of service must include
questions.explanation: Continuity of service depends on how the installation is divided and how much is lost when one circuit trips. The number of circuits is therefore a relevant assessment item.

questions.prompt: Automatic disconnection of supply provides protection against
questions.explanation: Automatic disconnection of supply protects against electric shock by disconnecting the circuit quickly when a fault makes exposed metalwork dangerous. It is not primarily overload or undervoltage protection.

questions.prompt: Basic insulation of live parts or barriers or enclosures provide
questions.explanation: Basic insulation, barriers and enclosures prevent contact with live parts during normal use. That is why they are basic protection measures.

questions.prompt: A 20A final circuit fed by a 230 V a.c. TT system must disconnect, in the event of an earth fault, within a maximum time of
questions.explanation: On a TT system the earth fault loop runs through the ground via electrodes, giving high loop impedance and limited fault current, so protection is by RCD. To compensate, a 230 V final circuit must clear within 0.2 seconds rather than the 0.4 s permitted on TN.

questions.prompt: A 13A socket outlet does NOT need to be additionally protected by an RCD provided it is

options.B: Only to be used by ordinary persons
options.D: Subject to a documented risk assessment

questions.explanation: The general rule is additional RCD protection for socket-outlets, but the regulations allow a specific omission where it is justified by a documented risk assessment. That record explains why the socket is not for general higher-risk use.

questions.prompt: The maximum earth loop impedance for a distribution circuit protected by a 32A BS 88-3 fuse is
questions.explanation: The maximum Zs value is taken from the fuse table for the device and disconnection time. For the 32 A BS 88-3 distribution-circuit case in the question, the value is 1.6 ohm.

questions.prompt: The maximum rating of an RCD required to protect a230 V TT installation where the earth fault loop impedance is 150 Ω is
questions.explanation: For TT systems using an RCD, the product of earth electrode resistance and residual operating current must stay within the touch-voltage limit. With 150 ohm, 300 mA is the largest listed value that satisfies that principle.

questions.prompt: The maximum disconnection time for circuits supplied by a reduced low voltage system is
questions.explanation: Reduced low voltage keeps the voltage to earth low enough that shock energy is much smaller, so rapid disconnection is less critical. This relaxes the requirement and allows up to 5 seconds for an earth fault to be cleared.

questions.prompt: A 16A BS EN 60898 Type B circuit breaker used to protect a three-phase reduced low voltage circuit is subject to a maximum earth fault loop impedance value of
questions.explanation: The maximum Zs is selected from the reduced-low-voltage table for a 16 A Type B breaker on the stated three-phase system. The correct listed value is 0.75 ohm.

questions.prompt: For the protective measure of electrical separation, the voltage of a separated circuit must not exceed
questions.explanation: Electrical separation is limited in voltage so the separated circuit remains within the permitted shock-risk envelope. The maximum separated-circuit voltage in the question is 500 V.

questions.prompt: Which of the following sources of supply would be suitable for SELV and PELV circuits?
questions.explanation: SELV and PELV supplies need safe separation from higher-voltage circuits. A safety isolating transformer is designed to provide that separation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following formulae is used where there is doubt regarding the effectiveness of supplementary bonding?
questions.explanation: The bonding resistance formula checks that any touch voltage during a fault remains at or below 50 V. Using R <= 50 V/Ia links the resistance limit to the current needed to operate the protective device.

questions.prompt: In order to protect against burns, a non-metallic electrical part intended to be touched but not hand held should not attain a surface temperature in excess of
questions.explanation: Non-metallic parts that may be touched can run hotter than hand-held parts, but still need a burn limit. The table value for a touched, non-hand-held non-metallic part is 80 C.

questions.prompt: The disconnection time for a 16.0 mm² conductor having a 'k' factor of 115 and carrying a fault current of 13 kA is
questions.explanation: The adiabatic equation rearranges to t = (kS/I)^2. With k = 115, S = 16 mm2 and I = 13 kA, the result is about 0.02 seconds.

questions.prompt: The minimum impulse withstand voltage for a 230 V electricity meter is
questions.explanation: An electricity meter at the origin is exposed to higher prospective overvoltage stresses than ordinary final equipment. For a 230 V meter, the minimum impulse withstand value selected is 6 kV.

questions.prompt: A conductor marked green-and-yellow throughout its length with additional blue markings at the termination is a
questions.explanation: Green-yellow identifies a protective function and blue identifies neutral. A conductor with green-yellow along its length and blue at the terminations is therefore a PEN conductor.

questions.prompt: The notice relating to an RCD requires the device to be operated via its test button
questions.explanation: An RCD's moving parts and tripping mechanism can stiffen or stick over time, so the user notice instructs regular pressing of the test button, traditionally quarterly, to confirm it still operates. Leaving it as long as a year could let a faulty device go undetected.

questions.prompt: One method of protecting a cable, that passes through a ceiling joist from damage, is to install it at a vertical distance from the top or bottom of the joist of at least
questions.explanation: Keeping a cable at least 50 mm from the top or bottom of a joist reduces the chance of damage from nails or screws. It is one accepted way to protect a cable passing through timber.

questions.prompt: The derating factor for a cable surrounded by thermal insulation for 200 mm is
questions.explanation: Thermal insulation traps heat around the cable, so the cable must be derated. For 200 mm of surrounding insulation, the factor selected is 0.63.

questions.prompt: Where underground telecommunication and power cables cross, the minimum clearance to be maintained between them is
questions.explanation: Keeping a minimum 100 mm separation where buried power and telecom cables cross limits the chance of mechanical damage during digging and reduces electromagnetic interference coupling between them. Closer crossings risk one cable being struck when the other is excavated.

questions.prompt: The magnetic circuit of an RCD shall enclose
questions.explanation: An RCD compares current leaving and returning through the live conductors. Its magnetic circuit must enclose all live conductors so any residual imbalance can be detected.

questions.prompt: Where an RCD is used for protection against fire, it shall have a maximum rating of
questions.explanation: RCDs used for fire protection respond to earth leakage that could cause heating or ignition. The maximum residual operating current in this context is 300 mA.

questions.prompt: Which of the following devices may only be used for functional switching?
questions.explanation: A semiconductor switching device can control normal operation, but it does not provide the physical separation needed for isolation or emergency switching. It is therefore limited to functional switching.

questions.prompt: A firefighter's switch should be mounted above ground level at a height of

options.A: 2.25 m with the switch OFF position at the top
options.B: 2.75 m with the switch OFF position at the bottom
options.C: 2.75 m with the switch OFF position at the top
options.D: 2.75 m with the switch ON position at the top

questions.explanation: A firefighter's switch is mounted no higher than 2.75 m so it stays out of casual reach yet remains visible and operable, and the OFF position is placed at the top so its state is instantly clear from the ground, with a means to stop it being switched back on.

questions.prompt: The minimum size of a buried copper earthing conductor not protected against mechanical damage or corrosion is
questions.explanation: A buried copper earthing conductor with no mechanical or corrosion protection needs a larger minimum size. The value selected for that higher-risk condition is 25 mm2.

questions.prompt: The minimum size of a protective conductor with a 'k' factor of 143 which disconnects in 0.3 s at a fault current of 800 A is
questions.explanation: Using S = I sqrt(t) / k gives about 3.1 mm2 for 800 A, 0.3 s and k = 143. The next suitable standard size in the options is 4.0 mm2.

questions.prompt: A distribution board containing circuits with high protective conductor currents shall have the information regarding these circuits positioned so as to be visible to

options.A: A person modifying or extending a circuit

questions.explanation: High protective conductor currents affect anyone modifying or extending the circuit because the protective path must remain reliable. The warning information therefore needs to be visible to that person.

questions.prompt: The earthing conductor for an installation supplied from a TN-S system is 16 mm². The minimum size of a main protective bonding conductor is
questions.explanation: Main protective bonding conductor size is selected from the BS 7671 sizing table for the supply and earthing arrangement. For the stated 16 mm2 earthing conductor in this TN-S example, the minimum answer is 10 mm2.

questions.prompt: An installation and its generator are not permanently fixed. In a TN, TT or an IT system an RCD shall be installed with a maximum rating of
questions.explanation: A non-permanently fixed generator and installation needs additional RCD protection because the arrangement is more exposed to connection and movement risks. The maximum rating in the question is 30 mA.

questions.prompt: Control equipment incorporating protection against overload shall be provided for every motor having a rating exceeding
questions.explanation: Motors larger than 0.37 kW draw enough current that a stalled or overloaded condition causes serious overheating and fire risk, so overload protection is mandatory above this rating. Smaller motors have low enough power that they are exempt.

questions.prompt: The inspection of an installation is NOT made to ensure

options.B: That equipment is correctly selected and erected
options.C: That it is not visible damaged or defective
options.D: That the requirements of the ESQCR are met

questions.explanation: BS 7671 inspection verifies selection, erection, visible condition and compliance with its own installation requirements. ESQCR is a separate statutory regime, so it is not what this inspection is made to ensure.

questions.prompt: The minimum value of insulation resistance and the applied test voltage for a 400 V circuit is
questions.explanation: A 400 V circuit is a low-voltage circuit up to 500 V, so the minimum acceptable insulation resistance is 1.0 MΩ. The high test stress proves the insulation withstands working voltage with a safe margin; lower values like 0.5 MΩ apply only to SELV/PELV circuits.

questions.prompt: Where surge protective devices cannot be disconnected for insulation resistance testing, the minimum value of insulation resistance and the applied test voltage are
questions.explanation: Surge protective devices begin conducting at higher voltages and a normal 500 V insulation test could operate and damage them, so where they cannot be disconnected the test is reduced to 250 V d.c. A minimum of 1.0 MΩ still confirms the wiring insulation is sound.

questions.prompt: The correct connection of socket-outlets and similar accessories is established by
questions.explanation: Polarity testing confirms that socket-outlets and similar accessories have line, neutral and protective connections in the correct positions. Functional or RCD tests do not prove that basic connection order.

questions.prompt: An installation is to have the following tests carried out: 1. polarity. 2. cpc continuity 3. earth electrode resistance. 4. insulation resistance. The correct sequence for these tests is
questions.explanation: Dead tests such as continuity and insulation resistance are done before live tests. In the listed set, cpc continuity comes first, then insulation resistance, then polarity, then the earth electrode test.

questions.prompt: The verification of voltage drop may be achieved by
questions.explanation: Voltage drop can be verified by using measured circuit impedance because voltage drop depends on circuit impedance and load current. It is not established by prospective fault-current measurement alone.

questions.prompt: A 13A socket-outlet may be installed in a bathroom if it is installed beyond the boundary of zone 1 by a horizontal distance of
questions.explanation: Socket-outlets are barred from the wetter zones of a bathroom because water lowers body resistance and raises shock risk. A general 13 A socket is only allowed once it sits at least 3.0 m horizontally beyond the zone 1 boundary, well away from the bath or shower.

questions.prompt: The external influence code for zone 0 of a swimming pool is
questions.explanation: Zone 0 of a swimming pool is the part subject to continuous immersion. AD8 is the external-influence code for that level of water presence.

questions.prompt: Cables buried in arable land on a farm should be at a minimum depth of
questions.explanation: Agricultural ground can be disturbed deeply by cultivation, so buried cables need a greater depth than ordinary garden or domestic routes. The minimum depth in arable land is 1.0 m.

questions.prompt: Electrical equipment installed outside in a caravan park shall have a mechanical impact code of at least
questions.explanation: Equipment outdoors on a caravan park is exposed to knocks from vehicles, towing and public handling, so it needs robust mechanical strength. An IK08 rating withstands a significant impact energy, suiting this harsh environment.

questions.prompt: Socket-outlets in a marina shall be protected

options.C: Individually by RCDs and overcurrent devices

questions.explanation: Marina socket-outlets supply equipment in a wet, exposed environment, so each outlet needs its own RCD and overcurrent protection. Group protection would not give the same individual fault control.

questions.prompt: Temporary installations of exhibitions should inspected and tested

options.D: Only after a fault has occurred

questions.explanation: Temporary exhibition installations can be repeatedly assembled and moved, so inspection and testing must happen after each assembly on site. That confirms the installation is safe before use.

questions.prompt: The flexible cable for connecting a mobile workshop to the supply shall have a minimum cross sectional area of
questions.explanation: A mobile workshop connection cable must be mechanically and electrically robust enough for a portable supply. The minimum copper conductor size selected is 2.5 mm2.

questions.prompt: A periodic inspection for a frequently used caravan should be carried out
questions.explanation: A frequently used caravan suffers vibration, movement and repeated connection and disconnection, which stresses cables and connections. An annual inspection therefore catches deterioration before it becomes dangerous, far sooner than a fixed building installation would need.

questions.prompt: All final circuits in a amusement park for lighting and socket-outlets and mobile equipment up to 32 A must have additional protection by
questions.explanation: Amusement-park final circuits for lighting, socket-outlets and mobile equipment up to 32 A require additional personal protection. A 30 mA or smaller RCD provides that additional protection.

questions.prompt: Heating unit in ceilings shall have a degree of protection of at least
questions.explanation: An embedded ceiling heating element is out of normal reach, so it only needs protection against access by large body parts and the largest solid objects, which IP1X provides. The first digit 1 sets that minimum level of protection against solid-body access.

questions.prompt: A 16 A BS 88-3 fuse carrying a fault current of 100 A will disconnect in
questions.explanation: Disconnection time is read from the fuse's time/current curve. A 16 A BS 88-3 fuse carrying 100 A is at roughly six times its rating, which from its characteristic gives a disconnection time of about 3 seconds; higher currents would clear faster.

questions.prompt: The maximum permissible voltage drop for a 400 V motor circuit is
questions.explanation: For a 400 V motor circuit, the usual voltage-drop limit for non-lighting final circuits is 5 percent. Five percent of 400 V is 20 V.

questions.prompt: The maximum value of earth fault loop impedance for a 32 A BS EN 60898 type B circuit breaker, for comparison with test values is
questions.explanation: A 32 A Type B breaker needs five times its rating, 160 A, to trip in the required time, so the loop impedance must be low. The tabulated maximum is about 1.37 Ω, but for comparison with measured test values it is corrected for conductor temperature to roughly 1.09 Ω.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 applies to
questions.explanation: Ref: 110.1.1 - Scope. BS 7671 expressly includes electric vehicle charging installations, while ships, lift installations under their own standards and lightning protection of buildings are outside this answer set.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 provides requirements for safety against the risk of

options.A: Arc fault detection in electrical installations

questions.explanation: Ref: 110.2. The correct option is arc-fault detection in electrical installations because that is within BS 7671's installation safety concerns; the other choices are excluded specialist environments.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not a statutory regulation?

options.B: Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 as amended
options.D: The Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 1992 as amended

questions.explanation: Ref: App.2. Electrical Safety First guidance is guidance, not law. The other options are statutory regulations made under legal authority.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 identifies that the type of wiring system shall be determined after consideration of
questions.explanation: Ref: 132.7 (vi). Wiring-system selection must consider electromagnetic interference because cable routes and containment can either create or reduce disturbance. Voltage drop and earthing matter elsewhere, but the cited design factor here is EMI.

questions.prompt: Co-ordination of the operating characteristics of two or more protective devices, such that, on the incidence of an overcurrent or residual current within stated limits, the device intended to operate does so, while the other(s) does (do) not, is known as
questions.explanation: Ref: Definitions alphabetical list. Selectivity means coordinated protective devices so the intended device operates and upstream or parallel devices remain closed. That is exactly the behavior described in the prompt.

questions.prompt: Implementation of measures to assess an electrical installation by means of which its effectiveness is proved, including ascertaining values by appropriate measurement is known as;
questions.explanation: Ref: Definitions alphabetical list. Testing is the use of measurements or operations to prove values and effectiveness. Inspection is visual assessment, while verification is the broader process that includes inspection and testing.

questions.prompt: Connection of the EV to the AC supply network utilizing an off-board charger where the control pilot function extends to equipment permanently connected to the AC supply is defined as
questions.explanation: Ref: Definitions alphabetical list. Mode 4 charging uses an off-board charger connected to the AC supply, with the control-pilot function extending to fixed supply equipment. That matches the EV charging arrangement described.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is a characteristic that should be assessed when considering the compatibility of equipment to avoid harmful effects upon other electrical equipment?

options.D: The rating of the protective device at the origin

questions.explanation: Ref: 331.1 (vi). Harmonic currents are a compatibility issue because they can disturb other equipment and affect the supply waveform. Ingress protection and circuit rating are different design considerations.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following does not comply when considering the connection of final circuits?

options.A: Due account should be taken of the consequence of the operation of a protective device
options.B: Each final circuit should be connected to a separate way in a distribution board
options.C: The wiring of each final circuit shall be electrically separate from every other final circuit
options.D: Where there are insufficient ways, circuits may be bunched to provide protection

questions.explanation: Ref: 314.2-314.4. Final circuits are normally kept electrically separate and properly arranged at distribution boards. Bunching circuits because there are insufficient ways undermines proper division and does not comply.

questions.prompt: Which protective measures are not generally permitted in each part of an installation?

options.C: Electrical separation for the supply of more than one item of current-using equipment

questions.explanation: Ref: 410.3.3. Electrical separation for more than one item is not generally permitted because a first fault can make the separated system less safe for multiple loads. ADS, double insulation and SELV/PELV are generally recognized protective measures.

questions.prompt: The maximum disconnection time for a TN-C-S, AC circuit supplying a three-phase sub-distribution board from a 63A fused-switch is
questions.explanation: Ref: 411.3.2.3. A sub-distribution board is a distribution circuit, not a small final circuit, so the longer 5 second maximum disconnection time applies in this TN-C-S example.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 requires an RCD with a rated operating current not exceeding 30mA to be provided for

options.A: AC final circuits supplying luminaires in domestic properties
options.B: All 13A socket outlets in all types of installation
options.C: Mobile equipment with a rated current exceeding 32A for use outdoors
options.D: Socket outlets with a rated current not exceeding 20A

questions.explanation: Ref: 411.3.4. Domestic AC final circuits supplying luminaires require 30 mA RCD additional protection. The rule is broader than sockets and specifically includes those lighting final circuits.

questions.prompt: Where an RCD is used for fault protection the circuit shall also incorporate
questions.explanation: Ref: 411.4.5 Fault protection. An RCD senses residual current, but a separate overcurrent protective device is still needed to protect the circuit from overload and short-circuit current.

questions.prompt: The maximum disconnection time for a TN-S, AC circuit supplying a 63A three-phase socket outlet is
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 41.1. A 63 A three-phase socket-outlet on a TN system falls under the shorter socket-outlet disconnection time. The table value for this case is 0.2 seconds.

questions.prompt: The maximum Zs value for TN-S, 400V AC circuit supplying a sub-distribution board, protected by a 63A BS88-2 fuse is
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 41.4. The maximum Zs is read from the BS 88-2 fuse table for the rating and disconnection time. For the 63 A sub-distribution-board case, the table value selected is 0.78 ohm.

questions.prompt: A 32 A type C circuit-breaker is used to give a disconnection time of 5 seconds in a reduced low voltage system with a nominal voltage to Earth (Uo) of 63.5 V. What is the maximum value of earth fault loop impedance (Zs)?
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 41.6 reduced low-voltage systems. The Zs value is taken from the reduced-low-voltage table for Uo 63.5 V and a 32 A Type C breaker. The listed maximum is 0.19 ohm.

questions.prompt: The maximum Zs value for TN-S, 400V AC circuit supplying a sub-distribution board, protected by a 63A Type D BS60898 circuit-breaker is
questions.explanation: A Type D breaker only trips instantaneously at 10 to 20 times its rated current, far higher than a Type B or C, so the earth fault loop impedance must be low enough to drive that large current and clear the fault in time. The permitted Zs is therefore much lower than for the same-rated lower-type devices.

questions.prompt: Where electrical equipment in a single location contains flammable liquid, the generally accepted lower limit for a significant quantity is
questions.explanation: Ref: 421.1.5. A significant quantity of flammable liquid increases fire risk from electrical equipment. The lower limit used in this rule is 25 litres in one location.

questions.prompt: In conditions BD2, BD3 or BD4, switchgear or control gear placed in an escape route shall be

options.A: Accessible to all persons to enable maximum utilization
options.B: Enclosed in a non-combustible cabinet or enclosure
options.C: Only permitted if they are installed to facilitate evacuation, such as fire alarm call points
options.D: Protected by a an RCD as detailed in 415.1

questions.explanation: Ref: 422.2.2. In evacuation conditions BD2, BD3 or BD4, switchgear in escape routes must not add fire load or obstruction risk. Enclosing it in a non-combustible cabinet or enclosure controls that risk.

questions.prompt: In locations of commercial significance, consideration should be given to the use of

options.A: Category I equipment throughout the installation
options.C: Mineral insulated cable according to BS EN 60702
options.D: Thermoplastic insulated cables capable of withstanding 70˚C

questions.explanation: Ref: 422.6. Locations of commercial significance may need wiring that maintains integrity and reduces fire damage risk. Mineral insulated cable is a robust choice for that purpose.

questions.prompt: To protect against burns, a non-metallic part intended to be touched but not hand-held should attain a maximum temperature of no more than
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 42.1. The table sets maximum surface temperatures to avoid burns. For a non-metallic part intended to be touched but not hand-held, the limit is 80 C.

questions.prompt: The operating characteristics of a device protecting a conductor against overload shall satisfy which of the following conditions

options.A: The current carrying capacity of the conductor (Iz) does not exceed 1.45 x I2
options.B: The current carrying capacity of the conductor (Iz) does not exceed the rated current of the device (In)
options.C: The design current (Ib) shall be more than the rated current of the device (In)
options.D: The rated current of the protective device (In) is not less than the design current (Ib)

questions.explanation: Ref: 433.1.1. Overload protection coordinates design current, device rating and cable capacity. The device rating In must be at least the design current Ib, while still not exceeding the cable's safe capacity.

questions.prompt: When calculating the effects of fault current, a copper conductor insulated in 90˚C thermosetting material, has a k factor of
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 43.1. The k factor represents conductor material, insulation and temperature limits in fault-current calculations. For copper with 90 C thermosetting insulation, the table value is 143.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not a consequence of overvoltage requiring protection against transient overvoltages to be provided

options.B: Interruption of commercial or industrial activity
options.C: Interruption of public services and/or damage to cultural heritage
options.D: Serious injury to, or loss of, human life

questions.explanation: Ref: 443.4 and note 7 of 443.1.1. Transient-overvoltage protection is required for consequences such as injury, public-service interruption or economic loss. Explosion or radioactive emissions are not the listed consequence in this BS 7671 rule.

questions.prompt: The lightning ground flash density value (Ng) relevant to London is
questions.explanation: Ground flash density is the average number of lightning strikes per square kilometre per year, read from a regional map for risk assessment. For the London area this value is 0.8, used when assessing the need for surge protection.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a recognised source of electromagnetic disturbances?
questions.explanation: Ref: 444.4.1. Motors, fluorescent lighting and transformers are common electromagnetic disturbance sources. An electrode water boiler is not one of the recognized examples in the listed answer set.

questions.prompt: A main switch intended for operation by ordinary persons, e.g. of a household, shall

options.A: Be capable of being locked in the 'on' position to avoid interruption to the supply
options.B: Be capable of breaking the full load current
options.C: Interrupt both live conductors of a single-phase supply
options.D: Provide separation of the line conductor of at least 5mm for isolation purposes

questions.explanation: Ref: 462.1.201. A main switch for ordinary persons on a single-phase supply has to interrupt both live conductors. That ensures neither line nor neutral remains connected when the installation is switched off.

questions.prompt: A three-phase power cable carrying a current of 15 Amps should be separated from a signal cable by a minimum distance of
questions.explanation: Power cables create electromagnetic fields that can induce noise into nearby signal cables, so a separation distance is specified to limit this coupling. The greater the power current and the more sensitive the signal, the larger the gap needed, giving 0.58 m here.

questions.prompt: A protective conductor shall be identified by a bi-colour combination green-yellow, of which proportion
questions.explanation: The green-and-yellow combination is reserved exclusively for protective conductors so it can never be confused with a live colour. One colour must cover 30 to 70 percent of the surface with the other making up the remainder, so a 70 percent yellow, 30 percent green split is valid.

questions.prompt: A notice shall be fixed prominently near an RCD, indicating that the RCD needs to be tested by operation of the test button every,
questions.explanation: An RCD relies on moving mechanical parts that can seize over time, so the test button must be pressed regularly to confirm it still trips. The notice reminds the user to do this at six-monthly intervals so a failed device is discovered before it is needed in a real fault.

questions.prompt: A BS EN 60309 plug and socket-outlet rated at 63A may be used for which purpose
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 537.4. A BS EN 60309 plug and socket-outlet rated at 63 A may be used for isolation where the table permits that device type. The rating and standard make it suitable for that switching function in the question.

questions.prompt: The selection of the means of connection need not take account of which one of the following;

options.A: The cross-sectional area of the conductor
options.B: The material of the conductor and its insulation
options.C: The number and shape of the wires forming the conductor
options.D: The prospective design current to be carried

questions.explanation: Ref: 526.2. Connection selection depends on conductor size, material, insulation and strand shape so the joint is mechanically and thermally sound. Prospective design current is not the listed connection-construction factor in the option set.

questions.prompt: Where a power cable is in the proximity of or crosses an underground telecommunications cable there should be a minimum clearance of;
questions.explanation: Keeping a minimum 100 mm clearance where power and telecoms cables cross or run close underground reduces the chance of mechanical damage during digging and limits electromagnetic interference into the communications circuit.

questions.prompt: Where an RCD provides for the protection against the risk of fire, it should have a rated residual operating current not exceeding
questions.explanation: Ref: 532.2. An RCD used for fire protection must operate at a residual current low enough to limit dangerous leakage heating. The maximum stated rating is 300 mA.

questions.prompt: Where protection against the effects of direct lightning strokes to a supply system is provided by the application of surge protection devices utilizing the Lightning Protection Zone concept, Critical equipment is located in;
questions.explanation: Lightning protection zones step down the surge energy as you move inwards, with each higher-numbered zone being better protected. The most sensitive critical equipment is therefore placed in LPZ 2, the innermost zone offered, where residual surge energy is lowest.

questions.prompt: When calculating the size of a protective conductor, the k factor for the steel armour used as a protective conductor, for a cable with 90˚C thermosetting insulation is
questions.explanation: The k factor reflects how much fault energy a conductor can carry before its temperature limit is reached. Steel has higher resistivity and lower thermal capacity than copper, so its k value is much lower; for steel armour with 90 C thermosetting insulation it is 46.

questions.prompt: High integrity protective connection (earthing) shall be utilised for all circuits intended to supply one or more items of equipment where the total protective conductor current is likely to exceed
questions.explanation: Ref: 543.7.1.203. High protective conductor current needs a more reliable earthing arrangement because loss of the cpc can create shock risk. The threshold in the rule is likely to exceed 10 mA.

questions.prompt: A radial final circuit feeding socket-outlets supplying several items of data processing equipment has a total protective conductor current in normal service of 18mA. This circuit must have a high integrity protective conductor

options.D: Of cross-sectional area less than 1 mm²

questions.explanation: Ref: 543.7.2.201(ii)(a). A ring-connected protective conductor gives two parallel earth paths around the circuit. That is one accepted high-integrity method for a radial socket circuit with high protective conductor current.

questions.prompt: An uninterruptible power supply source shall comply with
questions.explanation: Ref: 560.6.12(iv). UPS equipment for safety services must comply with the relevant UPS product standard. BS EN 62040-1 is the UPS safety standard named in the options.

questions.prompt: Where an autotransformer is connected to a circuit having a neutral conductor, the common terminal of the winding shall be connected to the
questions.explanation: Ref: 555.1.1. Connecting the common winding terminal to neutral keeps the autotransformer reference point tied to the system neutral. Connecting it to a protective or bonding conductor would mix protective and live functions incorrectly.

questions.prompt: When selecting wiring systems for safety-services, the cables that could be used in fire conditions may comply with
questions.explanation: Ref: 560.8.1(ii). Safety-service wiring may need to keep working during fire, so fire-resistant cable performance matters. IEC 60331-2 is the cable fire-resistance standard named in the options.

questions.prompt: When carrying out a visual inspection of an electrical installation, which one of the following does not have to be verified?

options.C: The methods of protection against electric shock
options.D: The presence of under-voltage protective devices

questions.explanation: Ref: 642.3. Inspection verifies the installation work, protection methods and relevant documentation or devices. The identity of the electricity supplier is not an inspection item for the installed wiring.

questions.prompt: When surge protection devices are installed, the total 'lead length' of connecting conductors should preferably not exceed
questions.explanation: Ref: 534.4.8 and Fig. 534.8. SPD connecting leads should be short because extra lead length increases let-through voltage during a surge. The preferred total lead length is not more than 0.5 m.

questions.prompt: When carrying out an inspection of a new installation, it is not necessary to verify the

options.B: Methods of protection against electric shock
options.C: Presence of diagrams, instructions and similar information
options.D: Total earth fault loop impedance for each circuit

questions.explanation: Ref: 642.3. Visual inspection checks selection, erection, protection methods and documentation before testing. Total earth fault loop impedance is verified by testing, not by visual inspection.

questions.prompt: An insulation resistance test is to be carried out on a 3-phase 400 V circuit. The test voltage and minimum acceptable reading would be
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 64. A 400 V circuit is tested for insulation resistance using the low-voltage test level. The table value is 500 V d.c. with a minimum acceptable result of 1 Mohm.

questions.prompt: When an addition is made to an existing installation, the contractor shall record on the Electrical Installation Certificate or the Minor Electrical Installation Works Certificate any

options.B: Defects found in the existing installation
options.C: Records of repair over the last five years
options.D: Voltage drop in the longest circuit

questions.explanation: Ref: Appendix 6 model forms. When adding to an existing installation, any defects found in the existing installation must be recorded. That prevents the certificate implying the old installation is defect-free.

questions.prompt: After completion of a periodic inspection, the completed documentation shall be given to the
questions.explanation: Ref: 653.6. Periodic inspection documentation is for the person who ordered the inspection so they can act on observations and recommendations. It is not primarily issued to insurers, local authorities or contractors.

questions.prompt: In a room containing a bath, electrical equipment installed in zone O shall have a degree of protection of at least
questions.explanation: Ref: 701.512.2. Zone 0 is the area most exposed to water immersion in a bathroom. Equipment there needs at least IPX7 protection.

questions.prompt: A flush downlighter in the ceiling less than 2.25 m height above floor level over a bath will need to fulfil the requirements of

options.A: Outside of zones, so no special requirements

questions.explanation: Ref: 701.512.2, 701.55(xi) and Fig. 701.2. A downlighter over a bath below 2.25 m falls within zone 1 conditions. It therefore has to meet the zone 1 equipment requirements.

questions.prompt: Which of the following protective measures is permitted in a room containing a bath or shower?
questions.explanation: Ref: 701.410.3.5 and 701.410.3.6. Bathrooms prohibit some protective measures such as obstacles and placing out of reach because ordinary users are exposed to wet conditions. Automatic disconnection of supply remains a permitted protective measure.

questions.prompt: In a swimming pool or other basin, the metallic covering or sheath of a wiring system in zones 0, 1 or 2 shall

options.A: Be connected to the supplementary bonding

questions.explanation: Ref: 702.522.21. Metallic sheaths or coverings in pool zones can become accessible conductive parts. Bonding them helps keep them at the same potential and reduces shock risk.

questions.prompt: The requirements of Section 704 of BS 7671 apply to

options.C: The requirements of Section 704 of BS 7671 apply to

questions.explanation: Section 704 covers construction and demolition site installations, which face harsh conditions, mechanical damage and high earth-fault risk. Ordinary rooms such as offices, cloakrooms and toilets are normal locations covered by the general requirements instead.

questions.prompt: In locations where livestock is kept, for all circuits other than socket-outlet circuits, an RCD shall be provided with a rating not exceeding
questions.explanation: Ref: 705.411.1(iii). Livestock locations are especially sensitive to touch voltages, so RCD protection is required on circuits beyond socket-outlet circuits. The rating limit in the prompt is 300 mA.

questions.prompt: Equipment on a pontoon in a marina that is subject to impact to level AG2 should have a mechanical protection code of
questions.explanation: IK codes rate resistance to mechanical impact, while IP codes rate ingress of solids and water. Since the AG2 classification describes an external impact hazard on the pontoon, the correct rating is the impact code IK08, not an IP figure.

questions.prompt: For marinas, the classification of external influence which does not need to be considered is
questions.explanation: Ref: 709.512.2. Marinas require consideration of water, foreign bodies and corrosion-related external influences. AP is not one of the external-influence classifications needed in the option set.

questions.prompt: In caravans, each final circuit shall be protected against Over-current by a device that disconnects

options.A: All live conductors in that circuit
options.C: The caravan and site supply system

questions.explanation: Ref: 721.43.1. Caravan final circuits need overcurrent devices that disconnect every live conductor in the affected circuit. That prevents a live conductor remaining energized after a fault.

questions.prompt: Electric dodgems shall only be operated at voltages not exceeding
questions.explanation: Fairground dodgems are touched by the public, often in damp conditions, so their supply is restricted for shock safety. The limit is 50 V a.c. or 120 V d.c., which is the upper boundary of the extra-low voltage band.

questions.prompt: In Group 1 and Group 2 Medical locations, the maximum voltage present between simultaneously accessible exposed-conductive-parts and/or extraneous-conductive-parts shall not exceed
questions.explanation: Ref: 710.411.3.2.5. Medical locations restrict voltage between simultaneously accessible conductive parts because patients may be especially vulnerable. The stated limit is 50 V a.c.

questions.prompt: The correct Rating factor for a 90ºC thermosetting cable operating at 35ºC ambient temperature is
questions.explanation: Ref: Appendix 4, Table 4B1. Ambient-temperature rating factors adjust cable capacity for heat dissipation. For 90 C thermosetting cable at 35 C ambient, the factor is 0.96.

questions.prompt: External influences coded BE are classified as

options.B: Conditions of evacuation in an emergency
options.D: Nature of processed or stored materials

questions.explanation: Ref: Appendix 5. External influence code BE concerns the nature of processed or stored materials. Those materials can affect fire, corrosion or explosion risk in the installation design.

questions.prompt: Items installed in a room containing a sauna must conform to at least
questions.explanation: A sauna produces high humidity and condensation, so enclosures must keep water out from any direction. IPX4 protects against splashing water from all sides, which is the minimum standard suitable for that environment.

questions.prompt: The correction factor for cables installed in free air with a 90°C thermosetting insulation and an ambient temperature of 40°C is
questions.explanation: Higher ambient temperature reduces a cable's ability to shed heat, so its current capacity must be derated using a factor below 1. For 90°C thermosetting insulation in free air at 40°C the rating factor is 0.96, a small reduction because the insulation tolerates heat well.

questions.prompt: An insulation resistance test performed on a 230v a.c. installation should be capable of producing a test voltage of
questions.explanation: Insulation resistance is tested with a steady d.c. voltage, and for a 230 V low-voltage installation the instrument must apply 500 V d.c. This stresses the insulation well above working voltage to reveal weaknesses, while the d.c. supply avoids capacitive charging effects that a.c. would cause.

questions.prompt: The fundamental principles of BS 7671 covering the protection against voltage disturbances etc., states that the installation design shall take into consideration the anticipated
questions.explanation: Ref: 134.1.1. Voltage disturbances and electromagnetic effects must be considered at design stage so equipment remains compatible and safe. Anticipated electromagnetic emissions are therefore a relevant design input.

questions.prompt: A neutral can be defined as a
questions.explanation: Ref: def. A neutral is a live conductor because it normally carries current and is connected to the supply system. It is not a protective conductor.

questions.prompt: A junction box can be installed within zone 1 of a swimming pool if it is

options.C: Sealed using a suitable gasket sealant

questions.explanation: Zone 1 around a swimming pool is a wet, high-risk area where normal mains voltage on accessible parts is dangerous. SELV limits the voltage to a safe level isolated from earth, so equipment supplied by SELV is permitted there.

questions.prompt: Basic protection protects against

options.A: Electric shock under earth fault conditions
options.B: Electric shock under fat free conditions
options.C: Electric shock under fault free conditions

questions.explanation: Ref: def. Basic protection protects users from electric shock in fault-free, normal conditions by preventing contact with live parts. Fault protection deals with single-fault conditions.

questions.prompt: When considering external influences, the code AA5 relates to the ambient temperature range
questions.explanation: Ref: 332.1. External-influence code AA relates to ambient temperature. AA5 corresponds to the normal range of +5 C to +40 C.

questions.prompt: Electrical installations shall be divided into circuits to

options.A: Allow easier access to the installation
options.B: Allow for expansion without changing the maximum demand
options.C: Allow more even distribution of power

questions.explanation: Ref: 314.1. Dividing installations into circuits can reduce electromagnetic interference and limit the effect of disturbances. It also helps reliability and maintainability, but the answer option here is EMI reduction.

questions.prompt: The maximum floor area served by a single 30A ring final circuit using socket outlets in a domestic installation is
questions.explanation: A 30 A or 32 A ring final circuit serving socket outlets in a dwelling is conventionally limited to a floor area of about 100 m². This keeps the diversified load within the circuit's capacity so the cable and protective device are not overloaded.

questions.prompt: An overcurrent protective device installed at the origin of a circuit must have a breaking capacity of

options.B: Equivalent or more than the prospective short circuit current
options.C: Equivalent to maximum earth fault current
options.D: Twice the prospective short circuit current

questions.explanation: Ref: App5. A protective device must be able to break the prospective short-circuit current at its point of installation. If its breaking capacity is lower, it may fail dangerously during a fault.

questions.prompt: Non sheathed cables for fixed wiring, other than protective conductors, should be installed in
questions.explanation: Ref: 341.1. Non-sheathed live conductors need an enclosure or wiring system that provides protection along their route. Trunking or conduit provides that mechanical and basic protection.

questions.prompt: One method of determining the external loop impedance is by taking a reading at

options.A: The furthest outlet from the supply origin
options.D: The supply and subtracting the values of R1 + R2

questions.explanation: Ref: 411.3.3. External earth fault loop impedance Ze is measured at the origin of the installation, normally with the installation isolated as appropriate. Measurements at final outlets include internal circuit impedance as well.

questions.prompt: If an electric fire has an element exposed to touch, this would increase the risk of electric shock by
questions.explanation: Ref: 411.4.4. An exposed heating element is a live part accessible in normal use, so the shock risk is from basic contact. Fault contact would involve exposed conductive parts becoming live because of a fault.

questions.prompt: The maximum disconnection time for a 400v a.c. final circuit with a TN supply is
questions.explanation: Higher system voltages produce higher and more dangerous touch voltages during a fault, so disconnection must happen faster. For a TN final circuit at 400 V the supply must be cut within 0.2 seconds to protect against electric shock.

questions.prompt: The maximum disconnection time for a 230v a.c. circuit with a TN supply is
questions.explanation: Distribution circuits and fixed equipment with no readily touchable parts are allowed a longer disconnection time than final circuits, because the shock risk is lower. On a TN supply this maximum is 5 seconds.

questions.prompt: When tested at 5 times the rated operating current, an RCD used for additional protection should operate within
questions.explanation: Ref: 443.1.1. A 30 mA RCD used for additional protection is tested at five times rated residual current for rapid operation. The maximum disconnection time for that test is 40 ms.

questions.prompt: Undervoltage protection is required when the restoration of power may cause
questions.explanation: Ref: 422.3.4. Undervoltage protection is needed where power restoration could restart machinery unexpectedly. Preventing automatic restart avoids injury and mechanical damage.

questions.prompt: Low voltage is defined as having a value which does not exceed
questions.explanation: Ref: Knowledge. Low voltage in BS 7671 terms does not exceed 1000 V a.c. or 1500 V d.c. The option gives the a.c. limit.
