questions.prompt: In the diagram below, a ring final circuit is wired in high impact PVC conduit. The number of single core cables installed in section A to B will be
questions.explanation: A ring final circuit runs out and back, so before it branches the conduit carries two line conductors, two neutrals and two circuit protective conductors. That makes six single-core cables sharing the section.

questions.prompt: A residual current device (RCD) works by

options.A: A magnetic device operating in the event of a fault between live and earth
options.B: A magnetic device operating in the event of a fault between neutral and earth
options.C: A thin element operating in the event of a fault between live and earth
options.D: A thin element operating in the event of a fault between neutral and earth

questions.explanation: Ref: 414.4.3. An RCD compares current in the live conductors and trips when leakage to earth creates an imbalance. That is represented by a magnetic sensing device operating for a live-to-earth fault.

questions.prompt: At the origin of an electrical installation, the prospective fault current must be taken into account when

options.C: Estimating the external fault loop impedance
options.D: Selecting the type of overcurrent device to be installed

questions.explanation: Ref: 424.1. Prospective fault current at the origin determines the breaking capacity and type of overcurrent protective device needed. The device must safely interrupt the worst expected fault current.

questions.prompt: Protective measures against electric shock can be achieved by automatic disconnection of the supply and in a.c. systems with additional protection by means of an rcd . Which of the following does not require this additional protection by an RCD?

options.A: Mobile equipment with a current rating not exceeding 13 A, for use outdoors
options.B: Mobile equipment with a current rating not exceeding 32 A, for use outdoors
options.C: Socket outlets for use under supervision of skilled or instructed persons
options.D: Socket outlets with a rated current not exceeding 20 A

questions.explanation: Ref: 444.1. Socket-outlets under the supervision of skilled or instructed persons can be treated differently from general-use sockets. The supervision reduces the need for the standard additional RCD protection in the option set.

questions.prompt: In a TN system, automatic disconnection of the supply in case of a fault in a 230-volt a.c. final circuit not exceeding 32 A shall have a maximum disconnection time of
questions.explanation: Ref: 434.5.2. For a TN system final circuit not exceeding 32 A at 230 V a.c., the maximum automatic-disconnection time is 0.4 seconds. This limits touch-voltage duration during faults.

questions.prompt: If a fault occurs in the HV system, and a magnitude of fault voltage of 430 volts occurs between exposed conductive parts and earth on the LV installation. What is the maximum tolerable duration of the fault?
questions.explanation: A high-voltage fault can briefly impose a stress voltage on the low-voltage installation's earthing. The higher this voltage, the shorter the time it can safely persist; at 430 V the permitted duration is 300 ms before it must be cleared.

questions.prompt: If a Line conductor of an IT system is earthed accidentally, the insulation and components rated for the Line to Neutral voltage can be temporarily stressed with a higher voltage. What value can this stress voltage reach up to?
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 41.4. In an IT system with one line accidentally earthed, unearthed conductors can be stressed by the line-to-line voltage. For a three-phase system that can be up to sqrt(3) times Uo.

questions.prompt: Class II equipment would provide

options.C: Earth fault loop impedance fault protection

questions.explanation: Ref: 544.1.1. Class II equipment uses double or reinforced insulation, so it provides both basic protection and fault protection without relying on an earth connection.

questions.prompt: Nuisance tripping from a large transformer installation can be prevented by

options.A: The use of a B type MCB
options.B: The use of a C type MCB
options.C: The use of a D type MCB

questions.explanation: Ref: 523.9. Large transformers can have high inrush current when energized. A Type D MCB tolerates higher short-duration inrush than Type B or C devices, reducing nuisance tripping.

questions.prompt: If a cable is buried in a wall less than 50mm depth and is not protected by metallic enclosures, the additional protection required is
questions.explanation: Ref: 514.9.1. A concealed cable less than 50 mm deep and not otherwise mechanically protected needs 30 mA RCD additional protection. This helps protect against shock if the cable is penetrated.

questions.prompt: The voltage drop between the origin of an installation and any load point on a low voltage circuit on a public distribution system should not exceed

options.B: 3% for lighting and 5% for other uses
options.D: 8% for lighting and 10% for other uses

questions.explanation: On a public low-voltage supply, voltage drop is limited to 3% for lighting and 5% for other uses so equipment receives adequate voltage. Lighting gets the tighter limit because lamps dim and flicker noticeably when starved of volts.

questions.prompt: At which one of the following terminations would a warning notice NOT need to be attached

options.D: An earthing terminal within a consumer unit

questions.explanation: Ref: 521.10.202. Bonding and earth-electrode terminations need warning labels because removal could make the installation unsafe. An earthing terminal inside a consumer unit is already part of the labelled enclosure and is not the same external clamp situation.

questions.prompt: Where a clamp is used for bonding purposes, a permanent label shall be fixed in a visible position with the wording
questions.explanation: Ref: 521.5.1. A bonding clamp label warns that the connection is a safety connection and must not be removed. The wording in the answer identifies it as a safety electrical connection.

questions.prompt: When designing a single circuit, correction factors are to be used and applied to the

options.A: Current carrying capacity of the cable
options.D: Nominal rating of the protective device

questions.explanation: Rating factors for grouping, ambient temperature and the like reduce a cable's effective current-carrying capacity, so the protective device's nominal rating must be coordinated with that lowered value to guarantee the conductor is properly protected against overload.

questions.prompt: When determining design current, the correction factor that is applied to a BS3036 rewireable fuse is
questions.explanation: Ref: 537.4.2.2. BS 3036 rewireable fuses need a 0.725 correction factor because their operating characteristics require extra derating. Applying it prevents the cable being overloaded before the fuse operates.

questions.prompt: A BS EN 61009 protective device is also known as a
questions.explanation: Ref: 532.1. A BS EN 61009 device combines residual-current protection with overcurrent protection. That combined device is an RCBO.

questions.prompt: A BS EN 60898 protective device is also known as a
questions.explanation: Ref: def. BS EN 60898 is the standard for domestic-type circuit-breakers. In common exam wording, that device is simply a circuit breaker or MCB.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does NOT give protection against basic contact
questions.explanation: Ref: 542.2.6. Basic contact protection is provided by insulation, barriers, enclosures or sometimes obstacles. Supplementary bonding reduces touch voltage under fault conditions, so it is not basic-contact protection.

questions.prompt: Outdoor lighting does NOT involve
questions.explanation: Ref: 533.1.2.2. Outdoor lighting in this context includes fixed lighting such as floodlighting, traffic signals and shelters. Festoon lighting is treated separately as temporary or decorative string lighting.

questions.prompt: In Great Britain the use of Combined protective and neutral (PEN) conductors is prohibited in consumers installations. One of the exceptions from this is

options.A: Where the installation is supplied by a privately owned transformer which has a metallic connection with the distributors network
options.B: Where the supply is feeding a swimming pool
options.C: Where the supply is feeding an agricultural installation
options.D: Where the supply is obtained from a private generating plant

questions.explanation: A PEN conductor depends on a sound earth back at the supply; losing it can make exposed metalwork live, so it is barred in consumers' installations. A private generating plant is a permitted exception because the user controls the whole system.

questions.prompt: Where a generating set is used as an additional source of supply in parallel with other sources, it shall be installed

options.A: On the load side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with no additional requirements
options.B: On the load side of all the protective devices to the final circuit which must be connected by plug and socket
options.C: On the supply side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with a number of additional requirements
options.D: On the supply side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with no additional requirements

questions.explanation: A generating set run in parallel with another source feeds into the installation upstream of the final-circuit protective devices, so it must be connected on the supply side rather than after them. Placing it there lets it share the load across the whole installation.

questions.prompt: Regarding auxiliary supplies to safety services, the maximum changeover time refers to

options.A: How long the safety source can supply the rated power output to the safety service
options.B: How often maintenance has to be carried out on the auxiliary supply
options.C: The frequency (in cycles per second) of the auxiliary supply feeding the safety service
options.D: The time It takes for the safety source to supply the power to the safety service, after the loss of the main power supply

questions.explanation: Ref: 544.1.1 and Table 54.8. Maximum changeover time is the time from loss of the normal supply until the safety source supplies the safety service. It is about restoration speed, not battery duration or maintenance interval.

questions.prompt: An insulation resistance test performed on a PELV installation should be capable of producing a test voltage of
questions.explanation: PELV operates at extra-low voltage, so its insulation is only stressed to a modest level. A 250V d.c. test applies a voltage suited to that band, proving the insulation without over-stressing low-voltage components; the 500V test is reserved for normal LV circuits.

questions.prompt: The paperwork that should be issued on completion of a new installation is

options.C: A schedule of test results, schedule of inspection and an electrical installation certificate

questions.explanation: Ref: 557.4.1 and Table 55.2. Completion of a new installation requires the Electrical Installation Certificate plus schedules of inspections and test results. A test sheet alone is not the complete certification package.

questions.prompt: A polarity test would be conducted to verify

options.A: Every fuse and single pole device is connected in the line conductor only
options.B: There is no breakdown of the conductor insulation
options.D: There is sufficiently low resistance to operate the protective device within its limits

questions.explanation: Ref: 559.5.1. Polarity testing confirms single-pole protective and switching devices are in the line conductor only. That prevents a circuit being apparently off while the line remains connected.

questions.prompt: A minor works certificate should be issued

options.B: When a property has been extended
options.C: Where an additional circuit is connected to an installation
options.D: Where an alteration not requiring an additional circuit is needed

questions.explanation: Ref: 643. A Minor Works Certificate is for an alteration or addition that does not involve adding a new circuit. Adding a circuit or a new installation needs fuller certification.

questions.prompt: Before conducting an insulation resistance test you should

options.B: Ensure that all lamps are removed
options.C: Ensure that the earth fault loop impedance is satisfactory
options.D: Ensure that the polarity is correct

questions.explanation: Ref: 643.3.2 and Table 64. Lamps and sensitive loads should be removed or disconnected before insulation-resistance testing so the test does not damage them or distort the reading.

questions.prompt: The minimum value of insulation resistance of a PELV circuit is
questions.explanation: Ref: 644.5. PELV circuits have the same low insulation-resistance threshold used for extra-low-voltage systems in this context. The minimum selected value is 0.5 Mohm.

questions.prompt: Self supported suspension cables within agricultural situations should be

options.A: At a height of a least 10m
options.B: At a height of a least 2m
options.C: At a height of a least 4m
options.D: At a height of a least 6m

questions.explanation: Agricultural sites involve tall machinery, vehicles and livestock, so self-supporting overhead cables must hang high enough to stay clear. A minimum height of about 6 m prevents contact or damage from passing plant and animals.

questions.prompt: If SELV or PELV is used within agricultural premises, barriers or enclosures must conform to at least
questions.explanation: Even on safe SELV/PELV systems, agricultural areas demand barriers that stop a finger reaching live parts. IPXXB specifies finger protection, guarding against accidental contact where livestock, moisture and handling make exposure more likely.

questions.prompt: In zone 1 of a swimming pool, a junction box can be installed if it is
questions.explanation: Zone 1 around a pool is a wet, high-risk area, so any junction box must be fed by SELV. With the supply limited to a safe extra-low voltage, even a fault cannot deliver a dangerous shock to a person in water.

questions.prompt: Zone 1 in a swimming pool installation is defined as the

options.B: The floor or surface expected to be occupied by persons
options.C: The horizontal plane 2m above the floor
options.D: The interior of the pool and a vertical plane 2m above the basin

questions.explanation: Zone 1 is the volume immediately surrounding the pool, bounded by the water's edge and rising to a vertical plane 2m above the basin. This captures the space a swimmer or bather can reach while wet, where shock risk is greatest.

questions.prompt: The specific IP rating for areas within zone 1 of a bathroom is
questions.explanation: Ref: 701.512.2. Bathroom zone 1 is exposed to splashing water, so equipment generally needs at least IPX4 protection. Higher ratings may be needed for water jets.

questions.prompt: In a bathroom zone 2 is defined as the

options.A: Area directly above the bath or shower
options.B: Area outside a 0.60m circumference from the bath or shower
options.C: Area within a 0.60m circumference from the bath or shower
options.D: Area within the bath or shower

questions.explanation: Ref: 709.411.4. Bathroom zone 2 is the area extending 0.60 m from the edge of the bath or shower area. The citation appears to point to marinas, so use the bathroom-zone figure to verify exact wording.

questions.prompt: In an amusement park an RCD would NOT be used to protect

options.B: Mobile equipment connected by a flexible cable

questions.explanation: Ref: 721.55.2.6 and Table 721. SELV circuits already limit shock risk by voltage and separation, so they do not need the same RCD additional protection as lighting, mobile equipment or socket circuits.

questions.prompt: On a mobile vehicle installation, a socket outlet or plug should conform to
questions.explanation: Ref: 714.1. Mobile-vehicle supply connections need robust industrial plugs and socket-outlets. BS EN 60309-2 is the relevant standard for those industrial pin-and-sleeve devices.

questions.prompt: On the d.c. side of a PV power supply system, the type of insulation that is preferable is
questions.explanation: Ref: 717.411.3.1.2. PV d.c. circuits remain energized when light is present, so stronger insulation is preferred. Class II insulation reduces reliance on earthing for fault protection.

questions.prompt: The minimum rating of socket outlets supplying a pitch on a caravan site should be
questions.explanation: Each caravan pitch must be served by a socket-outlet rated at least 16A so it can supply the typical demand of a touring caravan or motor home. A lower rating would not safely carry the expected heating, cooking and appliance load.

questions.prompt: BS EN 50085 relates to

options.D: Industrial plugs, couplers and socket outlets

questions.explanation: Ref: 715.524.201. BS EN 50085 is the product standard family for cable trunking and ducting systems. Conduit, conductors and industrial plugs are covered by different standards.

questions.prompt: The correction factor for cables installed in free air with 90°C thermosetting insulation and an ambient temperature of 40°C is
questions.explanation: Thermosetting cable is rated to 90°C, so at 40°C ambient it is still operating well below its limit and barely needs derating. The correction factor is therefore close to 1.0, giving 0.96; lower factors apply to cooler-rated PVC insulation.

questions.prompt: BS EN 60228 relates to

options.D: Industrial plugs, couplers and socket outlets

questions.explanation: Ref: Appx 4. BS EN 60228 classifies conductors of insulated cables, including conductor construction and resistance. It is not the trunking, conduit or plug standard.

questions.prompt: An insulation resistance test performed on a 230v a.c. installation should be capable of producing a test voltage of
questions.explanation: Ref: 110.1.1(vi). A 230 V insulation-resistance test uses the standard low-voltage test output of 500 V d.c. The cited reference is terse, so Table 64 is the place to verify the exact test value.

questions.prompt: What characteristics of supply should be determined before an installation design can begin?
questions.explanation: Ref: 110.2(vii). The nature of current, AC or DC, is a supply characteristic that must be known before design. It affects equipment selection, protective devices and fault behavior.

questions.prompt: A neutral can be defined as a
questions.explanation: Ref: 114.1. A neutral is a live conductor because it is part of the current-carrying system in normal operation. It is not a protective conductor.

questions.prompt: A junction box can be installed within zone 1 of a swimming pool if it is

options.C: Sealed using a suitable gasket sealant

questions.explanation: In the high-risk wet environment of pool zone 1, a junction box is only permitted when supplied by SELV. The safety extra-low voltage means a fault cannot produce a dangerous touch voltage to someone in or beside the water.

questions.prompt: Choose one of the following which does not fall under compatibility?
questions.explanation: Ref: Part 2. Compatibility concerns effects such as power factor, starting currents and transient overvoltages between equipment and supply. Continuity of service is a separate design consideration.

questions.prompt: If an electric fire has an element exposed to touch, this would increase the risk of electric shock by
questions.explanation: Ref: Part 2. An exposed heating element creates risk of direct contact with a live part in normal service. That is basic contact, not a fault-contact situation.

questions.prompt: The maximum disconnection time for a 230v a.c. circuit with a TN supply is
questions.explanation: 5s is the maximum disconnection time for distribution circuits and circuits rated above 32A on a TN system, where the fixed wiring is less likely to be in contact with a person. Final circuits up to 32A must clear faster, in 0.4s.

questions.prompt: If Ze is measured at 0.68Ω and R1+R2 is measured as 0.82Ω,the value of Zs would be
questions.explanation: Ref: 341.1. Earth fault loop impedance at a point in a circuit is Ze plus the circuit's R1+R2. Here 0.68 + 0.82 = 1.50 ohm.

questions.prompt: The maximum Zs for a 10A Type C circuit breaker protecting a standard discharge type lighting circuit is
questions.explanation: A Type C breaker needs roughly 10 times its rated current to trip instantly, so a 10A device requires about 100A of fault current. With a 230V supply, the loop impedance must stay at or below around 2.30Ω for that current to flow and disconnect in time.

questions.prompt: At the origin of an electrical installation, the prospective fault current must be taken into account when

options.C: Estimating the external fault loop impedance
options.D: Selecting the type of overcurrent device to be installed

questions.explanation: Ref: 411.3.2.4. Prospective fault current at the origin determines whether an overcurrent device can safely break the fault. Device type and breaking capacity must be chosen around that value.

questions.prompt: In a TN system, the maximum earth fault loop impedance Zs when using a 32 A , (gG) BS 88 fuse for a disconnection time of 0.4 seconds would be
questions.explanation: For a 32A BS 88 fuse to blow within 0.4s, enough fault current must flow, which sets a ceiling on loop impedance. Using the supply voltage divided by that required current gives a maximum Zs of 1.04Ω; above this the fuse would clear too slowly.

questions.prompt: In a TN system, the maximum earth fault loop impedance Zs when using a 32 A , type B circuit breaker for instantaneous operation would be
questions.explanation: A Type B breaker operates instantaneously at 5 times its rating, so 5 × 32 A = 160 A, and the maximum loop impedance is 230 V divided by 160 A, giving roughly 1.44 ohm. A lower Zs guarantees enough fault current to trip it quickly.

questions.prompt: Which of the following shall be used as a source of a FELV system?
questions.explanation: Ref: 311.1. FELV still requires a source with separation between windings so the extra-low-voltage side is not directly connected to the higher-voltage supply. Autotransformers and potentiometers do not provide that separation.

questions.prompt: Nuisance tripping from a large transformer installation can be prevented by

options.A: The use of a B type MCB
options.B: The use of a C type MCB
options.C: The use of a D type MCB

questions.explanation: Ref: 313.1. Large transformers can draw high inrush current at switch-on. A Type D MCB is less sensitive to short inrush peaks, so it reduces nuisance tripping.

questions.prompt: An installation protected by an RCD shall have a fixed notice stating

options.A: The test button should be pressed at 6 monthly intervals
options.B: The test button should be pressed monthly
options.C: The test button should be pressed occasionally
options.D: The test button should be pressed quarterly

questions.explanation: RCDs contain mechanical parts that can seize over time, so the notice instructs the user to press the integral test button quarterly to confirm the device still trips and provides protection.

questions.prompt: The maximum operating temperature of standard general purpose thermoplastic PVC cable is
questions.explanation: Ref: 418.3. Standard general-purpose thermoplastic PVC cable is rated for a maximum conductor operating temperature of 70 C. Higher temperatures require different insulation types.

questions.prompt: An unprotected cable concealed in a wall at a depth less than 50mm and installed outside the safe zones, shall be provided with

options.D: An RCD with operating current not exceeding 30mA

questions.explanation: Ref: 417.3. A cable less than 50 mm deep outside safe zones is vulnerable to nails, screws and drilling. A 30 mA RCD provides additional protection if the cable is damaged.

questions.prompt: Where a generating set is used as an additional source of supply in parallel with other sources, it shall be installed

options.A: On the load side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with no additional requirements
options.B: On the load side of all the protective devices to the final circuit which must be connected by plug and socket
options.C: On the supply side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with a number of additional requirements
options.D: On the supply side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with no additional requirements

questions.explanation: Running a generator in parallel with the public supply means both feed the installation, so it connects on the supply side ahead of the final-circuit protection, and this brings extra requirements covering matters like loss of mains and synchronising.

questions.prompt: Regarding auxiliary supplies to safety services, the maximum changeover time refers to

options.A: How long the safety source can supply the rated power output to the safety service
options.B: How often maintenance has to be carried out on the auxiliary supply
options.C: The frequency (in cycles per second) of the auxiliary supply feeding the safety service
options.D: The time It takes for the safety source to supply the power to the safety service, after the loss of the main power supply

questions.explanation: Maximum changeover time is how long it takes the safety source to supply the safety service after the normal supply fails. It is about transfer delay, not how long the standby source can run.

questions.prompt: The minimum value of insulation resistance test performed on a SELV installation is
questions.explanation: SELV operates at low voltage with no earth reference, so it is tested at 250 V DC and must read at least 0.5 megohms, confirming the insulation is sound and not leaking between conductors.

questions.prompt: When installing three phase equipment, an ADDITIONAL test that should be carried out is
questions.explanation: Ref: 433.1.1. Three-phase equipment needs phase sequence verified so motors and other phase-sensitive loads rotate or operate correctly. That is an additional check beyond ordinary polarity.

questions.prompt: Cables laid in arable or cultivated agricultural ground should be

options.D: Buried to a depth of 2.0m with mechanical protection

questions.explanation: Arable or cultivated land is regularly ploughed and worked by machinery to a significant depth, so cables must be buried at least 1.0 m down to keep them clear of any digging or tilling that could damage them.

questions.prompt: Socket outlets and hand held equipment rated up to and including 32A can have additional protection in the form of
questions.explanation: Electrical separation supplies the circuit from an isolating transformer with no earth reference, so a single fault to the surrounding metalwork cannot give a shock — making it a valid protective measure for these portable and socket loads. RCDs are the more common choice, but separation is the listed measure here.

questions.prompt: Within zone 1 of a swimming baths where water jets are used for cleaning purposes, installed electrical equipment should be rated
questions.explanation: Ref: Part 2. Water jets increase the water-ingress risk beyond ordinary splashing. Zone 1 equipment in that cleaning condition therefore needs IPX5 protection.

questions.prompt: In an area containing a bath or a shower, socket outlets must be installed
questions.explanation: Socket-outlets are kept well away from water to reduce the risk of shock when wet, so apart from limited exceptions they must sit at least 3 m horizontally from the boundary of zone 1 around a bath or shower.

questions.prompt: Floor and heating systems shall use a RCD as a means of automatic disconnection of supply with a current rating of
questions.explanation: Ref: 443.1.1. Floor and ceiling heating systems need RCD protection because heating elements can fault to surrounding conductive parts or coverings. The required residual current rating in the prompt is 30 mA.

questions.prompt: A mobile unit should have a connection between the

options.D: Vehicle chassis and main bonding terminal

questions.explanation: Ref: 422.3.9. Bonding the vehicle chassis to the main bonding terminal keeps accessible metalwork at the installation earth potential. That reduces shock risk if a fault occurs on the mobile unit.

questions.prompt: Photovoltaic equipment should always

options.A: Be considered energised on the a.c. side
options.B: Be considered energised on the d.c. side
options.C: Be used in certain listed countries only

questions.explanation: Ref: Appx 5. PV d.c. conductors can remain live whenever the array is illuminated, even if the a.c. side is isolated. That is why the d.c. side should be treated as energized.

questions.prompt: BS EN 50085 relates to

options.D: Industrial plugs, couplers and socket outlets

questions.explanation: BS EN 50085 is the product standard for cable trunking and cable ducting systems. The other options relate to conduit, plugs and cable conductors, which sit under different standards, so only trunking and ducting fits.

questions.prompt: BS 1362 relates to

options.B: 13A plugs, sockets, adaptors and connection units

questions.explanation: Ref: Table 52.1. BS 1362 is the standard for cartridge fuses used in 13 A plugs. BS 1363 covers the plugs and socket accessories themselves.

questions.prompt: BS7671 applies to
questions.explanation: Ref: 110.1(xii). BS 7671 includes photovoltaic supplies as part of its scope for electrical installations. Aircraft, distributor equipment and machine internals are excluded or covered by other rules.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 does not apply to
questions.explanation: Ref: 110.2(ii). Railway traction equipment is outside the normal scope of BS 7671. Fairgrounds and marinas are special installations covered by Part 7.

questions.prompt: Protection against electric shock under single fault conditions is
questions.explanation: Ref: Definitions. Fault protection is protection against electric shock under single-fault conditions. Basic protection is for normal conditions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not be defined as a live part?
questions.explanation: A live part is a conductor intended to be energised in normal use, including line and neutral conductors and the neutral bar. A PEN conductor also serves as the protective earth, so it is treated as a protective/earthed conductor rather than a live part.

questions.prompt: Every installation should be divided into circuits as necessary to avoid

options.B: Hazards to minimise inconvenience in the event of a fault

questions.explanation: Ref: 314.1(i). Circuit division reduces danger and inconvenience when a fault occurs because only the affected circuit should disconnect. It also makes isolation and maintenance more manageable.

questions.prompt: The protective measure 'automatic disconnection of supply'

options.A: Is a combination of basic and fault protection
options.B: Is a combination of under and over voltage protection
options.C: Is a method of reducing thermal effects
options.D: Is only permitted if the installation is under effective supervision

questions.explanation: Ref: 411.1(i)(ii). Automatic disconnection of supply combines basic protection with fault protection. It prevents normal contact with live parts and disconnects quickly if a fault makes exposed metalwork live.

questions.prompt: The maximum disconnection time for a 16A final circuit having Uo 230V ac on a TN system is
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 41. For a 16 A final circuit at Uo 230 V on a TN system, the table disconnection time is 0.4 seconds. This limits the duration of dangerous touch voltage.

questions.prompt: Where there is a danger of fire due to the nature of stored materials a motor with star – delta starting must be protected against excessive temperature
questions.explanation: Ref: 422.3.7. Star-delta motors can overheat in either starting or running configuration if a fault or abnormal condition occurs. Protection in both star and delta covers both operating states.

questions.prompt: In the event of failure of the provision for basic protection, additional protection may be provided by

options.C: Use of a RCD with lΔn not exceeding 30mA
options.D: Use of a time delay 100mA RCD

questions.explanation: Ref: 415.1.1. A 30 mA RCD is used as additional protection if basic protection fails. It is intended to reduce the duration of current through a person.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a method of fault protection
questions.explanation: Ref: 417.1. Placing out of reach is a basic-protection measure, not fault protection, because it only reduces access to live parts in normal conditions. Fault protection deals with exposed parts becoming live.

questions.prompt: For a TT system where disconnection in the case of earth fault is achieved by RCD, the maximum disconnection time for a general socket in a domestic kitchen is
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 41.1. TT systems normally rely on RCDs because earth fault current may be low. For the general socket circuit in the question, the maximum disconnection time is 0.2 seconds.

questions.prompt: In the event of an earth fault on the HV side of a substation, the LV installation may be affected by
questions.explanation: Ref: 422.2(ii). An HV earth fault can raise earth potentials and stress the LV installation insulation. The relevant effect is power-frequency stress voltage.

questions.prompt: Connection of extraneous conductive parts to the MET of an installation forms part of the requirements for
questions.explanation: Ref: 411.3.1.2. Main bonding of extraneous-conductive-parts to the MET is part of fault protection. It limits dangerous potential differences during earth faults.

questions.prompt: Thermoplastic PVC T&E buried less than 50mm must be protected by

options.B: Cpc the same size as the P & N

questions.explanation: Ref: 522.6.7. A thermoplastic T&E cable buried less than 50 mm deep is vulnerable to penetration. A 30 mA RCD provides additional protection where the cable lacks other accepted protection.

questions.prompt: RCD installed for protection against fire must have a rating not exceeding
questions.explanation: Ref: 532.1(i). RCDs used for fire protection are limited to 300 mA residual operating current. That level helps detect leakage faults that could cause overheating or fire.

questions.prompt: Which of the following may not be used as an earth electrode
questions.explanation: Ref: 542.2.1. Water utility supply pipes cannot be used as earth electrodes because continuity and ownership cannot be guaranteed. Purpose-made electrodes or suitable structural metalwork are acceptable options.

questions.prompt: Socket outlets with a rating not exceeding 20A for general use by ordinary persons should be
questions.explanation: Ref: 411.3.3(i) and 415.1. General-use socket-outlets up to 20 A need 30 mA RCD additional protection for ordinary persons. The RCD reduces shock risk from portable equipment and damaged leads.

questions.prompt: Lighting installations in bus shelters must be protected by
questions.explanation: Ref: 559.10.3.2 and 415.1. Bus-shelter lighting is accessible outdoors, so additional protection is required. A 30 mA RCD provides that protection.

questions.prompt: Busbar trunking systems must comply with
questions.explanation: Busbar trunking systems are factory-assembled, so they comply with the busbar trunking product standard, BS EN 60439-2. The other listed numbers cover plugs and couplers, miniature circuit breakers and cable trunking, which are different product types.

questions.prompt: The minimum acceptable value for insulation resistance in 230v supply is
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 61. For a 230 V low-voltage circuit, the minimum acceptable insulation resistance is 1.0 Mohm. Lower values indicate possible insulation deterioration or connected equipment affecting the test.

questions.prompt: Insulation resistance measured between line and neutral of a 230v domestic installation should not be less than
questions.explanation: Good insulation between live conductors should let almost no current leak across it, so on a 230 V (low voltage) circuit tested at 500 V the reading between line and neutral must be at least 1.0 megohm to be acceptable.

questions.prompt: A PV generator and array junction box must have a warning label indicating that

options.B: PV array must be cleaned regularly
options.D: Parts inside may still be live following isolation

questions.explanation: Ref: 712.537.2.2.5.1. PV d.c. equipment can remain live after isolation because the array can still generate voltage in light. The warning label alerts workers to that residual live risk.

questions.prompt: All circuits in a bathroom must have
questions.explanation: Ref: 701.411.3.3. Bathroom circuits require 30 mA RCD protection because wet conditions increase shock risk. The rule applies to all circuits serving the location.

questions.prompt: Electrical cables in Zone 1 of a fountain shall be protected against mechanical impact to
questions.explanation: Cables in zone 1 of a fountain are within reach and subject to knocks and water, so they must be protected to impact classification AG2 (medium severity) to withstand the mechanical stresses likely in that location.

questions.prompt: On agricultural premises an RCD may be used for protection against fire providing that the rating of the RCD does not exceed
questions.explanation: Ref: 705.411.1(iii). Agricultural premises have increased fire and shock risks from dust, moisture and livestock. RCD fire protection is limited to a maximum of 300 mA.

questions.prompt: Any luminaries of lighting chains used at a circus must be firmly fixed when at a height less than
questions.explanation: At a circus or fairground, low-hung lighting chains within easy reach of people could be pulled or struck, so any luminaire below 2.5 m must be firmly fixed to prevent it being dislodged and causing injury or a shock hazard.

questions.prompt: In a bathroom the protective measure of obstacles is
questions.explanation: Ref: 701.410.3.5. Obstacles are not permitted as a bathroom protective measure because wet, barefoot users cannot be expected to rely on barriers or distance. More robust measures such as ADS and RCD protection are required.

questions.prompt: Where a TN system of earthing is used in a marina the final circuits for the supply of a pleasure craft must not include
questions.explanation: Ref: 709.411.4. A PEN conductor must not be included in final circuits supplying pleasure craft in a marina. Loss of a PEN in that wet environment could make exposed metalwork dangerously live.

questions.prompt: For a 100 mA non-delay RCD to BSEN 61008 the residual test currents and maximum permitted disconnection times are
questions.explanation: A general-purpose (non-delay) RCD is tested at its rated current and at five times that value. At 100 mA it may take up to 300 ms to trip, but at 500 mA the higher fault current must disconnect it much faster, within 40 ms.

questions.prompt: Flat T & E cable clipped direct to a ceiling joist where thermal insulation exceeds 100mm thickness is installation method
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 4A2 Page 265. Flat twin-and-earth clipped to a joist with thermal insulation exceeding 100 mm is treated as installation method 101. That method reflects the reduced heat dissipation caused by insulation.

questions.prompt: To which of the following electrical installations does the IEE Regulations NOT apply?

options.D: Systems for transmission of energy to the public

questions.explanation: Regulation 110.2 lists the installations that fall outside the scope of BS 7671, and the public distribution network is one of them. Systems for the generation and transmission of energy to the public are governed by separate statutory regulations rather than the Wiring Regulations.

questions.prompt: The BS 7671 relates to permanent and temporary installations for:
questions.explanation: Regulation 110.1 sets out the types of installation BS 7671 covers, including temporary works such as construction and demolition sites. These sites are within scope because they are fixed installations of a permanent or temporary nature, even though Section 704 adds extra requirements for their harsh conditions.

questions.prompt: An a.c. voltage of 90 V between conductors is classified as:
questions.explanation: Under the Part 2 definitions, low voltage spans above 50 V up to 1000 V a.c. between conductors, so 90 V sits within that band. It exceeds the 50 V ceiling for extra-low voltage, placing it firmly in the low voltage category.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following types of installation is NOT included in the special installations recognised by the IEE Wiring Regulations?
questions.explanation: Part 7 of BS 7671 lists the special installations and locations given particular requirements, covering agricultural premises, saunas and swimming pools. Petrol filling stations are absent because their explosive-atmosphere risks are handled under separate hazardous-area standards rather than the Wiring Regulations.

questions.prompt: The MAXIMUM accessible distance that it should be assumed a person can reach when standing on a surface is:
questions.explanation: Regulation 417.3.3, dealing with protection by placing out of reach, defines arm's reach using fixed dimensions from the standing surface. The maximum distance a person is assumed able to reach upwards while standing is taken as 2.5 m, setting how far live parts must be kept.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 requires that the designer of a new installation shall:

options.C: Have at least three years experience

questions.explanation: Regulation 134.2.2 requires the designer to advise on the frequency of subsequent inspection and testing for the installation. Recommending future inspection and testing ensures the installation can be assessed over its life so that protective measures remain effective and safe.

questions.prompt: Non-sheathed cables for fixed wiring, other than protective conductors, should always be installed in:
questions.explanation: Regulation 521.10.1 requires non-sheathed cables for fixed wiring to be enclosed because they have no mechanical protection of their own. Housing them in conduit or trunking provides the containment and protection against damage that their single layer of insulation alone cannot give.

questions.prompt: A final circuit is the wiring between the:

options.A: Consumer's main earth terminal and circuit protective device
options.C: Main cut-out and the energy meter
options.D: Main switch and the distribution board

questions.explanation: The Part 2 definitions describe a final circuit as the circuit connected directly to current-using equipment, or to socket-outlets or other outlet points, downstream of a distribution board. It is therefore the wiring running from that board to the equipment it supplies.

questions.prompt: The prospective short circuit current at the origin of the consumer's installation must be taken into account when:

options.A: Estimating the external earth loop impedance
options.B: Selecting the system of earthing for the supply
options.C: Selecting the type of overcurrent protective device to be installed
options.D: Supplying diversity factor for the installation

questions.explanation: Regulation 434.5.1 requires every protective device to have a breaking capacity at least equal to the prospective fault current at its point of installation. The prospective short-circuit current at the origin therefore governs the type and rating of overcurrent device that can safely interrupt a fault.

questions.prompt: A system is defined as:

options.A: A single source of energy and an installation
options.B: The consumer's terminals of an installation
options.C: The distribution cables to an installation
options.D: The kWh meter and an installation

questions.explanation: In the Part 2 definitions a system means an electrical system comprising a single source of electrical energy together with an installation. Both elements are needed, since the source and its earthing arrangement combine with the installation to form the complete system, such as TN-S or TT.

questions.prompt: The total number of socket-outlets that may be connected to a fused spur is:

options.A: Equal to half the number of socket – outlets on the ring
options.B: Equal to the total number of socket – outlets on the ring
options.C: One twin or one single socket – outlet

questions.explanation: Appendix 15 shows that a fused spur taken from a ring final circuit is limited only by the rating of its protecting fuse, typically 13 A. Because that fuse caps the load, the number of socket-outlets fed from the spur is unlimited provided the demand stays within the fuse rating.

questions.prompt: Residual current circuit breakers shall NOT be used on a TN system where a circuit incorporates:
questions.explanation: A residual current device works by detecting imbalance between line and neutral, but a PEN conductor combines neutral and protective functions in one conductor. Regulation 411.4.4 prohibits this arrangement because the RCD cannot sense earth fault current where the protective and neutral currents share a single PEN conductor.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is a method of providing fault protection?
questions.explanation: Regulation 412 treats double or reinforced insulation as a recognised fault-protection measure, since a second layer of insulation prevents exposed metalwork becoming live if the basic insulation fails. The other listed methods provide only basic protection against contact with normally live parts.

questions.prompt: In addition to regular maintenance of an installation, which one of the following is NOT an essential requirement?

options.A: Periodic inspection and testing may be readily and safely carried out
options.B: Protective measures for safety remain effective
options.C: The name and address of the contractor is permanently displayed adjacent to the main intake position
options.D: The reliability of the equipment is sustained

questions.explanation: Regulation 341.1 requires that maintenance allows protective measures to stay effective, equipment reliability to be sustained, and inspection and testing to be carried out safely. Permanently displaying the contractor's name and address is not among these maintenance requirements, so it is not an essential condition.

questions.prompt: Where separated extra-low voltage is used to provide basic protection and fault protection, the nominal voltage shall NOT exceed:
questions.explanation: Where SELV or separated extra-low voltage provides both basic and fault protection, Regulation 414 limits the nominal voltage to the extra-low voltage band. The upper limit is 50 V a.c., the threshold below which the shock risk from direct contact is considered acceptably low.

questions.prompt: Overload current is defined as the overcurrent:

options.A: Flowing in a line conductor when in contact with exposed conductive parts
options.B: Occurring in a circuit which is electrically sound
options.C: Resulting from a fault of negligible impedance between live conductors of different phases
options.D: That causes protective devices to operate of correctly

questions.explanation: The Part 2 definitions describe overload current as an overcurrent occurring in a circuit that is electrically sound, with no fault present. It arises from excessive demand rather than a fault, distinguishing it from short-circuit current which flows between live conductors through negligible impedance.

questions.prompt: The IEE Regulations are designed to provide:

options.B: Instructions for every circumstance in an installation
options.D: Safety especially from fire, shock and burns

questions.explanation: Regulation 131.1 states that the fundamental purpose of the requirements is to provide for the safety of persons, livestock and property against the dangers arising from an installation. Protection from fire, electric shock and burns is precisely the safety this is intended to secure.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not permitted as a means of isolation in a circuit?
questions.explanation: Regulation 537.2.2.1 requires isolation to create a secure break in the supply, and semiconductor devices cannot provide this. A semiconductor may still pass leakage and offers no reliable air gap, so it is not acceptable as a means of isolation.

questions.prompt: When a line conductor comes in contact with the neutral conductor, the type of fault is called:
questions.explanation: A short circuit is a fault of negligible impedance between live conductors, so a line touching the neutral creates a path between two points that should be at different potentials. This drives a very high current that the protective device must clear, distinct from an earth fault to exposed metalwork.

questions.prompt: A means of isolation must be provided in an electrical installation. This is required to be:

options.A: Always placed next to the equipment it isolates

questions.explanation: Isolation devices must be clearly identified so anyone working on the installation can be certain which circuit or equipment has been made dead before starting. Reliable identification, typically by durable labelling, prevents accidental re-energisation and reduces the risk of working on apparently dead conductors that are still live.

questions.prompt: Which one of the arrangements complies with the IEE Wiring Regulations?

options.A: The fire fighter's switch is coloured red and fixed 2.5 m above the floor
options.B: The fire fighter's switch is coloured red and the off position is at the bottom
options.C: The fire fighter's switch is fixed 2 m above the floor and off at the bottom
options.D: The fire fighter's switch is fixed 4 m above the ground and the off at the top

questions.explanation: A firefighter's emergency switch must be coloured red and, to be reached safely from ground level, fixed at no more than 2.75 m above the floor or standing position. Mounting it at 2.5 m and clearly marked lets emergency services rapidly disconnect dangerous discharge lighting on arrival.

questions.prompt: A fire fighter's emergency switch should be provided for:

options.A: Emergency lighting systems operating at low voltage
options.B: Exterior discharge lighting installations exceeding low voltage
options.D: Multi-storey office block fire alarm circuits operating above low voltage

questions.explanation: A firefighter's emergency switch is required for exterior installations operating above low voltage, such as high-voltage discharge or neon signs, where firefighters could otherwise contact dangerous voltages. The switch lets them isolate the hazardous supply from a safe, accessible position before tackling a fire.

questions.prompt: The three general categories of external influence are environment, utilisation and:

options.D: The number and type of live conductors

questions.explanation: External influences are classified under three headings: environment, utilisation, and the construction of the building. Grouping the building's structure separately recognises that materials and design, such as combustibility or structural movement, affect how an installation must be specified and protected.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 details the requirements of devices for emergency switching. Which of the following devices would NOT satisfy these requirements?

options.A: A 32 A plug and socket outlet
options.B: A switch which breaks all live conductors
options.C: A switch which breaks the control circuit of a contactor
options.D: An emergency stop button which breaks the control circuit of a contactor

questions.explanation: Emergency switching devices must break all relevant live conductors in a single action and be capable of being operated reliably under fault conditions. A plug and socket outlet relies on someone withdrawing it and is not designed or intended to act as an emergency switching device.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is required to be considered by BS 7671 when assessing the general characteristics of an electrical installation?

options.D: The standard of electricians working on site

questions.explanation: When assessing general characteristics, the maintainability of an installation must be considered so that inspection, testing and repair can be carried out safely throughout its life. The frequency and quality of maintenance an installation will receive directly affects the design choices made at the outset.

questions.prompt: When calculating the voltage drop in an installation which one of the following should be taken into account?

options.C: The current rating of the fuse
options.D: The operating current of the fuse

questions.explanation: Voltage drop is assessed using the design current the circuit actually carries, since the volt drop depends on the load current flowing in the conductor, not on protective device ratings. Using the design current ensures the calculated drop reflects normal operating conditions and stays within permitted limits.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not considered when calculating the minimum current carrying capacity of live conductors of a cable?
questions.explanation: Minimum current-carrying capacity is found by applying rating factors for influences such as ambient temperature, grouping and the type of protective device to the conductor sizing. Voltage drop is a separate check on circuit length and load, so it is not part of the current-capacity calculation.

questions.prompt: For single circuit cable selection purposes the correction factors must be applied to the:

options.A: Current carrying capacity of the cable
options.B: Current rating of the protective device
options.D: The earth fault current of the circuit

questions.explanation: For a single circuit the correction factors are applied to the current rating of the protective device, because the cable must carry the device's rating without overheating once derated for its installation conditions. This ensures the chosen tabulated cable remains adequately protected against overload.

questions.prompt: The classification code for high wind is:
questions.explanation: External influences are coded by category, class and severity, with the A group covering environment and the 'S' subdivision describing wind and other mechanical influences. High wind therefore carries the classification AS3, the highest severity within that wind grouping.

questions.prompt: Rating factors are applied to the fuse rating of a circuit to determine the minimum current-carrying capacity of cables. A rating factor of 1 is used when a circuit is wired in 70o C thermoplastic insulated cable and operating in an ambient temperature of:
questions.explanation: The tabulated cable ratings are referenced to a standard ambient of 30 degrees C for thermoplastic insulated cables, so at that temperature no correction is needed. A rating factor of 1 applies because the operating conditions match the reference conditions used to derive the tabulated values.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not recognised by BS 7671:2018 as the sole means of earthing an installation?

options.B: Metal bars embedded in the building foundations
options.C: Metallic rod driven into the ground

questions.explanation: Gas and water service pipes are not permitted as the sole means of earthing because they may be replaced with plastic sections or removed without warning, breaking the earth path. A dedicated, reliable earthing arrangement such as an electrode or supply earth must be provided instead.

questions.prompt: A BS 1361 fuse, rated at 45 A, is carrying a fault current of 240A, the protective device should operate in:
questions.explanation: The time/current characteristic for a 45 A BS 1361 fuse shows that a fault current of 240 A, roughly five times its rating, falls on the part of the curve giving a disconnection time of about 5 seconds. Higher fault currents would clear faster, lower ones much more slowly.

questions.prompt: The maximum permissible earth fault loop impedance on a TN system for a ring final circuit protected by a 30 A BS 1361 fuse is:
questions.explanation: Maximum earth fault loop impedance values ensure the protective device disconnects within the required time so that touch voltages cannot persist. For a 30 A BS 1361 fuse meeting the relevant disconnection time on a TN system, the tabulated maximum Zs is 1.15 ohms.

questions.prompt: The wording of a permanent warning notice fixed at the point of connection of an earthing conductor to an earth electrode is:

options.D: Safety Electrical Connection – Do Not Remove

questions.explanation: A durable label reading 'Safety Electrical Connection - Do Not Remove' must be fixed at the connection of the earthing conductor to the earth electrode. The wording warns anyone that the connection is essential for safety, preventing its removal and the loss of earth protection.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following sources does not comply with BS 7671 as a SELV system?

options.A: A battery system operating at extra low voltage
options.B: A centre tapped transformer giving 55 V to earth
options.C: A motor generator with windings providing equivalent isolation to that of a safety isolating transformer
options.D: A safely isolating transformer to BS EN 61558

questions.explanation: A SELV system requires protective separation from earth, supplied typically by a safety isolating transformer or battery with no point connected to earth. A centre-tapped transformer giving 55 V to earth is deliberately earthed, so it forms a reduced low voltage system rather than a SELV one.

questions.prompt: The minimum size of a copper earthing conductor buried in the ground, NOT mechanically protected and NOT protected against corrosion is:
questions.explanation: An earthing conductor buried in the ground that is neither mechanically protected nor protected against corrosion must be at least 25 mm sq in copper. The larger cross-section provides reserve against corrosion loss and mechanical damage so the earth path remains reliable over time.

questions.prompt: When calculating the minimum cross-sectional area of a protective conductor, the following information is available: Fault current = 650 A Operating time of protective device = 0.35 sec Constant, k, for protective conductor material = 115 The selected size of the protective conductor should be:
questions.explanation: The adiabatic equation S = √(I²t)/k gives the minimum protective conductor size. With a 650 A fault for 0.35 s and k of 115, this yields roughly 3.3 mm², so the next standard size above the calculated minimum is the smallest acceptable conductor.

questions.prompt: When a residual current device protects a socket outlet in a domestic garage it must operate when:

options.A: An earth fault on the garage lighting circuit occurs
options.B: Someone comes in contact with exposed earth metalwork
options.C: Someone comes in direct contact with an exposed line conductor and earth
options.D: The protective conductor in a flexible cord to a lawn mower breaks

questions.explanation: An RCD provides additional protection against electric shock by detecting the imbalance between line and neutral that flows when current escapes to earth through a person. Direct contact between a live conductor and earth diverts current through the body, which the device senses and disconnects rapidly.

questions.prompt: Where an auto-transformer is connected to a single-phase supply (phase and neutral) the common terminal of the winding should be connected to the:
questions.explanation: An auto-transformer shares a single winding between input and output, so the common terminal sits at the supply reference point. Connecting it to the neutral keeps the shared portion of the winding at or near earth potential, limiting the voltage to earth and reducing shock risk.

questions.prompt: Circuit cables required to carry the starting, accelerating and load currents of motors shall have a current rating not less than:
questions.explanation: Conductors supplying motors must be rated to carry the steady full-load current continuously, since this is the current present during normal running. Although starting and accelerating draw higher transient currents, these are brief and are accommodated by the protective device coordination rather than by oversizing the cable.

questions.prompt: As part of a detailed inspection which of the following must be checked?

options.A: The manufacturer's name of any RCD fitted
options.C: The presence of fire barriers and protection against thermal effects
options.D: The prospective short circuit current at the origin of the installation

questions.explanation: Detailed inspection must confirm that measures protecting against the spread of fire and thermal effects are in place, including fire barriers and seals where wiring penetrates fire-rated elements. These passive measures cannot be checked by testing, so they must be verified by inspection before the installation is energised.

questions.prompt: Which of the following items should be included for checking during the initial verification of an installation:
questions.explanation: Initial verification requires confirming that the necessary diagrams, charts and instructions are present so the installation can be understood and safely maintained. Without this documentation, those operating or testing the installation lack the information needed to identify circuits and switching arrangements.

questions.prompt: One item that should be included on charts and diagrams made available to the person carrying out an inspection and test is:

options.B: The details of the original contract arrangements
options.C: The location details of portable equipment
options.D: The total number of outlets in the installation

questions.explanation: Diagrams and charts provided for inspection and testing must identify every means of isolation and switching, so circuits can be safely disconnected before work begins. Knowing where isolation points are located is essential for safe operation and for tracing the installation during testing.

questions.prompt: Which on of the following insulation resistance test results, meets the minimum acceptable value for an installation with a 400 V supply?
questions.explanation: For circuits up to and including 500 V, the minimum acceptable insulation resistance is 1.0 MΩ. A 400 V installation falls within this band, so any measured value at or above one megohm satisfies the requirement and confirms the insulation is sound.

questions.prompt: The test voltage required to carry out an insulation resistance test on an installation with a nominal supply voltage of 400 V is:
questions.explanation: Insulation resistance on circuits rated up to 500 V is tested at a DC test voltage of 500 V. Applying this raised voltage stresses the insulation realistically while remaining safe for the wiring, so a 400 V installation is tested at 500 V DC.

questions.prompt: An earth fault loop impedance test determines the actual value of:
questions.explanation: Zs is the total earth fault loop impedance, comprising the external impedance Ze plus the resistance of the circuit conductors R1 and R2. The loop impedance test measures this complete path so the result can be compared against the maximum permitted for the protective device to disconnect in time.

questions.prompt: Electrical installation certificates should be signed by those responsible for the:
questions.explanation: An Electrical Installation Certificate must be signed, or otherwise authenticated, by the competent persons responsible for the design, the construction, and the inspection and testing of the work. These three functions confirm that every stage of the installation meets the standard, even where one person undertakes all of them.

questions.prompt: The result and extent of a Periodic Inspection and Test shall be recorded and given to the:
questions.explanation: On completion of periodic inspection and testing, the report detailing its results and extent must be given to the person who ordered the work. They are responsible for the installation and need the findings to act on any recommendations and arrange remedial work.

questions.prompt: The following tests are to be carried out on a new installation 1 insulation resistance 2 continuity of ring final circuit 3 continuity of protective conductors 4 earth loop impedance 5 polarity
questions.explanation: Tests are performed in a set sequence so each builds on a safe foundation: continuity of protective conductors, then ring continuity, insulation resistance, and polarity are all done dead before earth fault loop impedance, which is a live test. This order protects the tester and gives valid results.

questions.prompt: One reason for carrying out a polarity test is:

options.A: Fuses are fitted in the phase conductor
options.D: The outer screwed contact is connected to the phase conductor

questions.explanation: Polarity testing confirms that single-pole devices such as fuses, circuit breakers and switches are connected in the line conductor and not the neutral. If protection were placed in the neutral, the circuit would remain live to earth when switched off, leaving a dangerous shock and fire risk.

questions.prompt: When carrying out a continuity of circuit protective conductor test, it is recommended that a test instrument operates at:

options.A: 20 V and delivers a short circuit current of 100 mA
options.B: 20 V and delivers a short circuit current of 200 mA
options.C: 50 V and delivers a short circuit current of 200 mA
options.D: 500 V and delivers a short circuit current of 100 mA

questions.explanation: Continuity of protective conductors should be tested with an instrument giving an open-circuit voltage between 4 and 24 V and a short-circuit current of at least 200 mA. This low test voltage with adequate current reliably detects high-resistance joints without endangering the tester.

questions.prompt: One of the purposes of an inspection prior to initial testing of an installation, is to verify that the installed equipment is:

options.A: Connected to the supply and energised
options.B: Exceeds the minimum insulation resistance value

questions.explanation: Inspection precedes testing to confirm by sight that equipment is correctly selected, properly installed and not visibly damaged before any voltage is applied. Detecting damage at this stage prevents an unsafe item being energised and protects both the tester and the installation.

questions.prompt: Electrical equipment installed above a swimming pool diving board should not be fixed at a height less than:
questions.explanation: In the zones around a swimming pool, equipment above the highest diving board or platform must be mounted at a sufficient height to keep it out of reach of people in or around the water. The minimum clearance of 2.5 m reduces the risk of contact in this wet location.

questions.prompt: Which of the following may be installed inside a hot air sauna?

options.A: A ceiling mounted cord operated light switch
options.B: A socket outlet fed from an SELV supply source
options.C: A thermostat mounted on the sauna
options.D: Any equipment and accessories to IP24

questions.explanation: A sauna is divided into temperature zones, and only equipment necessary for its operation, such as the heater and its controlling thermostat, may be installed in the hotter zones. The thermostat must withstand the high ambient temperature, whereas socket outlets and ordinary switchgear are not permitted there.

questions.prompt: Construction site special regulations apply to:
questions.explanation: The special requirements of Section 704 apply to temporary installations on construction and demolition sites, which expressly include earthworks. Permanent welfare buildings such as offices, canteens and toilets are treated as ordinary installations rather than the harsher site environment.

questions.prompt: In agricultural premises, an RCD may be used for protection against fire providing the operating current does not exceed:
questions.explanation: In agricultural and horticultural locations an RCD provided specifically for protection against fire is permitted a rated residual operating current of up to 300 mA. This higher threshold guards against fire-starting earth faults while avoiding the nuisance tripping that a 30 mA device would suffer in such conditions.

questions.prompt: The minimum cross-sectional area of any conductor in a caravan is:
questions.explanation: Wiring within a caravan or motor caravan must use conductors of at least 1.5 mm² cross-sectional area. The minimum reflects the mechanical stresses and vibration of a mobile unit, ensuring conductors are robust enough to resist fatigue and damage in service.

questions.prompt: The maximum permissible height for a caravan inlet is:
questions.explanation: The caravan inlet must be mounted no more than 1.8 m above ground level. Limiting the height keeps the connection point accessible for safe coupling of the supply flexible cable while remaining clear of standing water and ground-level damage.

questions.prompt: One method acceptable to the IEE Regulations for providing fault protection on circuits feeding street furniture is by:
questions.explanation: Highway power supplies and street furniture rely on the standard protective measure of automatic disconnection of supply for fault protection. This ensures a dangerous earth fault is cleared within the required time by the protective device, the same principle applied throughout general installations.

questions.prompt: BS7671 relates to electrical installations in and around buildings but excludes:
questions.explanation: The scope of BS 7671 covers fixed installations in and around buildings but explicitly excludes certain specialist systems, among them equipment of ships and offshore installations. These are governed by separate maritime standards rather than the Wiring Regulations.

questions.prompt: Parts 3 to 7 of BS 7671 covers in detail methods and practices which meets the requirements of:
questions.explanation: Chapter 13 sets out the fundamental principles for safety, and the detailed methods and practices in Parts 3 to 7 are the means of meeting those principles. Compliance with the detailed regulations is therefore deemed to satisfy the fundamental requirements.

questions.prompt: The IEE Regulations recognises that in electrical installations there is a risk of injury from:
questions.explanation: The fundamental principles recognise that an electrical installation presents a risk of injury from shock currents flowing through the body. Protection against electric shock is accordingly the first hazard the Regulations address through basic and fault protective measures.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following types of installations is NOT within the statutory control of an authoritative body?
questions.explanation: Special locations such as caravan sites, petrol stations and theatres are subject to statutory licensing or control by an authoritative body. An ordinary domestic dwelling carries no such specific statutory oversight, being governed instead by general building and wiring requirements.

questions.prompt: The type of building construction in which an installation is to be carried out may affect the design and safe operation of the installation. This effect is called:
questions.explanation: The nature of the building construction is one of the external influences that the designer must assess, since it affects how the installation is designed and operated safely. External influences cover environmental and structural factors imposed on the installation from outside the electrical system itself.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not classed as a Band 1 voltage circuit?
questions.explanation: Band I covers extra-low-voltage and signalling circuits such as SELV, bell and low-voltage signalling systems where shock protection at low voltage is the concern. A 230 V lighting circuit operates at low voltage and therefore falls within Band II, not Band I.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following external influences requires an increase in the current ratings of cables above those normally required?
questions.explanation: A high ambient temperature reduces a cable's ability to dissipate heat, so a rating factor must be applied that lowers its current-carrying capacity. The conductor must be sized larger than normal to compensate and stay within its permitted operating temperature.

questions.prompt: One of the general categories of external influences is:
questions.explanation: External influences are grouped into three general categories, the first of which is the environment, covering conditions such as temperature, water, dust and corrosive substances. The other categories concern utilisation and the construction of buildings around the installation.

questions.prompt: Where the circuit protective conductor is not a metal cable covering or metal trunking and conduit, the c.p.c for a ring final circuit must:

options.B: Be run in the form of a ring having both ends connected to the earthing terminal
options.D: Have a cross-sectional area not less than that of the live conductors of the ring

questions.explanation: Where the protective conductor is a separate conductor rather than a metallic enclosure, the cpc of a ring final circuit must itself be run as a ring with both ends connected to the earthing terminal. This provides two parallel earth paths and continuity even if one leg is broken.

questions.prompt: A TN-C-S system has:

options.A: A separate protective conductor connecting the source earth to the consumers main earth terminal
options.B: The exposed conductive parts of an installation connected to an earth electrode which is independent to the source
options.C: The neutral and earth functions combined in a single conductor in part of the system
options.D: The neutral and protective conductors are combined throughout the system

questions.explanation: In a TN-C-S system the neutral and protective functions are combined in a single PEN conductor for part of the system, typically the supply, then separated into distinct neutral and earth conductors within the installation. This combined-then-split arrangement is the defining feature of the system.

questions.prompt: Installations should be arranged so as to avoid danger and minimise inconvenience in the event of a fault and facilitate safe operation, inspection, testing and maintenance. One method of complying with this is to:

options.A: Connect all circuits on the radial principle
options.B: Divide the installation into lighting and power
options.C: Divide the installation into separate circuits
options.D: Fit an RCD at the main intake position

questions.explanation: Dividing the installation into separate circuits limits the consequences of a fault to one circuit, reduces inconvenience from a single failure and allows individual circuits to be isolated for testing and maintenance. This is how the requirement to avoid danger and facilitate safe operation is met.

questions.prompt: The prospective short circuit current at the origin of the consumer's installation must be taken into account when:

options.A: Assessing the methods to be used to provide basic protection
options.B: Assessing the value of the external earth loop impedance
options.C: Selecting the number of ways required for the main distribution board
options.D: Selecting the type of overcurrent protective device to be installed

questions.explanation: The prospective fault current at the origin determines the breaking capacity that a protective device must possess. The selected overcurrent device must be able to interrupt the maximum fault current safely, so this value governs the type and rating chosen.

questions.prompt: A two-storey domestic dwelling should have a minimum of two lighting circuits in order to:

options.A: Avoid danger in the event of a fault
options.B: Enable a greater variety of luminaires to be used
options.C: Reduce the load on the consumer unit
options.D: Use 10 A circuit breakers for the lighting circuits

questions.explanation: Providing at least two lighting circuits means that a fault clearing one circuit still leaves part of the dwelling illuminated, avoiding the danger of being left in total darkness. Subdividing the installation in this way is a direct application of the requirement to avoid danger in the event of a fault.

questions.prompt: With reference to the general characteristics of an electrical installation, the maximum demand should be:
questions.explanation: Regulation 311.1 requires maximum demand to be assessed rather than taken as the simple sum of every connected load. Because circuits and appliances rarely all draw full current at once, diversity is applied so that conductors and protective devices can be economically yet safely sized.

questions.prompt: The requirements for both basic and fault protection can be provided by SELV. One suitable source of SELV would be a:
questions.explanation: SELV provides both basic and fault protection by limiting voltage and keeping the circuit electrically separated from earth and from higher-voltage systems. A 50 V storage battery satisfies this because it is an independent extra-low-voltage supply with no electrical connection to the mains or earth.

questions.prompt: Residual current circuit breakers shall NOT be used on a TN system where a circuit incorporates:
questions.explanation: An RCD operates by detecting the imbalance between line and neutral currents. A PEN conductor combines neutral and protective functions in one conductor, so normal return current would flow through the RCD's sensing path and cause unwanted tripping, which is why Regulation 414.4.4 forbids this arrangement.

questions.prompt: A component of a support system consisting of regularly spaced elements which mechanically retains a cable is defined as a cable:
questions.explanation: By definition a cable cleat is a support component made of regularly spaced elements that mechanically retains a cable along its run. Unlike trays or ladders that merely carry cables, cleats grip the cable at intervals and resist the mechanical forces produced under fault conditions.

questions.prompt: SELV can be used as a means to meet the requirements of both basic and fault protection. In such cases the nominal voltage must not exceed:
questions.explanation: Regulation 414.1.1 sets the upper nominal limit for SELV and PELV at 50 V ac. Keeping below this touch-voltage threshold means the voltage itself is low enough that, combined with circuit separation, it provides both basic and fault protection without further measures.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following classifications of external influences would be appropriate for an item of electrical equipment installed where it would be subject to an atmosphere where heavy dust is present?
questions.explanation: The external influence classification in Appendix 5 uses code AE for the presence of foreign solid bodies, with the final digit rising as severity increases.
