AE6 denotes a heavy-dust environment, so equipment must be selected with an enclosure rating able to exclude that quantity of dust.

questions.prompt: The fault current due to an earth fault of negligible impedance in a 400 V, three phase, four wire circuit having an earth loop impedance of 0.3 ohms, is:
questions.explanation: Earth fault current is found from the phase voltage to earth divided by the earth fault loop impedance. In a 400 V three-phase four-wire system the line-to-earth voltage is 230 V, so 230 divided by 0.3 ohms gives approximately 767 A.

questions.prompt: A section of a factory requires urgent repairs to a machine. The type of switching provided to allow this work to proceed would be switching for:
questions.explanation: Switching for mechanical maintenance is provided so that non-electrical work, such as repairing a machine, can be carried out safely with the equipment made dead. Regulation 537.3 distinguishes this from emergency switching, since the need here is planned removal of power rather than rapid response to danger.

questions.prompt: The correct classifications of an external influence consisting of light dust is:
questions.explanation: Within the AE classification of Appendix 5 for solid foreign bodies, lower numbers indicate lighter contamination. AE4 corresponds to the presence of light dust, guiding the designer toward equipment with an ingress protection rating suited to that modest level of dust.

questions.prompt: Lz is the current rating of a circuit conductor. The requirements for overload current protection are fulfilled when:
questions.explanation: Overload protection under Regulation 433.1.1 requires the design current to be no greater than the device rating, which in turn must not exceed the conductor's current-carrying capacity. Only the values Ib 9 A, In 15 A and Iz 17 A satisfy this ascending relationship.

questions.prompt: Where the overcurrent device is intended to afford protection against overload, l2 must NOT exceed lz times:
questions.explanation: The second condition of Regulation 433.1.1 limits the current ensuring effective operation of the device, I2, to 1.45 times the conductor's rating Iz. This ceiling keeps the conductor below a damaging temperature during sustained small overloads before the protective device finally operates.

questions.prompt: A fault current caused by the line and neutral conductors to come in contact with each other is referred to as:
questions.explanation: A short-circuit fault is defined as an overcurrent resulting from a fault of negligible impedance between live conductors, such as line touching neutral. Because there is almost no impedance in the fault path, very large currents flow that the protective device must clear rapidly.

questions.prompt: A 230 V single-phase circuit supplying a pump motor is protected by a 20 A circuit breaker to BS EN 60898 type B. The minimum value of fault current to ensure compliance with thermal and shock constraints is:
questions.explanation: A type B device to BS EN 60898 operates instantaneously at five times its rated current, so a 20 A breaker needs at least 100 A of fault current to trip within the required time. This minimum value ensures both thermal protection of the cable and prompt disconnection for shock safety.

questions.prompt: Where a means of isolation is provided in an electrical installation, the means must be:
questions.explanation: Regulation 537.2.2.6 requires that a device used for isolation be clearly identified by durable marking, normally a label indicating the installation or circuit it isolates. This ensures the correct device is operated when work is carried out, preventing inadvertent reconnection or isolation of the wrong circuit.

questions.prompt: Overload current is an overcurrent occurring in a circuit:
questions.explanation: An overload current is defined as an overcurrent occurring in a circuit that is electrically sound, meaning there is no fault. It arises simply because the connected load exceeds the design value, which distinguishes it from short-circuit or earth-fault currents caused by insulation failure.

questions.prompt: The designer/installer of a ceiling heating system must provide a plan for the installation. Information NOT required on the plan would be the:

options.C: Number of rooms within the installation

questions.explanation: Regulation 753.514 lists the information a heating-system plan must record so the installation can be maintained safely without damaging the elements. Details such as the number and position of heating units and junction boxes are essential, whereas the number of rooms is not required.

questions.prompt: When 13 A socket outlets are wired from a fused spur using 70o thermoplastic insulated cable with copper conductors, the minimum conductor size permissible is:
questions.explanation: Appendix 15 covers the standard circuit arrangements for socket outlets fed from a fused spur. With the spur protected by a 13 A fuse, a 1.5 mm² thermoplastic copper conductor has sufficient current-carrying capacity to be the minimum permissible size.

questions.prompt: The correction factor for a cable surrounded by thermal insulation for a length of 200 mm is:
questions.explanation: Table 52.2 gives derating factors for cables enclosed in thermal insulation because trapped heat cannot dissipate, raising conductor temperature. For a length of about 200 mm surrounded by insulation, a factor of 0.63 is applied to reduce the cable's rated current-carrying capacity accordingly.

questions.prompt: When selecting a cable for a single circuit installation, correction factors are to be used and applied to the:

options.C: Nominal current of the protective device
options.D: Total current taken by the installation

questions.explanation: Appendix 4 builds correction factors into the cable selection process by relating tabulated current-carrying capacity back to the protective device. The rating of the device must be divided by the applicable factors, so the factors are applied against the nominal current of the protective device to find the required cable size.

questions.prompt: Where protection against overload is provided by a semi-enclosed fuse to BS 3036, the current rating of the cable must be at least:

options.A: 0.725 times the current rating of the fuse
options.B: 0.725 times the design current of the circuit
options.C: The nominal current rating of the fuse divided by 0.725
options.D: The same rating as the design current of the circuit

questions.explanation: Regulation 433.1.3 recognises that semi-enclosed BS 3036 fuses have poor fusing characteristics and need extra current to operate reliably. To ensure overload protection still functions, the cable's current-carrying capacity must be at least the fuse's nominal rating divided by 0.725.

questions.prompt: Correct co-ordination between conductors and overcurrent protection device is achieved when:

options.B: Ln exceeds the lowest current carrying capacity lz
options.C: ln is not less than the design current lb
options.D: The current causing effective operation (l2) exceeds 1.45 l2

questions.explanation: Regulation 433.1.1 requires that the protective device rating In is not less than the design current Ib, so the cable carries the intended load without the device tripping. In must also not exceed the conductor's current-carrying capacity, but the first coordination condition is In being at least Ib.

questions.prompt: In order to calculate the minimum value of the cross-sectional area of a protective conductor the following information is available Fault current = 300 A Operating time of the protective device = 0.6 s Constant k, for protective conductor material = 115 The minimum, cross-sectional area of the protective conductor should be:
questions.explanation: The adiabatic equation in Regulation 543.1.3 gives the minimum cross-sectional area as the square root of (I squared times t) divided by k. With 300 A, 0.6 s and k of 115, this yields about 2.02 mm squared, so the next standard size of 2.5 mm squared is required.

questions.prompt: The rating factor to be applied for eight equally loaded circuits grouped together in conduit is:
questions.explanation: Table 4C1 in Appendix 4 lists grouping rating factors for circuits bunched in conduit or trunking. For eight equally loaded circuits enclosed together the tabulated reduction factor is 0.52, reflecting the mutual heating that lowers each cable's safe current-carrying capacity.

questions.prompt: A circuit is protected by a 10 A BS 3036 semi-enclosed (rewireable) fuse. The minimum permissible current rating (lz) of a conductor protected by this fuse would be:
questions.explanation: Appendix 5 reflects the 0.725 factor needed for BS 3036 rewireable fuses to operate dependably on overload. Dividing the 10 A fuse rating by 0.725 gives 13.8 A, the minimum conductor current-carrying capacity Iz that ensures the fuse still protects against overload.

questions.prompt: An office installation is connected to a TT system and earth fault protection is provided by a residual current device. The product of the rated residual operating current of the device and the earth electrode resistance plus the protective conductor's resistance connecting it to the exposed conductive parts shall not exceed:
questions.explanation: Regulation 411.5.3 limits the touch voltage that can appear on exposed-conductive-parts of a TT system to the conventional safe value of 50 V. The product of the RCD's rated residual operating current and the earthing resistance must therefore not exceed 50 V.

questions.prompt: A circuit is connected to a TN system, the maximum permissible earth fault loop impedance (Zs) for a 32 A socket outlet circuit protected by a BS 88 fuse is:
questions.explanation: Table 41.2 lists maximum earth fault loop impedances that guarantee disconnection within the required time for socket-outlet circuits. For a 32 A BS 88 fuse on a 230 V TN system, the tabulated Zs of 1.04 ohms ensures the fault current is high enough to clear the fault promptly.

questions.prompt: Regulation 434.5.2 gives the maximum time which may be permitted for a fault to be maintained without damaging the conductors. Assume a prospective fault current of 1000 A with a copper 25 mm² cable with 70o C thermoplastic insulation. The clearance time (t) is:
questions.explanation: Regulation 434.5.2 uses the adiabatic relationship t equals (k squared times S squared) divided by I squared to find how long a conductor can carry fault current safely. With k of 115, a 25 mm squared copper conductor and 1000 A, this gives roughly 8.2 s before the insulation is damaged.

questions.prompt: The purpose of having equipotential bonding conductors connected to the other services as close as practicable to their entry into the premises is to:

options.A: Ensure that earth leakage is minimised
options.B: Ensure that the maximum current will flow to earth under fault conditions
options.C: Reduce the chance of electrolytic corrosion between metal sheath of cable and metal pipes
options.D: Reduce the chance of shock risk within the premises

questions.explanation: Main bonding connected close to the point of entry creates equipotentiality between incoming metallic services and the electrical earthing. This keeps exposed and extraneous-conductive-parts at a similar potential during a fault, reducing the voltage that could appear between simultaneously accessible parts and so reducing the shock risk to people.

questions.prompt: Where practicable main equipotential bonding to the gas services in a building should be made:

options.B: Within 6 m of the meter on the supply side
options.C: Within 600 mm of the meter on the consumer's side
options.D: Within 600 mm of the meter on the supply side

questions.explanation: Regulation 544.1.2 requires main bonding to gas to be made at the consumer's side of the meter, within 600 mm of it and before any branch pipework. This ensures the connection captures the installation's metalwork while avoiding the supplier's side and the meter itself.

questions.prompt: Heating cables laid directly in soil, roads or building structures must be installed so that they are:

options.A: At least 1 m below the surface
options.B: Completely embedded in the substance which they are intended to heat
options.C: Fed only from an extra-low voltage supply

questions.explanation: Regulation 554.4.3 requires heating cables buried in soil, roads or structures to be fully embedded in the medium they are meant to heat. Complete embedment ensures heat dissipates into the surrounding material rather than allowing the cable to overheat against an air pocket.

questions.prompt: For circuits of TN or TT systems, the outer contact of Edison type screw lamp holders must be connected to the:
questions.explanation: Connecting the outer screw thread of an Edison-type lampholder to the neutral keeps the easily touched external contact at near-earth potential. Reserving the line conductor for the recessed centre contact greatly reduces the risk of shock when a person changes a lamp.

questions.prompt: The temperature limit for non-metallic equipment which is intended to be touched but not hand held is:
questions.explanation: Table 42.1 sets surface temperature limits to protect against burns. Non-metallic accessible parts that are intended to be touched but not hand-held may reach up to 80 degrees C, a higher limit than metal because non-metals transfer heat to the skin more slowly.

questions.prompt: The correct grouping factor for 6 circuits of three conductors per circuit, run in the same conduit is:
questions.explanation: Table 4C1 in Appendix 4 gives the grouping factor for circuits bunched together in a single conduit. For six circuits enclosed in the same conduit the tabulated reduction factor is 0.57, accounting for the combined heating effect that derates each cable.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following does NOT determine the frequency of periodic inspection and testing of an installation?

options.A: Any external influence to which it is subjected
options.B: Formal qualifications of the inspection and test staff

questions.explanation: Regulation 622.1 bases the interval between periodic inspections on factors affecting the installation itself, such as its type, the external influences it faces, and how often it is maintained. The qualifications of the inspecting staff relate to competence, not to how frequently inspection is required.

questions.prompt: Every new installation on completion and before being energised must FIRST be:

options.A: Given a test for insulation resistance
options.C: Tested for continuity of protective conductors
options.D: Tested for continuity of ring circuit conductors

questions.explanation: Regulation 610.1 requires initial verification to begin with inspection, carried out before testing and with the installation de-energised where practicable. This detailed visual examination confirms equipment is correctly selected and installed and that no obvious dangers exist before any test current is applied.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following items should be included for checking during the initial verification of an installation?

options.C: Presence of all diagrams and instructions

questions.explanation: Initial verification under Regulation 610.2 compares the installation against the design information that should accompany it. As Regulation 514.9.1 requires diagrams, charts and instructions to be provided, confirming their presence is a proper part of checking the installation is complete and safe to operate.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following British Standards covers residual current devices?
questions.explanation: Appendix 1 lists the British Standards referenced by BS 7671, and residual current operated circuit-breakers without integral overcurrent protection fall under BS EN 61008. The other standards relate to safety transformers, miniature circuit-breakers and switchgear, not stand-alone RCDs.

questions.prompt: For an insulation resistance test on a 230 V ac installation containing surge protected socket-outlets, the value of the test voltage may be:
questions.explanation: Regulation 612.3.2 allows the insulation resistance test voltage to be reduced to 250 V dc where surge protective devices or other voltage-sensitive equipment are connected. This prevents the normal 500 V test from damaging the SPDs while still confirming adequate insulation.

questions.prompt: When a 30 mA residual current device used to provide additional protection is tested at a residual current of 150 mA, the device should open in no more than:
questions.explanation: Where an RCD provides additional protection under Regulation 415.1.1, a test current of five times its rated residual operating current must trip it within 40 ms. The faster disconnection at 150 mA confirms the device will act quickly enough to protect against direct contact shock.

questions.prompt: The minimum value of insulation resistance when measured at the consumer unit of a 230 V domestic installation is:
questions.explanation: Table 61 sets the minimum acceptable insulation resistance for a circuit at low voltage up to 500 V, which is 1.0 megohm measured with a 500 V dc test. A lower value indicates deteriorated insulation that could allow dangerous leakage currents to flow.

questions.prompt: The results of periodic inspection and testing should be recorded on a report and signed by the:

options.B: Person carrying out the inspection and test

questions.explanation: Regulation 634.1 requires the inspection and test report to be signed by a competent person who actually carried out the work, taking responsibility for the accuracy of the recorded results. This ensures accountability rests with the individual who assessed the installation's condition.

questions.prompt: Equipment fitted in Zone 1 of a bathroom must:

options.A: Be fed from a plug and socket outlet
options.B: Be rated at a voltage not exceeding 12 V
options.C: Have a minimum IP rating of IPX4
options.D: Have a minimum IP rating of IPX5

questions.explanation: Regulation 701.512.2 sets minimum ingress protection by bathroom zone, and equipment in Zone 1 must be at least IPX4 to withstand splashing water. This guards against water entering enclosures where someone may be using a bath or shower nearby.

questions.prompt: In agricultural premises, an RCD may be used for protection against fire providing the operating current does not exceed:
questions.explanation: Regulation 705.422.7 addresses fire risks in agricultural and horticultural premises, where an RCD rated at no more than 300 mA must protect against fire. This limit ensures the device disconnects persistent earth leakage before it can ignite combustible materials common to such locations.

questions.prompt: For all caravans using a mains electricity supply, an instruction notice must be fixed:

options.A: At or near the main distribution point
options.B: Near the main electrical isolating switch inside the caravan
options.C: On the inside of the main door of the caravan
options.D: Under the cover of the caravan electricity inlet box

questions.explanation: Regulation 721.537.2.1.1.1 requires the operating instruction notice to be displayed near the main isolating switch inside the caravan, where the user connects and disconnects the supply. Placing it there ensures the occupant reads the correct connection and earthing procedure before energising the installation.

questions.prompt: In a swimming pool which of the following protective measures is NOT applicable to equipment installed in Zone 2?

options.B: Protection by an RCD in accordance with Regulation 415.1.1
options.C: Protection by earth free local equipotential bonding

questions.explanation: Under Regulation 702.410.3.4.3, equipment in swimming pool Zone 2 may be protected by SELV, electrical separation or a 30 mA RCD. Earth-free local equipotential bonding is excluded here because it is unsuitable for the wet conditions and accessible nature of pool surrounds.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following may be installed inside Zone 1 of a hot air sauna?

options.A: A ceiling mounted cord operated light switch
options.C: A thermostat attached to the side of the sauna

questions.explanation: Regulation 703.512.2 permits only equipment suited to the high temperatures inside a sauna's hot zone, such as the thermostat controlling the heater. Switches, shaver sockets and general accessories are excluded because they cannot reliably withstand the extreme heat of Zone 1.

questions.prompt: With regards to a transportable unit, a notice fixed in a prominent position on the unit need not display:
questions.explanation: Regulation 717.514 requires a transportable or mobile unit to carry a notice giving its supply type, voltage rating and maximum power demand so it can be connected safely. The supply frequency is not among the mandated details, as it does not affect safe connection.

questions.prompt: Particular requirements are included in BS 7671 for electrical installations of:
questions.explanation: Part 7 of BS 7671 contains particular requirements for special locations, and Section 701 specifically covers rooms containing a bath or shower. These areas demand extra measures because the combination of water and body contact greatly increases the risk of electric shock.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following types of installation is NOT included in the special installations recognised by BS 7671
questions.explanation: Part 7 lists the special installations and locations with particular requirements, including agricultural premises, saunas and swimming pools. Petrol filling stations involve explosive atmospheres governed by separate hazardous-area standards, so they are not among the special locations covered by BS 7671.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following sets of regulations is non-statutory?

options.D: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations

questions.explanation: As Regulation 114.1 explains, BS 7671 is a code of practice rather than a law, so it is non-statutory. The Electricity at Work Regulations and similar instruments are statutory because they are made under Acts of Parliament and carry the force of law.

questions.prompt: A d.c. voltage of 125 V between conductors is classified as:
questions.explanation: The Definitions classify voltage bands by magnitude, with low voltage spanning above 50 V up to 1000 V ac or above 120 V up to 1500 V dc between conductors. At 125 V dc the supply exceeds the extra-low voltage limit, placing it firmly in the low voltage band.

questions.prompt: The type of system known as PME is also referred to as:
questions.explanation: The Definitions describe PME, or protective multiple earthing, as a TN-C-S system where the supply combines neutral and protective functions in one conductor before separating them within the installation. This combined-then-separated arrangement is exactly what the TN-C-S designation denotes.

questions.prompt: A circuit protective conductor connects:

options.A: A gas pipe to the main earthing terminal
options.B: A water pipe to the earth terminal of a switch in a bathroom
options.C: The main earthing terminal to the earth terminal of a socket outlet
options.D: Two water pipes in a bathroom

questions.explanation: A circuit protective conductor, as defined in BS 7671, connects exposed-conductive-parts of equipment back to the main earthing terminal, providing a path for fault current. Running from the main earthing terminal to a socket-outlet's earth terminal is precisely this function.

questions.prompt: An external influence categorised as AG1 applies to a:
questions.explanation: Appendix 5 classifies external influences, and AG denotes mechanical impact severity with AG1 representing low impact conditions typical of an ordinary house. Factories, workshops and quarries experience harsher mechanical stresses and so attract higher AG classifications.

questions.prompt: A building constructed solely of wood would have an external influence category of:
questions.explanation: External influences are classified by the construction materials present, and CA2 denotes a building constructed predominantly of combustible materials such as wood. This higher category triggers extra precautions for wiring systems to limit the spread of fire.

questions.prompt: A fire fighter's emergency switch should be provided for:

options.A: Exterior discharge lighting installations exceeding low-voltage
options.B: Factory fire alarm circuits operating at low-voltage

questions.explanation: A firefighter's emergency switch is required to isolate exterior discharge lighting operating above low voltage, because the high open-circuit voltages of such installations present a real danger to firefighters tackling a blaze. The switch lets them cut the supply quickly from outside the building.

questions.prompt: The protective conductor used within a final circuit has high protective conductor currents in excess of 10 mA when supplying more than one item of electrical equipment. The minimal cross-sectional area may be 4 mm², provided that:

options.A: Additional protection from the use of a residual current device is present
options.B: Individual items of equipment are supplied through an isolating transformer
options.C: The protective conductor has additional mechanical protection
options.D: The protective conductor is in the form of a complete ring

questions.explanation: Where high protective conductor currents flow, a robust earth connection is essential, so a reduced 4 mm cross-sectional area is only acceptable when the conductor is given additional mechanical protection against damage. This safeguards continuity of the earth path that disconnection relies upon.

questions.prompt: Installations should be arranged so as to avoid hazards in the event of a fault, and to facilitate safe operation, inspection, testing and maintenance. One method of complying with this is to:

options.A: Connect all circuits on the radial principle
options.B: Connect all circuits on the ring principle
options.C: Divide the installation into bands of circuits
options.D: Divide the installation into separate circuits

questions.explanation: Dividing an installation into several separate circuits limits the consequences of a single fault to one circuit, while allowing the remainder to stay energised. This also makes inspection, testing and maintenance safer because individual sections can be isolated without shutting everything down.

questions.prompt: A domestic 30A radial final circuit is used to supply BS 1363 socket outlets. If the floor area to be served is 55m², the rating of the protective device and the live conductor's csa must not be less than:
questions.explanation: A 30A radial supplying BS 1363 socket outlets may serve a floor area up to about 75 square metres, so 55 square metres is comfortably within its scope. The minimum live conductor size for a 30A radial of this type is 4 mm to carry the load safely.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not a characteristic of the supply?
questions.explanation: The characteristics that must be assessed are properties of the incoming supply itself, such as nominal voltage, frequency and earth fault loop impedance Ze. Emergency switching is a protective measure designed into the installation, not an inherent feature of the supply.

questions.prompt: The number and type of live conductors of a new electrical supply to a building may be determined:

options.A: After consultation with the local distributor
options.B: By enquiry to the local council offices
options.D: By reference to the Electricity, Safety, Quality and Continuity

questions.explanation: The number and type of live conductors depend on how the distributor's network is configured, information only the local distribution network operator can confirm. Consulting them ensures the installation design matches the actual supply arrangement provided to the premises.

questions.prompt: Basic protection protects persons and/or livestock from contact with:

options.B: Exposed conductive parts made live by a fault

questions.explanation: Basic protection guards against direct contact with parts that are intended to be live in normal service, preventing shock under healthy conditions. Contact with parts made live only by a fault falls instead under fault protection, which is a separate measure.

questions.prompt: The requirements regarding basic protection have not been applied if livestock comes into contact with:

options.A: A protective conductor carrying fault current
options.B: An exposed terminal within a faulty enclosure
options.C: Exposed conductive parts made live by a fault
options.D: Extraneous conductive parts made live by an earth fault

questions.explanation: Basic protection is meant to prevent contact with normally live parts, so an accessible exposed terminal inside a faulty enclosure means that protection has failed. The enclosure should have prevented anyone, including livestock, from reaching the live terminal in the first place.

questions.prompt: One method of providing basic protection is by:
questions.explanation: Basic protection works by physically preventing contact with live parts, and enclosing or placing barriers around them achieves exactly this. Methods like automatic disconnection or electrical separation address faults rather than preventing direct contact during normal service.

questions.prompt: A piece of electrical equipment having a protective conductor current of 15 mA is to be connected to the supply by means of a 16A plug and socket outlet complying with BS EN 60309-2. The cross sectional area of the protective conductor of the associated flexible cable shall not be less than:
questions.explanation: When the protective conductor current exceeds 10 mA, a reliable high-integrity earth connection is needed, and for a flexible cable supplying a plug and socket this means a protective conductor of at least 2.5 mm. The larger size resists damage and maintains a dependable earth path.

questions.prompt: The temperature limit for non-metallic equipment which is intended to be touched but not hand-held is:
questions.explanation: Accessible non-metallic surfaces that may be touched but are not hand-held are permitted a higher temperature limit than metal, because non-metals conduct heat to the skin more slowly. A limit of 80 degrees Celsius prevents burns while allowing for this reduced heat transfer.

questions.prompt: The prospective fault current at the origin of an electrical installation must be taken into account when:

options.C: Estimating the external earth fault loop impedance
options.D: Selecting the type of overcurrent device to be installed

questions.explanation: An overcurrent device must be able to interrupt the largest fault current it could ever see, so the prospective fault current at the origin determines the required breaking capacity. Choosing a device with adequate rating ensures it clears a fault safely rather than failing.

questions.prompt: Omission of devices for protection against overload is NOT permitted for:

options.B: Circuits which supply fire extinguishing devices

questions.explanation: Overload protection may be omitted only where unexpected disconnection is more dangerous than the overload itself, but this does not extend to emergency lighting circuits. These must retain overcurrent protection so a fault cannot create a further hazard, and they remain subject to fault protection.

questions.prompt: The nominal rating of an overcurrent protective device should be:

options.B: Equal to the prospective short-circuit current
options.C: Greater than the current carrying capacity of the conductors
options.D: Not less than the design current

questions.explanation: For coordination between conductor and device, the protective device rating must be at least the design current so it does not trip under normal load, yet not exceed the cable's current-carrying capacity. Setting it no less than the design current satisfies the first of these conditions.

questions.prompt: The means of isolation for a particular item of equipment may be installed in a position remote from that equipment, providing that it:

options.A: Can be locked in the off position using a lock and key common to all other such isolators
options.B: Can be locked in the off position using a lock and key that are unique to that isolator
options.C: Is located so as to be in full view of persons working on the equipment
options.D: Is manually operated and a visual display is located next to the equipment

questions.explanation: A remote isolator is only safe if it cannot be inadvertently re-energised while someone works on the equipment, so it must be lockable off with a key unique to that device. A common key would let another person unlock it, defeating the purpose of secure isolation.

questions.prompt: A firefighter's switch should be installed at not more than:

options.A: 2.75m from the ground and the 'off' position at the bottom
options.B: 2.75m from the ground and the 'off' position at the top
options.C: 2.75m from the ground and the 'on' position at the top and coloured red
options.D: 2m from the ground and the 'off' position at the bottom and coloured red

questions.explanation: A firefighter's switch must be reachable and unambiguous, so it is fitted no higher than 2.75 metres above the ground with the off position at the top. This consistent arrangement lets firefighters confirm at a glance that the supply has been cut.

questions.prompt: Where the nominal voltage of an installation is 230V, the required minimum impulse withstand voltage for Category II equipment for overvoltage protection is:
questions.explanation: Equipment is rated by overvoltage category according to its position in the installation, and for a 230V supply Category II equipment requires a minimum impulse withstand of 2.5 kV. This ensures the equipment can survive transient overvoltages without insulation breakdown.

questions.prompt: In a location where a risk of danger from fire exists due to manufacture or storage of combustible materials, enclosures of heaters shall not attain a surface temperature under normal working conditions exceeding:
questions.explanation: Regulation 422.3.2 limits surface temperatures of equipment in conditions presenting a fire risk from combustible materials. Capping a heater enclosure at 90 degrees Celsius under normal working conditions keeps it well below the ignition point of nearby dust and stored materials.

questions.prompt: For a.c., the preferred frequencies which are taken into account in BS 7671 are:
questions.explanation: Regulation 110.1 sets the scope of BS 7671, and the frequencies it accounts for are 50 Hz, 60 Hz and 400 Hz. These cover standard UK mains, common overseas supplies and the higher frequency used in aircraft and certain specialist installations.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following external influences requires an increase in the current ratings of cables above those normally required?

options.C: Possible vertically falling drops of water

questions.explanation: The Appendix 4 rating tables assume a reference ambient temperature, and higher ambient temperatures reduce a cable's ability to dissipate heat. A correction factor is therefore applied to increase the required current rating so the conductor does not exceed its permitted operating temperature.

questions.prompt: To prevent circulating eddy currents (an electromagnetic effect) in steel conduit, trunking or cable armouring:

options.A: All live conductors of a circuit must be contained in the same enclosure
options.B: Line and neutral conductors are to be kept separate
options.D: The enclosures should be solidly earthed

questions.explanation: Regulation 521.5.2 requires all live conductors of a circuit to share one ferromagnetic enclosure. If line and neutral are separated, their magnetic fields no longer cancel, inducing circulating eddy currents that heat the steel and waste energy.

questions.prompt: It is required that all circuits in a barn on an agricultural installation be protected by an RCD. The maximum rating (lΔn) for a circuit protected by a 40A BS 88 protective device should not exceed:
questions.explanation: For agricultural locations, Regulation 705.411.1 requires circuits supplying socket-outlets up to 32 A to have 30 mA RCD protection, while other circuits up to that protective rating may use up to 300 mA. This balances fire protection against nuisance tripping on a 40 A circuit.

questions.prompt: In agricultural premises in locations where tractors are used, which one of the following methods of installation shall NOT be applied:

options.A: Cables in arable ground shall be buried at a depth of at least 1m
options.B: Cables shall be buried at a depth of at least 0.6m with additional protection
options.C: Self supporting suspension cables at a height in excess of that accessible by rodents
options.D: Self supporting suspension cables at a height of at least 6m

questions.explanation: Regulation 705.522.16 addresses cable installation methods where agricultural vehicles operate. Suspending cables merely above rodent reach gives no margin for tall machinery such as tractors and loaders, so that method is excluded in favour of buried cables or self-supporting suspension at least six metres high.

questions.prompt: A permanent warning notice must be fixed at or near the point of connection of every earthing conductor to an earth electrode. This notice must bear the words:

options.A: Earth Bonding Connection, Do Not Remove
options.B: Earth Electrical Connection, Do Not Remove
options.C: Safety Bonding Connection, Do Not Remove
options.D: Safety Electrical Connection, Do Not Remove

questions.explanation: Regulation 514.13.1 requires a durable warning notice at the connection of every earthing conductor to its electrode, reading 'Safety Electrical Connection - Do Not Remove'. This prevents anyone from disconnecting the earth during later work and unknowingly removing a vital safety provision.

questions.prompt: Overcurrent protection may be provided by a:
questions.explanation: Overcurrent protection against both overload and fault current may be afforded by a circuit breaker, which Regulations 432 and 433 recognise for this duty. A disconnector or linked switch only isolates, and an RCD detects residual earth-fault current rather than overcurrent.

questions.prompt: Where ADS is the means of providing fault protection and a 20 A type B circuit breaker to BS EN 60898 is used, the maximum earth fault loop impedance is:
questions.explanation: Table 41.3 lists maximum earth fault loop impedances for the 0.4 second disconnection time using BS EN 60898 breakers. A 20 A Type B device trips magnetically at five times its rating, so the loop impedance must not exceed 2.3 ohms to guarantee disconnection.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is excluded as a protective earth electrode?

options.C: Underground structural metalwork embedded in foundations
options.D: Welded metal reinforcement of concrete embedded in the earth

questions.explanation: Regulation 542.2.4 specifically prohibits using the metalwork of public water services as an earth electrode. Such pipework may be replaced with plastic or altered by the utility, so it cannot be relied upon to provide a stable, low-resistance connection to earth.

questions.prompt: A copper earthing conductor not mechanically protected and not protected against corrosion is buried in soil. The minimum size of the earthing conductor is:
questions.explanation: Table 54.1 sets minimum buried earthing conductor sizes according to whether mechanical and corrosion protection are present. Where a copper conductor has neither, 25 square millimetres is required so that corrosion and physical damage cannot reduce it below a safe cross-section.

questions.prompt: By employing an RCD protected socket-outlet to supply a Class II portable tool, the user is:

options.A: Protected against an earth fault in the windings of the tool
options.B: Protected against breakage of the protective conductor of the flexible cable
options.C: Provided with additional fault protection against contact with a live conductor exposed by carelessness of the user
options.D: Unable to operate the tool until the earthing circuit is complete and monitored

questions.explanation: Per Regulation 415.1.1, a 30 mA RCD provides additional protection that supplements the basic measures. With a Class II tool, this guards the user should a live conductor become exposed through carelessness or damage, disconnecting quickly before a shock proves harmful.

questions.prompt: A 13A socket-outlet supplies mobile equipment for use outdoors. Additional protection should be provided by means of a:
questions.explanation: Regulation 411.3.3 requires socket-outlets up to 32 A for general use, including mobile outdoor equipment, to have additional protection by a 30 mA RCD. This rapidly disconnects earth-fault or contact currents in the higher-risk outdoor environment before they become dangerous.

questions.prompt: In order to prevent the spread of fire where a wiring system passes through elements of building structures, any holes must be sealed around the cables. Which of the following is NOT a requirement for such sealing materials?

options.A: It shall be compatible with the material of the wiring system
options.B: It shall be of adequate mechanical stability to withstand the stresses which may arise
options.C: It shall prevent thermal movement of the wiring system
options.D: It shall resist relevant external influences to the same degree as the wiring system

questions.explanation: Regulation 527.2.7 requires sealing to match the wiring system's external influences, withstand the stresses involved and be compatible with the cables. It must also accommodate thermal movement rather than prevent it, since restraining a cable's natural expansion could damage the seal or wiring.

questions.prompt: Where an autotransformer is used for step-up purposes:

options.A: A linked switch breaking all live conductors must be used
options.B: A single-pole switch can be used

questions.explanation: Regulation 555.1.3 requires that an autotransformer used for step-up be controlled by a linked switch breaking all live conductors. Because the windings are electrically common, leaving any pole connected could energise the apparatus, so simultaneous disconnection of every live conductor is essential.

questions.prompt: When installing socket outlets which will be mounted vertically on a wall or working surface, they should be:

options.A: Mounted 50mm from the floor level or working surface
options.B: Mounted so that the flexible cord and plug are 50mm from floor or working surface level
options.C: Mounted so the flexible cord and plug top can be withdrawn or inserted without mechanical damage
options.D: Shuttered and suitable for a.c. and complying with BS 1363

questions.explanation: Regulation 553.1.6 concerns the practical positioning of socket-outlets so the plug and its flexible cord can be inserted and withdrawn without mechanical damage. A fixed dimension is not specified; the governing requirement is safe, damage-free access to the accessory.

questions.prompt: Any circuit or equipment vulnerable to a particular test should be identified by:

options.A: A visual inspection prior to testing
options.B: The inventory for the building being tested
options.C: The manufacturer's warning notice on the equipment
options.D: The provision of a legible diagram, chart or table prior to testing

questions.explanation: Regulation 514.9.1 requires diagrams, charts or tables to be provided showing the installation's circuits and characteristics. Consulting this documentation before testing identifies equipment vulnerable to a particular test, such as electronic devices, so it can be disconnected to avoid damage.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following tests is carried out after the supply is connected?

options.B: Continuity of ring final circuit conductors

questions.explanation: Under the Regulation 612 sequence, most tests are made dead before connection, but RCD operation can only be verified once the supply is energised. The device needs live conditions to inject a residual current and confirm it disconnects within the required time.

questions.prompt: The purpose of the inspection conducted prior to testing an installation is to verify that:

options.A: All electrical cables and conduits are pointed orange for identification
options.B: All ring final circuit connections are correct
options.C: Equipment is not damaged or defective
options.D: Only British Standard equipment is installed

questions.explanation: Initial inspection precedes testing precisely to confirm by visual examination that installed equipment is sound and correctly selected. Spotting damage or defects before energising prevents a dangerous condition being missed or made worse once test instruments apply voltage.

questions.prompt: When testing a 230V installation, the minimum value of insulation resistance is:
questions.explanation: For circuits at nominal voltages up to 500V, including standard 230V installations, the insulation resistance test applied at 500V dc must read at least 1 megohm. A lower value indicates deteriorated insulation that could allow leakage current and earth faults.

questions.prompt: No alteration shall be made to an existing installation unless the:

options.B: Existing equipment meets BS and BS EN standards
options.C: It is established that the alteration will not impair the safety of the existing installation

questions.explanation: Additions and alterations are only permitted once it is confirmed that the work will not degrade the safety of the existing installation. This ensures the existing earthing, bonding and protective devices remain adequate for the modified arrangement before any new work proceeds.

questions.prompt: The inspecting and testing required during a periodic inspection should be recorded on a Periodic Inspection Report and carried out by:
questions.explanation: Periodic inspection and testing must be undertaken by a skilled person competent in such work, since interpreting results and judging an installation's condition demands sound knowledge and experience. Recording findings on the report relies on that competence to reach safe, defensible conclusions.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following factors does not affect the frequency of periodic inspection?
questions.explanation: The interval between periodic inspections is governed by factors such as the installation type, its use and operation, and the frequency and quality of maintenance. Provision of supplies for safety services is a design matter, not one of the determinants used to set inspection intervals.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following numbers is the correct grouping factor for six circuits installed as method B?
questions.explanation: Where several circuits are grouped together, mutual heating reduces each cable's safe current-carrying capacity, so a rating factor is applied. For six circuits grouped in this installation arrangement the appropriate reduction factor is 0.57, derived from the grouping tables in Appendix 4.

questions.prompt: The reference for the installation method that has multi-core cables having a non metallic sheath, in surface mounted conduit is:
questions.explanation: Multicore cables with a non-metallic sheath run in surface-mounted conduit correspond to installation reference method B. The conduit enclosure influences how heat dissipates from the cable, so this method determines the current-carrying capacity taken from the tables.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following classifications of external influences would be appropriate for an item of electrical equipment installed where it would be subject to 'splashes of water'?
questions.explanation: External influences are classified by code in Appendix 5, where the presence of water is the AD category. Splashing water from any direction is denoted AD4, which dictates that equipment be selected with a suitable degree of ingress protection against that condition.

questions.prompt: In rooms containing a bath or shower, the measures of protection by obstacles and placing out of reach are:
questions.explanation: Protection by obstacles and by placing out of reach relies on the behaviour of careful or skilled persons, so it is never acceptable in locations containing a bath or shower. The wet conditions and reduced body resistance there demand more robust protective measures.

questions.prompt: The nominal supply voltage on temporary installations in shows and stands shall not exceed 230/400 V ac, or
questions.explanation: Temporary installations at shows, stands and exhibitions are limited to a nominal supply not exceeding 230/400V ac or 500V dc. Capping the voltage in these transient, public-facing setups limits the severity of shock and fault energy where wiring is disturbed frequently.

questions.prompt: In a conduit system on an agricultural installation where livestock are kept, the external influence shall be classified as:
questions.explanation: Where livestock are kept, conduit and wiring systems face corrosive agents such as ammonia and damp, so the external influence is classified AF4 for substantial corrosion. Equipment and enclosures must therefore be selected to withstand that aggressive environment without deteriorating.

questions.prompt: On agricultural premises, heating appliances shall be fixed so as to maintain an appropriate distance from livestock. In the absence of manufacturer's guidance, a radiant heater used in the vicinity of livestock should be placed at a distance of not less than:
questions.explanation: Radiant heaters near animals present a fire and burn risk, so absent manufacturer guidance they must be kept at least 0.5m from livestock and combustible material. This clearance limits radiant heat reaching animals, bedding and structure that could ignite or cause injury.

questions.prompt: In a caravan park, the maximum number of socket outlets which can be protected by an RCD is:
questions.explanation: Each caravan pitch socket-outlet must be individually protected by its own RCD, so a single device may serve only one outlet. Individual protection ensures a fault on one caravan's supply does not disconnect or endanger users of neighbouring pitches.

questions.prompt: In exhibitions, protection against thermal effects must be provided for luminaries mounted below a height of:
questions.explanation: In exhibitions, stands and shows, luminaires mounted below 2.5m or otherwise accessible must have additional protection against thermal effects. At low mounting heights the public can readily contact hot surfaces, so guarding against burns and fire becomes mandatory.

questions.prompt: For household installations, as a rule of thumb, the floor area served by a single 20A radial circuit using socket outlets to BS 1363 may be:
questions.explanation: As a design rule of thumb in Appendix 15, a 20A radial circuit feeding BS 1363 socket-outlets is suited to a floor area of up to 50 square metres. This keeps the connected load and voltage drop within what the smaller radial conductor and protective device can handle.

questions.prompt: Prior to an inspection in accordance with BS 7671, the competent person carrying out the work shall normally:

options.B: Disconnect the installation from the supply
options.C: Ensure that all switches are off
options.D: Ensure that the supply is connected

questions.explanation: Inspection of an installation is normally carried out with it disconnected from the supply, since much of the examination involves contact with conductors and enclosures. Working dead removes the shock risk while connections, bonding and equipment condition are assessed.

questions.prompt: To which one of the following situations does BS 7671 apply?

options.A: The design of an electrical installation for a caravan site
options.B: The inspection and testing of the electrical installation on an oil rig

questions.explanation: BS 7671 applies to fixed installations such as the design of an electrical installation for a caravan site. It does not govern equipment manufacture or the public distribution network, which fall under separate standards and statutory regulation.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is listed under exclusions from the scope of BS 7671?
questions.explanation: Lightning protection systems are expressly excluded from the scope of BS 7671, being covered instead by their own standard, BS EN 62305. The Wiring Regulations address fixed electrical installations rather than the dedicated arrangements for capturing and dissipating lightning strikes.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following sets of regulations is non-statutory?

options.D: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations

questions.explanation: Regulation 114.1 confirms that BS 7671 is a code of practice rather than a legal instrument, so it carries no statutory force in its own right. Compliance is widely cited as evidence of meeting the statutory Electricity at Work and similar Regulations, but the standard itself is non-statutory guidance.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 defines low voltage a.c. between conductors as voltage:

options.A: Above 250 V a.c. but below 1000 V a.c
options.B: Above 50 V a.c. but below 500 V a.c
options.C: Below 1000 V a.c. but above 50 V a.c

questions.explanation: The Definitions section sets low voltage a.c. between conductors as exceeding 50 V but not exceeding 1000 V. The 50 V lower limit marks the boundary above extra-low voltage, while 1000 V is the upper limit before high voltage begins.

questions.prompt: An ordinary person is a person who:
questions.explanation: Under the Definitions, persons are categorised by competence as skilled, instructed, or ordinary. An ordinary person is neither skilled nor instructed, so they have no electrical training or supervision and the installation must protect them without relying on any electrical knowledge.

questions.prompt: A 12 V fire alarm circuit is classified by BS 7671 as:
questions.explanation: The Definitions place extra-low voltage telecommunication, signalling, control and similar circuits in Band I, since a 12 V fire alarm operates well below 50 V a.c. Band I covers circuits where protection against electric shock is provided by the low voltage value itself.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is NOT a classification of external influence?
questions.explanation: Appendix 5 classifies external influences under three headings: environment, utilisation, and construction of buildings, each given a code letter. Current rating is a property of the cable or device chosen, not an external condition acting on the installation, so it is not an external influence.

questions.prompt: The type of building construction is an external influence which, in an electrical installation, will affect the choice of:
questions.explanation: Appendix 5 lists construction of buildings as an external influence covering materials and structural movement. These factors govern how cables can be fixed and which wiring systems and equipment will withstand the building's design, so they directly shape the choice of equipment and wiring.

questions.prompt: Non-sheathed cables for fixed wiring, other than protective conductors, should always be installed in:
questions.explanation: Regulation 521.10.1 requires non-sheathed cables for fixed wiring to be enclosed in conduit, ducting or trunking. The single layer of insulation gives no mechanical protection, so an enclosure is needed to guard the cable and prevent contact with live conductors.

questions.prompt: Domestic ring final circuits are used to supply BS 1363 socket outlets. If the floor area to be served is limited to 50 m², the cable feeding the circuit must be:
questions.explanation: Appendix 15 specifies a standard 32 A ring final circuit wired in 2.5 mm² copper serving a floor area up to 100 m². At 50 m² this cable size remains correct, the ring arrangement sharing load between two legs so the smaller conductor suffices.

questions.prompt: A domestic final ring circuit may:

options.B: Require additional protection by an RCD
options.C: Supply a cooker rated at 2.5 kW
options.D: Supply any number of socket-outlets over an area of 200 m2

questions.explanation: Appendix 15 notes that socket-outlet circuits generally require additional protection by a 30 mA RCD, reflecting the wider requirement for sockets up to 32 A used by ordinary persons. A ring cannot lawfully feed unlimited sockets over 200 m² or a fixed cooker.

questions.prompt: Where thermoplastic insulated and sheathed cables are installed in a plastered wall at a depth of 20 mm and are not protected against mechanical damage, they must be:

options.C: Protected by a 30 mA RCD and run in the "safe zones"

questions.explanation: Regulation 522.6.6 permits buried cables less than 50 mm deep only within prescribed safe zones, and 522.6.7 adds that without mechanical protection or earthed armour they must have additional protection by a 30 mA RCD. Both measures therefore apply together.

questions.prompt: A two-storey domestic dwelling should have a minimum of two lighting circuits in order to:

options.A: Avoid danger in the event of a fault
options.B: Enable a greater variety of luminaries to be used
options.D: Reduce the load on the consumer's control unit

questions.explanation: Regulation 314.1 requires installations to be divided into circuits to avoid danger and minimise inconvenience on a fault. Splitting lighting across two circuits means a single fault cannot plunge the whole dwelling into darkness, leaving safe egress lighting on the other floor.

questions.prompt: A system is defined as:

options.A: A single source of energy and an installation
options.B: The consumer's terminals of an installation
options.C: The distribution cables to an installation
options.D: The kWh meter and an installation

questions.explanation: The Definitions describe a system as an electrical installation supplied from a single source of energy, such as the public network or a generator. This pairing of source and installation is what the system letters like TN-S and TT actually classify.

questions.prompt: The term "basic protection" refers to:

options.C: Protection against electric shock under a single fault condition
options.D: Protection against electric shock under fault free conditions

questions.explanation: Per the Definitions, basic protection guards against electric shock under fault-free conditions, meaning contact with parts that are intentionally live in normal service. It is achieved by insulation and barriers, and is distinct from fault protection, which addresses dangers arising under a fault.

questions.prompt: Within a 230 V single-phase, metal clad fuse board, access to the line and neutral busbars are protected by insulation and by secured intermediate barriers. The fuse board may be:

options.B: Opened without use of a key or tool
options.C: Used to accommodate ELV circuit conductors

questions.explanation: Regulation 416.2.4 allows a barrier or enclosure to be opened without a key or tool only where intermediate barriers prevent contact with live parts and cannot be removed without a tool. With insulation and secured intermediate barriers in place, that condition is met.

questions.prompt: A socket-outlet used for a SELV system should:

options.D: Not have a protective conductor contact

questions.explanation: Because a SELV system is electrically separated from earth and protective conductors, its socket-outlets must not accept a plug from other systems and must have no protective conductor contact. This prevents earth connections that would defeat the separation on which SELV safety depends.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is recognised as a means of providing fault protection?

options.B: Protection by insulation of live parts
options.D: Protection by placing out of reach

questions.explanation: Automatic disconnection of supply is the principal recognised measure for fault protection, as set out around Regulation 411.3.2. Insulation, obstacles and placing out of reach address basic protection against contact with normally live parts, not protection under fault conditions.

questions.prompt: Where SELV is used in normally dry conditions, basic protection is unnecessary where the nominal voltage does not exceed:
questions.explanation: Regulation 414.4.5 allows basic protection to be omitted for SELV in dry conditions where the nominal voltage does not exceed 25 V a.c. Below this threshold the touch voltage is considered low enough that contact with live parts presents no significant shock risk.

questions.prompt: Obstacles may be used to provide basic protection providing:

options.B: The circuit voltage does not exceed 250 V
options.C: The installation is contained within steel conduit
options.D: The installation is under the control of a skilled person

questions.explanation: Regulation 417.1 permits obstacles and placing out of reach only where access is restricted to skilled or instructed persons under supervision. Obstacles merely prevent unintentional contact and can be bypassed deliberately, so they are unsuitable where ordinary persons have access.

questions.prompt: Overload current is defined as the overcurrent:

options.A: Flowing in a phase conductor when in contact with exposed conductive parts
options.B: Occurring in a circuit which is electrically sound
options.C: Resulting from a fault of negligible impedance
options.D: That causes protective devices to operate correctly

questions.explanation: An overload arises in a circuit that is otherwise healthy and correctly wired, where current exceeds the rated value through normal use rather than insulation failure. This distinguishes it from a short-circuit, which results from a fault of negligible impedance between live conductors.

questions.prompt: An overload current could arise when:

options.A: A forward/reverse controller attempts to switch a motor both directions simultaneously
options.B: An electrician drills into a busbar chamber and touches a live
options.C: Contamination of a motor terminal block results in tracking
options.D: Excessive mechanical load is applied to an electric motor

questions.explanation: Overload current flows in an electrically sound circuit carrying more than its design current, typically when a motor is mechanically overloaded and draws excess current to meet demand. The other situations involve faults to earth or tracking, which are short-circuit or fault conditions, not overload.

questions.prompt: Where the overcurrent device is intended to afford protection against overload, l2 must not exceed lz multiplied by:
questions.explanation: The coordination rule for overload protection requires the conventional operating current I2 of the device to not exceed 1.45 times the lowest current-carrying capacity Iz of the conductor. This limits the time the cable can be overloaded so its insulation is not damaged by sustained excess current.

questions.prompt: Omission of devices for protection against overload is not permitted for:

options.B: Circuits which supply fire extinguishing devices

questions.explanation: Overload protection may be omitted where unexpected disconnection could cause greater danger than the overload itself, but never on circuits supplying emergency lighting where continuity of supply matters yet safe loading must still be assured. Such safety circuits must retain their overload device.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following may be used to provide emergency switching for an electric motor?

options.A: A device which latches in the off position
options.B: A key switch latched in the on position
options.D: A switch fuse with a removable handle

questions.explanation: Emergency switching must rapidly remove the hazard and stay off, so a device that latches in the off position prevents inadvertent re-energisation while the danger persists. A simple plug, key switch or removable handle does not guarantee the supply remains disconnected during the emergency.

questions.prompt: A section of a factory requires urgent non-electrical repairs to a machine. The type of switching provided to allow this work to proceed would be switching for:
questions.explanation: Switching that allows non-electrical work on machinery to proceed safely is switching for mechanical maintenance, which lets the equipment be stopped and kept inoperative while repairs are carried out. It guards against unexpected mechanical movement rather than addressing an electrical emergency.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following shall not be used as an isolator?
questions.explanation: An isolator must create a reliable, secure break in the supply, but semiconductor devices only block conduction electronically and do not provide a guaranteed physical separation of contacts. They cannot be trusted to fully disconnect a circuit and so are not permitted for isolation.

questions.prompt: Where PME conditions apply, the main protective bonding conductor shall be:

options.A: Determined after consultation with the consumer
options.B: Half the csa of the earthing conductor and with reference to Table 54.7
options.C: Selected in accordance with the supply neutral and Table 54.8
options.D: The same csa as the incoming line conductor

questions.explanation: Under PME conditions the main protective bonding conductor carries diverted neutral currents, so its size is determined by the cross-sectional area of the supply neutral rather than the earthing conductor. Table 54.8 sets the minimum bonding size against that neutral conductor.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following cannot be used as an earth electrode?

options.D: Welded reinforcement of concrete embedded in the earth

questions.explanation: A copper water supply pipe is unsuitable as an earth electrode because the metallic service may be replaced with plastic sections, breaking the earth path without warning. Electrodes must be permanently reliable, so dedicated rods, tapes, plates or buried structural metalwork are required instead.

questions.prompt: Using Table 54.7 of BS 7671, the minimum cross-sectional area of a circuit protective conductor with a 10 mm² line conductor will be:
questions.explanation: Table 54.7 gives the protective conductor size from the line conductor by the adiabatic relationship, and for line sizes above 16 mm squared the cpc is half the line size. For a 10 mm squared line conductor, however, the cpc must equal it at 10 mm squared.

questions.prompt: In order to calculate the minimum value of the cross-sectional area of a protective conductor, the following information is available: Fault current = 700 A Operating time of protective device = 0.4 s Constant k, for protective conductor material = 115 The selected size of the protective conductor should be:
questions.explanation: The adiabatic equation gives the minimum cpc area as the square root of I squared t divided by k, so here the square root of 700 squared times 0.4 divided by 115 gives roughly 3.85 mm squared. The next standard size above this calculated value is 4 mm squared.

questions.prompt: Supplementary bonding conductors having mechanical protection connected between two extraneous conductive parts are subject to a minimum cross-sectional area of:
questions.explanation: Supplementary bonding conductors connecting two extraneous-conductive-parts must have a minimum cross-sectional area of 2.5 mm squared where mechanical protection is provided, rising to 4 mm squared without it. The mechanical protection allows the smaller conductor because it is shielded from physical damage.

questions.prompt: In a marina, corrosive elements exist, structures can move, mechanical damage can occur, a possible presence of flammable fuel is present and an increase in the risk of electric shock is possible. Which one of the following is NOT taken into consideration when determining any external influence requirements?

options.A: Contact of body with earth potential
options.D: The reduced resistance of salt water

questions.explanation: When assessing external influences in a marina, the relevant factors are those raising shock risk, such as presence of water, contact with earth potential and reduced body resistance. The specific reduced resistance of salt water is not itself listed as a determining external influence.

questions.prompt: A final circuit supplying 13 A socket-outlets is to be used by ordinary persons. The circuit must be provided with:

options.B: Additional protection in accordance with Regulation 415.1

questions.explanation: Socket-outlets up to 32 A used by ordinary persons require additional protection by a 30 mA RCD in accordance with Regulation 415.1, because such users cannot be relied upon to recognise hazards. This fast-acting protection limits the duration of any earth-fault shock to a safe level.

questions.prompt: Socket outlets which are under the supervision of skilled persons:

options.B: Must be mounted 450 mm above the floor
options.D: Must disconnect within 5 s in the event of an earth fault

questions.explanation: Additional RCD protection of socket-outlets can be omitted where the installation is under the supervision of skilled or instructed persons, as they are trained to avoid and manage electrical risk. The competence of the users removes the need for this further safeguard.

questions.prompt: Ceiling roses are only allowed where the circuit voltage does not exceed:
questions.explanation: Ceiling roses are only permitted on circuits whose voltage does not exceed 250 V, reflecting their construction and the typical lighting circuits they serve. Above this voltage the accessory is not suitable and an alternative connection method must be used.

questions.prompt: The minimum cross-sectional area for a buried copper earthing conductor that is provided with mechanical protection but no protection against corrosion is:
questions.explanation: A buried copper earthing conductor that is mechanically protected but not protected against corrosion must be at least 25 mm squared, because corrosion gradually reduces the effective conductor area over time. The larger section preserves a reliable earth path despite this deterioration.

questions.prompt: When an insulation monitoring device (IMD) is installed:

options.A: An IT system must not be used
options.B: Instruction must be available that indicate how to switch the device off if it detects a fault
options.C: It must be designed in such a way that it is impossible to modify the setting without the use of a tool, if the location is accessible to ordinary persons
options.D: It must be set to a higher value corresponding to the normal insulation of the system

questions.explanation: An insulation monitoring device guards an IT system, so its trip setting must not be casually altered where ordinary persons have access. It must therefore be designed so the setting cannot be changed without a tool, preventing tampering that would defeat the protection.

questions.prompt: A circuit with a design current of 45 A is installed using a cable with a current rating of 50 A. If the voltage drop for the cable is 8 mV per amp per metre, the circuit voltage drop for a 10 m run will be:
questions.explanation: Voltage drop is found from the design current, not the cable rating, multiplied by the tabulated millivolt-per-amp-per-metre figure and the length. Here 45 A times 8 mV times 10 m gives 3600 mV, or 3.6 V, the value used to confirm the limit is met.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following should be taken into consideration when calculating the voltage drop in an installation?

options.A: Current carrying capacity of the conductors
options.C: Nominal current setting of the protective device
options.D: The current that ensures effective operation of the protective device

questions.explanation: Appendix 4 bases voltage drop on the actual load the circuit carries, so the design current Ib is used in the calculation. The conductor rating or protective device setting governs overload protection, not the volt drop a connected load will experience.

questions.prompt: On a mobile or transportable unit, plugs used to connect the unit to the supply shall comply with BE EN 60309-2 and:

options.A: Any plug and socket outlets shall afford a degree of protection of not less than IP44 if located inside
options.B: Appliance inlets with their enclosures shall provide a degree of protection of at least IP44
options.C: Shall be enclosed in a metal enclosure
options.D: The plug part be on the supply distribution board

questions.explanation: Regulation 717.55.1 covers mobile and transportable units, where connection points are exposed to weather and rough handling. Appliance inlets and their enclosures must therefore achieve at least IP44, guarding against solid objects and splashing water at the supply connection.

questions.prompt: The fault current due to an earth fault of negligible impedance in a 400 V, three phase, four wire circuit having an earth fault loop impedance of 0.3 F is:
questions.explanation: Prospective fault current is the applicable voltage divided by the earth fault loop impedance. For a single line-to-earth fault the phase voltage of about 230 V applies, so 230 divided by 0.3 ohms yields roughly 766.6 A, confirming the device can safely interrupt it.

questions.prompt: A 30 A protective device to BS 1361 when carrying a fault current of 200 A should operate in:
questions.explanation: The time/current characteristics in Appendix 3 plot how long each device takes to clear a given fault current. Reading the BS 1361 30 A fuse curve at 200 A gives an operating time of 0.4 s, which is the figure used to verify disconnection times.

questions.prompt: A black sleeve or disc is placed on one of the conductors of a three core MICC cable. This indicates the:

options.B: line 1 of a three phase a.c. circuit
options.C: Line 2 of a three phase a.c. circuit
options.D: Line 3 of a three phase a.c. circuit

questions.explanation: Table 51 sets the identification scheme for conductors, and on MICC cables coloured sleeves or discs mark each line. A black marker denotes the second line conductor, L2, allowing the three phases to be correctly identified at terminations.

questions.prompt: An unfused spur connected to a 30 A ring circuit may supply:

options.B: One twin socket-outlet or one single socket-outlet
options.D: Two twin socket-outlets or one fixed appliance

questions.explanation: Appendix 15 limits an unfused spur from a 30 A ring final circuit so it feeds only a single point. That means one single or one twin socket-outlet, keeping the spur load within the conductor's capacity since it is not separately protected.

questions.prompt: Prior to an inspection in accordance with BS 7671, the competent person carrying out the test shall normally:

options.B: Disconnect the installation from the supply
options.C: Ensure that all switches are off
options.D: Ensure that the supply is connected

questions.explanation: Regulation 611.1 covers inspection, which is the visual examination of the installation. This is normally carried out with the installation disconnected from the supply so that conductors, connections and equipment can be examined safely before any energised testing begins.

questions.prompt: A legible diagram, chart or table relating to an installation must be provided to indicate:

options.A: Any circuit of equipment vulnerable to a typical test
options.B: Location of all portable equipment for testing purposes
options.C: That the original installation design has not changed
options.D: The location of all fixed equipment for testing purposes

questions.explanation: Regulation 514.9.1 requires diagrams or charts that record information needed for safe working. This includes identifying any circuit or equipment vulnerable to a particular test, so that a tester knows to take precautions or isolate sensitive devices beforehand.

questions.prompt: When carrying out an insulation resistance test on a 230 V socket outlet circuit incorporating surge protective devices (SPD), the test voltage may be reduced to:
questions.explanation: Regulation 612.3.2 allows the insulation resistance test voltage to drop to 250 V d.c. where surge protective devices or other voltage-sensitive equipment are connected. This avoids damaging the SPDs while still proving the insulation is sound between live conductors and earth.

questions.prompt: During an initial verification, a test result fails to comply with BS 7671 Part 6. The procedure to be adopted is to:

options.B: Make good and complete the Electrical Installation Certificate
options.C: Make good and complete the Periodic Inspection Report
options.D: Record the fault on the Periodic Inspection Report

questions.explanation: Under Regulation 612.1, where a test fails during initial verification the fault must be rectified and the test repeated until it complies. Only then can the Electrical Installation Certificate, which certifies a new installation, be completed; a periodic report would not apply here.

questions.prompt: For circuits having a nominal voltage above 500 V, the minimum insulation resistance is:
questions.explanation: Table 61 lists minimum insulation resistance values against nominal voltage band. Circuits operating above 500 V are tested at 1000 V d.c. and must achieve at least 1 megohm, confirming the insulation remains adequate at the higher stress these systems impose.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is the required test procedure if an existing installation is extended to include extra lighting and socket outlets?

options.A: All relevant tests must be carried out
options.C: No testing is required, only visual inspection

questions.explanation: Regulation 633.1 treats an addition or alteration as work requiring verification in its own right. Extending a circuit to add lighting and socket-outlets means all relevant tests must be applied to confirm the new and affected parts comply before being placed in service.

questions.prompt: It is a requirement of BS 7671 that a Schedule of Test Results should always be attached to an Electrical Installation Certificate for:

options.D: New installations, alterations or additions to existing installations

questions.explanation: Appendix 6 requires a Schedule of Test Results to accompany every Electrical Installation Certificate, since the certificate must be supported by recorded evidence. This applies to new installations and to any alteration or addition, providing a verifiable record that the work was tested.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 requires that the person ordering installation work must be informed of the:

options.C: Name and address of the regional electricity company

questions.explanation: The guidance accompanying the certification forms in Appendix 6 states that the person ordering the work should be advised of the recommended interval for the next inspection. Informing them of the need for periodic testing ensures the installation continues to be assessed for safety over its life.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following factors does not affect the frequency of the periodic inspection?
