questions.explanation: A plug and socket outlet is not a recognised device for emergency switching because withdrawing a plug carrying load current can draw an arc and is not a deliberate, single-action means of disconnection. Emergency switching must be by a device capable of safely interrupting full load in one movement.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is required to be considered by BS 7671 when assessing the general characteristics of an electrical installation?

options.D: The standard of electricians working on site

questions.explanation: Assessing general characteristics requires considering maintainability so that periodic inspection, testing and repair can be carried out safely throughout the installation's life. The frequency and quality of maintenance the user can provide must be allowed for at the design stage.

questions.prompt: When calculating the voltage drop in an installation which one of the following should be taken into account?

options.C: The current rating of the fuse
options.D: The operating current of the fuse

questions.explanation: Voltage drop is the product of conductor impedance and the current actually flowing, so it is calculated using the circuit design current rather than the protective device rating. Using the real load current gives the true drop and confirms equipment receives adequate voltage in normal operation.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not considered when calculating the minimum current carrying capacity of live conductors of a cable?
questions.explanation: Minimum current-carrying capacity is found by applying correction factors for ambient temperature, grouping and the type of protective device to the design current. Voltage drop is a separate check on conductor length and load, not a factor in sizing the conductor for thermal current capacity.

questions.prompt: For single circuit cable selection purposes the correction factors must be applied to the:

options.A: Current carrying capacity of the cable
options.B: Current rating of the protective device
options.D: The earth fault current of the circuit

questions.explanation: For a single circuit, the rating or correction factors are applied to the current rating of the protective device to establish the minimum tabulated current-carrying capacity the cable must have. This ensures the conductor can carry the protective device's nominal current under the actual installation conditions.

questions.prompt: The classification code for high wind is:
questions.explanation: External influences use a two-letter code with the first letter A for environment. High wind speed is classified AS3, distinguishing it from other mechanical and environmental codes so that equipment and fixings can be selected to withstand the expected forces.

questions.prompt: Rating factors are applied to the fuse rating of a circuit to determine the minimum current-carrying capacity of cables. A rating factor of 1 is used when a circuit is wired in 70℃ thermoplastic insulated cable and operating in an ambient temperature of:
questions.explanation: Tabulated current ratings for 70-degree thermoplastic cables are based on a reference ambient temperature of 30 degrees Celsius. At that temperature no temperature correction is needed, so a rating factor of 1 applies and the tabulated value is used directly.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not recognised by BS 7671:2018 as the sole means of earthing an installation?

options.B: Metal bars embedded in the building foundations
options.C: Metallic rod driven into the ground

questions.explanation: Gas and water service pipes must not be used as the sole means of earthing because they may be replaced with plastic sections or removed by the utility, breaking the earth path without warning. Only a reliable dedicated electrode or supply earth provides a permanent connection.

questions.prompt: A BS 1361 fuse, rated at 45 A, is carrying a fault current of 240A, the protective device should operate in:
questions.explanation: Disconnection times depend on the fault current relative to the fuse rating. With 240 A through a 45 A BS 1361 fuse the ratio falls in the slower part of the time-current curve, giving an operating time of about 5 seconds rather than the rapid 0.4 second clearance of a heavier fault.

questions.prompt: The maximum permissible earth fault loop impedance on a TN system for a ring final circuit protected by a 30 A BS 1361 fuse is:
questions.explanation: The maximum earth fault loop impedance must be low enough for the 30 A BS 1361 fuse to disconnect within the required time. The tabulated limiting value for this device on a TN system is 1.15 ohms, ensuring sufficient fault current flows to operate it quickly.

questions.prompt: The wording of a permanent warning notice fixed at the point of connection of an earthing conductor to an earth electrode is:

options.D: Safety Electrical Connection - Do Not Remove

questions.explanation: A permanent label reading "Safety Electrical Connection - Do Not Remove" must be fixed at the earth electrode connection. The wording warns anyone working nearby that the conductor is essential to safety and must never be disconnected, since removing it would leave the installation unearthed.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following sources does not comply with BS 7671 as a SELV system?

options.A: A battery system operating at extra low voltage
options.B: A centre tapped transformer giving 55 V to earth
options.C: A motor generator with windings providing equivalent isolation to that of a safety isolating transformer
options.D: A safely isolating transformer to BS EN 61558

questions.explanation: A SELV system must be electrically separated from earth, so a centre-tapped transformer referenced to earth at 55 V does not qualify. Any deliberate earth connection means it is reduced low voltage or a different system, not the earth-free arrangement SELV requires for protection.

questions.prompt: The minimum size of a copper earthing conductor buried in the ground, NOT mechanically protected and NOT protected against corrosion is:
questions.explanation: A buried copper earthing conductor that is neither mechanically protected nor protected against corrosion must be at least 25 mm squared. The larger size provides a margin against gradual corrosion and mechanical damage in the soil so the earth connection remains reliable over time.

questions.prompt: When calculating the minimum cross-sectional area of a protective conductor, the following information is available: Fault current = 650 A Operating time of protective device = 0.35 sec Constant, k, for protective conductor material = 115 The selected size of the protective conductor should be:
questions.explanation: Using the adiabatic equation, the minimum area equals the square root of the fault current squared times the time, divided by k. Here that gives roughly 3.3 mm squared, so the next standard size up, 4.0 mm squared, must be selected to withstand the fault energy.

questions.prompt: When a residual current device protects a socket outlet in a domestic garage it must operate when:

options.A: An earth fault on the garage lighting circuit occurs
options.B: Someone comes in contact with exposed earth metalwork
options.C: Someone comes in direct contact with an exposed line conductor and earth
options.D: The protective conductor in a flexible cord to a lawn mower breaks

questions.explanation: An RCD on a socket outlet provides additional protection against electric shock, operating on the residual current that flows when a person bridges a line conductor to earth. Detecting this imbalance lets it disconnect quickly enough to limit the duration of a potentially fatal contact.

questions.prompt: Where an auto-transformer is connected to a single-phase supply (phase and neutral) the common terminal of the winding should be connected to the:
questions.explanation: The common terminal of an auto-transformer winding must connect to the neutral so the shared portion of the winding sits at near-earth potential. This keeps the unswitched part of the circuit close to earth potential, reducing shock risk compared with referencing it to the line conductor.

questions.prompt: Circuit cables required to carry the starting, accelerating and load currents of motors shall have a current rating not less than:
questions.explanation: Conductor selection must account for a motor's heavy starting and accelerating surges, but those are short-lived; thermal capacity is governed by the sustained load, so the cable need only carry the full-load current continuously. Designing for the brief inrush would massively oversize every motor circuit.

questions.prompt: As part of a detailed inspection which of the following must be checked?

options.A: The manufacturer's name of any RCD fitted
options.C: The presence of fire barriers and protection against thermal effects
options.D: The prospective short circuit current at the origin of the installation

questions.explanation: Detailed inspection verifies fixed safety provisions that cannot be confirmed by later testing, including fire barriers, sealing of penetrations and protection against thermal effects. These guard against fire spread and heat damage and form a required part of the inspection schedule before testing begins.

questions.prompt: Which of the following items should be included for checking during the initial verification of an installation:
questions.explanation: Initial verification requires checking that diagrams, charts and instructions are present so the installation can be safely operated and maintained. Contract paperwork and site minutes are administrative and have no bearing on whether the electrical installation itself is safe and properly documented.

questions.prompt: One item that should be included on charts and diagrams made available to the person carrying out an inspection and test is:

options.B: The details of the original contract arrangements
options.C: The location details of portable equipment
options.D: The total number of outlets in the installation

questions.explanation: Charts and diagrams provided to the inspector must show how the installation is divided and controlled, including all isolation and switching arrangements. This lets anyone working on it identify the correct points to isolate circuits safely before maintenance or fault-finding.

questions.prompt: Which on of the following insulation resistance test results, meets the minimum acceptable value for an installation with a 400 V supply?
questions.explanation: For a 400 V circuit the test voltage applied is 500 V dc and the minimum acceptable insulation resistance is 1.0 megohm. A result at or above this confirms adequate separation between live conductors and earth; anything lower indicates deteriorated or damaged insulation.

questions.prompt: The test voltage required to carry out an insulation resistance test on an installation with a nominal supply voltage of 400 V is:
questions.explanation: Insulation resistance on a low voltage installation up to 500 V nominal is tested by applying 500 V dc. This stresses the insulation above its working voltage to reveal weaknesses, while remaining safe for the conductors and connected wiring being verified.

questions.prompt: An earth fault loop impedance test determines the actual value of:
questions.explanation: An earth fault loop impedance test measures the complete impedance of the path a fault current follows, from the point of measurement around the supply transformer and back. That total figure is Zs, which determines whether protective devices will disconnect quickly enough.

questions.prompt: Electrical installation certificates should be signed by those responsible for the:
questions.explanation: An Electrical Installation Certificate carries separate declarations for design, construction and inspection and testing, each signed by the competent person responsible for that work. This assigns clear accountability for every stage so any defect can be traced to who was responsible.

questions.prompt: The result and extent of a Periodic Inspection and Test shall be recorded and given to the:
questions.explanation: The findings of a periodic inspection and test must be given to the person who ordered the work, since they are responsible for the installation and for acting on any defects reported. The report informs decisions about remedial work and continued safe use.

questions.prompt: The following tests are to be carried out on a new installation 1 insulation resistance 2 continuity of ring final circuit 3 continuity of protective conductors 4 earth loop impedance 5 polarity The correct order of carrying out the tests is:
questions.explanation: Dead tests are performed before energising and in a sequence that builds confidence safely: protective conductor continuity, then ring continuity, then insulation resistance, then polarity, with earth loop impedance carried out live last. Checking earthing first ensures later tests are conducted on a safe installation.

questions.prompt: One reason for carrying out a polarity test is:

options.A: Fuses are fitted in the phase conductor
options.D: The outer screwed contact is connected to the phase conductor

questions.explanation: Polarity must be verified so that single-pole protective devices, fuses and switches are connected in the line conductor rather than the neutral. If wrongly placed in the neutral, equipment would remain live even when switched or fused off, creating a serious shock risk.

questions.prompt: When carrying out a continuity of circuit protective conductor test, it is recommended that a test instrument operates at:

options.A: 20 V and delivers a short circuit current of 100 mA
options.B: 20 V and delivers a short circuit current of 200 mA
options.C: 50 V and delivers a short circuit current of 200 mA
options.D: 500 V and delivers a short circuit current of 100 mA

questions.explanation: A continuity test instrument should drive a current of at least 200 mA from a source of 4 to 24 V so the measurement is reliable through joints and connections. The low voltage keeps testing safe while the current confirms a sound, low-resistance protective path.

questions.prompt: One of the purposes of an inspection prior to initial testing of an installation, is to verify that the installed equipment is:

options.A: Connected to the supply and energised
options.B: Exceeds the minimum insulation resistance value

questions.explanation: Inspection before testing is carried out with the installation de-energised, so its purpose is to confirm by sight that equipment is correctly selected, installed and not visibly damaged. Functional and electrical performance can only be confirmed afterwards by the relevant tests.

questions.prompt: Electrical equipment installed above a swimming pool diving board should not be fixed at a height less than:
questions.explanation: Around swimming pools the area above a diving board is a higher-risk zone where people may be wet and reaching upward. Fixing electrical equipment no lower than 2.5 metres keeps it out of normal reach, reducing the chance of contact in these dangerous conditions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following may be installed inside a hot air sauna?

options.A: A ceiling mounted cord operated light switch
options.B: A socket outlet fed from an SELV supply source
options.C: A thermostat mounted on the sauna
options.D: Any equipment and accessories to IP24

questions.explanation: Inside a hot air sauna the extreme temperatures rule out normal accessories and socket outlets, but the control thermostat for the heater must be located there to sense and regulate the cabin temperature. It is selected to withstand the heat of its zone.

questions.prompt: Construction site special regulations apply to:
questions.explanation: The special requirements for construction and demolition sites apply to the harsh, temporary conditions of the work itself, such as earthworks, where wet ground, damage and reduced body resistance raise shock risk. Permanent welfare facilities like offices and canteens follow ordinary installation rules.

questions.prompt: In agricultural premises, an RCD may be used for protection against fire providing the operating current does not exceed:
questions.explanation: Agricultural premises carry a high fire risk from dust, livestock and combustible materials, so an RCD used for fire protection must operate at no more than 300 mA. This limits sustained earth leakage that could ignite a fire while avoiding nuisance tripping.

questions.prompt: The minimum cross-sectional area of any conductor in a caravan is:
questions.explanation: Caravan wiring is subject to vibration and flexing in service, so conductors must be robust enough to resist mechanical fatigue and breakage. A minimum cross-sectional area of 1.5 square millimetres ensures every conductor has adequate strength as well as current-carrying capacity.

questions.prompt: The maximum permissible height for a caravan inlet is:
questions.explanation: Section 708 limits the mounting height of a caravan pitch supply inlet so that the connecting flexible cable stays clear of damage and the socket-outlet remains accessible. Placing the inlet no higher than 1.8 m above ground keeps it within safe reach and protects the trailing lead.

questions.prompt: One method acceptable to the IEE Regulations for providing fault protection on circuits feeding street furniture is by:
questions.explanation: Street furniture such as lighting columns relies on automatic disconnection of supply for fault protection, since a protective device clears an earth fault within the required time. Electrical separation and earth-free bonding are unsuited to outdoor fixed equipment, so disconnection is the practical measure here.

questions.prompt: BS7671 applies to:
questions.explanation: The scope of BS 7671 in Chapter 11 extends to fixed installations including photovoltaic supplies, which feed energy into a consumer's installation. Aircraft, the distributor's network equipment and the electrical equipment of machines are specifically excluded as they fall under other standards.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 does not apply to:
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 excludes railway traction equipment, rolling stock and signalling because those systems are governed by separate dedicated standards. Fairgrounds, marinas and photovoltaic systems are each addressed by their own special-location parts within the Regulations and so remain in scope.

questions.prompt: Protection against electric shock under single fault conditions is:
questions.explanation: Fault protection guards against electric shock under single-fault conditions, typically a failure of basic insulation that makes an exposed-conductive-part live. Basic protection covers normal conditions, so protection during one fault is precisely what the definition of fault protection describes.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not be defined as a live part?
questions.explanation: A live part is a conductor intended to be energised in normal use, which by definition includes the neutral. A PEN conductor combines protective earthing and neutral functions and is excluded from the definition of a live part, so it would not be classed as one.

questions.prompt: Every installation should be divided into circuits as necessary to avoid:

options.B: Hazards to minimise inconvenience in the event of a fault

questions.explanation: Chapter 31 requires installations to be divided into circuits so a single fault does not disable everything at once. Separate circuits limit hazards, ease fault-finding and testing, and minimise the inconvenience and danger caused when one circuit is interrupted.

questions.prompt: The protective measure 'automatic disconnection of supply':

options.A: Is a combination of basic and fault protection
options.B: Is a combination of under and over voltage protection
options.C: Is a method of reducing thermal effects
options.D: Is only permitted if the installation is under effective supervision

questions.explanation: Automatic disconnection of supply is a complete protective measure that combines basic protection, normally by insulation or barriers, with fault protection by protective earthing, equipotential bonding and timely disconnection. Both elements together guard against shock under normal and single-fault conditions.

questions.prompt: The maximum disconnection time for a 16A final circuit having Uo 230V ac on a TN system is:
questions.explanation: On a TN system a final circuit up to 63 A supplying socket-outlets or portable equipment at 230 V must disconnect within 0.4 seconds. The shorter time reflects the higher risk where people may be in contact with exposed-conductive-parts during a fault.

questions.prompt: Where there is a danger of fire due to the nature of stored materials a motor with star - delta starting must be protected against excessive temperature:
questions.explanation: Where stored materials create a fire risk, a star-delta motor must be protected against excessive temperature in both the star and delta connections. Overload sensing in only one configuration could leave the windings unprotected during the other, allowing dangerous overheating to develop.

questions.prompt: In the event of failure of the provision for basic protection, additional protection may be provided by:

options.C: Use of a RCD with lΔn not exceeding 30mA
options.D: Use of a time delay 100mA RCD

questions.explanation: Additional protection is provided by a residual current device with a rated operating current not exceeding 30 mA, which disconnects quickly if basic protection fails and a person contacts a live part. It supplements other measures rather than replacing them.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a method of fault protection:
questions.explanation: Placing out of reach is a measure for basic protection against contact with live parts in normal use, not for fault protection. Earthing and bonding, electrical separation and Class II equipment are recognised methods of providing protection under fault conditions.

questions.prompt: For a TT system where disconnection in the case of earth fault is achieved by RCD, the maximum disconnection time for a general socket in a domestic kitchen is:
questions.explanation: On a TT system a final circuit up to 63 A supplying socket-outlets must disconnect within 0.2 seconds, the shorter time reflecting the higher earth-fault loop impedance typical of TT earthing. An RCD readily achieves this rapid operation for the kitchen socket.

questions.prompt: In the event of an earth fault on the HV side of a substation, the LV installation may be affected by:
questions.explanation: An earth fault on the high-voltage side of a substation raises the earth potential, and this can impose a power frequency stress voltage across the insulation of the low-voltage installation. Section 442 addresses limiting and withstanding such transferred voltages.

questions.prompt: Connection of extraneous conductive parts to the MET of an installation forms part of the requirements for:
questions.explanation: Connecting extraneous-conductive-parts to the main earthing terminal creates the main protective bonding that forms part of fault protection by automatic disconnection. Bonding holds these parts near earth potential so dangerous touch voltages cannot persist during an earth fault.

questions.prompt: Thermoplastic PVC T&E buried less than 50mm must be protected by:

options.B: Cpc the same size as the P & N

questions.explanation: Cables concealed in a wall at a depth of less than 50 mm without earthed mechanical protection must have additional protection by a 30 mA RCD. This guards against shock should a nail or screw penetrate the cable and make accessible metalwork live.

questions.prompt: RCD installed for protection against fire must have a rating not exceeding:
questions.explanation: Where a residual current device is provided to give protection against fire, its rated residual operating current must not exceed 300 mA. This threshold detects the leakage currents associated with insulation breakdown that can cause ignition, while avoiding nuisance tripping on normal leakage.

questions.prompt: Which of the following may not be used as an earth electrode:
questions.explanation: A water utility's metal supply pipe must not be used as an earth electrode because the supplier may replace sections with plastic, removing the earth path without warning. Earth plates, structural steelwork and welded reinforcement provide reliable buried metal contact instead.

questions.prompt: Socket outlets with a rating not exceeding 20A for general use by ordinary persons should be:
questions.explanation: General-use socket-outlets up to 20A intended for use by ordinary persons must have additional protection by a 30mA RCD. This guards against electric shock if a person contacts a live part or where portable equipment outdoors develops a fault, since 30mA disconnects fast enough to prevent ventricular fibrillation.

questions.prompt: Lighting installations in bus shelters must be protected by:
questions.explanation: Bus shelters are outdoor public locations where vandalism and weather make cable damage likely, so the lighting must have additional protection by a 30mA RCD. This rapid residual-current device disconnects quickly enough to protect anyone who contacts a live part following such damage.

questions.prompt: Busbar trunking systems must comply with:
questions.explanation: Busbar trunking is a type-tested low-voltage assembly, so it must conform to BS EN 60439-2, the standard covering busbar trunking systems. Compliance ensures the assembly has verified ratings for current-carrying capacity, short-circuit withstand and temperature rise under fault conditions.

questions.prompt: The minimum acceptable value for insulation resistance in 230v supply is:
questions.explanation: For circuits operating up to 500V, including a 230V supply, the minimum acceptable insulation resistance is 1.0 megohm when tested at 500V DC. This margin confirms the insulation is sound and limits leakage current that could otherwise cause shock, fire or nuisance tripping.

questions.prompt: Insulation resistance measured between line and neutral of a 230v domestic installation should not be less than:
questions.explanation: Insulation resistance between live conductors of a 230V installation, tested at 500V DC, must be at least 1.0 megohm. A reading at or above this value confirms the insulation between line and neutral is intact and leakage current is negligibly small.

questions.prompt: A PV generator and array junction box must have a warning label indicating that:

options.B: Parts inside may still be live following isolation
options.C: PV array must be cleaned regularly

questions.explanation: A photovoltaic array cannot be switched off; it continues to generate voltage whenever exposed to light. The junction box therefore needs a label warning that live parts may remain energised after isolation, alerting anyone working on the DC side to the persistent shock hazard.

questions.prompt: All circuits in a bathroom must have:
questions.explanation: Locations containing a bath or shower are special locations of increased shock risk because wet skin lowers body resistance. All circuits serving such a room must have additional protection by a 30mA RCD so that any fault current is disconnected before it can cause harm.

questions.prompt: Electrical cables in Zone 1 of a fountain shall be protected against mechanical impact to:
questions.explanation: Zone 1 of a fountain is a location where people and equipment are exposed, so cables must withstand a high degree of mechanical impact, classified AG2 (medium severity). Selecting equipment to this external-influence rating ensures the wiring resists knocks without damage to its insulation.

questions.prompt: On agricultural premises an RCD may be used for protection against fire providing that the rating of the RCD does not exceed:
questions.explanation: On agricultural and horticultural premises, where livestock and combustible materials raise the fire risk, an RCD used for protection against fire must have a rated residual operating current not exceeding 300mA. This limits earth leakage to a level that disconnects before heating can ignite a fire.

questions.prompt: Any luminaries of lighting chains used at a circus must be firmly fixed when at a height less than:
questions.explanation: At fairgrounds, amusement parks and circuses, luminaires in lighting chains positioned lower than 2.5m above ground are within easy reach of people. They must therefore be firmly fixed and suitably guarded to prevent contact, displacement or damage that could expose live parts.

questions.prompt: In a bathroom the protective measure of obstacles is:
questions.explanation: In a location containing a bath or shower, protection by obstacles and placing out of reach are not permitted because the wet conditions and reduced body resistance demand more reliable measures. Only full basic and fault protection that prevents contact with live parts is acceptable here.

questions.prompt: Where a TN system of earthing is used in a marina the final circuits for the supply of a pleasure craft must not include:
questions.explanation: In a marina the supply to a pleasure craft must not use a PEN conductor, so PME earthing facilities cannot be exported to the boat. The combined neutral and earth carries load current, and a break would raise the craft's metalwork to a dangerous potential in the water.

questions.prompt: For a 100 mA non-delay RCD to BSEN 61008 the residual test currents and maximum permitted disconnection times are:
questions.explanation: A general-type RCD must operate within 300ms at its rated residual current of 100mA, and within 40ms when subjected to five times that rating, here 500mA. Testing at both currents confirms the device disconnects fast enough to provide effective additional protection.

questions.prompt: Flat T & E cable clipped direct to a ceiling joist where thermal insulation exceeds 100mm thickness is installation method:
questions.explanation: Flat twin-and-earth cable clipped to a joist and covered by more than 100mm of thermal insulation cannot dissipate heat freely, so it is classed as reference method 101. This severe derating reflects the restricted cooling and requires a substantially reduced current-carrying capacity.

questions.prompt: BS 7671:2018 applies to

options.A: Electric fences covered by BS EN 60335-2-76
options.C: Lightning protection of buildings covered by BS 6651
options.D: Onshore units of electrical shore connections for inland navigation vessels

questions.explanation: Onshore units supplying electrical shore connections to inland navigation vessels fall within the scope of BS 7671. Electric fences, lift installations and lightning protection are each governed by their own dedicated standards and are specifically excluded from these wiring regulations.

questions.prompt: Which of the following voltages are not within the scope of BS 7671:2018
questions.explanation: The regulations apply to AC up to 1000V and DC up to 1500V, so a range stated as 0V to 1500V AC lies outside their scope. Above 1000V AC the installation is high voltage and falls under different standards and safety requirements.

questions.prompt: Switching off electrical loads for variable periods to optimise demand is known as
questions.explanation: Switching loads off for variable periods to reduce or smooth maximum demand is termed load shedding. It is an energy-management technique that limits peak current drawn from the supply, easing strain on the installation and reducing maximum demand charges.

questions.prompt: Installations should be arranged so as to avoid danger and minimise inconvenience in the event of a fault and facilitate safe operation, inspection, testing and maintenance. One method of complying with this is to

options.A: Connect all circuits on the radial principle
options.B: Divide the installation into lighting and power
options.C: Divide the installation into separate circuits
options.D: Fit an RCD at the main intake position

questions.explanation: Dividing an installation into separate circuits limits the effect of a single fault to one circuit, so the rest stays energised. This minimises inconvenience, reduces danger and allows individual circuits to be isolated for safe inspection, testing and maintenance without shutting down the whole installation.

questions.prompt: A component of a support system consisting of regularly spaced elements which mechanically retains a cable is defined as a cable
questions.explanation: A cleat is the support component made of regularly spaced elements that grips and mechanically retains a cable along its run. Brackets, ladders and trays support cables but do not clamp them at intervals in the way the defined term requires.

questions.prompt: Measures reducing the effect of electromagnetic interferences shall be given consideration by
questions.explanation: Mitigating electromagnetic interference is a design decision because it depends on circuit layout, segregation, screening and equipment selection chosen at the design stage. The designer must allow for these influences before installation, since the installer or tester cannot retrofit such measures effectively.

questions.prompt: When considering the frequency of maintaining installed electrical equipment, which of the following is not an essential requirement

options.B: Protective measures for safety remain effective
options.C: Regular periodic inspection and testing shall be carried out
options.D: The nature of current and frequency

questions.explanation: Maintenance frequency is governed by factors like safe access, continued effectiveness of protective measures and the need for periodic inspection and testing. The nature of the current and frequency is a supply characteristic relevant to design, not a driver of how often equipment must be maintained.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a measure of 'fault protection'
questions.explanation: Fault protection guards against contact with parts made live by a fault, achieved by automatic disconnection, Class II construction or protective equipotential bonding. A metal consumer unit enclosure is a fire-containment and basic-protection measure, not a recognised method of fault protection.

questions.prompt: Protection against transient overvoltages need not be provided where the consequence caused by overvoltage could

options.B: Result in interruption of commercial activity
options.C: Result in loss of human life

questions.explanation: Surge protection against transient overvoltage can be omitted only where a surge would cause no serious consequence, such as no interruption to public services. Where overvoltage could risk human life, serious injury or interruption of commercial activity, protection becomes necessary because the consequences are significant.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct

options.A: Each electrical installation shall have provisions for isolation from each supply
options.B: In TN-C-S systems the PEN conductor may be isolated or switched
options.C: In TN-S and TN-C-S systems the switching of the neutral conductor is always required
options.D: Where residual electrical energy is potentially present, suitable means need not be provided for its discharge

questions.explanation: Every installation must have a means of isolating it from each source of supply so it can be made safely dead for work. A PEN conductor must never be switched or isolated, and residual stored energy must always be provided with a means of discharge.

questions.prompt: In an IT system, where touch voltage is limited to 50V, what is the maximum resistance of the earth electrode and protective conductor for exposed conductive parts when the fault current is 200A
questions.explanation: The earth fault loop in an IT system must hold the touch voltage at or below 50V, so the electrode and protective conductor resistance cannot exceed the voltage divided by the fault current. With 50V and 200A this gives 50/200, which equals 0.25 ohms.

questions.prompt: The requirements for both basic and fault protection can be provided by SELV. One suitable source of SELV would be a
questions.explanation: A SELV source must be electrically independent of higher-voltage circuits and incapable of exceeding the extra-low-voltage limit. A 50V storage battery is an independent low-voltage source, whereas generators and transformers rated at higher voltages, or simple step-down transformers, do not provide the required separation.

questions.prompt: The prospective short circuit current at the origin of the consumer's installation must be taken into account when

options.A: Assessing the methods to be used to provide basic protection
options.B: Assessing the value of the external earth loop impedance
options.C: Selecting the number of ways required for the main distribution board
options.D: Selecting the type of main overcurrent protective device to be installed

questions.explanation: The prospective short-circuit current at the origin sets the breaking capacity a protective device must safely interrupt. The main overcurrent device must therefore be selected with a rated capacity at least equal to this fault current, otherwise it could fail destructively under fault conditions.

questions.prompt: When protecting against burns a metallic part intended to be touched but not hand held shall be limited to a maximum temperature of
questions.explanation: Accessible metallic parts intended to be touched but not gripped are limited to 70 degrees Celsius to prevent burns from incidental contact. Parts that are hand-held continuously are held to a lower limit because the skin is exposed to the heat for longer.

questions.prompt: RCDs have to are required to have the button marked 'T' or 'Test' pressed for mechanical operation every
questions.explanation: Pressing the test button operates the RCD mechanism and confirms it will trip, but this only verifies mechanical function rather than the protective settings. Carrying this out roughly every six months helps ensure the device has not seized and remains able to operate when needed.

questions.prompt: A protective conductor shall not pass through a RCD

options.B: Except where unavoidable and in the reverse direction
options.C: Except where unavoidable and passed through in both directions

questions.explanation: A protective conductor must not be threaded through an RCD because its current would unbalance the residual sensing and cause nuisance tripping or impaired operation. Only where unavoidable may a circuit protective conductor pass through, looped in both directions so the net flux through the core cancels.

questions.prompt: A Type 2 SPDs is installed in a single phase CT2 system and connected between L-N. Its nominal discharge current (Inspd) shall be not less than
questions.explanation: For a Type 2 surge protective device connected line-to-neutral in a single-phase installation, the nominal discharge current rating must be at least 5kA. This ensures the device can repeatedly divert expected switching and induced surge currents without failing prematurely.

questions.prompt: In a TN system with a line conductor of 25mm2 the required size of the earthing conductor, shall be
questions.explanation: Where the earthing conductor is the same material as the line conductor, sizing follows the adiabatic relationship: equal to the line size up to 16mm2, then half above 35mm2. A 25mm2 line conductor falls in the middle band, requiring a minimum 16mm2 earthing conductor.

questions.prompt: In the formula S = √If2t/k the symbol 'k' represents

options.A: A factor applied to conductor materials
options.B: The amplitude of the fault current
options.C: The minimum size of the cpc
options.D: The time the fault current exists

questions.explanation: In the adiabatic equation, k is a factor derived from the conductor material and its insulation, accounting for its resistivity, heat capacity and permitted temperature limits. It determines how much fault energy the conductor can withstand before reaching its limiting temperature.

questions.prompt: A cable installed under a floor or above a ceiling, without mechanical protection, should be run at least

options.A: 100 mm from the top or bottom of the joist or batten
options.B: 25 mm from the top or bottom of the joist or batten
options.C: 30 mm from the top or bottom of the joist or batten
options.D: 50 mm from the top or bottom of the joist or batten

questions.explanation: An unprotected cable through joists or above a ceiling must sit at least 50mm from the top or bottom surface. This depth keeps the cable beyond the reach of nails and screws driven into the timber, protecting it from accidental penetration.

questions.prompt: If a main protective bonding conductor cannot be connected to the gas service pipe close to the meter because the meter is external to the building the bond should be connected

options.A: At the point of entry to the building
options.B: Before the point of entry to the building
options.D: Within two meters of the gas meter

questions.explanation: Main protective bonding to a metallic gas service must connect to the consumer's side of the meter, as near as practicable to the point of entry into the building. Where the meter is external, the connection is made at the point of entry to keep the bond effective inside the installation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following devices may be used for emergency switching
questions.explanation: A device for emergency switching must reliably interrupt the supply in a single action and not reconnect unintentionally. A circuit breaker meets this because it provides positive, mechanically reliable disconnection, unlike semiconductor devices, plug-and-socket arrangements or luminaire connection devices.

questions.prompt: Initial verification of an installation shall be made by

options.B: Inspection and testing person qualified to C&G 2391
options.D: Skilled person(s) competent in such work

questions.explanation: Verification must be carried out by people with the knowledge and experience relevant to the work, so they can judge whether the installation is safe. The Regulations frame this competence as a skilled person competent in such work rather than a particular named qualification.

questions.prompt: Measuring instruments should be in accordance with
questions.explanation: Instruments and measuring equipment used for testing should comply with the relevant standard so that readings are accurate and the test itself does not introduce danger. Using equipment built to the correct specification gives confidence that verification results are reliable.

questions.prompt: When completing an Electrical Installation Certificate which of the following can only be ascertained by enquiry or measurement
questions.explanation: Some installation characteristics cannot be read directly and must be established by asking the supply provider or by measurement. The earthing arrangement, for example, depends on the distributor's network and so is determined by enquiry rather than simple observation.

questions.prompt: On a construction site a final circuit supplying a socket-outlet with a rated current not exceeding 32A when protected by an RCD the rated residual operating current not greater than
questions.explanation: On construction sites the increased risk of shock means socket-outlets up to 32A require additional protection against direct contact and earth faults. A residual current device with an operating current not exceeding 30mA gives the fast disconnection needed to protect people in these harsher conditions.

questions.prompt: Zone 1 extends horizontally from the side of a bath for a distance of
questions.explanation: The zoning around a bath defines where electrical equipment faces the greatest moisture and contact risk. Zone 1 reaches a limited horizontal distance from the bath edge, taken as 0.6m, marking the area where only equipment with suitable protection may be installed.

questions.prompt: In agricultural premises, an r.c.d. may be used for protection against fire providing the operating current does NOT exceed
questions.explanation: In agricultural premises the higher fire risk means residual current devices are used to limit earth leakage that could ignite materials. An operating current not exceeding 300mA detects fault energy early enough to reduce fire risk while avoiding nuisance tripping.

questions.prompt: A 230V circuit is protected by a 50A Type B circuit-breaker to BS EN 6089The minimum value of fault current to ensure compliance with maximum disconnection times is
questions.explanation: A Type B breaker operates instantaneously at around five times its rated current, so a 50A device needs roughly 250A of fault current to trip within the required time. Meeting this minimum ensures the circuit disconnects fast enough to limit shock risk.

questions.prompt: Multicore cables on a perforated tray are designated reference method
questions.explanation: Installation methods are classified by reference letters that reflect how heat dissipates from the cable. Multicore cables laid on a perforated tray sit in free air with good ventilation, which corresponds to reference method E and its higher current-carrying capacity.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 includes requirements for:
questions.explanation: The scope of the Regulations extends beyond new work to cover changes made to existing installations. Alterations and additions must meet the same safety requirements, so any modification is brought within the standard rather than left unregulated.

questions.prompt: The IEE Regulations provide

options.D: Safety especially from fire, shock and burns

questions.explanation: The Regulations exist primarily to protect people and property from the hazards electricity creates. Their fundamental purpose is safety, especially guarding against fire, electric shock and burns, rather than acting as a complete design manual for every situation.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following electrical installations is NOT covered by BS 7671?

options.B: Lightning protection of buildings to BS EN 62305

questions.explanation: The Regulations set out specific exclusions for systems governed by their own standards. Lightning protection of buildings falls under BS EN 62305 and is treated as a separate discipline, so it lies outside the scope of the wiring rules.

questions.prompt: The IEE Regulations are non-statutory but, if they are adhered to compliance with which one of the following statutory regulations is most likely?

options.C: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002
options.D: The Health and Safety at Work Act 1974

questions.explanation: The wiring rules are not law in themselves but support compliance with statutory duties. Following them helps satisfy the general obligation to ensure safety under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, which underpins safe working in this field.

questions.prompt: Which of the following electrical installations IS covered by the IEE Regulations?
questions.explanation: The standard covers a wide range of fixed installations, including the temporary and special locations associated with public events. Exhibitions and fairs fall within scope because their electrical systems still need to meet the same safety requirements as permanent installations.

questions.prompt: The IEE Regulations state requirements intended to provide:

options.B: Instructions for lightning protection of buildings

questions.explanation: The overriding intent of the Regulations is to protect people who use or work near electrical installations. Their requirements are framed around the safety of persons rather than achieving the cheapest design or covering every conceivable circumstance.

questions.prompt: The IEE Regulations recognises that in electrical installations there is a risk of injury from:
questions.explanation: The Regulations are concerned chiefly with the hazards arising directly from electricity itself. Among these, the risk of injury from shock currents passing through the body is a central danger the requirements are designed to prevent.

questions.prompt: When choosing the type of wiring system for an installation, consideration should be given to:

options.A: Accessibility of wiring to persons and livestock
options.B: The experience of the installing electrician

questions.explanation: Selecting a wiring system involves considering the external influences it will face in service. Whether wiring is accessible to people and livestock affects the risk of damage and contact, so this must be weighed when choosing a suitable method.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 requires that:

options.A: All installations have a main switch
options.B: The installation main switch switches the line conductor only
options.C: The main switch must have BS 88 fuses
options.D: There must be an effective means of cutting off all voltages of every installation

questions.explanation: Every installation must be capable of being made safe for work or in an emergency. The Regulations therefore require an effective means of cutting off all voltages, so the supply can be fully isolated rather than partially disconnected.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 requires that the person carrying out the inspection and testing shall:

options.A: Be competent to carry out the testing
options.D: Have at least three years' experience

questions.explanation: Reliable inspection and testing depends on the judgement and knowledge of the individual carrying it out. The Regulations require that person to be competent for the work, since only sound competence ensures faults are correctly identified and the installation verified as safe.

questions.prompt: An overcurrent occurring in a circuit that is electrically sound is defined as:
questions.explanation: An overload is an overcurrent that arises in a circuit with no electrical fault, where the conductors and insulation remain intact but the load drawn simply exceeds the circuit's rated capacity. This distinguishes it from fault currents, which flow through damaged or short-circuited paths.

questions.prompt: The term fault protection refers to:

options.D: Protection against electric shock under fault conditions

questions.explanation: Fault protection guards against electric shock when a fault, such as a breakdown of basic insulation, makes an exposed-conductive-part live. Measures like automatic disconnection of supply ensure dangerous touch voltages are removed quickly under those fault conditions, protecting anyone in contact.

questions.prompt: The design current of a circuit is the current:

options.A: A fuse is designed to carry
options.C: Causing effective operation of the device

questions.explanation: Design current is the current intended to be carried by a circuit during normal service. It forms the starting point for sizing conductors and selecting the protective device, since the cable and device must comfortably handle the expected working load.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is an exposed conductive part?

options.C: The casing of a central heating pump
options.D: The casing of Class II equipment

questions.explanation: An exposed-conductive-part is conductive metalwork of equipment that can be touched and is not normally live but could become live under a fault. The pump casing fits this, whereas pipes and radiators are extraneous parts and Class II equipment has no such reliance on earthing.

questions.prompt: A short circuit current is defined as:

options.B: An over current occurring in an electrically sound circuit
options.C: The current occurring during a fault between live conductors of negligible impedance
options.D: The current rating of the fuse

questions.explanation: A short-circuit current is the overcurrent resulting from a fault of negligible impedance between conductors normally at different potentials, such as line and neutral. Because the connecting path has almost no resistance, the prospective current can be very large and demands rapid disconnection.

questions.prompt: A d.c. voltage of 80V between conductors is classified as being:
questions.explanation: Voltage bands place anything not exceeding 120V d.c. between conductors within extra-low voltage. At 80V d.c. the circuit sits comfortably below that threshold, so it is classified as extra-low rather than low voltage.

questions.prompt: The part of a fuse that is designed to melt when the fuse operates is called the fuse____
questions.explanation: The element is the calibrated conductive part within a fuse that carries normal current but heats and melts when an overcurrent persists. Its controlled melting breaks the circuit, while the carrier and link simply hold or connect the fuse in place.

questions.prompt: A person with technical knowledge or sufficient experience to enable him/her to avoid dangers that electricity may create is defined as:
questions.explanation: A skilled person is defined by their technical knowledge or experience, enabling them to recognise and avoid the dangers electricity can create. This goes beyond an instructed person, who only works safely under the supervision or guidance of a skilled person.

questions.prompt: Protective conductor current is a current that:

options.B: Appears in a protective conductor such as leakage current
options.C: Is the same value as the design current
options.D: Only flows when there is an earth fault

questions.explanation: Protective conductor current is the current that flows in a protective conductor under normal, healthy conditions, for example the leakage current arising from equipment with filters or capacitive coupling. It exists without any fault present, unlike an earth fault current.

questions.prompt: An overload current could arise when:

options.A: A forward/reverse controller attempts to switch a motor to both directions simultaneously
options.B: An electrician drills through a busbar chamber and touches a live busbar with the drill
options.C: Contamination of a motor terminal block results in tracking
options.D: Excessive mechanical load is applied to an electric motor

questions.explanation: An overload occurs in a sound circuit when the connected load demands more current than intended, such as a motor asked to drive an excessive mechanical load. The conductors remain undamaged, so the rise in current is overload rather than a fault current.

questions.prompt: The type of building construction in which an installation is to be carried out may affect the design and safe operation of the installation. This effect is called:
questions.explanation: Conditions arising from the surroundings, including the type of building construction, are treated as external influences that the designer must assess. These influences affect equipment selection and installation methods so that the installation operates safely in its particular environment.

questions.prompt: In addition to regular maintenance of an installation, which one of the following is NOT an essential requirement?

options.A: Periodic inspection and testing may be readily and safely carried out
options.B: Protective measures for safety remain effective
options.C: The name and address of the contractor is permanently displayed adjacent to the mains
options.D: The reliability of the equipment is sustained

questions.explanation: The essential maintenance requirements are that protective measures stay effective, equipment reliability is sustained, and periodic inspection and testing can be done safely. Displaying the contractor's name and address by the mains is not among these safety-related requirements.

questions.prompt: The three general categories of external influence are environment, utilisation and:

options.D: The number and type of live conductors

questions.explanation: External influences are grouped into three broad categories: environment, utilisation, and the construction of buildings. Each addresses a different aspect, with building construction covering factors such as the materials used and the structural design that affect the installation.

questions.prompt: With reference to the general characteristics of an electrical installation, the maximum demand should be:

options.A: Assessed and diversity may be taken into account

questions.explanation: Maximum demand should be assessed for each circuit and the whole installation, and diversity may be applied where loads are unlikely to operate fully and simultaneously. This realistic estimate avoids oversizing conductors and protective devices while still meeting the genuine load.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following statements is a requirement of BS 7671:2018?

options.A: All fixed installations must be in accordance with the relevant EMC regulations
options.B: Consideration should be given to the need to carry out periodic inspection during the life of the installation
options.C: Electromagnetic interference is not considered when planning and designing an installation
options.D: Storage batteries may be used as a source of electrical energy for a safety service

questions.explanation: Consideration must be given to the need for periodic inspection and testing throughout an installation's life, so that deterioration is found and safety is maintained over time. This forms part of the general design requirements rather than being an optional afterthought.

questions.prompt: The external influence having a classification of AD8 would indicate a condition of:
questions.explanation: Within the external influence classification for water, the AD code rises with severity, and AD8 denotes submersion where equipment is permanently and totally under water. This is more onerous than immersion, requiring equipment suitable for continuous underwater conditions.

questions.prompt: Where a wiring system is installed in a building whose structure has an external influence category CB4, the wiring system shall be:
questions.explanation: Classification CB4 indicates building movement, so a wiring system must accommodate that flexing without damage. A flexible wiring system can absorb the relative movement of the structure, whereas a rigid system would risk being stressed or broken.

questions.prompt: The Classification code for high wind is:
questions.explanation: Wind is an environmental external influence coded under the AS classification, with AS3 denoting high wind severity. The letter pair identifies the influence as wind, and the numeral indicates the degree to which the installation is exposed to it.

questions.prompt: An external influence categorised as AG1 applies to a:
questions.explanation: External influence code AG covers impact, and category AG1 denotes low severity mechanical stresses typical of ordinary domestic conditions. A dwelling experiences only light impact, so a house fits AG1, whereas factories, workshops and quarries face higher mechanical stress classifications.

questions.prompt: When considering continuity of service to life support systems, which one of the following should be considered?

options.A: Selection of protective device to achieve discrimination
options.B: The fixing height of switches and socket
options.C: The number of persons in the building
options.D: The type of cable to be used

questions.explanation: Continuity of supply to critical loads like life support depends on a fault clearing only the affected circuit, not the whole system. Selecting protective devices to achieve discrimination ensures the device nearest the fault operates first, leaving upstream supplies intact for essential equipment.

questions.prompt: A 230 V single phase circuit supplying a pump motor is protected by a 20 A type C circuit breaker to BS EN 6089The minimum value of fault current to ensure compliance with the thermal and shock requirements is:
questions.explanation: A type C circuit breaker requires a current of ten times its rating to guarantee fast magnetic tripping within the required time. For a 20 A device that minimum is 200 A, ensuring both shock disconnection times and thermal protection of conductors are satisfied.

questions.prompt: Given that the fault current on a 16A BS 88 fuse is 60A, the corresponding disconnection time is:
questions.explanation: Reading the time/current characteristic for a 16 A BS 88 fuse, a fault current of around 60 A intersects the curve at roughly 3 seconds. The relatively modest overcurrent produces a slow disconnection rather than near-instantaneous clearance, reflecting the fuse's inverse time response.

questions.prompt: From the time/current characteristic for a 30A BS 3036 fuse, the approximate current required to operate this device at a time of 5 s is:
questions.explanation: Rewireable BS 3036 fuses have a shallow time/current curve, so reaching the 5 second disconnection point for a 30 A device needs a current well above its rating. The characteristic shows approximately 87 A produces that operating time.

questions.prompt: A 15A protective device to BS3036 when carrying a fault current of 180A has an operating time of:
questions.explanation: A fault current of 180 A is many multiples of a 15 A rewireable fuse rating, driving the element well into its fast-melting region. At this high overcurrent the BS 3036 characteristic gives an operating time of about 0.1 seconds.

questions.prompt: A 30A protective device to BS1361 when carrying a fault current of 200A will operate in:
questions.explanation: Following the BS 1361 cartridge fuse time/current characteristic for a 30 A device, a fault current of 200 A corresponds to a disconnection time of roughly 0.4 seconds. The cartridge construction clears faster than a rewireable fuse at the same overcurrent.

questions.prompt: The symbol used to denote the operating current of the device protecting a circuit against overload is:
questions.explanation: In the coordination relationship for overload protection, the symbol I2 represents the current ensuring effective operation of the protective device within the conventional time. It is one of the values, alongside design current and conductor capacity, used to verify a device protects its circuit.

questions.prompt: A 230 V 30 A radial circuit is protected by a BS 3036 device. If the value of earth loop impedance for the circuit is 2.3@, disconnection under Line/earth fault condition will occur in:
questions.explanation: With a 230 V supply and 2.3 ohm loop impedance the fault current is about 100 A. Reading this against the 30 A BS 3036 characteristic gives a disconnection time of around 3 seconds, satisfying the permitted time for this circuit type.

questions.prompt: The fault current due to an earth fault of negligible impedance in a 400V, three phase four-wire circuit having an earth loop impedance of 0.3 @ is:
questions.explanation: In a 400 V three-phase four-wire system the relevant fault path uses the phase-to-neutral voltage of 230 V. Dividing 230 V by the 0.3 ohm earth loop impedance gives approximately 767 A of prospective earth fault current.

questions.prompt: A single-phase circuit is to be wired using single-core cables having 90℃ thermosetting insulation with copper conductors and protected by a BS 3036 protective device. For an ambient temperature of 55℃, identify which of the following is the ambient temperature rating factor to be used when determining the size of the conductor.
questions.explanation: Ambient temperature correction factors come from the rating factor tables, applied relative to the device type. For a rewireable BS 3036 fuse protecting 90 degree thermosetting cable at 55 degrees ambient, the appropriate correction factor is 0.76, reducing the conductor's effective rating.

questions.prompt: A circuit with a design current of 45 A is installed using a cable with a current rating of 50 A. If the voltage drop for the cable is 8.0mV/A/m, the circuit voltage drop for a 10 m run will be:
questions.explanation: Voltage drop is found by multiplying the tabulated millivolt per ampere per metre figure by the design current and route length. Here 8.0 mV times 45 A times 10 m gives 3600 mV, which equals a circuit voltage drop of 4 V.

questions.prompt: The required current carrying capacity of a circuit conductor has been determined as 22 A. Using the appropriate cable selection table, which of the following is the correct minimum conductor size for three single core thermoplastic cover Light Duty mineral insulated cables with copper conductors clipped direct in flat formation?
questions.explanation: Sizing requires choosing the smallest conductor whose tabulated current carrying capacity meets or exceeds the determined 22 A. For light duty mineral insulated cables clipped direct, a 1.5 mm2 conductor provides the first rating above 22 A, making it the correct minimum size.

questions.prompt: For cable selection purposes the rating factors must be applied to the:

options.A: Current breaking capacity of the protective device
options.B: Current rating of the protective device
options.D: Tabulated current carrying capacity of the cable

questions.explanation: Rating factors for ambient temperature, grouping and similar conditions are applied to the protective device current to establish the minimum tabulated capacity the cable must have. This ensures the conductor remains protected once derating reduces its real current carrying ability.

questions.prompt: A 230 V heating circuit has a design current of 20 A. Length of run for the 6mm2 thermoplastic insulated cable is 25 m. The volt drop for the cable is 7.1mV/Am. The volt drop under full load conditions is:
questions.explanation: Voltage drop equals the tabulated millivolt per ampere per metre value times the design current times the run length. Multiplying 7.1 mV by 20 A by 25 m yields 3550 mV, which rounds to a full-load voltage drop of 3.6 V.

questions.prompt: In an installation a conduit from a lighting distribution board contains 8 identical circuits. The grouping factor Cg to be applied is:
questions.explanation: Grouping several loaded circuits together causes mutual heating, so a correction factor below one must be applied. For eight circuits bunched in a single conduit the grouping factor is 0.52, significantly reducing each cable's permissible current.

questions.prompt: Table 4A2 - The Schedule of Methods of Installation of cables describes non-sheathed cables in conduit on a wooden or masonry wall. This is classified as Reference Method:
questions.explanation: The schedule of installation methods classifies non-sheathed cables drawn into conduit on a wooden or masonry wall as Reference Method B. This reference method then determines which current carrying capacity column applies when sizing the conductors.

questions.prompt: The required current carrying capacity of a circuit conductor has been determined as 42 A. Using the appropriate cable selection table, which of the following is the correct minimum conductor size for three single core thermoplastic covered Heavy Duty mineral insulated cables with copper conductors and sheaths installed on cable tray in flat formation.
questions.explanation: The correct size is the smallest conductor whose tabulated rating equals or exceeds the required 42 A. For heavy duty mineral insulated cables on tray in flat formation, a 4.0 mm2 conductor gives the first capacity above 42 A and is therefore the minimum.

questions.prompt: The fault current due to an earth fault of negligible impedance in a 400V, three phase, four wire circuit having an earth loop impedance of 0.3 ohms, is:
questions.explanation: Fault current equals the circuit voltage divided by the earth loop impedance. For a single phase to earth fault the relevant voltage is the line-to-earth value of roughly 230 V, so 230 divided by 0.3 ohms gives approximately 767 A.

questions.prompt: The rating or setting of an overcurrent protection device must be such that it operates at a current which is not greater than that of the conductor capacity by a factor not exceeding:
questions.explanation: Coordination rules require that the current ensuring effective operation of the device does not exceed 1.45 times the conductor's current-carrying capacity. This limit keeps the cable's let-through energy within safe thermal limits so overload conditions are interrupted before insulation is damaged.

questions.prompt: Class II electrical equipment will provide:
questions.explanation: Class II construction relies on double or reinforced insulation rather than an earthed metal enclosure. The basic insulation provides basic protection against contact with live parts, while the supplementary or reinforced layer provides fault protection should the basic insulation fail.

questions.prompt: Which of the following sources of supply would NOT be accepted as providing separated extra-low voltage?

options.A: A centre tapped transformer giving 55 V to earth
options.B: A Class II safety isolating transformer to BS EN 61558-2-6
options.C: A motor generator set giving BS EN 61558-2-6 isolation
options.D: An electric device in which the output voltage cannot exceed E.L.V. in the case of an internal fault

questions.explanation: SELV demands true separation between the live conductors and earth, achieved by a safety isolating transformer or equivalent source. A centre-tapped transformer referenced to earth at 55 V deliberately connects the system to earth, which is reduced low voltage rather than a separated source.

questions.prompt: A 230 V ac circuit is protected by a 6 A circuit breaker and feeds a number of luminaries. The maximum disconnection time in the event of a fault is:
questions.explanation: A final circuit not exceeding 32 A on a 230 V TN system must disconnect within 0.4 seconds. This short time limits the duration of dangerous touch voltages on exposed-conductive-parts during an earth fault, protecting against electric shock.

questions.prompt: Correct co-ordination between conductors and overcurrent protection device is achieved when:

options.B: Ln exceeds the lowest current carrying capacity lz
options.C: Ln is not less than the design current lb
options.D: The current causing effective operation (I2) exceeds 1.45 l2

questions.explanation: The first coordination condition is that the device's nominal current rating is not less than the design current of the circuit. This ensures the protective device can carry the intended load continuously without nuisance operation while still safeguarding the conductor.

questions.prompt: The requirements for overload current protection are fulfilled when:
questions.explanation: Overload protection requires the design current to be no greater than the device rating, and the rating no greater than the cable's current-carrying capacity. Only the combination of 10 A load, 15 A device and 18 A cable satisfies that ascending order.

questions.prompt: In order to comply with IEE Regulations, the current rating of a BS 3036 fuse should NOT exceed that of the lowest rated conductor in the circuit multiplied by:
questions.explanation: A BS 3036 semi-enclosed rewirable fuse has poor fusing characteristics and a high fusing factor, so the conductor rating is derated. Multiplying the lowest conductor capacity by 0.725 ensures the cable is not overloaded before this slow-acting fuse operates.

questions.prompt: Regulation 434.5.2 gives a maximum time which may be permitted for a fault to be maintained without damaging the conductors. Assume a prospective fault current of 1000 A and a 25 mm2 70℃ thermoplastic cable with a copper conductor, the maximum permitted fault duration is:
questions.explanation: The adiabatic equation relates withstand time to the conductor's cross-sectional area, the k factor and the prospective fault current. For a 25 mm thermoplastic copper cable at 1000 A the calculation yields a permitted fault duration of about 8.2 seconds.

questions.prompt: Devices intended to give protection against both overload and short circuit currents must be capable of breaking currents up to:

options.D: The maximum prospective fault current at the point of installation

questions.explanation: A device giving both overload and short-circuit protection must have a breaking capacity at least equal to the maximum prospective fault current at its point of installation. Otherwise it could fail to clear the highest fault energy it might be called upon to interrupt.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following supplies is NOT suitable for a SELV system?

options.B: Engine-driven generator giving equivalent isolation as BS EN 61558-2-6

questions.explanation: A SELV source must keep the low-voltage circuit electrically separated from earth and from higher-voltage systems. An earthed secondary transformer connects that winding to earth, breaking the required separation, so it cannot provide a genuine SELV supply.

questions.prompt: The temperature limit for non-metallic equipment which is intended to be touched but not hand held is:
questions.explanation: Accessible parts of equipment have temperature limits to prevent burns and degradation. Non-metallic surfaces intended to be touched but not gripped may reach a higher limit of 80 degrees Celsius, since brief contact transfers less heat than continuous holding.

questions.prompt: The maximum earth fault loop impedance for a 110 V (55 V to earth) circuit protected by a 32 A type B circuit breaker to BS EN 60898
questions.explanation: Maximum loop impedance is found from the line-to-earth voltage divided by the current causing disconnection within the required time. A 32 A type B breaker trips at five times rating, so 55 V divided by 160 A gives about 0.34 ohms.

questions.prompt: The characteristic to be ascertained for an external supply in order that the breaking capacity of the overload protective device for an installation can be determined is:
questions.explanation: The breaking capacity of a protective device must exceed the highest fault current it could face. That worst case is set by the prospective short-circuit current available from the external supply, so this characteristic must be obtained from the distributor.

questions.prompt: The maximum phase to earth voltage of a "Reduced Low Voltage System" is defined as:
questions.explanation: A reduced low voltage system limits shock risk on construction sites by using a centre-tapped 110 V supply. With the centre point earthed, each line conductor sits at 55 V to earth, giving a maximum phase-to-earth value of 63.5 V at the extreme.

questions.prompt: Correct co-ordination between conductors and an over-current protective device is achieved when:
questions.explanation: Coordination requires the device's nominal rating to be no greater than the conductor's current-carrying capacity. Keeping the rating below the cable's safe capacity ensures the protective device operates before the conductor is thermally overloaded under sustained overcurrent.

questions.prompt: For the purpose of over voltage control, a suspended cable having insulated conductors with earthed metallic covering is deemed to be:

options.A: A bare or pvc covered cable

questions.explanation: For overvoltage control the protection depends on how exposed a cable is to atmospheric surges. A suspended cable with an earthed metallic covering shields the conductors much like buried wiring, so it is treated as an underground cable for surge assessment.

questions.prompt: Correct co-ordination between conductors and an over-current protective device is achieved when:

options.B: Ln exceeds the lowest current carrying capacity lz
options.C: Ln is not less that the design current lb
options.D: The current causing effective option (l2) exceeds 1.45Iz

questions.explanation: The first coordination requirement is that the device's nominal current rating is not less than the circuit design current. This lets the protective device carry the intended load continuously without nuisance tripping while still protecting the conductor from overload.

questions.prompt: When considering over-voltage protection, direct lightning strikes on low voltage lines of the supply network are:
questions.explanation: Overvoltage protection considers transients arriving along the supply network, but a direct lightning strike onto the low voltage lines releases energy so far beyond ordinary surge levels that it cannot realistically be designed against. For this reason such direct strikes are not taken into account in the assessment.

questions.prompt: Which of the following sources of supply would NOT be accepted for Separated Extra-Low Voltage?

options.A: A centre tapped transformer giving 55 V to earth
options.B: A Class II safety isolating transformer
options.C: A motor generator set giving BS EN 61558-2-6 isolation
options.D: An electrical device in which the output voltage cannot exceed ELV in the case of an internal fault

questions.explanation: Separated extra-low voltage requires a source giving genuine electrical separation from earth and from other circuits, such as a Class II safety isolating transformer or an equivalent isolated source. A centre-tapped transformer referenced to give 55 V to earth has a deliberate earth connection, so it cannot provide the separation SELV demands.

questions.prompt: The MAXIMUM accessible distance that it should be assumed a person can reach when standing on a surface is:
questions.explanation: When assessing arm's reach for protection against contact with live or hazardous parts, the limits of the zone are based on a person reaching with bare hands. From a standing surface the assumed maximum reach upwards extends to 2.50 m, which defines how far live parts must be kept out of reach.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following characteristics of the supply to a building could NOT be determined by an enquiry to the supplier?

options.A: Nature of the current and the frequency
options.B: The prospective short circuit at the origin of the installation
options.C: The type and rating of the protective device
options.D: The value of the earth fault current at the earth acting at the origin of the installation electrode within a TT system

questions.explanation: The distributor can state the supply characteristics at the origin such as the nature and frequency of the current, the prospective short-circuit current and the type and rating of the protective device. The earth fault loop value at a TT installation depends on the consumer's own electrode resistance, so it must be measured by the installer rather than supplied.

questions.prompt: An electric cooker may be connected to a ring final circuit providing it:

options.C: Is no more than 2 metres from the nearest socket outlet

questions.explanation: A ring final circuit is designed for an aggregate of small loads spread around it, not for a single high-current appliance. A cooker may only be served from it if its rating is modest, not exceeding 2 kW, so it does not concentrate excessive load at one point and overload the conductors.

questions.prompt: A permanent warning notice must be fixed at or near the point of connection of every earthing conductor to an earth electrode. This notice must bear the words:

options.C: Safety Electrical Connection - Do Not Remove
options.D: Safety Electrical Earth - Do Not Remove
