questions.explanation: A durable label is required at every earthing and main bonding connection so that anyone working on the installation understands the conductor's safety function. It must read "Safety Electrical Connection - Do Not Remove" to warn against disconnecting a part that maintains protection against electric shock.

questions.prompt: A ceiling rose must not be installed in any circuit operating at voltages exceeding:
questions.explanation: A ceiling rose is constructed and rated for ordinary domestic-style lighting and is not designed to withstand higher voltage stress. It must therefore only be connected in circuits whose nominal voltage does not exceed 250 V, and only one flexible cord may normally be suspended from it.

questions.prompt: When a copper earthing conductor mechanically protected is buried in the ground and is not protected against corrosion, is must have a cross sectional area of at least:
questions.explanation: An earthing conductor buried in the ground must be sized to survive both mechanical disturbance and corrosion over its life. Where it is mechanically protected but not protected against corrosion, copper must be at least 25 mm² so it retains adequate cross-section and a reliable earth path.

questions.prompt: If the cable is totally enclosed in thermal insulation for a distance of 2 m, the correction factor (Ci) will be:
questions.explanation: Thermal insulation traps heat around a cable and severely restricts its ability to dissipate, so the current-carrying capacity must be derated. Where a cable is totally surrounded by thermal insulation for around 0.5 m or more, the worst-case correction factor applied is 0.5, roughly halving its rating.

questions.prompt: Where a supplementary bonding conductor is NOT mechanically protected, the minimum csa allowed is:
questions.explanation: A supplementary bonding conductor must withstand the mechanical stresses of installation if it is not given mechanical protection. To provide that robustness, the minimum cross-sectional area permitted for an unprotected copper bonding conductor is 4 mm², reducing the risk of damage breaking the equipotential connection.

questions.prompt: The csa of a supplementary bonding conductor connecting two extraneous conductive parts and enclosed in metal conduit must NOT be less than:
questions.explanation: Where a supplementary bonding conductor is mechanically protected, for example by being enclosed in metal conduit, the need for added mechanical robustness is removed. The conductor may then be reduced to a minimum of 2.5 mm² copper while still providing the required equipotential connection between the extraneous-conductive-parts.

questions.prompt: The minimum size of a supplementary bonding conductor connecting two exposed conductive parts and IS mechanically protected is:

options.C: Not less than the larger protective conductor connecting the two parts
options.D: Not less than the smaller protective conductor connecting the two parts

questions.explanation: Supplementary bonding between two exposed-conductive-parts must be able to carry the fault current that the smaller of the associated circuit protective conductors carries. Its cross-section therefore need not be less than that smaller protective conductor, ensuring the bond is at least as capable as the path it supplements.

questions.prompt: Using Table 54.7, select the smallest suitable cross sectional area of 70℃ thermoplastic steel wire armouring for a 16 mm2 SWA cable given k2 is 51.
questions.explanation: The armour acts as the circuit protective conductor, so its cross-section must satisfy the adiabatic equation using the k value for the armour material. With k2 of 51 for the steel-wire armour, the smallest armour csa meeting the required thermal withstand for a 16 mm² cable is 36 mm².

questions.prompt: Maximum permitted voltage drop on an installation is:

options.C: From the installations origin to the furthest point

questions.explanation: Voltage drop is assessed across the whole installation, not just one section, so that equipment at the extremity still receives an adequate voltage. The permitted limit therefore applies from the origin of the installation to the furthest point of use, covering all distribution and final circuit conductors in between.

questions.prompt: The maximum rating of an over current protective device for a lighting circuit using E14 type lampholders is:
questions.explanation: Each type of lampholder has a maximum protective device rating set to suit its current-carrying capability and thermal limits. Small Edison-screw E14 lampholders are rated for circuits protected by an overcurrent device of no more than 16 A, preventing the holder from being overloaded.

questions.prompt: When carrying out a continuity of protective conductors test on a circuit, the test equipment must produce a test voltage of between 4 V and 24 V and a short circuit current not less than:
questions.explanation: A continuity test must drive enough current through the protective conductor to confirm a sound low-resistance connection rather than relying on a stray high-resistance path. The instrument therefore delivers a low test voltage between 4 V and 24 V together with a short-circuit current of at least 0.2 A.

questions.prompt: For circuits having a nominal voltage above 500 V, the minimum insulation resistance is:
questions.explanation: Insulation resistance test voltages and minimum acceptable values rise with the circuit's nominal voltage to prove the insulation withstands the working stress. For circuits operating above 500 V the test is applied at 1000 V d.c. and the measured insulation resistance must be at least 1 MΩ.

questions.prompt: One of the purposes of an inspection prior to initial testing of an installation is to verify that the installed equipment is:

options.A: Connected to the supply and energised
options.B: Exceeds the minimum insulation resistance value

questions.explanation: Inspection precedes testing and is carried out with the installation safely isolated, so it confirms what can be seen rather than energised performance. One of its purposes is to verify that installed equipment is not visibly damaged in a way that would impair safety before any test instruments are applied.

questions.prompt: Which of the following four tests should NOT be carried out with the supply on:
questions.explanation: Insulation resistance testing applies a high test voltage across conductors that must be isolated from the supply, both to obtain a valid reading and to avoid damaging connected equipment. Loop impedance, RCD operation and prospective short-circuit measurements all rely on the supply being live.

questions.prompt: The IEE Regulations require where relevant, the first test on a completed installation to be:
questions.explanation: Continuity of protective conductors is verified first because the safety of all later dead tests and the integrity of the earthing system depend on a proven low-resistance path to earth. Confirming this connection underpins the protective measures relied upon throughout the rest of the sequence.

questions.prompt: Which of the following need NOT be carried out in the visual inspection of the installation?

options.A: Correct connection of socket outlets and lamp holders
options.C: The correct connection of the supply authorities fuse

questions.explanation: The distributor's cut-out and fuse remain the property and responsibility of the supply authority, so the inspector must not work on or verify them. Conductor identification, correct accessory connections and fire barriers all fall within the installation and are properly subject to visual inspection.

questions.prompt: It is a requirement of the Regulations that a Schedule of Test Results should always be attached to an Electrical Installation Certificate for:

options.A: All initial verification of new circuits

questions.explanation: An Electrical Installation Certificate must always be accompanied by schedules of inspection and test results recording the measured values for every new circuit. This documentation provides the evidence that initial verification was carried out and that the installation meets the required standards before being placed into service.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a requirement of the Periodic Inspection and Test Report?

options.A: The form should be accompanied by a Schedule of test Results
options.B: The form should be sent to the originator of the request for the Periodic Inspection and Test
options.C: The form should be signed by the engineer of the Regional Electricity Company (REC)
options.D: The form should be signed by the person carrying out the Inspection and Test

questions.explanation: A condition report is completed and signed by the competent person who actually carried out the inspection and testing, not by a distributor's engineer who has no involvement in the work. Their signature certifies the findings and assigns professional responsibility for the assessment made.

questions.prompt: When carrying out a detailed inspection, which one of the following must be verified? a) presence of fire barriers
questions.explanation: Presence of fire barriers is confirmed by detailed visual inspection, since sealing of openings where wiring passes through fire-rated walls and floors cannot be measured electrically. Loop impedance, prospective fault current and RCD operation are established by instrument tests rather than inspection.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following does NOT influence the frequency of periodic inspection and testing of an installation?

options.A: Any external influence to which it is subjected
options.B: Formal qualification of the Inspection and Test staff

questions.explanation: Frequency of periodic inspection is set by the nature of the installation, the external influences acting on it and how well it is maintained, since these govern how quickly its condition can deteriorate. The qualifications of inspecting staff do not change how often reassessment is needed.

questions.prompt: When testing a three phase and neutral installation for insulation resistance to earth using a 1000 V insulation resistance tester, with all live conductors connected together, the minimum insulation resistance should not be less than:
questions.explanation: For circuits operating up to 500 volts, including ordinary low-voltage three-phase systems, the minimum acceptable insulation resistance measured at 500 volts d.c. is 1 megohm. A lower reading suggests deteriorated insulation or moisture ingress that could allow dangerous leakage currents to flow.

questions.prompt: For an initial verification of an electrical installation, which test would be carried out first?
questions.explanation: Earth continuity is checked first because every subsequent test and the protection afforded against electric shock depend on a sound, continuous protective conductor path. Establishing this connection before energising confirms that exposed metalwork can be safely cleared of fault current.

questions.prompt: The minimum value of insulation resistance between live conductors of an SELV circuit is:
questions.explanation: SELV and PELV circuits operate at very low voltages, so their integrity is verified using a 250 volt d.c. test, and the minimum acceptable insulation resistance is 0.5 megohm. This lower threshold reflects the reduced test voltage applied to these extra-low-voltage separated systems.

questions.prompt: Given the following numbered tests, select the sequence in which the first four tests should be conducted for a new installation: Functional Insulation Resistance Polarity Continuity of Ring Final Conductors Continuity of Protective Conductors
questions.explanation: Dead tests follow a defined order so that each builds on a proven foundation: protective conductor continuity, then ring final continuity, then insulation resistance, then polarity, before any energised checks. This corresponds to the sequence five, four, two, three of the listed items.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for an inspection of an electrical installation?

options.B: Complies with the requirements for portable appliance testing
options.C: Correctly selected and erected in accordance with BS 7671
options.D: Not visibly damaged or defective so as to impair safety

questions.explanation: Portable appliance testing concerns the in-service maintenance of plug-in equipment under separate arrangements, not the fixed installation. Inspection requires confirming correct selection and erection to BS 7671, compliance with the labelling and identification rules, and that equipment is undamaged and safe.

questions.prompt: Statement 1 - a polarity test is carried out with an insulation resistance tester Statement 2 - a polarity test will confirm that the screw thread of an Edison screw lamp holder is connected to the neutral of the supply

options.C: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
options.D: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false

questions.explanation: Polarity is verified using a continuity test, not an insulation resistance tester, so statement one is false. Confirming correct polarity does prove that the outer screw thread of an Edison screw lampholder connects to the neutral rather than the line conductor, making statement two true.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following tests would be conducted to verify protection by electrical separation of SELV circuits?

options.B: A penetration test using a 1mm diameter wire to IP4X
options.C: A withstand voltage of at least 2kV rms
options.D: An insulation resistance test at 250 V d.c

questions.explanation: Electrical separation of SELV circuits relies on the separated wiring being electrically isolated from other systems and earth. This is confirmed by an insulation resistance test applied at 250 volts d.c., which proves the separation is intact and no unintended connection exists to higher-voltage circuits.

questions.prompt: The minimum insulation resistance value between live conductors on a 230 V lighting circuit is:
questions.explanation: A 230 volt lighting circuit falls within the low-voltage range tested at 500 volts d.c., for which the minimum acceptable insulation resistance is 1 megohm. Readings below this indicate degraded insulation that could permit leakage currents and compromise the safety of the circuit.

questions.prompt: Which of the following items of information is NOT required by the person carrying out an inspection and test on an installation:

options.A: The maximum demand after diversity has been applied
options.B: The maximum demand before diversity has been applied
options.C: The method selected to prevent danger from shock in the event of an earth fault
options.D: The type of earthing arrangement employed

questions.explanation: Maximum demand is only meaningful after diversity has been applied, since that reflects the realistic load the installation will carry. The inspector also needs the earthing arrangement and the protective measures against shock, but the pre-diversity figure serves no practical verification purpose.

questions.prompt: Of the following, which is NOT an item of information to be made available to the person conducting the inspection and test of a new installation?

options.A: The location of the Regional Electricity Company's supply transformer
options.B: The maximum demand after diversity has been applied

questions.explanation: The inspector needs the supply characteristics that affect verification, namely nominal voltage and frequency, the earthing arrangement and the maximum demand after diversity. The physical location of the distributor's transformer has no bearing on inspecting and testing the installation and is not required information.

questions.prompt: With reference to the degree of protection of enclosures used in swimming pools where water jets are likely to be used for cleaning purposes, the index of protection must be to:
questions.explanation: Where water jets are used for cleaning in swimming pool locations, enclosures must resist that ingress, so a minimum of IPX5 protection against jetting water is required. Lower ratings would not withstand directed jets and could allow water to reach live parts.

questions.prompt: When under floor heating is provided in a swimming pool area, the electric heating unit embedded in the floor shall incorporate a metallic sheath connected to:

options.B: The main earthing terminal of the installation

questions.explanation: In a swimming pool location, all extraneous and exposed conductive parts within the zones must be tied together by local supplementary bonding to limit touch voltages. The metallic sheath of a floor heating unit is therefore connected to this supplementary equipotential bonding rather than directly back to the main earthing terminal.

questions.prompt: In a touring caravan, instructions must be provided which include information relating to:

options.C: The position of any gas appliances
options.D: The use of obstacles to provide basic protection

questions.explanation: A caravan is connected and disconnected by lay users at successive pitches, so the fixed installation requires durable instructions left in place. These must include a description of the installation so the occupier understands its make-up, ratings and how to use it safely without specialist knowledge.

questions.prompt: In the absence of manufacturers' guidance, a radiant heater used in the vicinity of livestock should be placed at a distance not less than:
questions.explanation: Radiant heaters in agricultural and horticultural premises produce concentrated heat that can ignite bedding, dust or the animals themselves if mounted too close. Where the manufacturer gives no figure, a minimum clearance of 0.5 m from livestock and combustible material is applied to reduce fire and burn risk.

questions.prompt: Where socket outlets are used in a caravan park, each socket-outlet forming part of the caravan pitch supply equipment shall be individually:

options.B: Protected by a 30 mA RCD and be provided with an individual overcurrent protection
options.C: Protected by an overcurrent device and be mounted no more than 0.5m from the ground

questions.explanation: Caravan pitch supplies serve outdoor equipment connected by flexible leads, giving a high risk of electric shock from damaged cables. Each socket-outlet must therefore have individual overcurrent protection and be protected by its own 30 mA RCD so a fault on one pitch does not affect others and disconnects fast enough to prevent fatal shock.

questions.prompt: In agricultural premises, final circuits supplying socket-outlets with a rating not exceeding 32 A must be protected by an RCD with a residual operating current not exceeding:
questions.explanation: Wet conditions and the lowered body resistance of people and animals in agricultural premises make additional shock protection essential. Socket-outlet circuits rated up to 32 A must therefore be protected by a 30 mA RCD, the level recognised as providing protection against fatal electric shock.

questions.prompt: All structural metal parts of a caravan that are accessible from within the caravan must be:

options.A: Bonded to the nearest accessory earthing terminal
options.B: Connected to the main earthing terminal within the caravan

questions.explanation: A caravan body forms a metal enclosure where a fault could otherwise leave structural metalwork live at touch. Connecting all accessible structural metal parts to the caravan's main earthing terminal ensures any fault current is carried safely to earth and protective devices operate, keeping exposed metal at earth potential.

questions.prompt: On a dairy farm, the particular requirements of section 705 within the IEE Regulations do NOT apply to:
questions.explanation: Section 705 addresses the harsh, wet and livestock-related risks specific to agricultural and horticultural production areas. Staff dwellings on a farm are ordinary domestic premises covered by the general requirements, so the special agricultural rules do not extend to them.

questions.prompt: A domestic consumer decides to install a shower cubicle in a room. Any socket outlets within the room shall be:

options.B: Fixed no more than 0.5 m from the floor
options.D: Situated at least 3 m from the edge of Zone 1

questions.explanation: A room containing a shower is treated like a bathroom location with defined zones around the water source. Socket-outlets must be kept at least 3 m horizontally from the boundary of zone 1, placing them well clear of splashing and wet hands to reduce the risk of shock.

questions.prompt: Every plug and socket outlet rated at 16 A for use on a construction site, shall comply with:
questions.explanation: Construction sites demand robust, weatherproof connections with defined keyway and voltage-band arrangements that ordinary domestic plugs cannot provide. Industrial plugs and socket-outlets to BS EN 60309-2 are therefore specified, giving mechanical strength, ingress protection and colour-coded voltage identification suited to site conditions.

questions.prompt: In an area where there is vehicle movement on a caravan park, the minimum height for overhead cables is:
questions.explanation: Overhead conductors on a caravan park must be high enough to clear tall vehicles, towed caravans and manoeuvring traffic. A minimum height of 6 m is required in areas subject to vehicle movement so cables cannot be struck or pulled down, whereas a lower clearance suffices only where no vehicles pass.

questions.prompt: The maximum permissible height for a caravan inlet is:
questions.explanation: The caravan inlet must sit where a user can reach it to connect the supply lead but high enough to stay clear of ground splashing and damage. A maximum mounting height of 1.8 m balances accessibility for connection with protection of the inlet from the wet ground.

questions.prompt: Where an electric heating element is embedded in the floor of a bathroom it should be:

options.A: Buried to a depth not less than 50 mm
options.B: Covered by an earthed metal grid which is connected to the protective conductor

questions.explanation: A heating element buried in a bathroom floor could energise the floor surface if its insulation failed, creating a shock risk to bare wet feet. Covering it with an earthed metal grid connected to the protective conductor provides supplementary protection, carrying fault current to earth and triggering disconnection.

questions.prompt: In Zone 1 of a swimming pool installation where a circuit is supplied by SELV, the voltage must not exceed:
questions.explanation: Within the immediate pool zone, wet skin and immersion drastically reduce body resistance, so even low voltages are dangerous. SELV is therefore limited to 25 V a.c. in zones 0 and 1, a reduced threshold recognising the greatly increased shock risk in and around the water.

questions.prompt: In a building containing a swimming pool, junction boxes may be installed in:
questions.explanation: Zones 0 and 1 of a pool are the wettest, most hazardous areas where enclosures and connections are tightly restricted. Junction boxes are only permitted in zone 2, where the lower water exposure makes accessory installation acceptable provided the appropriate ingress protection is met.

questions.prompt: In a swimming pool which of the following protective measures is NOT applicable to equipment installed in Zone 2

options.A: Automatic disconnection of supply using an RCD in accordance with Regulation 415.1.1
options.B: Electrical separation supplying one item of equipment

questions.explanation: Protection by obstacles and placing out of reach rely on people behaving carefully and are not accepted in swimming pool locations because wet, barefoot users cannot be relied upon to avoid live parts. Measures such as SELV, electrical separation or automatic disconnection by RCD are required instead.

questions.prompt: The minimum degree of protection for equipment inside a sauna must be:
questions.explanation: Inside a sauna, equipment is exposed to steam, water splashing and condensation rather than fine solid ingress. A minimum rating of IPX4 ensures enclosures resist splashing water from any direction, protecting against moisture penetration in the humid heat-cabin environment.

questions.prompt: Temporary electrical installations used for exhibitions shall be:

options.A: Inspected and tested on site after each assembly
options.B: Supplied at a voltage not exceeding 250 V
options.D: Wired using copper cable having a cross-sectional area not less than 2.5 mm2

questions.explanation: Exhibition, show and stand installations are repeatedly dismantled, transported and reassembled, so their integrity cannot be assumed from one event to the next. They must be inspected and tested on site after each assembly to confirm the wiring, connections and protective measures remain safe before energising.

questions.prompt: Section 704 deals specifically with temporary installations for construction and demolition sites during the period of construction or demolition and includes:
questions.explanation: Section 704 covers the temporary supplies used while construction or demolition work is actually in progress, including activities such as earthworks. Permanent welfare facilities like offices, canteens and toilets are ordinary installations outside its scope once they are no longer part of the temporary construction supply.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 includes requirements for

options.B: Circuits operating at voltages exceeding 1000 V deriving from installations not exceeding 1000V A.C

questions.explanation: The scope of BS 7671 reaches circuits operating above 1000 V where they are derived from a low-voltage installation not exceeding 1000 V AC, such as discharge lighting. The supply side governs whether such higher-voltage circuits fall within the Regulations.

questions.prompt: BS 7671:2018 applies to

options.A: Electric fences covered by BS EN 60335-2-76
options.C: Lightning protection of buildings covered by BS 6651
options.D: Onshore units of electrical shore connections for inland navigation vessels

questions.explanation: Although lift, electric fence and lightning protection installations have their own dedicated standards and sit outside the Regulations, the onshore units of shore connections for inland navigation vessels are expressly brought within scope. They are treated as fixed electrical installations on land.

questions.prompt: Which of the following voltages are not within the scope of BS 7671:2018
questions.explanation: The Regulations apply up to 1000 V AC and 1500 V DC, covering extra-low and low voltage installations. A nominal 1500 V AC supply exceeds the AC upper limit and therefore lies outside the voltage range to which the standard applies.

questions.prompt: Switching off electrical loads for variable periods to optimise demand is known as
questions.explanation: Load shedding deliberately disconnects selected loads for variable periods to keep total demand within the available capacity or to reduce peak consumption. It manages demand directly rather than simply measuring or improving the efficiency of energy use.

questions.prompt: Installations should be arranged so as to avoid danger and minimise inconvenience in the event of a fault and facilitate safe operation, inspection, testing and maintenance. One method of complying with this is to

options.A: Connect all circuits on the radial principle
options.B: Divide the installation into lighting and power
options.C: Divide the installation into separate circuits
options.D: Fit an RCD at the main intake position

questions.explanation: Dividing an installation into separate circuits limits the consequences of a single fault, since only the affected circuit loses supply while others continue. It also allows individual circuits to be isolated for safe inspection, testing and maintenance without shutting the whole installation down.

questions.prompt: A component of a support system consisting of regularly spaced elements which mechanically retains a cable is defined as a cable
questions.explanation: A cleat is defined as a support component made of regularly spaced elements that mechanically retain a cable. Unlike a continuous tray or ladder, it grips the cable at intervals to hold it firmly in position along its route.

questions.prompt: Measures reducing the effect of electromagnetic interferences shall be given consideration by
questions.explanation: Reducing electromagnetic interference depends on decisions about segregation, cable routing, screening and earthing that are made when the installation is planned. These belong to the designer, who selects measures appropriate to the equipment and environment before erection begins.

questions.prompt: When considering the frequency of maintaining installed electrical equipment, which of the following is not an essential requirement

options.B: Protective measures for safety remain effective
options.C: Regular periodic inspection and testing shall be carried out
options.D: The nature of current and frequency

questions.explanation: Effective maintenance requires that protective measures stay effective, that periodic inspection and testing is carried out, and that adequate light and access are available. The nature of the current and its frequency is a design characteristic of the supply, not a factor governing maintenance frequency.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a measure of 'fault protection'
questions.explanation: Fault protection guards against contact with parts made live by a fault, using methods such as automatic disconnection, Class II construction or protective equipotential bonding. A metal consumer-unit enclosure addresses fire containment, not protection against electric shock under fault conditions.

questions.prompt: Protection against transient overvoltages need not be provided where the consequence caused by overvoltage could

options.B: Result in interruption of commercial activity
options.C: Result in loss of human life

questions.explanation: Protection against transient overvoltage may be omitted only where the consequences of an overvoltage are tolerable, such as causing no interruption to public services. Where overvoltage could result in loss of life, serious injury or disruption of commercial activity, protection must be provided.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct

options.A: Each electrical installation shall have provisions for isolation from each supply
options.B: In TN-C-S systems the PEN conductor may be isolated or switched
options.C: In TN-S and TN-C-S systems the switching of the neutral conductor is always required
options.D: Where residual electrical energy is potentially present, suitable means need not be provided for its discharge

questions.explanation: Every installation must have provision to be isolated from each of its supplies so it can be made safe for work. A PEN conductor must never be isolated or switched, and means to discharge stored energy must always be provided where it could be present.

questions.prompt: In an IT system, where touch voltage is limited to 50V, what is the maximum resistance of the earth electrode and protective conductor for exposed conductive parts when the fault current is 200A
questions.explanation: The earth-fault loop resistance must hold the touch voltage at or below 50 V for the prospective fault current. With 50 V limited at 200 A, the permitted resistance is 50 divided by 200, giving 0.25 ohms.

questions.prompt: The requirements for both basic and fault protection can be provided by SELV. One suitable source of SELV would be a
questions.explanation: A SELV source must supply a voltage not exceeding 50 V AC and be electrically separated from higher-voltage circuits and from earth. A 50 V storage battery meets these requirements, providing both basic and fault protection without a connection to a hazardous supply.

questions.prompt: The prospective short circuit current at the origin of the consumer's installation must be taken into account when

options.A: Assessing the methods to be used to provide basic protection
options.B: Assessing the value of the external earth loop impedance
options.C: Selecting the number of ways required for the main distribution board
options.D: Selecting the type of main overcurrent protective device to be installed

questions.explanation: Protective devices must be able to safely interrupt the largest current that could flow under fault conditions. The prospective short-circuit current at the origin therefore determines the breaking capacity, and hence the type, of the main overcurrent protective device.

questions.prompt: When protecting against burns a metallic part intended to be touched but not hand held shall be limited to a maximum temperature of
questions.explanation: To prevent burns, an accessible metallic part intended to be touched but not hand-held is limited to 70 degrees Celsius. The lower limit reflects that brief incidental contact can still scald skin even where the part is not gripped continuously.

questions.prompt: RCDs have to are required to have the button marked 'T' or 'Test' pressed for mechanical operation every
questions.explanation: The test button verifies the mechanical tripping mechanism of an RCD and should be operated about every six months. Regular operation confirms the device will still disconnect on a residual fault, since a seized mechanism would otherwise go undetected.

questions.prompt: A protective conductor shall not pass through a RCD

options.B: Except where unavoidable and in the reverse direction
options.C: Except where unavoidable and passed through in both directions

questions.explanation: An RCD works by detecting the imbalance between line and neutral currents, so a protective conductor passing through it would distort that balance and cause nuisance tripping. Where routing it through is unavoidable, it must pass in both directions so its current cancels.

questions.prompt: A Type 2 SPDs is installed in a single phase CT2 system and connected between L-N. Its nominal discharge current (Inspd) shall be not less than
questions.explanation: For a Type 2 surge protective device connected between line and neutral, the nominal discharge current must be at least 5 kA. This rating ensures the device can repeatedly divert the expected surge energy to earth without failing.

questions.prompt: In a TN system with a line conductor of 25mm2 the required size of the earthing conductor, shall be
questions.explanation: Where the earthing conductor is copper and unprotected against corrosion but protected mechanically, its size relates to the line conductor through Table 54.7. For a 25mm2 line conductor the earthing conductor must be at least half that, so 16mm2 is the smallest acceptable cross-section.

questions.prompt: In the formula S = √If2t/k the symbol 'k' represents

options.A: A factor applied to conductor materials
options.B: The amplitude of the fault current
options.C: The minimum size of the cpc
options.D: The time the fault current exists

questions.explanation: In the adiabatic equation S equals the square root of (I squared t) divided by k, the factor k accounts for the conductor material and its insulation, reflecting how much heat the conductor can absorb before reaching its limiting temperature. Copper and aluminium therefore have different k values.

questions.prompt: A cable installed under a floor or above a ceiling, without mechanical protection, should be run at least

options.A: 100 mm from the top or bottom of the joist or batten
options.B: 25 mm from the top or bottom of the joist or batten
options.C: 30 mm from the top or bottom of the joist or batten
options.D: 50 mm from the top or bottom of the joist or batten

questions.explanation: Cables run through or near joists without mechanical protection must be kept at least 50mm from any surface where nails or screws might be driven in. This safe distance reduces the risk of a fixing penetrating the cable and creating a live or damaged conductor.

questions.prompt: If a main protective bonding conductor cannot be connected to the gas service pipe close to the meter because the meter is external to the building the bond should be connected

options.A: At the point of entry to the building
options.B: Before the point of entry to the building
options.D: Within two meters of the gas meter

questions.explanation: Main protective bonding to a gas installation must be made to the consumer's hard metal pipework, as near as practicable to the point of entry. Where the meter sits outside, the connection is made where the pipe enters the building, ensuring the bond covers the installation it protects.

questions.prompt: Which of the following devices may be used for emergency switching
questions.explanation: A device for emergency switching must be capable of interrupting full load current in a single action and be readily operable. A circuit breaker meets this, whereas plugs, semiconductor devices and luminaire connectors are unsuitable for reliably breaking load under emergency conditions.

questions.prompt: Initial verification of an installation shall be made by

options.B: Inspection and testing person qualified to C&G 2391
options.D: Skilled person(s) competent in such work

questions.explanation: Inspection and testing carries real risk and demands sound technical judgement, so the Regulations require it to be undertaken by skilled persons competent in such work. Competence here means the knowledge, experience and ability to recognise hazards, not merely holding a particular qualification.

questions.prompt: Measuring instruments should be in accordance with
questions.explanation: Rewireable semi-enclosed fuses are manufactured to BS 3036, which sets out the construction and performance of that type of protective device. Measuring instruments and their performance are instead governed by the BS EN 61557 series, so this pairing is the one tied to BS 3036.

questions.prompt: When completing an Electrical Installation Certificate which of the following can only be ascertained by enquiry or measurement
questions.explanation: The earthing arrangement of the supply cannot simply be read from a label and must be established by enquiry to the distributor or by direct measurement and inspection. Other supply characteristics such as the protective device rating can usually be determined by observation alone.

questions.prompt: On a construction site a final circuit supplying a socket-outlet with a rated current not exceeding 32A when protected by an RCD the rated residual operating current not greater than
questions.explanation: Construction sites are harsh environments with damp conditions and heavy use of portable equipment, raising the shock risk. Socket-outlet circuits rated up to 32A must therefore have additional protection by an RCD with a residual operating current not exceeding 30mA.

questions.prompt: Zone 1 extends horizontally from the side of a bath for a distance of
questions.explanation: In a location containing a bath, zone 1 is the volume above the rim, but where the dimensions are defined it extends only a limited distance horizontally from the bath edge. That horizontal limit is 0.6m, beyond which the less onerous zone 2 requirements apply.

questions.prompt: In agricultural premises, an r.c.d. may be used for protection against fire providing the operating current does NOT exceed
questions.explanation: In agricultural and horticultural premises the elevated fire risk means RCD protection is required, but a device intended to guard against fire need not be as sensitive as one for shock protection. A residual operating current up to 300mA is permitted for fire protection here.

questions.prompt: A 230V circuit is protected by a 50A Type B circuit-breaker to BS EN 6089The minimum value of fault current to ensure compliance with maximum disconnection times is
questions.explanation: A Type B breaker is designed to trip magnetically at around five times its rated current for fast disconnection. For a 50A device that threshold is roughly 250A, so the fault current must reach at least this value to guarantee the required disconnection time.

questions.prompt: Multicore cables on a perforated tray are designated reference method
questions.explanation: Reference methods describe how a cable is installed for current-carrying purposes. Multicore cables supported on a perforated cable tray fall under reference method E, which recognises the good air circulation around the cable and so allows a higher rated current than enclosed methods.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 includes requirements for

options.B: Circuits operating at voltages exceeding 1000 V deriving from installations not exceeding 1000V A.C

questions.explanation: The scope of the Regulations covers low voltage installations but also extends to circuits operating above 1000V where they are derived from an installation not exceeding 1000V AC, such as discharge lighting. High-voltage distribution and lightning protection systems fall outside this scope.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following types of installations is NOT within the statutory control of an authoritative body
questions.explanation: Many premises such as petrol stations, theatres and caravan sites are subject to licensing or statutory oversight by an authoritative body. Ordinary domestic dwellings are not controlled in that way, relying instead on Building Regulations and BS 7671 for electrical safety.

questions.prompt: Open circuit voltage is represented by the symbol
questions.explanation: Standard symbols keep terminology consistent across the Regulations. Open-circuit voltage, the voltage present when no load current flows, is denoted Uoc, distinguishing it from the nominal line-to-earth voltage Uo used in shock-protection calculations.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not an example of an 'Earth fault'

options.A: A loose earth clamp connecting a protective earth bonding conductor to a water pipe
options.D: Low phase to earth fault current failing to operate the circuit protective device

questions.explanation: An earth fault is a fault between a live conductor and earth or an exposed-conductive-part, such as a poor bonding connection or insufficient fault current to operate the protective device. A short circuit occurs between live conductors, so it is not classed as an earth fault.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 requires designers to take into account the frequency and quality of maintenance an installation can reasonably be expected to receive when
questions.explanation: Designers must consider how much maintenance an installation will realistically receive, because equipment that may be poorly maintained needs to be more robust and reliable. This judgement directly informs the selection and reliability specification of the equipment used.

questions.prompt: The compatibility of harmful effects upon electrical equipment would not need to be assessed for
questions.explanation: Compatibility under BS 7671 considers external influences that one item of equipment can impose on another, such as earth leakage currents, harmonics and transient overvoltages or undervoltages. Low-frequency oscillations are not among the disturbances listed for this assessment, so they need not be evaluated.

questions.prompt: Referring to protection against fire caused by electrical equipment, if used, an AFDD shall be placed

options.A: At the origin of all final circuits
options.B: At the origin of the circuit to be protected
options.C: At the origin of the installation

questions.explanation: An arc fault detection device must protect the specific final circuit it serves, so it is installed at the origin of that circuit to monitor the conductors throughout their length. Placing it elsewhere, such as the installation origin, would leave individual circuits unmonitored for series and parallel arcing faults.

questions.prompt: In an IT system which of the following can be used as a monitoring device:
questions.explanation: In an IT system the first fault may not be cleared automatically, so continuous insulation monitoring is required to give warning. Residual current monitors detect leakage and signal a developing fault, whereas overcurrent devices and RCDs are protective rather than monitoring devices.

questions.prompt: Where the circuit protective conductor is not a metal cable covering or metal trunking and conduit, the c.p.c for a ring final circuit must

options.B: Be run in the form of a ring having both ends connected to the earthing terminal
options.D: Have a cross-sectional area equal to that of the live conductors of the ring

questions.explanation: A ring final circuit's protective conductor must itself form a continuous ring with both ends terminated at the earthing terminal, mirroring the live conductors. This guarantees two parallel earth paths so that a single break does not leave any socket without an effective connection to earth.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum temperature for an accessible metallic part of equipment not intended to be touched during normal operation
questions.explanation: To prevent burns from accessible metalwork not intended to be handled, BS 7671 limits its surface temperature under normal load. Eighty degrees Celsius is the ceiling for accessible metallic parts, keeping incidental contact below the threshold at which injury occurs.

questions.prompt: A horizontal top surface of a barrier or enclosure which is readily accessible shall provide a degree of protection of at least
questions.explanation: Readily accessible horizontal top surfaces collect dust and debris and invite objects being placed on them, so they need greater ingress protection than vertical faces. A minimum of IP5X guards against harmful dust ingress that could otherwise compromise the barrier or enclosure.

questions.prompt: Which of the following devices gives additional protection against contact with live parts but must not be relied upon for basic protection
questions.explanation: An RCD provides additional protection by disconnecting quickly on earth leakage, limiting the duration of shock if basic and fault protection fail. It is a backup only and must not be the sole means of basic protection, which relies on insulation, barriers or enclosures.

questions.prompt: In the event of a fault the likely result due to the circuit earth loop impedance being higher than allowed in BS 7671 is

options.A: A short-circuit current will not operate the protective device
options.B: The cable may be damaged before the protective device operates under fault conditions
options.C: The protective device will be damaged due to high fault currents
options.D: The protective device will have to be replaced

questions.explanation: If earth fault loop impedance exceeds the permitted value, fault current is too low to operate the protective device within the required disconnection time. The conductors then carry that fault current for too long, so the cable may be thermally damaged before the device clears the fault.

questions.prompt: A PEN conductor shall be marked by which one of the following methods

options.A: Alternating green yellow and blue throughout its length
options.C: Blue throughout its length, with green-and-yellow at the terminations

questions.explanation: A PEN conductor combines neutral and protective functions, so it is identified blue along its length to show the neutral role, with green-and-yellow at the terminations to indicate the protective function. This dual marking warns that the conductor carries both duties.

questions.prompt: When selecting an RCD for general purposes the Type that may be used is
questions.explanation: A Type AC device responds to alternating residual currents and suits general-purpose circuits supplying ordinary resistive and inductive loads. Where electronic equipment can produce smooth DC or higher-frequency leakage, a Type A, F or B would instead be specified to detect those waveforms.

questions.prompt: Which of the following may not be used as an earth electrode

options.A: A metal object immersed in water
options.B: Lead sheath of cables in effective contact with earth
options.C: Underground structural metalwork embedded in foundations

questions.explanation: Earth electrodes must give a stable, reliable connection to the general mass of earth. A metal object merely immersed in water is not accepted because water levels and conditions vary, so it cannot guarantee a dependable low-resistance earth path.

questions.prompt: In the formula Zs = Ze + (R1 + R2) what does R2 signify

options.C: Resistance of the main earth conductor

questions.explanation: In the loop impedance expression, Ze is the external impedance, R1 is the line conductor resistance and R2 is the resistance of the circuit protective conductor. Adding R1 and R2 to Ze gives the total earth fault loop impedance Zs for the circuit.

questions.prompt: Where cables at different voltage Bands are to be run in the same trunking or assembly which of the following is not permitted

options.A: All cables at different voltage bands must be effectively segregated
options.B: All cables must be insulated to Band I standards
options.C: All non-segregated cables must be insulated to the highest voltage present
options.D: Each conductor of a multicore cable is insulated for the highest voltage present in the cable

questions.explanation: Where different voltage bands share an enclosure, every cable must be insulated for the highest voltage present, or the circuits must be effectively segregated. Insulating all cables only to Band I standards is not permitted because lower-rated insulation cannot safely withstand the higher band's voltage.

questions.prompt: A means of isolation may be installed remote from the equipment if:

options.A: It is fitted with non-interchangeable keys
options.B: It is hand operated and a visual display is activated near the equipment
options.C: It is in full view of people working on the equipment
options.D: The isolator can be secured in the open position

questions.explanation: A remote isolator is acceptable only if it cannot be inadvertently reclosed while someone works downstream. Securing it in the open position, for example by locking off, ensures the supply stays disconnected even though the device is out of sight of the equipment.

questions.prompt: When cables are placed directly in the ground (other than a special location) they should be buried at a depth
questions.explanation: Cables laid directly in the ground must be deep enough to avoid normal disturbance and mechanical damage from digging or surface activity. A burial depth of at least one metre, with marker tape or covers, provides this protection in ordinary locations.

questions.prompt: A factory requires repairs to a machine. The type of switching to allow this work to go ahead would be switching for
questions.explanation: Switching off for mechanical maintenance is provided so that non-electrical work such as repairing or cleaning a machine can proceed safely. It disconnects the supply to prevent the equipment starting or moving while a person works on its mechanical parts.

questions.prompt: Which of the following persons is not responsible signing an Electrical Installation Certificate
questions.explanation: An Electrical Installation Certificate carries declarations for design, construction, and inspection and testing, signed by the persons responsible for those duties. The person ordering the work is the recipient, not a signatory, so they do not sign the certificate itself.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect

options.A: Inspection and test schedules must accompany all periodic inspection reports
options.B: Periodic inspection and testing must be carried out by an accredited electrician
options.C: Previous inspection and test results must be taken into account, if available, during a current inspection and test
options.D: The extent and results of periodic inspection and tests must be recorded

questions.explanation: Periodic inspection and testing must be carried out by a skilled, competent person, but BS 7671 does not require formal accreditation as an electrician. The other statements correctly reflect that schedules, previous results and the extent and findings must all be recorded.

questions.prompt: Defects or omissions identified during an initial verification should be

options.A: Corrected before the certificate is issued
options.C: Noted on the certificate, and the client should be informed
options.D: Pointed out to the designer when the certificate has been completed

questions.explanation: Initial verification confirms an installation is safe for use, so any defect or omission found during inspection and testing must be put right before certification. Issuing a certificate over uncorrected faults would wrongly declare the work compliant and fit for service.

questions.prompt: Cables in cultivated ground shall be buried to a depth of at least:
questions.explanation: Cultivated or regularly disturbed ground is likely to be ploughed or dug, so buried cables need extra cover to protect them from mechanical damage. A minimum depth of one metre keeps them clear of normal cultivation activity and reduces the risk of penetration.

questions.prompt: In a room containing a sauna, all equipment in Zone 3 shall withstand a minimum temperature of
questions.explanation: Zone 3 of a sauna is the highest region where air temperatures climb significantly during operation. Equipment installed there must be rated to withstand at least 125 degrees Celsius so that insulation and enclosures do not degrade or fail in the elevated heat.

questions.prompt: A PV convertor shall have a switch-disconnector provided on

options.A: Both the A.C. and D.C. sides
options.B: Neither the A.C. nor the D.C. sides

questions.explanation: Photovoltaic arrays remain live in daylight and cannot simply be switched off, so the d.c. side of the inverter requires a switch-disconnector to allow safe isolation. This lets the converter be separated from the generating modules for maintenance and fault work.

questions.prompt: In medical locations socket-outlets intended to supply ME equipment shall be
questions.explanation: Socket-outlets feeding medical electrical equipment must be unswitched to prevent the supply being accidentally interrupted during a procedure. Removing the local switch ensures life-supporting or monitoring equipment is not inadvertently disconnected by someone operating the outlet.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the strongly preferred system for portable hand lamps in confined locations
questions.explanation: Confined conducting locations greatly increase shock severity because contact with surrounding metalwork is hard to avoid. Separated extra-low voltage is strongly preferred for portable handlamps because it has no earth reference and a low voltage, minimising the danger if a fault or contact occurs.

questions.prompt: BS 5266 relates to
questions.explanation: BS 5266 is the British Standard covering the application and installation of emergency lighting in premises. It sets out how escape routes and key areas are illuminated when the normal supply fails so that occupants can leave safely.

questions.prompt: BS7671 relates to electrical installations in and around buildings but excludes:
questions.explanation: BS 7671 applies to electrical installations in and around buildings but specifically excludes equipment on board ships, which is governed by separate marine standards. Other specialist installations such as mines and traction systems are likewise outside its scope.

questions.prompt: Parts 3 to 7 of BS 7671 covers in detail methods and practices which meets the requirements of:
questions.explanation: Chapter 13 sets out the fundamental principles for safety, and the detailed methods in Parts 3 to 7 are the practical means of meeting those objectives. Following the later parts is therefore deemed to satisfy the fundamental requirements stated in Chapter 13.

questions.prompt: The IEE Regulations recognises that in electrical installations there is a risk of injury from:
questions.explanation: The Regulations are concerned principally with electrical dangers, and the foremost of these is the risk of injury from shock currents passing through the body. Protective measures throughout the standard are aimed at limiting the chance and severity of such currents.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following types of installations is NOT within the statutory control of an authoritative body?
questions.explanation: Special premises such as petrol stations, theatres and caravan sites are subject to additional statutory licensing or authority control because of their particular hazards. Ordinary domestic installations carry no such statutory licensing body, relying instead on the general regulatory framework.

questions.prompt: The type of building construction in which an installation is to be carried out may affect the design and safe operation of the installation. This effect is called:
questions.explanation: The nature of a building's construction is treated as a condition imposed on the installation from outside the electrical system itself. Such factors are classified as external influences, which the designer must assess so that equipment selection and erection suit the surroundings.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not classed as a Band 1 voltage circuit?
questions.explanation: Band I covers extra-low voltage and signalling circuits where protection against shock relies on the low voltage value, such as SELV, bell and 25 V signalling circuits. A 230 V lighting circuit is a normal low-voltage supply and therefore falls into Band II.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following external influences requires an increase in the current ratings of cables above those normally required?
questions.explanation: A conductor's current-carrying capacity is set by how readily it can shed heat to its surroundings. In high ambient temperatures less heat is dissipated, so a derating factor is applied that effectively requires a larger or more highly rated cable than under standard conditions.

questions.prompt: One of the general categories of external influences is:
questions.explanation: External influences are grouped into broad categories, of which environment is one, alongside utilisation and building construction. The environmental category covers conditions such as temperature, water, dust and corrosion that the installation must be designed to withstand.

questions.prompt: Where the circuit protective conductor is not a metal cable covering or metal trunking and conduit, the c.p.c for a ring final circuit must:

options.B: Be run in the form of a ring having both ends connected to the earthing terminal
options.D: Have a cross-sectional area not less than that of the live conductors of the ring

questions.explanation: On a ring final circuit every conductor, including the circuit protective conductor, is run as a continuous loop with both ends terminated at the earthing terminal. This ring arrangement preserves earth continuity even if one leg is broken, maintaining the protective path.

questions.prompt: A TN-C-S system has:

options.A: A separate protective conductor connecting the source earth to the consumers main earth terminal
options.B: The exposed conductive parts of an installation connected to an earth electrode which is independent to the source
options.C: The neutral and earth functions combined in a single conductor in part of the system
options.D: The neutral and protective conductors are combined throughout the system

questions.explanation: In a TN-C-S system the neutral and protective functions share a single combined conductor for part of the supply, typically the distributor's network, before separating into distinct neutral and earth conductors within the installation. This combined section is the defining PME feature.

questions.prompt: Installations should be arranged so as to avoid danger and minimise inconvenience in the event of a fault and facilitate safe operation, inspection, testing and maintenance. One method of complying with this is to:

options.A: Connect all circuits on the radial principle
options.B: Divide the installation into lighting and power
options.C: Divide the installation into separate circuits
options.D: Fit an RCD at the main intake position

questions.explanation: Dividing an installation into separate circuits limits the consequences of a fault to one circuit, allows other parts to stay in service, and lets work be carried out on isolated sections. This reduces danger and inconvenience while making inspection, testing and maintenance safer.

questions.prompt: The prospective short circuit current at the origin of the consumer's installation must be taken into account when:

options.A: Assessing the methods to be used to provide basic protection
options.B: Assessing the value of the external earth loop impedance
options.C: Selecting the number of ways required for the main distribution board
options.D: Selecting the type of overcurrent protective device to be installed

questions.explanation: The prospective short-circuit current sets the maximum fault energy a device may have to interrupt, so the protective device must have a breaking capacity at least equal to it. This governs the choice of overcurrent device so it can clear a fault safely without rupturing or welding closed.

questions.prompt: A two-storey domestic dwelling should have a minimum of two lighting circuits in order to:

options.A: Avoid danger in the event of a fault
options.B: Enable a greater variety of luminaires to be used
options.C: Reduce the load on the consumer unit
options.D: Use 10 A circuit breakers for the lighting circuits

questions.explanation: Splitting the lighting across two circuits means a single fault or tripped protective device cannot plunge the whole dwelling into darkness. Retaining some lighting avoids the danger of people being left unable to see stairs or exits, which is the reason division of an installation is required.

questions.prompt: With reference to the general characteristics of an electrical installation, the maximum demand should be:
questions.explanation: Connected loads rarely all operate simultaneously at full rating, so maximum demand is assessed by applying allowances for diversity rather than simply summing every load. This realistic figure avoids oversizing cables and switchgear while still ensuring the supply and protective devices are adequately rated.

questions.prompt: The requirements for both basic and fault protection can be provided by SELV. One suitable source of SELV would be a:
questions.explanation: SELV requires a safety source that is electrically separated from earth and from higher-voltage circuits, with no live part exceeding the extra-low-voltage band. A storage battery operating at 50 V provides this independent, isolated source, whereas generators and auto-transformers retain a connection to or derivation from the mains supply.

questions.prompt: Residual current circuit breakers shall NOT be used on a TN system where a circuit incorporates:
questions.explanation: A PEN conductor combines neutral and protective functions in one conductor, so residual current devices cannot work correctly because the return current would not flow back through the device to balance it. RCDs must therefore be positioned where the protective and neutral functions are already separated.

questions.prompt: A component of a support system consisting of regularly spaced elements which mechanically retains a cable is defined as a cable:
questions.explanation: A cleat is defined as a support component made of regularly spaced elements that mechanically grips and retains a cable along its run. Unlike a tray or ladder that carries cables continuously, a cleat clamps the cable at intervals to fix its position.

questions.prompt: SELV can be used as a means to meet the requirements of both basic and fault protection. In such cases the nominal voltage must not exceed:
questions.explanation: SELV sits within the extra-low-voltage band, and where it provides both basic and fault protection without further measures the nominal voltage must not exceed 50 V ac. Above this level the touch voltage could become dangerous, so additional protective provisions would otherwise be required.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following classifications of external influences would be appropriate for an item of electrical equipment installed where it would be subject to an atmosphere where heavy dust is present?
questions.explanation: External influences are classified by category and severity, and the presence of dust falls under the AE code for the presence of foreign solid bodies. Heavy dust represents a high severity within that category, so AE6 is the appropriate classification for selecting suitably enclosed equipment.

questions.prompt: The fault current due to an earth fault of negligible impedance in a 400 V, three phase, four wire circuit having an earth loop impedance of 0.3 ohms, is:
questions.explanation: In a four-wire circuit an earth fault is driven by the phase voltage to earth, not the line-to-line value, so the 230 V phase voltage is divided by the loop impedance. Dividing 230 V by 0.3 ohms gives approximately 767 A as the fault current.

questions.prompt: A section of a factory requires urgent repairs to a machine. The type of switching provided to allow this work to proceed would be switching for:
questions.explanation: Repairing or servicing a machine requires the supply to be cut and held off so the equipment cannot start unexpectedly while a person works on it. This is switching off for mechanical maintenance, which protects against danger from movement of the machinery rather than from electric shock alone.

questions.prompt: The correct classifications of an external influence consisting of light dust is:
questions.explanation: The presence of dust is graded within the AE classification of external influences according to severity. Light dust corresponds to the lower AE4 grade, distinguishing it from moderate or heavy dust conditions that demand more heavily protected enclosures.

questions.prompt: Lz is the current rating of a circuit conductor. The requirements for overload current protection are fulfilled when:
questions.explanation: Overload protection is satisfied when the design current does not exceed the device rating, and the device rating does not exceed the conductor's current-carrying capacity. With 9 A design current, a 15 A device and 17 A conductor capacity, both conditions hold so the conductor is properly protected.

questions.prompt: Where the overcurrent device is intended to afford protection against overload, l2 must NOT exceed lz times:
questions.explanation: The current ensuring effective operation of the protective device, I2, must not exceed 1.45 times the conductor's current-carrying capacity. This limit keeps the conductor within a temperature it can tolerate for the short time before the device operates, preventing damage to insulation under sustained overload.

questions.prompt: A fault current caused by the line and neutral conductors to come in contact with each other is referred to as:
questions.explanation: A short-circuit fault is the contact between live conductors, such as line and neutral, that are normally at different potentials when the circuit is sound. The very low impedance of this path produces a large fault current that the protective device must rapidly clear.

questions.prompt: A 230 V single-phase circuit supplying a pump motor is protected by a 20 A circuit breaker to BS EN 60898 type B. The minimum value of fault current to ensure compliance with thermal and shock constraints is:
questions.explanation: A type B device to BS EN 60898 operates instantaneously at five times its rated current, so a 20 A device needs at least 100 A of fault current to trip in the required time. Reaching this magnetic threshold ensures disconnection fast enough to satisfy thermal and shock-protection limits.

questions.prompt: Where a means of isolation is provided in an electrical installation, the means must be:
questions.explanation: An isolating device must be clearly identifiable so that anyone can confirm which installation or circuit it controls before working on it. Durable labelling prevents the wrong device being operated and ensures the intended part is actually made dead, supporting safe isolation.

questions.prompt: Overload current is an overcurrent occurring in a circuit:
questions.explanation: Overload current arises in a circuit that is electrically sound with no fault between conductors; the overcurrent results from too much connected load rather than a short-circuit or earth fault. Distinguishing this is important because overload protection allows a longer disconnection time than fault protection.

questions.prompt: The designer/installer of a ceiling heating system must provide a plan for the installation. Information NOT required on the plan would be the:

options.C: Number of rooms within the installation

questions.explanation: The installation plan for a ceiling heating system must record technical details needed for safe operation and inspection, such as the position of junction boxes, the number of heating units and the leakage capacitance. The count of rooms is not safety-relevant information and is therefore not required.

questions.prompt: When 13 A socket outlets are wired from a fused spur using 70o thermoplastic insulated cable with copper conductors, the minimum conductor size permissible is:
questions.explanation: A fused spur is protected by a 13 A fuse in the spur unit, so the cable beyond it only has to carry that limited current. A 1.5 mm2 copper conductor has ample current-carrying capacity for a 13 A maximum, making it the smallest size permitted for socket outlets fed this way.

questions.prompt: The correction factor for a cable surrounded by thermal insulation for a length of 200 mm is:
questions.explanation: Where a cable runs through thermal insulation over a short length, heat cannot dissipate freely and the rating must be derated. For a length of about 200 mm the de-rating factor settles at 0.63, reflecting the reduced ability to shed heat over that span of enclosure.

questions.prompt: When selecting a cable for a single circuit installation, correction factors are to be used and applied to the:

options.C: Nominal current of the protective device
options.D: Total current taken by the installation

questions.explanation: Correction factors for grouping, ambient temperature and insulation reduce how much current a cable may safely carry, so they are applied to the protective device rating to find the minimum tabulated capacity needed. Dividing the nominal device current by the factors gives the required current-carrying capacity before selecting the cable size.

questions.prompt: Where protection against overload is provided by a semi-enclosed fuse to BS 3036, the current rating of the cable must be at least:

options.A: 0.725 times the current rating of the fuse
options.B: 0.725 times the design current of the circuit
options.C: The nominal current rating of the fuse divided by 0.725
options.D: The same rating as the design current of the circuit

questions.explanation: Semi-enclosed rewireable fuses to BS 3036 have an imprecise fusing factor and may not operate until well above their rated current. Applying the 0.725 factor, the cable's current-carrying capacity must be at least the nominal fuse rating divided by 0.725 so the conductor is not overloaded before the fuse clears.

questions.prompt: 3Correct co-ordination between conductors and overcurrent protection device is achieved when:

options.B: Ln exceeds the lowest current carrying capacity lz
options.C: Ln is not less than the design current lb
options.D: The current causing effective operation (l2) exceeds 1.45 l2

questions.explanation: Co-ordination requires the device rating In to be at least the design current Ib, so the protection does not nuisance-trip on the intended load. This first condition of the overload rules ensures the device sits above the circuit demand while still protecting the conductor below it.

questions.prompt: In order to calculate the minimum value of the cross-sectional area of a protective conductor the following information is available Fault current = 300 A Operating time of the protective device = 0.6 s Constant k, for protective conductor material = 115 The minimum, cross-sectional area of the protective conductor should be:
questions.explanation: The adiabatic equation gives S equal to the square root of I squared times t, divided by k. With 300 A, 0.6 s and k of 115, this yields roughly 2 mm2, so the next standard conductor of 2.5 mm2 is the minimum size that withstands the fault energy.

questions.prompt: The rating factor to be applied for eight equally loaded circuits grouped together in conduit is:
questions.explanation: Grouping several loaded circuits together in a single conduit traps heat, so each cable's rating must be reduced. For eight enclosed circuits bunched in conduit the tabulated grouping factor is 0.52, accounting for the mutual heating that limits safe current-carrying capacity.

questions.prompt: A circuit is protected by a 10 A BS 3036 semi-enclosed (rewireable) fuse. The minimum permissible current rating (lz) of a conductor protected by this fuse would be:
questions.explanation: Because a BS 3036 fuse may not blow until well above its rating, the protected conductor must carry at least the fuse rating divided by 0.725. For a 10 A fuse this gives 10 divided by 0.725, which equals about 13.8 A as the minimum required current-carrying capacity.

questions.prompt: An office installation is connected to a TT system and earth fault protection is provided by a residual current device. The product of the rated residual operating current of the device and the earth electrode resistance plus the protective conductor's resistance connecting it to the exposed conductive parts shall not exceed:
questions.explanation: On a TT system the RCD plus earth electrode must limit the touch voltage on exposed metalwork to a safe level. The rated residual operating current multiplied by the earth loop resistance must not exceed 50 V, the conventional limit above which prolonged contact becomes dangerous.

questions.prompt: A circuit is connected to a TN system, the maximum permissible earth fault loop impedance (Zs) for a 32 A socket outlet circuit protected by a BS 88 fuse is:
questions.explanation: Maximum earth fault loop impedance ensures the protective device disconnects within the required time when a fault occurs. For a 32 A socket circuit protected by a BS 88 fuse on a TN system, the tabulated limit needed to meet that disconnection time is 1.04 ohms.

questions.prompt: Regulation 434.5.2 gives the maximum time which may be permitted for a fault to be maintained without damaging the conductors. Assume a prospective fault current of 1000 A with a copper 25 mm2 cable with 70℃ thermoplastic insulation. The clearance time (t) is:
questions.explanation: The maximum withstand time follows from the adiabatic relationship t equals k squared times S squared divided by I squared. For a 25 mm2 copper cable with k of 115 carrying 1000 A, this gives about 8.2 s before the insulation reaches its limiting temperature.

questions.prompt: The purpose of having equipotential bonding conductors connected to the other services as close as practicable to their entry into the premises is to:

options.A: Ensure that earth leakage is minimised
options.B: Ensure that the maximum current will flow to earth under fault conditions
options.C: Reduce the chance of electrolytic corrosion between metal sheath of cable and metal pipes
options.D: Reduce the chance of shock risk within the premises

questions.explanation: Main bonding ties incoming metallic services to the main earthing terminal near their entry, keeping all exposed and extraneous metalwork close to the same potential. This limits the voltage that could appear between simultaneously accessible parts during a fault, reducing the shock risk to anyone inside the premises.

questions.prompt: Where practicable main equipotential bonding to the gas services in a building should be made:

options.B: Within 6 m of the meter on the supply side
options.C: Within 600 mm of the meter on the consumer's side
options.D: Within 600 mm of the meter on the supply side

questions.explanation: Main bonding to the gas installation must connect to the consumer's pipework so the bond stays effective regardless of any non-conductive sections in the supply. It is made within 600 mm of the meter outlet on the consumer's side, before any branch or tee, to bond the metalwork entering the building.

questions.prompt: Heating cables laid directly in soil, roads or building structures must be installed so that they are:

options.A: At least 1 m below the surface
options.B: Completely embedded in the substance which they are intended to heat
options.C: Fed only from an extra-low voltage supply

questions.explanation: Soil and floor heating cables rely on the surrounding material to absorb and dissipate the heat they produce. They must be fully embedded in the substance they are intended to heat so they cannot overheat, since air pockets or exposed runs would let the cable reach excessive temperatures.

questions.prompt: For circuits of TN or TT systems, the outer contact of Edison type screw lamp holders must be connected to the:
questions.explanation: On TN or TT systems the outer screw thread of an Edison-type lampholder is the part most readily touched when changing a lamp. Connecting that outer contact to the neutral keeps the accessible thread at near-earth potential, so it is not live while the centre contact carries the line conductor.

questions.prompt: The temperature limit for non-metallic equipment which is intended to be touched but not hand held is:
questions.explanation: Accessible parts have temperature limits set to prevent burns from prolonged contact. For non-metallic surfaces intended to be touched but not gripped during normal use, the limit is 80 degrees, higher than for metal because non-metals transfer heat to the skin more slowly.

questions.prompt: The correct grouping factor for 6 circuits of three conductors per circuit, run in the same conduit is:
questions.explanation: Several circuits sharing one conduit heat each other, so their ratings are reduced by a grouping factor. For six bunched circuits enclosed in the same conduit the tabulated factor is 0.57, reflecting the mutual heating from that number of loaded cables in close proximity.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following does NOT determine the frequency of periodic inspection and testing of an installation?

options.A: Any external influence to which it is subjected
options.B: Formal qualifications of the inspection and test staff

questions.explanation: The interval between periodic inspections is set by the installation's type, the external influences it faces, and how frequently it is maintained, since these affect how quickly its condition can deteriorate.
