The qualifications of the inspecting staff are a competence matter and have no bearing on the assessed frequency.

questions.prompt: Every new installation on completion and before being energised must FIRST be:

options.A: Given a test for insulation resistance
options.C: Tested for continuity of protective conductors
options.D: Tested for continuity of ring circuit conductors

questions.explanation: Inspection precedes testing during initial verification. A thorough visual inspection of the de-energised installation confirms correct selection and erection of equipment and identifies obvious defects before any voltage is applied, so it is carried out first to avoid energising a dangerous installation.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following items should be included for checking during the initial verification of an installation?

options.C: Presence of all diagrams and instructions

questions.explanation: Initial verification confirms that the information needed to operate and maintain the installation safely is present. Diagrams, charts and instructions describing the circuits, protective devices and isolation arrangements must be available, as inspectors and future users rely on them rather than on contractual or site-management paperwork.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following British Standards covers residual current devices?
questions.explanation: BS EN 61008 is the product standard for residual current operated circuit-breakers without integral overcurrent protection (RCCBs). The other standards cover transformers, circuit-breakers for overcurrent and low-voltage switchgear, so RCDs of the RCCB type are specified to this standard.

questions.prompt: For an insulation resistance test on a 230 V ac installation containing surge protected socket-outlets, the value of the test voltage may be:
questions.explanation: Where surge protective devices or sensitive electronic equipment are present, applying the usual 500 V dc test could damage them. The test voltage is therefore reduced to 250 V dc, with the SPDs disconnected or the lower voltage used, so the insulation is still checked without harming the protection.

questions.prompt: When a 30 mA residual current device used to provide additional protection is tested at a residual current of 150 mA, the device should open in no more than:
questions.explanation: Where an RCD provides additional protection, testing at five times its rated residual current must cause it to trip within 40 ms. At 150 mA, which is five times 30 mA, this fast disconnection limits the duration of any shock current to a value the human body can tolerate.

questions.prompt: The minimum value of insulation resistance when measured at the consumer unit of a 230 V domestic installation is:
questions.explanation: For circuits operating up to 500 V, including a 230 V installation, the insulation resistance measured at 500 V dc must be at least 1.0 megohm. This minimum confirms that leakage between live conductors and earth is low enough to prevent dangerous currents and nuisance tripping.

questions.prompt: The results of periodic inspection and testing should be recorded on a report and signed by the:

options.B: Person carrying out the inspection and test

questions.explanation: The competent person who actually performed the inspection and testing must sign the report, taking responsibility for the recorded condition and results. This accountability ensures the assessment reflects work genuinely carried out, rather than being authorised by someone who did not observe the installation firsthand.

questions.prompt: Equipment fitted in Zone 1 of a bathroom must:

options.A: Be fed from a plug and socket outlet
options.B: Be rated at a voltage not exceeding 12 V
options.C: Have a minimum IP rating of IPX4
options.D: Have a minimum IP rating of IPX5

questions.explanation: Zone 1 of a bathroom is directly exposed to water spray and splashing around the bath or shower, so equipment there must withstand water ingress. A minimum protection rating of IPX4 ensures enclosures resist splashing water from any direction, reducing the risk of electric shock in wet conditions.

questions.prompt: In agricultural premises, an RCD may be used for protection against fire providing the operating current does not exceed:
questions.explanation: Agricultural premises carry a heightened fire risk from dust, livestock and combustible materials, so RCDs are used for fire protection. A device with a rated operating current not exceeding 300 mA disconnects earth fault currents before they can ignite materials, giving protection against fire rather than shock.

questions.prompt: For all caravans using a mains electricity supply, an instruction notice must be fixed:

options.A: At or near the main distribution point
options.B: Near the main electrical isolating switch inside the caravan
options.C: On the inside of the main door of the caravan
options.D: Under the cover of the caravan electricity inlet box

questions.explanation: A caravan's electrical supply can be connected and disconnected frequently and incorrectly, so users need clear guidance. An instruction notice positioned near the main isolating switch inside the caravan ensures the connection and disconnection procedure is read where the supply is controlled, helping prevent unsafe use.

questions.prompt: In a swimming pool which of the following protective measures is NOT applicable to equipment installed in Zone 2?

options.B: Protection by an RCD in accordance with Regulation 415.1.1
options.C: Protection by earth free local equipotential bonding

questions.explanation: In a swimming pool, earth-free local equipotential bonding is not permitted in Zone 2 because the wet conductive environment makes it impractical and unsafe. SELV, electrical separation and RCD protection are the recognised measures, since they limit voltage or rapidly disconnect supply where people are immersed.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following may be installed inside Zone 1 of a hot air sauna?

options.A: A ceiling mounted cord operated light switch
options.C: A thermostat attached to the side of the sauna

questions.explanation: Inside a sauna only equipment able to withstand the extreme heat may be installed, and that is essentially the sauna's own control gear. A thermostat mounted on the sauna is designed for these temperatures, whereas switches, shaver sockets and general fittings cannot tolerate the conditions in the hottest zone.

questions.prompt: With regards to a transportable unit, a notice fixed in a prominent position on the unit need not display:
questions.explanation: A transportable unit's notice warns users about safe connection to differing supplies, so it must state the supply type, voltage rating and maximum power demand. The supply frequency is not required, as it does not affect the safe connection and isolation information the user needs at the unit.

questions.prompt: Characteristics of available supplies does not include

options.B: Equipment conforming to safety in compliance with BS 7671

questions.explanation: The characteristics of available supplies describe what the incoming source provides, such as the type of supply, maximum demand permitted and prospective fault current. Equipment complying with BS 7671 relates to the installation's own design and selection, not to the inherent characteristics of the supply itself.

questions.prompt: The IET Wiring Regulations provide
questions.explanation: BS 7671 is a non-statutory standard giving guidance on good practice for the design and erection of installations. Compliance is widely accepted as meeting the relevant legal duties, but the Regulations themselves are not law and do not set out specifications, drawings or statutes.

questions.prompt: The letters SCPD represent
questions.explanation: SCPD stands for short-circuit protective device, the protective device whose function is to interrupt the high currents arising from a short circuit. Identifying it as a device, rather than a current or voltage, reflects its role in safely clearing fault currents before damage occurs.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 defines extra-low voltage A.C. as not exceeding
questions.explanation: Extra-low voltage is the band not exceeding 50 V ac or 120 V dc between conductors or to earth. These limits define the voltage threshold below which reduced shock-protection requirements apply, distinguishing ELV systems such as SELV and PELV from low-voltage installations.

questions.prompt: Newly installed equipment must be compatible with existing equipment. Which of the following is not listed under 'Compatibility' as likely to have a harmful effect upon other electrical equipment
questions.explanation: Compatibility requires that new equipment does not adversely affect other equipment or the supply through effects such as DC feedback, leakage current, harmonics and unbalanced loads. Environmental considerations concern external conditions acting on the equipment, not a harmful effect the equipment imposes on other apparatus.

questions.prompt: BS7671 prohibits installation circuit arrangements where

options.B: The complete installation is protected by a RCD

questions.explanation: A borrowed neutral takes the return path from a different circuit's neutral, so that neutral can stay live even when the borrowing circuit is isolated. This defeats safe isolation and overloads the shared neutral, which is why the arrangement is prohibited.

questions.prompt: Protection by obstacles or placing out of reach shall be restricted to
questions.explanation: Obstacles and placing out of reach only guard against unintentional contact, not deliberate touching, so they cannot be relied upon by ordinary users. They are permitted only in areas under the control of skilled or instructed persons who understand the residual risk.

questions.prompt: In a reduced low voltage system (Uo = 55V single-phase) where the disconnection time is 5s, what is the maximum Zs where the protection device is a 20A type B circuit breaker
questions.explanation: Maximum Zs is found by dividing the nominal voltage to earth by the device's tripping current. For a 20A type B breaker, Ia is five times rating, so 55V divided by roughly 100A gives about 0.52 ohms for disconnection within the required time.

questions.prompt: What is the required minimum impulse withstand voltage for Category III equipment with a nominal voltage of 277/480V
questions.explanation: Rated impulse withstand voltage is selected from the overvoltage category and the system's nominal voltage band. Category III equipment within the 277/480V band must withstand a 4.0 kV impulse to survive the transient overvoltages expected at that point in a fixed installation.

questions.prompt: The characteristics of the protective devices and circuit impedances shall fulfil

options.D: Zs x Ia ≤ Uo x Cmin

questions.explanation: For automatic disconnection, the earth fault loop must let enough current flow to operate the device within the required time. The condition Zs multiplied by Ia must not exceed Uo times Cmin, where Cmin accounts for the worst-case low supply voltage.

questions.prompt: SELV can be used as a means to meet the requirements of both basic and fault protection. The nominal voltage must not exceed
questions.explanation: SELV relies on a safely separated low-voltage source so that contact with live parts is not dangerous, removing the need for disconnection. The upper limit of 50V a.c. is the conventional touch-voltage threshold below which shock risk is acceptably low under dry conditions.

questions.prompt: One method of basic protection is
questions.explanation: Basic protection prevents contact with parts that are live in normal service, and insulating those live parts physically encloses them. Equipotential bonding, automatic disconnection and RCDs are fault-protection measures, acting only after a fault has already occurred.

questions.prompt: Wiring systems shall be supported such that premature collapse in the event of fire. One example of an acceptable single support system is
questions.explanation: Supports must not fail before the cable in a fire, otherwise dropped wiring can hamper escape and firefighting. Metallic fixings such as copper clips retain their grip when plastics soften and melt, so they qualify as suitable fire-resistant support.

questions.prompt: Normally devices for the protection against overload and fault currents should be placed where there is a reduction in the csa of a conductor. However, the protection device may be placed after the csa reduction up to a distance of not more than
questions.explanation: A protective device is normally placed exactly where conductor size reduces, but a short unprotected length is tolerated if it is installed to minimise fault risk. That length must not exceed 3.0m so any fault is cleared before the smaller conductor is damaged.

questions.prompt: The minimum required Uc of a SPD connected between line conductors in a TN system is
questions.explanation: A surge protective device must keep withstanding the system voltage continuously without conducting, so its maximum continuous operating voltage Uc is set above the nominal line voltage. In a TN system between line conductors this minimum is 1.1 times U to allow for normal voltage variation.

questions.prompt: A warning notice must be fixed at or near the point of connection of earthing conductors to earth electrodes bearing the words

options.C: Safety Electrical Connection - Do Not Remove
options.D: Safety Electrical Earth - Do Not Remove

questions.explanation: Earthing and bonding connections are vital safety links whose removal could leave exposed metalwork dangerous, yet they may look insignificant. A durable label reading 'Safety Electrical Connection - Do Not Remove' warns anyone working nearby not to disconnect them.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not normally be recognised as being a supply source for safety services

options.A: A generator supplying power, via the grid, to a hospital
options.B: A separate feeder of the supply network effectively independent of the normal feeder

questions.explanation: A safety-services source must remain available when the normal supply fails, so it must be independent of that supply. A generator feeding through the grid depends entirely on the public network and therefore cannot guarantee power during a mains failure.

questions.prompt: When selecting electrical equipment consideration need not be given to
questions.explanation: Equipment must be selected so it suits the actual supply and conditions, meaning voltage, frequency, current and compatibility all directly affect safe operation. Documentation is part of recording the installation, not a characteristic the equipment itself must be chosen against.

questions.prompt: When the line conductor of a TN system is 25mm2 and the earthing conductor is 16 mm2 the main protective bonding conductor must have a minimum cross-sectional area of at least
questions.explanation: Main protective bonding conductors are sized in relation to the supply neutral, generally at least half its cross-sectional area subject to a minimum. For a 25mm2 line conductor in a TN system this gives a required 10mm2 bonding conductor.

questions.prompt: As a means of isolation in a circuit it is NOT permissible to use a
questions.explanation: Isolation must provide a reliable, secure break in the supply that can be proven open and held safely. A semiconductor switch only interrupts current electronically and can fail to a conducting state, so it cannot be trusted to give true isolation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect

options.A: For a fixed installation flexible conductors of csa less than 10mm2 may serve as a PEN conductor
options.B: No means of switching shall be inserted in the outer conductor of a concentric cable
options.C: The use of PEN conductors is permitted within an installation where authorisation has been obtained
options.D: The use of PEN conductors is permitted within an installation where the supply is obtained from a private generating plant

questions.explanation: A PEN conductor combines neutral and protective functions, so a broken conductor would leave exposed metalwork live, demanding a robust fixed conductor. Flexible conductors below 10mm2 are too easily damaged for this duty, making that statement the incorrect one.

questions.prompt: On Electrical Certificates which of the following box(s) should be ticked within the section titled 'Number and Type of Live Conductors' when dealing with a normal domestic single-phase installation
questions.explanation: The certificate records the actual supply characteristics, and a standard domestic installation is alternating current fed by a single line and neutral. The correct entries are therefore AC together with 1-phase, 2-wire to describe that arrangement accurately.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not required to be inspected

options.A: Correct connection of accessories and equipment
options.B: Installation of suitable SPDs, where required

questions.explanation: Inspection checks the physical installation against the safety requirements, covering correct connections, presence of notices and devices such as SPDs. The installer's personal qualifications are a competence matter, not a feature of the installation that inspection assesses.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect

options.A: A 'condition report inspection schedule' and 'schedule of test results' must accompany an electrical installation condition report
options.B: An electrical installation condition report has classification codes C1, C2, C3 and FI
options.C: An electrical installation condition report must be completed by a fully qualified electrician
options.D: Where possible, results from previous inspection and testing must be taken into account during the completion of an electrical installation condition report

questions.explanation: A condition report only requires a competent person, not a particular trade title; the inspector must have the necessary knowledge, experience and skill for the work. There is no rule restricting completion to a 'fully qualified electrician', so that statement is the incorrect one.

questions.prompt: Which of the following methods of 'fault protection' is allowed in highway power supplies and equipment
questions.explanation: Part 7 restricts highway power supplies and street furniture to automatic disconnection of supply as the fault-protection measure. Earth-free bonding, non-conducting locations and placing out of reach rely on supervision and are not permitted in such publicly accessible installations.

questions.prompt: In which Zones, if any, can heated towel-rails be installed in a bathroom

options.B: Three metres from the side of the bath

questions.explanation: Within the bathroom zoning of Section 701, Zone 2 is the region beyond the immediate splash area of the bath or shower. A heated towel rail of suitable rating and IP protection may be fixed there, whereas Zones 0 and 1 demand stricter limits.

questions.prompt: Construction site special regulations apply to
questions.explanation: Section 704 applies to the actual construction and demolition work, including earthworks, where the increased risk of mechanical damage and reduced body resistance exists. Permanent site canteens, offices and toilets are treated as ordinary installations under the general regulations, not the special construction-site rules.

questions.prompt: When a converter is installed as part of a photovoltaic power supply system an isolation device is

options.B: Required on both the A.C. and the D.C. sides

questions.explanation: For photovoltaic systems an isolating device must be provided on both the a.c. and d.c. sides of the converter, because the d.c. array remains live in daylight and cannot simply be switched off. Isolation on both sides allows the inverter to be safely worked on.

questions.prompt: 2What is the recommended maximum area covered by a radial final socket circuit protected by a 20A protection device
questions.explanation: Appendix 15 recommends that a 20A radial socket circuit serves a floor area of up to about 50 square metres. The limit reflects the diversified load and voltage drop that the protective device and cable can reasonably support over that area.

questions.prompt: The rating factor (Ca) at an ambient air temperature of 45℃ applied to 70℃ PVC cable is
questions.explanation: The ambient temperature correction factor Ca for 70 degree thermoplastic insulation falls below unity once the air exceeds the 30 degree reference. At 45 degrees the rating must be reduced to roughly 0.79 so the conductor does not exceed its permitted operating temperature.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 does not set out

options.A: Electrical Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations
options.B: Rules for the design of electrical installations
options.C: Rules for the verification of electrical installations
options.D: Technical requirements enabling electrical installations to conform to Chapter 13

questions.explanation: BS 7671 provides technical requirements for design, erection and verification so installations meet the fundamental principles of Chapter 13. It does not itself enact statutory rules such as the Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations, which are separate legislation, so that option is what it does not set out.

questions.prompt: Which of the following frequencies are not within the scope of BS 7671
questions.explanation: The scope of BS 7671 covers installations operating at nominal frequencies of 50Hz, 60Hz and 400Hz. A frequency of 100Hz falls outside those stated values and is therefore not within the standard's scope.

questions.prompt: Extra-low voltage is within voltage band
questions.explanation: The voltage bands defined in BS 7671 place extra-low voltage, which does not exceed 50V a.c. or 120V ripple-free d.c., within Band I. Band II covers the higher voltages such as normal 230V supplies used for general fixed wiring.

questions.prompt: Fire detection systems, fire alarm systems, smoke extraction and heat extraction systems are examples of
questions.explanation: A safety service is an electrical system intended to protect or warn persons in the event of a hazard, or essential to their evacuation. Fire detection, alarm, smoke and heat extraction systems all fall within that definition because they support life safety during an emergency.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not a characteristic of the supply

options.A: The nature of the current and frequency
options.B: The rating of final circuit protective devices
options.C: The rating of the overcurrent protective device at the origin
options.D: The Ze external to the installation

questions.explanation: The characteristics of the supply that must be determined relate to what the distributor provides, such as the nature of current and frequency, the origin device rating and the external earth fault loop impedance Ze. The rating of final circuit protective devices is decided by the installation designer, not a supply characteristic.

questions.prompt: Continuity of service requires which of the following characteristics to be considered
questions.explanation: Continuity of service is achieved by dividing the installation into a suitable number of circuits so that a fault or maintenance on one does not interrupt the others. Considering the number of circuits limits the consequences of any single failure and aids fault location.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect

options.A: AC final circuits supplying luminaires must be protected by a RCD not exceeding 30mA
options.B: Metallic pipes entering a building having an insulating section at the point of entry need not be connected to the protective equipotential bonding
options.C: No switching device may be inserted in a PEN conductor
options.D: The maximum disconnection times stated in Table 41.1 do not apply to final circuits rated at 32A supplying only fixed connected current using equipment

questions.explanation: Table 41.1 disconnection times do apply to final circuits up to 63A supplying socket outlets or up to 32A supplying fixed equipment; the longer times of Table 41.1 only relax for distribution circuits. Stating they do not apply to a 32A fixed-equipment circuit is therefore incorrect.

questions.prompt: Residual current circuit breakers shall NOT be used on a TN system where a circuit incorporates

options.C: PEN conductors on the load side

questions.explanation: An RCD relies on detecting the imbalance between line and neutral currents. If a PEN conductor exists on the load side, neutral current can return through the earthed PEN and bypass the device, so combining the line and PEN functions downstream defeats residual current operation.

questions.prompt: The maximum earth fault loop impedance (Zs), within BS 7671:2018, using a 16A Type B circuit breaker will be
questions.explanation: For a Type B device the magnetic trip needs five times its rated current, so a 16A breaker must clear at about 80A. Dividing the touch voltage by that current, with the standard adjustment for conductor warming, gives a maximum Zs of around 2.73 ohms.

questions.prompt: When sizing and selecting cables which of the following formulae is correct
questions.explanation: Correct coordination requires the design current to be no greater than the device rating, which in turn must not exceed the cable's current-carrying capacity, expressed as Ib less than or equal to In less than or equal to Iz. This ensures the cable is protected against overload by its device.

questions.prompt: Cables in escape routes must achieve a level of light transmittance of at least
questions.explanation: Cables installed in escape routes must allow adequate visibility during an emergency, so wiring systems there are required to achieve a light transmittance of at least 60 percent. This helps maintain the effectiveness of escape lighting if smoke or obscuration occurs.

questions.prompt: Which of the following items does not offer 'basic' protection

options.B: A live part placed out of reach

questions.explanation: Basic protection guards against contact with parts that are normally live, using insulation, barriers, enclosures or placing out of reach. A bare lampholder leaves live terminals accessible once a lamp is removed, so on its own it provides no inherent protection against direct contact.

questions.prompt: In a TN-C-S earthing system the 'T' has which of the following meanings

options.B: Direct electrical connection of exposed-conductive-parts to earth
options.C: One point connected to earth through a high impedance
options.D: The direct connection of one point to earth

questions.explanation: In earthing system codes the letter 'T' stands for the French 'terre', denoting a direct connection of one point to earth. For the supply side this means the source neutral or star point is bonded directly to the general mass of earth rather than through any impedance.

questions.prompt: In order to avoid unwanted tripping of a RCD but the accumulation of earth leakage currents downstream of the RCD shall not be more than

options.A: 10% of the rated residual operating current
options.B: 20% of the rated residual operating current
options.C: 30% of the rated residual operating current
options.D: 50% of the rated residual operating current

questions.explanation: To prevent nuisance tripping, the steady earth leakage current present downstream should be limited so the residual device is not held near its operating threshold. Keeping accumulated leakage below 30% of the rated residual operating current leaves adequate margin against unwanted disconnection while preserving fault sensitivity.

questions.prompt: Which of the following shall not be used for the termination of lighting points to the fixed wiring system

options.A: A batten lampholder complying with BS EN 60598
options.C: A connection unit complying with BS 1363-4
options.D: An installation coupler complying with BS EN 61535

questions.explanation: Ceiling roses are restricted to one outgoing flexible cord and are not designed for multiple or high-loading lighting arrangements, and BS 444 is a withdrawn standard. Termination of lighting points should use current devices such as lampholders, connection units or installation couplers manufactured to in-force standards.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not allowed regarding switching devices in protective conductors

options.A: A switching device interlocked with multipole linked switching device with the protective conductor interrupted last
options.C: Multipole linked switching with the protective conductor interrupted after the live conductors
options.D: Single pole switching in the protective conductor

questions.explanation: A protective conductor must remain continuous so that exposed-conductive-parts stay reliably earthed at all times. Single-pole switching in the protective conductor could break the earth path while the circuit stays live, leaving metalwork dangerous, so it is prohibited except in the tightly controlled cases permitted for special circumstances.

questions.prompt: A symbol showing an upside down triangle with the number 110 inside it represents

options.D: The temperature rating of a thermally protected ballast

questions.explanation: An inverted triangle bearing the number 110 is the marking for an electronic converter used with extra-low-voltage luminaires. It identifies the unit as a converter rather than a wound transformer, informing the installer about the type of supply equipment feeding the fitting.

questions.prompt: Firefighter's switches must be placed at a height no greater than
questions.explanation: Firefighter's emergency switches must be reachable by attending crews, so their mounting position is capped. Placing the switch no higher than 2.75m above the ground or operating surface keeps it accessible for rapid isolation during an emergency while remaining clear of normal interference.

questions.prompt: It must not be possible to alter the overcurrent setting of a device by an ordinary person without

options.C: Use of a key or tool

questions.explanation: Overcurrent protective settings are a safety-critical design value that must not be casually changed. Requiring a key or tool to adjust the setting ensures only skilled or instructed persons can alter it, preventing an ordinary person from inadvertently defeating the intended discrimination or protection.

questions.prompt: What is the k factor of a 90℃ thermosetting aluminium cable where the protective conductor is not incorporated in a cable and not bunched with cables
questions.explanation: The k factor reflects the conductor material and its permitted initial and final temperatures during a fault. For a 90°C thermosetting aluminium protective conductor that is separate, neither incorporated in a cable nor bunched, the applicable adiabatic value is 116, used in the cross-section check S = √(I²t)/k.

questions.prompt: When completing an Electrical Installation Condition Report an 'Unsatisfactory' assessment shall be recorded when which of the following conditions is recorded
questions.explanation: Condition codes rank danger: C1 is danger present, C2 is potentially dangerous, C3 is improvement recommended, and FI means further investigation is required. A C2 indicates a real risk needing urgent remedy, so its presence makes the overall assessment Unsatisfactory.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following tests is carried out after the supply is connected

options.B: Continuity of ring final circuit conductors

questions.explanation: RCD operation is verified by checking that the device disconnects within its required time when a residual current is applied, which needs the installation energised. Dead tests like continuity and insulation resistance are completed first, but functional RCD testing is carried out after the supply is connected.

questions.prompt: An insulation resistance test to be carried out on a 3-phase 500V circuit. The test voltage and minimum acceptable reading would be
questions.explanation: Insulation resistance is measured with a steady d.c. test voltage to stress the insulation without capacitive effects. For a circuit operating up to 500V, a 500V d.c. test is applied and the reading must be at least 1.0 megohm to confirm the insulation is sound.

questions.prompt: Every socket-outlet, in a caravan park, shall be individually protected by an RCD having a rated residual operating current not exceeding
questions.explanation: Caravan parks present wet conditions and outdoor use where earth fault risk is high, so additional protection for personal safety is required. Each socket-outlet must have its own RCD rated at no more than 30mA to give fast disconnection if someone contacts a fault.

questions.prompt: The minimum cross sectional area for a cable carrying up to 25A for caravan connections shall be
questions.explanation: The flexible connecting cable for a caravan must carry the connection current without overheating while withstanding mechanical handling. For loads up to 25A a minimum conductor cross-sectional area of 4mm² provides adequate current capacity and robustness for the repeated coupling and movement involved.

questions.prompt: Floor heating systems shall have a surface temperature of not more than
questions.explanation: Floor heating can be in continuous contact with skin, so excessive surface temperature risks burns and discomfort. Limiting the floor surface to no more than 35°C protects occupants who may stand or sit on it for prolonged periods while still delivering useful warmth.

questions.prompt: Electrical equipment installed in Zone 0 within a bathroom will have a minimum degree of protection to
questions.explanation: Zone 0 is the interior of the bath or shower basin, where equipment can be fully immersed in water. A minimum protection of IPX7 ensures the enclosure withstands the effects of temporary immersion, which is the level of water ingress credibly present in that location.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following protective measures is not applicable to equipment in Zone 2 of a swimming pool

options.B: Protection by an RCD in accordance with Regulation 415.1.1

questions.explanation: Around swimming pools the permitted protective measures are tightly restricted to those reliably effective in wet conditions, such as SELV, electrical separation and RCD protection. Protection by obstacles relies on people behaving carefully and gives no real barrier in this high-risk wet environment, so it is not accepted.

questions.prompt: What is the correction factor for 70℃ pvc cable, in free air, in an ambient temperature of 50℃
questions.explanation: Rated cable current is based on a reference ambient, so hotter surroundings reduce the safe carrying capacity. For 70°C pvc cable in free air at 50°C ambient, the rating factor of 0.71 is applied to derate the tabulated current and avoid the conductor exceeding its permitted temperature.

questions.prompt: When determining current carrying capacity, multicore cable in flush cable trunking in the floor the Reference Method is
questions.explanation: Cables installed in trunking are treated like cables in conduit for heat dissipation, so the standard tables assign Reference Method B to conductors enclosed in trunking. The enclosure restricts air flow around the cable, giving a lower current-carrying capacity than a clipped-direct run.

questions.prompt: Characteristics of available supplies does not include

options.B: Equipment conforming to safety in compliance with BS 7671

questions.explanation: The characteristics of the supply describe what the distributor provides, such as nominal voltage, maximum demand, prospective fault current and earthing arrangements. Equipment conforming to BS 7671 is an outcome of the installation design, not a property of the incoming supply itself.

questions.prompt: The IET Wiring Regulations provide
questions.explanation: BS 7671 is a non-statutory code of practice giving guidance on good installation practice rather than law in its own right. Compliance is generally accepted as meeting the safety duties imposed by legislation such as the Electricity at Work Regulations.

questions.prompt: The letters SCPD represent
questions.explanation: SCPD stands for short-circuit protective device, the device whose duty is to interrupt fault currents safely. Identifying it as a device, rather than a current or voltage value, matters because its breaking capacity and operating characteristic must suit the prospective fault current at that point.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 defines extra-low voltage A.C. as not exceeding
questions.explanation: Extra-low voltage is the band not exceeding 50V a.c. or 120V ripple-free d.c. between conductors or to earth. These thresholds mark the level below which the risk of electric shock is significantly reduced, underpinning protective measures such as SELV and PELV.

questions.prompt: Newly installed equipment must be compatible with existing equipment. Which of the following is not listed under 'Compatibility' as likely to have a harmful effect upon other electrical equipment
questions.explanation: Compatibility addresses electrical effects newly installed equipment may impose on other items, such as d.c. feedback, leakage current and unbalanced loads. Environmental considerations concern external influences acting on the installation rather than interference one piece of equipment causes another.

questions.prompt: BS7671 prohibits installation circuit arrangements where

options.B: The complete installation is protected by a RCD

questions.explanation: A borrowed neutral takes the return current of one circuit through the neutral of another, defeating correct circuit identification and isolation. This arrangement is prohibited because it can leave a conductor live when its own circuit is switched off, creating a serious shock hazard during maintenance.

questions.prompt: Protection by obstacles or placing out of reach shall be restricted to
questions.explanation: Obstacles and placing out of reach only guard against unintentional contact, not deliberate access, so they offer incomplete protection. For this reason they are restricted to locations under the control of skilled persons who understand the residual risk of touching live parts.

questions.prompt: In a reduced low voltage system (Uo = 55V single-phase) where the disconnection time is 5s, what is the maximum Zs where the protection device is a 20A type B circuit breaker
questions.explanation: For a 20A type B circuit breaker, instantaneous operation requires about five times rated current, giving Ia of roughly 100A. Dividing the 55V nominal earth-fault voltage by that current yields a maximum loop impedance of approximately 0.52 ohms to ensure disconnection.

questions.prompt: What is the required minimum impulse withstand voltage for Category III equipment with a nominal voltage of 277/480V
questions.explanation: Impulse withstand voltage is graded by overvoltage category and nominal voltage to ensure equipment survives transient surges. For Category III equipment on a 277/480V system, the required minimum rated impulse withstand voltage is 4.0kV, reflecting the surge stress expected at distribution level.

questions.prompt: The characteristics of the protective devices and circuit impedances shall fulfil

options.D: Zs x Ia ≤ Uo x Cmin

questions.explanation: For automatic disconnection to work, the earth-fault loop impedance must be low enough that fault current reaches the device's operating value within the permitted time. The condition Zs x Ia must not exceed Uo x Cmin, where Cmin accounts for the minimum expected supply voltage.

questions.prompt: SELV can be used as a means to meet the requirements of both basic and fault protection. The nominal voltage must not exceed
questions.explanation: SELV relies on a safe extra-low voltage that cannot give a dangerous shock under both normal and fault conditions. The nominal value must not exceed 50V a.c., the upper limit of the extra-low voltage band, allowing it to provide basic and fault protection together.

questions.prompt: One method of basic protection is
questions.explanation: Basic protection prevents contact with parts that are intended to be live in normal service. Insulating live parts achieves this directly, since insulation can only be removed by destruction, whereas disconnection, bonding and RCDs act as fault protection after a fault has occurred.

questions.prompt: Wiring systems shall be supported such that premature collapse in the event of fire. One example of an acceptable single support system is
questions.explanation: Supports must not allow cables to fall and obstruct escape routes if their fixings fail in a fire. Plastic clips, ties and trunking soften and collapse under heat, so a metallic fixing such as copper clips is needed to keep wiring in place.

questions.prompt: Normally devices for the protection against overload and fault currents should be placed where there is a reduction in the csa of a conductor. However, the protection device may be placed after the csa reduction up to a distance of not more than
questions.explanation: Protective devices should sit at the point where conductor cross-section reduces, but a short unprotected length is tolerated for practical connection. That length must not exceed 3.0m, provided it is installed to minimise the risk of fault and is kept clear of combustible material.

questions.prompt: The minimum required Uc of a SPD connected between line conductors in a TN system is
questions.explanation: A surge protective device must keep withstanding the system voltage continuously without conducting, so its maximum continuous operating voltage Uc must exceed the nominal voltage with margin. In a TN system Uc must be at least 1.1 times the line voltage to allow for normal supply variation.

questions.prompt: A warning notice must be fixed at or near the point of connection of earthing conductors to earth electrodes bearing the words

options.C: Safety Electrical Connection - Do Not Remove
options.D: Safety Electrical Earth - Do Not Remove

questions.explanation: Earthing and bonding connections can look like redundant metalwork and risk being disturbed by other trades. A durable label reading Safety Electrical Connection - Do Not Remove warns anyone working nearby that the connection is essential and must be left intact.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not normally be recognised as being a supply source for safety services

options.A: A generator supplying power, via the grid, to a hospital
options.B: A separate feeder of the supply network effectively independent of the normal feeder

questions.explanation: A supply for safety services must remain available when the normal supply fails, so it has to be independent of it. A generator feeding through the grid shares the same failure path as the normal supply, so it does not provide the required independent source.

questions.prompt: When selecting electrical equipment consideration need not be given to
questions.explanation: Equipment must be selected so it suits the supply and conditions it meets, so voltage, frequency and compatibility with other equipment all matter. Documentation accompanies products but is not itself an electrical characteristic governing whether the equipment is fit for the installation.

questions.prompt: When the line conductor of a TN system is 25mm2 and the earthing conductor is 16 mm2 the main protective bonding conductor must have a minimum cross-sectional area of at least
questions.explanation: Main protective bonding conductors in a TN system are sized in relation to the supply neutral, typically half its cross-sectional area subject to a minimum. For a 25mm2 line conductor this gives 10mm2, which is the smallest size permitted here.

questions.prompt: As a means of isolation in a circuit it is NOT permissible to use a
questions.explanation: Isolation requires a device that provides a reliable, verifiable break in all live supply conductors with adequate contact separation. A semiconductor switch cannot give that guaranteed off-load isolating gap, so it is not acceptable as a means of isolation even though it can switch current.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect

options.A: For a fixed installation flexible conductors of csa less than 10mm2 may serve as a PEN conductor
options.B: No means of switching shall be inserted in the outer conductor of a concentric cable
options.C: The use of PEN conductors is permitted within an installation where authorisation has been obtained
options.D: The use of PEN conductors is permitted within an installation where the supply is obtained from a private generating plant

questions.explanation: A PEN conductor combines neutral and earth, so it must be robust and never rely on a thin flexible cable. The Regulations prohibit flexible conductors below 10mm2 acting as a PEN, making that statement the incorrect one.

questions.prompt: On Electrical Certificates which of the following box(s) should be ticked within the section titled 'Number and Type of Live Conductors' when dealing with a normal domestic single-phase installation
questions.explanation: A standard domestic supply is alternating current delivered through one line and one neutral, so it is described as single-phase, two-wire. Both the AC and the 1-phase, 2-wire boxes therefore correctly record the nature of the live conductors present.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not required to be inspected

options.A: Correct connection of accessories and equipment
options.B: Installation of suitable SPDs, where required

questions.explanation: Inspection verifies the physical installation and its safety provisions, such as correct connections, danger notices and any required surge protection. The installer's qualifications are a competence matter recorded elsewhere and are not part of what the installation inspection itself examines.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect

options.A: A 'condition report inspection schedule' and 'schedule of test results' must accompany an electrical installation condition report
options.B: An electrical installation condition report has classification codes C1, C2, C3 and FI
options.C: An electrical installation condition report must be completed by a fully qualified electrician
options.D: Where possible, results from previous inspection and testing must be taken into account during the completion of an electrical installation condition report

questions.explanation: A condition report must be produced by a competent, skilled person, but there is no requirement that they hold full electrician status; competence to assess that installation is what matters. The accompanying schedules and the C1, C2, C3 and FI coding are genuine requirements.

questions.prompt: Which of the following methods of 'fault protection' is allowed in highway power supplies and equipment
questions.explanation: Highway power supplies and street equipment rely on automatic disconnection of supply for fault protection, where protective devices cut the supply quickly enough to prevent a dangerous touch voltage persisting. The more specialised measures are not suited to this exposed public environment.

questions.prompt: In which Zones, if any, can heated towel-rails be installed in a bathroom

options.B: Three metres from the side of the bath

questions.explanation: Bathroom zoning restricts where equipment may be installed by distance from water. A fixed heated towel rail is permitted from Zone 2 outwards, since Zone 2 lies clear of the immediate splash area within Zone 1 around the bath itself.

questions.prompt: Construction site special regulations apply to
questions.explanation: The special requirements for construction and demolition sites apply to the actual building, civil engineering and earthworks activity, where conditions are arduous and supplies temporary. Permanent welfare facilities such as offices, canteens and toilets are treated as ordinary installations, not site work.

questions.prompt: When a converter is installed as part of a photovoltaic power supply system an isolation device is

options.B: Required on both the A.C. and the D.C. sides

questions.explanation: A photovoltaic system has live generation on both sides of the converter, so the DC array and the AC mains both remain energised. Isolation must therefore be provided on the AC and DC sides so the converter can be safely disconnected for work.

questions.prompt: 2What is the recommended maximum area covered by a radial final socket circuit protected by a 20A protection device
questions.explanation: A radial socket circuit protected at 20A is recommended to serve a floor area of up to 50 square metres, keeping likely demand within the cable and device rating. Larger areas risk overload and call for a higher-rated radial or a ring circuit.

questions.prompt: The rating factor (Ca) at an ambient air temperature of 45℃ applied to 70℃ PVC cable is
questions.explanation: Higher ambient temperature reduces a cable's ability to shed heat, so a derating factor below one is applied. For 70 degree PVC cable in a 45 degree ambient the correction factor is 0.79, lowering the permitted current-carrying capacity accordingly.

questions.prompt: The IET Wiring Regulations provide
questions.explanation: The Wiring Regulations set out the requirements and principles for a safe installation rather than working drawings or step-by-step instructions. They give the designer the framework needed to design an installation, leaving detailed methods to the competent person.

questions.prompt: No addition or alteration shall be made until checks have been carried out on the
questions.explanation: Before any addition or alteration, the existing equipment, earthing and bonding must be confirmed adequate to carry the new load safely. Connecting extra circuits to under-rated or unsuitable existing equipment could overload it and create a hazard.

questions.prompt: Where would you most expect to find a 'spur'

options.D: A ring or radial final circuit

questions.explanation: A spur is a branch taken from an existing circuit to supply an additional point, so it only exists where there is a final circuit to extend. It is therefore associated with a ring or radial final circuit feeding socket outlets.

questions.prompt: Having regard to frequency and quality of maintenance work on electrical equipment which of the following need not be considered

options.A: Are periodic inspections and testing being carried out regularly
options.B: Are protective measures for safety effective
options.D: The amount of disruption while carrying out maintenance work

questions.explanation: When assessing maintainability the designer must consider how reliable the equipment is, whether protective measures stay effective and whether inspection and testing can be done. The level of disruption maintenance causes is an operational inconvenience, not a safety factor governing the design.

questions.prompt: Diversity may be taken into account when considering

options.C: The rating of the protection device
options.D: The size of the meter tails

questions.explanation: Diversity recognises that not every load operates at full power simultaneously, so the assessed maximum demand of the installation can be reduced below the simple sum of connected loads. This realistic figure then informs the sizing of supply equipment.

questions.prompt: Every installation shall be divided into circuits, as necessary, to

options.A: Facilitate safe inspection, testing and maintenance
options.B: Maximise the number of final circuits
options.C: Provide fault protection from electric shock
options.D: Reduce the effects of electric shock

questions.explanation: Dividing an installation into separate circuits limits the extent of any one circuit, so that part can be isolated while the rest stays live. This makes inspection, testing, fault-finding and maintenance safer and minimises danger and inconvenience when one circuit must be switched off.

questions.prompt: Where electrical separation is the protective measure the voltage of the separated circuit shall not exceed
questions.explanation: Electrical separation isolates a circuit from earth and from other circuits using a safety source such as an isolating transformer. The separated circuit voltage must not exceed 500V so that insulation and separation distances remain adequate and a single fault cannot create a dangerous touch voltage.

questions.prompt: Supplementary equipotential bonding is considered as a part of
questions.explanation: Supplementary equipotential bonding does not stop a fault occurring; it limits the touch voltage between simultaneously accessible conductive parts should automatic disconnection be too slow. Because it acts under fault conditions to reduce shock risk, it is classed as a measure of fault protection.

questions.prompt: Barriers and enclosures must provide a degree of protection against live parts of at least
questions.explanation: Barriers and enclosures must prevent contact with live parts, so they require at least IPXXB or IP2X protection. This stops a standard test finger from reaching hazardous live parts, providing reliable basic protection against direct contact during normal use.

questions.prompt: Within domestic (household) premises, consumer units shall

options.A: Be manufactured from non-combustible material or be within a non-combustible enclosure
options.B: Be manufactured to a particular size and shape
options.C: Be manufactured to another BS EN standard
options.D: Have their enclosure manufactured from combustible material

questions.explanation: Following amendments addressing consumer-unit fires, switchgear assemblies in dwellings must have enclosures of non-combustible material such as steel, or be contained within a non-combustible enclosure. This limits the spread of fire should a loose or overheating connection arise inside the unit.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following statements regarding A.C. lighting systems in domestic premises is correct

options.A: All final circuits supplying luminaires require RCD protection
options.B: Final circuits supplying luminaires do not require RCD protection
options.C: Final circuits supplying luminaires require RCD protection only if wired in PVC sheathed cable
options.D: Final circuits supplying luminaires where on enters a bathroom require RCD protection

questions.explanation: Additional protection by a 30mA RCD is required for AC final circuits supplying luminaires in domestic premises. This guards against shock from cable damage and faulty fittings, and limits fire risk, so every lighting final circuit in a dwelling must be RCD protected.

questions.prompt: The maximum temperature for an accessible part of non-metallic equipment intended to be touched but not held is
questions.explanation: Non-metallic surfaces transfer heat to the skin more slowly than metal, so a higher limit is tolerable. For a non-metallic accessible part intended to be touched but not gripped, the maximum temperature is 80°C, preventing burns during brief contact in normal service.

questions.prompt: In a TN system the disconnection time for a distribution circuit is limited to
questions.explanation: Distribution circuits and final circuits exceeding 63A feed downstream protection rather than supplying equipment directly, so a longer time is permitted. In a TN system the maximum disconnection time for such distribution circuits is 5 seconds, while final circuits up to 63A require faster disconnection.

questions.prompt: RCDs may operate at any value of residual current in excess of

options.A: 10% of the rated residual operating current
options.B: 20% of the rated residual operating current
options.C: 30% of the rated residual operating current
options.D: 50% of the rated residual operating current

questions.explanation: An RCD is guaranteed to trip at its rated residual operating current, but must not nuisance-trip at low leakage. It may operate at any residual current above 50% of its rated value, so a 30mA device can respond to currents as low as 15mA.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can not be used as a main earthing conductor
questions.explanation: Earthing must rely on a permanent, reliably conductive path under the installer's control. A water supply pipe cannot be used as a main earthing conductor because sections may be replaced with plastic or removed, breaking the earth path without warning.

questions.prompt: Line 3 of a three-phase A.C. circuit should be identified by which of the following
questions.explanation: The harmonised cable colours identify the three line conductors of an AC circuit as brown for L1, black for L2 and grey for L3. Line 3 is therefore identified by grey, ensuring consistent phase identification across installations.

questions.prompt: The maximum temperature for an accessible part of hand held metallic equipment is
questions.explanation: Metal conducts heat rapidly into the skin, so hand-held metallic parts have the strictest limit. The maximum temperature for an accessible metallic part that is gripped in normal use is 55°C, preventing burns during prolonged contact.

questions.prompt: Which of the following must not be used as an earth electrode
questions.explanation: An earth electrode must provide a stable, dedicated connection to the general mass of earth. A gas service pipe must never be used because it is not under electrical control, may be replaced in non-conductive material, and introducing fault current onto it creates an explosion hazard.

questions.prompt: Luminaires marked with an 'F' inside a triangle are suitable for mounting
questions.explanation: The 'F' in a triangle marking shows a luminaire is designed to limit surface temperatures so it can be safely fixed directly to a normally flammable surface. Without this mark, additional clearance or non-combustible backing would be needed to avoid igniting the mounting material.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not be checked during functional testing
questions.explanation: Functional testing confirms that assembled equipment such as alarms, indicators and controls actually operates as intended. The effectiveness of isolation padlocks is a matter of safe isolation procedure, not equipment function, so it falls outside what functional testing verifies.

questions.prompt: One purpose of the inspection conducted prior to testing an installation is to verify that

options.A: All ring final circuit connections are correct
options.B: Equipment is not damaged or defective
options.C: Equipment is not damaged or defective so as to impair safety
options.D: Only British Standard equipment is installed

questions.explanation: The inspection carried out before testing is a visual check confirming installed equipment complies and is not visibly damaged or defective in a way that would impair safety. This ensures the installation is safe to energise before live tests are applied.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not required during periodic inspection and testing

options.A: Checking provision for the safety of persons and livestock from shock and burns
options.B: Checking that the installation is not damaged as to impair safety
options.C: Checking that the property is protected against damage from fire and heat due to an installation fault
options.D: Confirmation that the clients equipment is working correctly

questions.explanation: Periodic inspection and testing assesses the safety of the installation itself, covering shock, burns, fire and damage that could impair safety. Confirming that the client's own appliances work correctly is outside its scope, as it concerns equipment performance rather than installation safety.

questions.prompt: On a construction site a final circuit supplying hand-held equipment with a rated current not exceeding 32A when protected by an RCD the rated residual operating current not greater than
questions.explanation: On construction sites, where conditions are wet and equipment is heavily handled, shock risk is high. A final circuit up to 32A supplying hand-held equipment must have additional protection by an RCD not exceeding 30mA, which disconnects quickly enough to protect against fatal shock.

questions.prompt: Protection against electric shock regarding vehicle charging installations requires disconnection of live conductors within
questions.explanation: Electric vehicle charging points feeding caravans and similar mobile equipment fall outside the standard final-circuit limit, so automatic disconnection is permitted to take place within 5 seconds rather than the 0.4 second limit applied to ordinary 230 V socket-outlet circuits.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum number of socket-outlets that may be grouped together in one enclosure on a caravan pitch
questions.explanation: On a caravan park each pitch is supplied individually, and to keep pitches separate and prevent overloading a single enclosure no more than four socket-outlets may be grouped together. This limits how many units draw from one point and keeps the supply arrangement clear.

questions.prompt: If cleaning by use of water jets in a room containing a sauna heater electrical equipment shall have a degree of protection against ingress of at least
questions.explanation: Where cleaning is carried out using water jets, equipment must resist jets of water from any direction, which is the IPX5 rating. The X indicates no specific solid-object requirement here, while the 5 confirms protection against pressurised water jets used during washing down.

questions.prompt: The number items of electrical equipment that may be connected to the secondary winding of an isolating transformer when electrical separation is being used in a conducting location with restricted movement is
questions.explanation: In a conducting location with restricted movement, electrical separation must supply only a single item of equipment from each secondary winding. Connecting more than one would allow a second fault path between items, undermining the separation that keeps the protective measure safe.

questions.prompt: 2Ordinary persons may be capable of access to electrical equipment under the 'utilisation' category
questions.explanation: The BA classification describes the capability of persons, and BA1 covers ordinary persons who are neither skilled nor instructed in electrical matters. The AA categories instead relate to ambient temperature, so they cannot describe a person's competence to access equipment.

questions.prompt: What will be the operating time for a 60A BS 3036 protective device when the value of fault current is 205A
questions.explanation: The BS 3036 rewireable fuse time/current characteristic shows that a 60 A fuse needs around 205 A, roughly three and a half times its rating, to operate within 5 seconds. Lower fault currents would take longer, so 5 seconds is the disconnection time achieved at this value.

questions.prompt: Particular requirements are included in BS 7671 for electrical installations of:
questions.explanation: Part 7 of BS 7671 sets particular requirements for special installations and locations where increased risk exists. A location containing a bath or shower carries heightened shock risk from water and reduced body resistance, so it has its own dedicated set of additional requirements.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following types of installation is NOT included in the special installations recognised by BS 7671
questions.explanation: Part 7 lists the special installations and locations recognised by BS 7671, including agricultural premises, saunas and swimming pools. Petrol filling stations involve flammable atmospheres governed by separate hazardous-area standards, so they are not among the special installations covered here.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following sets of regulations is non-statutory?

options.D: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations

questions.explanation: BS 7671 is a British Standard and code of practice, not law, so it is non-statutory. The Electricity at Work Regulations and the Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations are statutory instruments, and compliance with BS 7671 is the recognised way to satisfy them.

questions.prompt: A d.c. voltage of 125 V between conductors is classified as:
questions.explanation: Voltage bands define the classifications, and low voltage spans up to 1000 V a.c. or 1500 V d.c. between conductors. At 125 V d.c. the value exceeds the extra-low voltage band, which ends at 120 V d.c., so it is classified as low voltage.

questions.prompt: The type of system known as PME is also referred to as:
questions.explanation: Protective Multiple Earthing combines the neutral and protective functions in the supply cable, then separates them at the installation into distinct neutral and earth conductors. This combined-then-separated arrangement is the TN-C-S system, where the supply network is TN-C and the installation is TN-S.

questions.prompt: A circuit protective conductor connects:

options.A: A gas pipe to the main earthing terminal
options.B: A water pipe to the earth terminal of a switch in a bathroom
options.C: The main earthing terminal to the earth terminal of a socket- outlet
options.D: Two water pipes in a bathroom

questions.explanation: A circuit protective conductor connects exposed-conductive-parts of a circuit back to the main earthing terminal, providing the fault path for automatic disconnection. Linking the main earthing terminal to a socket-outlet's earth terminal is exactly this function; connections to pipework are instead bonding conductors.

questions.prompt: An external influence categorised as AG1 applies to a:
questions.explanation: The AG external-influence classification grades mechanical impact, and AG1 denotes low severity. A dwelling experiences only minor impact compared with the heavy knocks found in factories, workshops or quarries, so a house falls into the lowest impact category.

questions.prompt: A building constructed solely of wood would have an external influence category of:
questions.explanation: The CA classification covers building construction materials, where CA1 is non-combustible and CA2 is combustible. A structure built entirely of wood is combustible, so it is categorised CA2, which then influences the wiring and fire precautions selected for it.

questions.prompt: A fire fighter's emergency switch should be provided for:

options.A: Exterior discharge lighting installations exceeding low-voltage
options.B: Factory fire alarm circuits operating at low-voltage

questions.explanation: A firefighter's emergency switch is required for discharge lighting operating above low voltage, because such circuits carry dangerous high voltages that firefighters must be able to isolate quickly. Exterior installations exceeding low voltage therefore need this means of rapid disconnection.

questions.prompt: The protective conductor used within a final circuit has high protective conductor currents in excess of 10 mA when supplying more than one item of electrical equipment. The minimal cross-sectional area may be 4 mm2, provided that:

options.A: Additional protection from the use of a residual current device is present
options.B: Individual items of equipment are supplied through an isolating transformer
options.C: The protective conductor has additional mechanical protection
options.D: The protective conductor is in the form of a complete ring

questions.explanation: Where protective conductor current exceeds 10 mA, a robust earth path is essential, so a reduced 4 mm cross-section is only acceptable if the conductor is given additional mechanical protection against damage. This safeguards the high-integrity earthing on which the connected equipment depends.

questions.prompt: Installations should be arranged so as to avoid hazards in the event of a fault, and to facilitate safe operation, inspection, testing and maintenance. One method of complying with this is to:

options.A: Connect all circuits on the radial principle
options.B: Connect all circuits on the ring principle
options.C: Divide the installation into bands of circuits
options.D: Divide the installation into separate circuits

questions.explanation: Dividing an installation into separate circuits limits the consequences of a single fault and allows parts to be isolated independently for inspection, testing and maintenance. This containment prevents one fault disabling the whole installation and supports safe working on individual circuits.

questions.prompt: A domestic 30A radial final circuit is used to supply BS 1363 socket outlets. If the floor area to be served is 55m2, the rating of the protective device and the live conductor's csa must not be less than:
questions.explanation: A 30 A radial circuit feeding BS 1363 socket-outlets may serve a floor area up to about 75 square metres, so 55 square metres is within range. The conductors must carry the full 30 A, which requires a minimum 4 mm live cross-sectional area.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not a characteristic of the supply?
questions.explanation: The characteristics of a supply describe the source itself - its nominal voltage, frequency and earth fault loop impedance Ze at the origin. Emergency switching is a protective measure the designer provides within the installation, not an inherent property of the incoming supply.

questions.prompt: The number and type of live conductors of a new electrical supply to a building may be determined:

options.A: After consultation with the local distributor
options.B: By enquiry to the local council offices
options.D: By reference to the Electricity, Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations

questions.explanation: The number and type of live conductors, such as single-phase two-wire or three-phase four-wire, depends on the supply the network operator can offer. This is established by consulting the local distributor, who confirms the available arrangement before the installation is designed.

questions.prompt: Basic protection protects persons and/or livestock from contact with:

options.B: Exposed conductive parts made live by a fault

questions.explanation: Basic protection guards against contact with parts that are intended to be live in normal service. By insulating or enclosing those live parts, persons and livestock are prevented from touching them during everyday use, before any fault has occurred.

questions.prompt: The requirements regarding basic protection have not been applied if livestock comes into contact with:

options.A: A protective conductor carrying fault current
options.B: An exposed terminal within a faulty enclosure
options.C: Exposed conductive parts made live by a fault
options.D: Extraneous conductive parts made live by an earth fault

questions.explanation: Basic protection prevents contact with normally live parts during ordinary service. If an enclosure is faulty and leaves an exposed terminal accessible, the barrier intended to keep live parts out of reach has failed, so the requirement for basic protection has not been satisfied.

questions.prompt: One method of providing basic protection is by:
questions.explanation: Basic protection works by physically preventing contact with live parts in normal service. Barriers or enclosures, alongside insulation of live parts, achieve this directly. Automatic disconnection and electrical separation are fault protection measures, acting only after a fault develops.

questions.prompt: A piece of electrical equipment having a protective conductor current of 15 mA is to be connected to the supply by means of a 16A plug and socket outlet complying with BS EN 60309-The cross sectional area of the protective conductor of the associated flexible cable shall not be less than:
questions.explanation: Where the protective conductor current exceeds 10 mA, a high-integrity earth connection is required. For a single flexible cable supplying such equipment, the protective conductor must have a cross-sectional area of at least 2.5 mm2 to ensure a robust, reliable earth path.

questions.prompt: Where a PEN conductor is installed it should be identified by the use of the following coloured marks

options.A: Blue throughout it's length with green and yellow at the terminations
options.C: Green and yellow throughout it's length

questions.explanation: A PEN conductor combines neutral and protective functions in one conductor. It is identified blue throughout its length, with green-and-yellow markings added at the terminations, signalling that it performs both the neutral and the earthing role at those points.

questions.prompt: The temperature limit for non-metallic equipment which is intended to be touched but not hand-held is:
questions.explanation: Accessible parts must not reach temperatures that burn on touch. Non-metallic surfaces conduct heat more slowly than metal, so a higher limit of 80 degrees Celsius applies to parts intended to be touched but not gripped, since brief contact is tolerable.

questions.prompt: The prospective fault current at the origin of an electrical installation must be taken into account when:

options.C: Estimating the external earth fault loop impedance
options.D: Selecting the type of overcurrent device to be installed

questions.explanation: Overcurrent devices must safely interrupt the largest fault current that can flow at their point of installation. The prospective fault current at the origin therefore sets the breaking capacity required, so the device chosen can clear a fault without damage or danger.

questions.prompt: Omission of devices for protection against overload is NOT permitted for:

options.B: Circuits which supply fire extinguishing devices

questions.explanation: Overload protection may be omitted only where unexpected disconnection is more dangerous than the overload itself. Emergency lighting must remain reliably available, so its supply circuits are not among those permitted to omit overload protection in that way.

questions.prompt: The nominal rating of an overcurrent protective device should be:

options.B: Equal to the prospective short-circuit current
options.C: Greater than the current carrying capacity of the conductors
options.D: Not less than the design current

questions.explanation: A protective device must carry the intended load without nuisance tripping, so its nominal rating must be at least the design current of the circuit. It must also stay below the cable's current-carrying capacity so the conductors are protected against overload.

questions.prompt: The means of isolation for a particular item of equipment may be installed in a position remote from that equipment, providing that it:

options.A: Can be locked in the off position using a lock and key common to all other such isolators
options.B: Can be locked in the off position using a lock and key that are unique to that isolator
options.C: Is located so as to be in full view of persons working on the equipment
options.D: Is manually operated and a visual display is located next to the equipment

questions.explanation: A remote isolator must be securable so the supply cannot be restored while someone works on the equipment. A lock and key unique to that isolator prevents another person inadvertently re-energising the circuit using a common key, keeping the dead state under reliable control.

questions.prompt: A firefighter's switch should be installed at not more than:

options.A: 2.75m from the ground and the 'off' position at the bottom
options.B: 2.75m from the ground and the 'off' position at the top
options.C: 2.75m from the ground and the 'on' position at the top and coloured red
options.D: 2m from the ground and the 'off' position at the bottom and coloured red

questions.explanation: A firefighter's switch must be operable and clearly readable from ground level. Mounting it no higher than 2.75 metres keeps it within reach, and placing the off position at the top lets firefighters confirm at a glance that the supply has been isolated.

questions.prompt: Where the nominal voltage of an installation is 230V, the required minimum impulse withstand voltage for Category II equipment for overvoltage protection is:
questions.explanation: Equipment must withstand transient overvoltages appropriate to its position in the installation. For a 230 V single-phase supply, Category II equipment such as appliances and portable tools requires a minimum impulse withstand of 2.5 kV to survive surges reaching it through the wiring.

questions.prompt: In a location where a risk of danger from fire exists due to manufacture or storage of combustible materials, enclosures of heaters shall not attain a surface temperature under normal working conditions exceeding:
questions.explanation: Where combustible materials are manufactured or stored, heater enclosures must stay well below the ignition risk of nearby dust and material. Limiting the surface temperature to 90 degrees Celsius under normal conditions reduces the chance of igniting accumulated combustible matter.

questions.prompt: For a.c., the preferred frequencies which are taken into account in BS 7671 are:
questions.explanation: The regulations are written around the supply frequencies likely to be encountered. The preferred values of 50 Hz, 60 Hz and 400 Hz cover standard mains distribution and the higher frequency used in aircraft and similar specialised systems.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following external influences requires an increase in the current ratings of cables above those normally required?

options.C: Possible vertically falling drops of water

questions.explanation: A cable's rating assumes a reference ambient temperature. A higher ambient reduces the temperature difference available to dissipate heat, so the conductor reaches its limit at a lower current. A rating factor must therefore increase the size, effectively requiring more copper, to compensate.

questions.prompt: To prevent circulating eddy currents (an electromagnetic effect) in steel conduit, trunking or cable armouring:

options.A: All live conductors of a circuit must be contained in the same enclosure
options.B: Line and neutral conductors are to be kept separate
options.D: The enclosures should be solidly earthed

questions.explanation: Currents in line and neutral conductors are equal and opposite, so their magnetic fields cancel. Keeping all the live conductors of a circuit within the same steel enclosure ensures this cancellation, preventing the net magnetic flux that would otherwise induce heating eddy currents in the steel.

questions.prompt: It is required that all circuits in a barn on an agricultural installation be protected by an RCD. The maximum rating (lΔn) for a circuit protected by a 40A BS 88 protective device should not exceed:
questions.explanation: In agricultural and horticultural installations, RCDs protecting final circuits are rated to suit the hazard, and where fire protection is the aim a 300 mA device is the permitted maximum. Circuits supplying socket-outlets demand 30 mA, but a 40 A BS 88 circuit may rely on the 300 mA threshold for fire safety.
