questions.prompt: In agricultural premises in locations where tractors are used, which one of the following methods of installation shall NOT be applied:

options.A: Cables in arable ground shall be buried at a depth of at least 1m
options.B: Cables shall be buried at a depth of at least 0.6m with additional protection
options.C: Self supporting suspension cables at a height in excess of that accessible by rodents
options.D: Self supporting suspension cables at a height of at least 6m

questions.explanation: Where tractors and tall machinery operate, overhead cables must be high enough to clear that traffic, so a fixed minimum such as 6 m is specified. Setting suspension height merely above rodent reach ignores vehicle clearance and would risk contact, so that method is not acceptable.

questions.prompt: A permanent warning notice must be fixed at or near the point of connection of every earthing conductor to an earth electrode. This notice must bear the words:

options.A: Earth Bonding Connection, Do Not Remove
options.B: Earth Electrical Connection, Do Not Remove
options.C: Safety Bonding Connection, Do Not Remove
options.D: Safety Electrical Connection, Do Not Remove

questions.explanation: A durable label reading "Safety Electrical Connection - Do Not Remove" must be fixed at every earthing conductor connection to an electrode, at bonding connections to extraneous-conductive-parts, and at the main earth terminal. The wording warns anyone working nearby not to disturb a connection essential to the safety of the installation.

questions.prompt: Overcurrent protection may be provided by a:
questions.explanation: Overcurrent protection guards against both overload and fault current, and a circuit-breaker performs this by automatically opening under those conditions. Disconnectors and linked switches provide isolation only, while an RCD responds to residual earth-leakage current, not to overcurrent, so it cannot fulfil that protective function.

questions.prompt: Where ADS is the means of providing fault protection and a 20 A type B circuit breaker to BS EN 60898 is used, the maximum earth fault loop impedance is:
questions.explanation: For a Type B device the magnetic trip operates at around five times rated current, so disconnection within the required time depends on the loop impedance being low enough to drive that current. For a 20 A Type B breaker the tabulated maximum earth fault loop impedance is 2.3 ohms.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is excluded as a protective earth electrode?

options.C: Underground structural metalwork embedded in foundations
options.D: Welded metal reinforcement of concrete embedded in the earth

questions.explanation: Permitted earth electrodes are those whose contact with the general mass of earth is reliable and under the installation's control, such as plates, rods and structural metalwork in foundations. The metalwork of public water mains must not be used, since the utility may insert plastic sections that destroy continuity.

questions.prompt: A copper earthing conductor not mechanically protected and not protected against corrosion is buried in soil. The minimum size of the earthing conductor is:
questions.explanation: An earthing conductor buried in soil must resist both mechanical damage and corrosion, so reducing its size depends on the protection provided. A copper conductor that is neither mechanically protected nor protected against corrosion must be at least 25 mm to remain reliable over its service life.

questions.prompt: By employing an RCD protected socket-outlet to supply a Class II portable tool, the user is:

options.A: Protected against an earth fault in the windings of the tool
options.B: Protected against breakage of the protective conductor of the flexible cable
options.C: Provided with additional fault protection against contact with a live conductor exposed by carelessness of the user
options.D: Unable to operate the tool until the earthing circuit is complete and monitored

questions.explanation: An RCD detects the small residual current that flows if a person touches a live conductor and provides rapid disconnection, giving additional protection. With a Class II tool there is no earth fault path to monitor, so the RCD's value lies in covering live contact caused by carelessness or insulation failure.

questions.prompt: A 13A socket-outlet supplies mobile equipment for use outdoors. Additional protection should be provided by means of a:
questions.explanation: Socket-outlets up to 32 A for general use, and equipment used outdoors, require additional protection by a 30 mA RCD because outdoor conditions raise the risk of shock. The RCD disconnects rapidly on earth leakage, limiting the duration of any contact with a faulty live part.

questions.prompt: In order to prevent the spread of fire where a wiring system passes through elements of building structures, any holes must be sealed around the cables. Which of the following is NOT a requirement for such sealing materials?

options.A: A) it shall be compatible with the material of the wiring system
options.B: It shall be of adequate mechanical stability to withstand the stresses which may arise
options.C: It shall prevent thermal movement of the wiring system
options.D: It shall resist relevant external influences to the same degree as the wiring system

questions.explanation: Sealing around a wiring system penetrating a fire-rated barrier must restore the fire resistance, withstand mechanical stresses, resist external influences as the wiring does, and remain compatible with the cable. It is not required to prevent thermal movement; the seal must in fact permit normal expansion without losing integrity.

questions.prompt: Where an autotransformer is used for step-up purposes:

options.A: A linked switch breaking all live conductors must be used
options.B: A single-pole switch can be used

questions.explanation: A step-up autotransformer raises the voltage to its load, so isolating only one pole could leave conductors live. A linked switch that breaks all live conductors simultaneously is required to ensure the whole circuit is made dead, preventing a dangerous voltage remaining downstream during isolation.

questions.prompt: When installing socket outlets which will be mounted vertically on a wall or working surface, they should be:

options.A: Mounted 50mm from the floor level or working surface
options.B: Mounted so that the flexible cord and plug are 50mm from floor or working surface level
options.C: Mounted so the flexible cord and plug top can be withdrawn or inserted without mechanical damage
options.D: Shuttered and suitable for a.c. and complying with BS 1363

questions.explanation: Socket-outlets must be positioned so the plug and its flexible cord can be inserted and withdrawn freely without straining or chafing against the floor or working surface. Mounting them so the plug top clears such damage protects the cord's insulation and the connection from harm in service.

questions.prompt: Any circuit or equipment vulnerable to a particular test should be identified by:

options.A: A visual inspection prior to testing
options.B: The inventory for the building being tested
options.C: The manufacturer's warning notice on the equipment
options.D: The provision of a legible diagram, chart or table prior to testing

questions.explanation: Before testing, the inspector needs a record of any circuits or equipment that could be damaged by a particular test, such as electronic devices vulnerable to insulation testing. A legible diagram, chart or table provides this information so tests are applied safely and nothing sensitive is harmed.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following tests is carried out after the supply is connected?

options.B: Continuity of ring final circuit conductors

questions.explanation: Most initial tests are dead tests performed before energising, but verifying RCD operation needs the device to trip under genuine residual current. Confirming an RCD's effectiveness therefore requires the supply connected, so it is carried out as a live test once the installation is energised.

questions.prompt: The purpose of the inspection conducted prior to testing an installation is to verify that:

options.A: All electrical cables and conduits are pointed orange for identification
options.B: All ring final circuit connections are correct
options.C: Equipment is not damaged or defective
options.D: Only British Standard equipment is installed

questions.explanation: Inspection precedes testing to confirm by examination that the installed equipment is correctly selected, suitably erected and not visibly damaged or defective before any test current is applied. This visual check catches faults that could make subsequent testing dangerous or that testing alone would not reveal.

questions.prompt: When testing a 230V installation, the minimum value of insulation resistance is:
questions.explanation: For a 230 V circuit the insulation resistance is tested at 500 V d.c., and the measured value must reach at least 1 megohm to confirm the insulation adequately separates live conductors and earth. A lower reading indicates deterioration or a fault that could allow dangerous leakage.

questions.prompt: No alteration shall be made to an existing installation unless the:

options.B: Existing equipment meets BS and BS EN standards
options.C: It is established that the alteration will not impair the safety of the existing installation

questions.explanation: Any addition or alteration must not reduce the safety of the existing installation, so it must first be established that the existing earthing, bonding and protective devices remain adequate for the changed arrangement. Proceeding without that check could leave the installation unable to provide the required protection.

questions.prompt: The inspecting and testing required during a periodic inspection should be recorded on a Periodic Inspection Report and carried out by:
questions.explanation: Periodic inspection and testing assesses whether an existing installation remains safe for continued use, which calls for sound judgement of condition and risk. The work must be carried out and reported by a competent person with the skill and experience to recognise defects and interpret results correctly.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following factors does not affect the frequency of periodic inspection?
questions.explanation: The interval between periodic inspections is set from the kind of installation, how it is used and operated, and the quality and frequency of maintenance it receives. Provision of supplies for safety services is a design feature of the installation, not a factor that determines how often it must be reassessed.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following numbers is the correct grouping factor for six circuits installed as method B?
questions.explanation: Where several loaded circuits are bunched together they each run hotter, so a grouping correction factor is applied to reduce the assumed current-carrying capacity. For six circuits grouped in a touching arrangement that derating factor works out at 0.57, accounting for the mutual heating between them.

questions.prompt: The reference for the installation method that has multi-core cables having a non metallic sheath, in surface mounted conduit is:
questions.explanation: Installation reference methods classify how a cable dissipates heat. Multicore non-sheathed cables run in surface-mounted conduit on a wall correspond to reference method B, which sets the current-carrying capacity used when sizing the conductor from the tabulated ratings.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following classifications of external influences would be appropriate for an item of electrical equipment installed where it would be subject to 'splashes of water'?
questions.explanation: External influences are coded by category, with AD describing the presence of water. The classification AD4 covers splashing water from any direction, so equipment in such a location must have an enclosure rated to withstand splashes rather than just falling drops or mere humidity.

questions.prompt: In rooms containing a bath or shower, the measures of protection by obstacles and placing out of reach are:
questions.explanation: Protection by obstacles and by placing out of reach relies on the discipline of skilled or instructed persons, which cannot be assumed where people are wet and have reduced body resistance. In locations containing a bath or shower these measures are therefore prohibited entirely, and only full basic and fault protection is acceptable.

questions.prompt: The nominal supply voltage on temporary installations in shows and stands shall not exceed 230/400 V ac, or
questions.explanation: Temporary installations for shows, stands and amusement devices face harsh handling and public exposure, so voltage limits are tightened. The nominal supply must not exceed 230/400 V ac, and for direct current the upper limit is set at 500 V dc to keep shock and fault energy within safe bounds.

questions.prompt: In a conduit system on an agricultural installation where livestock are kept, the external influence shall be classified as:
questions.explanation: Agricultural buildings where livestock are kept are dusty, corrosive and physically demanding environments. Conduit and wiring systems must therefore be classified for the presence of corrosive or polluting substances at AF4, ensuring the materials chosen resist the ammonia, moisture and slurry typically present.

questions.prompt: On agricultural premises, heating appliances shall be fixed so as to maintain an appropriate distance from livestock. In the absence of manufacturer's guidance, a radiant heater used in the vicinity of livestock should be placed at a distance of not less than:
questions.explanation: Radiant heaters in livestock areas can ignite bedding or burn animals if placed too close. Where the manufacturer gives no figure, a minimum separation of 0.5 m from livestock and combustible material is required to limit the fire and burn risk from the radiated heat.

questions.prompt: In a caravan park, the maximum number of socket outlets which can be protected by an RCD is:
questions.explanation: Caravan pitches draw flexible leads into damp outdoor conditions where earth faults are likely, so RCD protection must remain selective and reliable. Each socket-outlet is therefore individually protected by its own RCD, so a fault on one pitch cannot disconnect supplies to neighbouring caravans.

questions.prompt: In exhibitions, protection against thermal effects must be provided for luminaries mounted below a height of:
questions.explanation: Luminaires at exhibitions and shows are within easy reach of the public and can run hot, creating a burn and fire risk. Where they are mounted below 2.5 m from floor level, additional protection against thermal effects and mechanical damage is required to keep people safe.

questions.prompt: For household installations, as a rule of thumb, the floor area served by a single 20A radial circuit using socket outlets to BS 1363 may be:
questions.explanation: A 20 A radial using BS 1363 socket-outlets is limited by voltage drop and likely loading rather than an absolute count. As a practical rule of thumb the floor area it serves should not exceed 50 m2, keeping the diversified demand within the circuit's capacity.

questions.prompt: Prior to an inspection in accordance with BS 7671, the competent person carrying out the work shall normally:

options.B: Disconnect the installation from the supply
options.C: Ensure that all switches are off
options.D: Ensure that the supply is connected

questions.explanation: Inspection and testing must be carried out safely and without risk of electric shock to the person doing the work. The installation is therefore normally disconnected from the supply and made dead before inspection begins, so live parts cannot be touched and continuity and insulation checks give valid readings.

questions.prompt: To which one of the following situations does BS 7671 apply?

options.A: The design of an electrical installation for a caravan site
options.B: The inspection and testing of the electrical installation on an oil rig

questions.explanation: BS 7671 governs the design, erection and verification of fixed electrical installations in and around buildings, including special locations such as caravan and camping sites. Designing the installation for a caravan site falls squarely within that scope, unlike public supply networks or equipment manufacture.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is listed under exclusions from the scope of BS 7671?
questions.explanation: BS 7671 covers fixed electrical installations but not every electrical system on a site. Lightning protection systems are specifically excluded from its scope because they are addressed by their own dedicated standard, whereas marinas, saunas and swimming pools are special locations the Regulations expressly cover.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following sets of regulations is non-statutory?

options.D: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations

questions.explanation: Statutory regulations are imposed directly by law and carry legal force in themselves. BS 7671 is a national standard, not a statute, so it is non-statutory; however, complying with it is widely accepted as a means of satisfying the legal duties set by the Electricity at Work Regulations.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 defines low voltage a.c. between conductors as voltage:

options.A: Above 250 V a.c. but below 1000 V a.c
options.B: Above 50 V a.c. but below 500 V a.c
options.C: Below 1000 V a.c. but above 50 V a.c

questions.explanation: The voltage band definitions set the thresholds at which different protective requirements apply. Low voltage in alternating current is defined as exceeding 50 V but not exceeding 1000 V between conductors, the band that covers ordinary 230/400 V mains supplies.

questions.prompt: An ordinary person is a person who:
questions.explanation: Persons are classified by their electrical competence to decide which protective measures are acceptable. An ordinary person is one who is neither skilled nor instructed in electrical work, so the installation must protect them without relying on any knowledge or supervision on their part.

questions.prompt: A 12 V fire alarm circuit is classified by BS 7671 as:
questions.explanation: Voltage bands separate low-energy signalling circuits from supply circuits so they can be segregated appropriately. A 12 V fire alarm circuit operates at extra-low voltage and falls within Band I, the band reserved for circuits where protection against electric shock is assured by the low voltage itself.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is NOT a classification of external influence?
questions.explanation: External influences are classified in three lettered categories: environment, utilisation, and construction of buildings. Current rating is a property of cables and protective devices selected to suit those influences, not an influence acting on the installation itself.

questions.prompt: The type of building construction is an external influence which, in an electrical installation, will affect the choice of:
questions.explanation: How a building is constructed determines hazards such as combustible materials, structural movement or restricted access. These factors drive the selection of suitable equipment and the wiring system, so that the cables and accessories chosen can withstand the conditions present.

questions.prompt: Non-sheathed cables for fixed wiring, other than protective conductors, should always be installed in:
questions.explanation: Non-sheathed single-insulated cables rely on an enclosure for their mechanical and additional electrical protection. Other than where used as protective conductors, they must be drawn into conduit, trunking or ducting so the insulation is not exposed to damage.

questions.prompt: Domestic ring final circuits are used to supply BS 1363 socket outlets. If the floor area to be served is limited to 50 m2, the cable feeding the circuit must be:
questions.explanation: A standard 30 A or 32 A domestic ring final circuit serving up to 50 square metres is designed around 2.5 square millimetre copper conductors. The ring topology shares load between two legs, allowing this size to carry the circuit demand safely.

questions.prompt: A domestic final ring circuit may:

options.B: Require additional protection by an RCD
options.C: Supply a cooker rated at 2.5 kW
options.D: Supply any number of socket-outlets over an area of 200 m2

questions.explanation: Socket-outlets rated up to 32 A for general use, and circuits likely to supply portable equipment outdoors, require additional protection by a 30 mA RCD. This guards against electric shock if a cable is damaged or an appliance develops an earth fault.

questions.prompt: Where thermoplastic insulated and sheathed cables are installed in a plastered wall at a depth of 20 mm and are not protected against mechanical damage, they must be:

options.C: Protected by a 30 mA RCD and run in the "safe zones"

questions.explanation: Cables concealed in a wall at less than 50 mm depth without earthed mechanical protection must lie in the prescribed zones and be protected by a 30 mA RCD. The RCD provides rapid disconnection should a nail or screw penetrate the cable.

questions.prompt: A two-storey domestic dwelling should have a minimum of two lighting circuits in order to:

options.A: Avoid danger in the event of a fault
options.B: Enable a greater variety of luminaries to be used
options.D: Reduce the load on the consumer's control unit

questions.explanation: Splitting lighting across at least two circuits ensures that a fault tripping one protective device cannot plunge the whole dwelling into darkness. Retaining light on a separate circuit prevents the danger of people moving about an unlit building.

questions.prompt: A system is defined as:

options.A: A single source of energy and an installation
options.B: The consumer's terminals of an installation
options.C: The distribution cables to an installation
options.D: The kWh meter and an installation

questions.explanation: A system, in the defined sense, comprises a single source of electrical energy together with the installation it supplies. This pairing is what the earthing system classifications such as TN-S, TN-C-S and TT describe.

questions.prompt: The term "basic protection" refers to:

options.C: Protection against electric shock under a single fault condition
options.D: Protection against electric shock under fault free conditions

questions.explanation: Basic protection guards people against contact with parts that are live during normal, fault-free operation. It is achieved by measures such as insulation or barriers that prevent touching intended live parts, distinct from fault protection which acts under fault conditions.

questions.prompt: Within a 230 V single-phase, metal clad fuse board, access to the line and neutral busbars are protected by insulation and by secured intermediate barriers. The fuse board may be:

options.B: Opened without use of a key or tool
options.C: Used to accommodate ELV circuit conductors

questions.explanation: Where live busbars are guarded by insulation and secured intermediate barriers, the basic protection does not depend on the enclosure door. The board may therefore be opened without a key or tool, since exposed live parts remain inaccessible.

questions.prompt: A socket-outlet used for a SELV system should:

options.D: Not have a protective conductor contact

questions.explanation: A SELV system is isolated from earth and must not be confused with circuits requiring an earth connection. Its socket-outlets must not accept plugs from other systems and must have no protective conductor contact, preserving electrical separation from earth.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is recognised as a means of providing fault protection?

options.B: Protection by insulation of live parts
options.D: Protection by placing out of reach

questions.explanation: Automatic disconnection of supply is the principal recognised measure for fault protection, relying on protective devices to cut off a faulty circuit within the required time. Insulation, obstacles and placing out of reach are basic-protection measures, not fault protection.

questions.prompt: Where SELV is used in normally dry conditions, basic protection is unnecessary where the nominal voltage does not exceed:
questions.explanation: For SELV in dry locations basic protection against direct contact may be omitted only at very low voltages. The threshold for normally dry conditions is 25 V a.c., below which the shock risk from touching live parts is considered acceptably low.

questions.prompt: Obstacles may be used to provide basic protection providing:

options.B: The circuit voltage does not exceed 250 V
options.C: The installation is contained within steel conduit
options.D: The installation is under the control of a skilled person

questions.explanation: Obstacles only prevent unintentional contact and can be bypassed deliberately, so they are permitted solely where skilled or instructed persons are in control. Such persons understand the risk, so accidental approach to live parts is not relied upon for ordinary people.

questions.prompt: Overload current is defined as the overcurrent:

options.A: Flowing in a phase conductor when in contact with exposed conductive parts
options.B: Occurring in a circuit which is electrically sound
options.C: Resulting from a fault of negligible impedance
options.D: That causes protective devices to operate correctly

questions.explanation: An overload is an overcurrent arising in a circuit that is otherwise electrically sound, with no insulation failure or short between conductors. It results from excessive demand rather than a fault, distinguishing it from fault currents of negligible impedance.

questions.prompt: An overload current could arise when:

options.A: A forward/reverse controller attempts to switch a motor both directions simultaneously
options.B: An electrician drills into a busbar chamber and touches a live busbar with the drill
options.C: Contamination of a motor terminal block results in tracking
options.D: Excessive mechanical load is applied to an electric motor

questions.explanation: Overload occurs in a healthy circuit drawing more current than intended. A motor forced to work against excessive mechanical load draws more current to meet the demand, raising conductor temperature, whereas tracking or contact with a busbar produces fault current instead.

questions.prompt: Where the overcurrent device is intended to afford protection against overload, l2 must not exceed lz multiplied by:
questions.explanation: For overload protection the conventional operating current I2 must not exceed 1.45 times the cable's continuous current-carrying capacity Iz. This coordination ensures the device operates before prolonged current causes the conductor insulation to reach a damaging temperature.

questions.prompt: Omission of devices for protection against overload is not permitted for:

options.B: Circuits which supply fire extinguishing devices

questions.explanation: Overload devices may be omitted only where sudden disconnection could cause greater danger than the overload itself, such as certain safety circuits. Emergency lighting is not among the permitted omissions, so its supply must retain overload protection.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following may be used to provide emergency switching for an electric motor?

options.A: A device which latches in the off position
options.B: A key switch latched in the on position
options.D: A switch fuse with a removable handle

questions.explanation: Emergency switching must positively interrupt the supply and stay open until deliberately reset, so a device that latches in the off position prevents the motor restarting unexpectedly while the danger is being dealt with. A handle, plug or key left in the on position offers no such security.

questions.prompt: A section of a factory requires urgent non-electrical repairs to a machine. The type of switching provided to allow this work to proceed would be switching for:
questions.explanation: Switching off for non-electrical work on a machine, such as clearing or repairing moving parts, is switching off for mechanical maintenance. It secures the supply so the equipment cannot start while a person works on it, which is distinct from emergency or functional switching.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following shall not be used as an isolator?
questions.explanation: Isolation must produce a secure, verifiable break in every supply conductor, and semiconductor devices only block conduction electronically without providing a reliable physical separation. They can fail to a conducting state, so they are not permitted to perform the isolating function.

questions.prompt: Where PME conditions apply, the main protective bonding conductor shall be:

options.A: Determined after consultation with the consumer
options.B: Half the csa of the earthing conductor and with reference to Table 54.7
options.C: Selected in accordance with the supply neutral and Table 54.8
options.D: The same csa as the incoming line conductor

questions.explanation: Where protective multiple earthing applies, the combined neutral and earth carries diverted neutral current, so the main bonding conductor is sized from the supply neutral cross-sectional area using Table 54.8. This ensures the bonding can safely carry those currents rather than being based simply on the earthing conductor size.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following cannot be used as an earth electrode?

options.D: Welded reinforcement of concrete embedded in the earth

questions.explanation: A metallic water supply pipe cannot be relied upon as an earth electrode because sections may be replaced with plastic, breaking continuity to the general mass of earth. The electrode must remain a permanent, stable connection, which a service pipe outside the installer's control cannot guarantee.

questions.prompt: Using Table 54.7 of BS 7671, the minimum cross-sectional area of a circuit protective conductor with a 10 mm2 line conductor will be:
questions.explanation: When the protective conductor is the same material as the line conductor, Table 54.7 requires it to equal the line cross-sectional area for line sizes up to and including 16 mm2. A 10 mm2 line conductor therefore needs a 10 mm2 protective conductor to handle fault current safely.

questions.prompt: In order to calculate the minimum value of the cross-sectional area of a protective conductor, the following information is available: Fault current = 700 A Operating time of protective device = 0.4 s Constant k, for protective conductor material = 115 The selected size of the protective conductor should be:
questions.explanation: Applying the adiabatic equation S equals the square root of (I squared times t) divided by k gives the square root of (700 squared times 0.4) divided by 115, which is roughly 3.8 mm2. The next available standard size that meets this minimum is 4 mm2.

questions.prompt: Supplementary bonding conductors having mechanical protection connected between two extraneous conductive parts are subject to a minimum cross-sectional area of:
questions.explanation: A supplementary bonding conductor linking two extraneous-conductive-parts must have a minimum cross-sectional area of 2.5 mm2 where it has mechanical protection. The protection allows the smaller size; without it, a 4 mm2 minimum would apply to guard against damage.

questions.prompt: In a marina, corrosive elements exist, structures can move, mechanical damage can occur, a possible presence of flammable fuel is present and an increase in the risk of electric shock is possible. Which one of the following is NOT taken into consideration when determining any external influence requirements?

options.A: Contact of body with earth potential
options.D: The reduced resistance of salt water

questions.explanation: The reduced resistance of salt water is a consequence of the conditions rather than an independent external influence, so it is not assessed separately. Presence of water, contact with earth potential and reduced body resistance are the genuine factors evaluated when determining shock-protection requirements in a marina.

questions.prompt: A final circuit supplying 13 A socket-outlets is to be used by ordinary persons. The circuit must be provided with:

options.B: Additional protection in accordance with Regulation 415.1

questions.explanation: Socket-outlets up to 32 A intended for use by ordinary persons require additional protection by a 30 mA RCD, the measure described in Regulation 415.1. This guards against the heightened risk of direct contact when untrained people connect portable equipment.

questions.prompt: Socket outlets which are under the supervision of skilled persons:

options.A: An IT system must not be used
options.B: Instruction must be available that indicate how to switch the device off if it detects a fault
options.C: It must be designed in such a way that it is impossible to modify the setting without the use of a tool, if the location is accessible to ordinary persons
options.D: It must be set to a higher value corresponding to the normal insulation of the system

questions.explanation: Under the supervision of skilled persons in an IT system, the insulation monitoring device may be set to a higher value matching the system's normal insulation level. The supervision and competence of those persons justifies the relaxed setting that would be unsafe for ordinary users.

questions.prompt: 3Ceiling roses are only allowed where the circuit voltage does not exceed:
questions.explanation: Ceiling roses are designed and rated for low-voltage lighting circuits, so their use is restricted to circuits where the voltage does not exceed 250 V. Above that they would be unsuitable for the insulation and creepage demands placed on the accessory.

questions.prompt: 3The minimum cross-sectional area for a buried copper earthing conductor that is provided with mechanical protection but no protection against corrosion is:
questions.explanation: A buried copper earthing conductor with mechanical protection but no corrosion protection must be at least 25 mm2. The larger size provides a sacrificial allowance so that gradual corrosion of the buried metal does not reduce the conductor below a safe fault-carrying capacity.

questions.prompt: When an insulation monitoring device (IMD) is installed:

options.A: An IT system must not be used
options.B: Instruction must be available that indicate how to switch the device off if it detects a fault
options.C: It must be designed in such a way that it is impossible to modify the setting without the use of a tool, if the location is accessible to ordinary persons
options.D: It must be set to a higher value corresponding to the normal insulation of the system

questions.explanation: An insulation monitoring device must be constructed so its settings cannot be altered without a tool where ordinary persons can reach it. This prevents inadvertent or unauthorised changes that would defeat the device's role in detecting a first fault on an IT system.

questions.prompt: A circuit with a design current of 45 A is installed using a cable with a current rating of 50 A. If the voltage drop for the cable is 8 mV per amp per metre, the circuit voltage drop for a 10 m run will be:
questions.explanation: Voltage drop is found from the tabulated millivolt-per-amp-per-metre figure multiplied by the design current and route length. Here 8 mV times 45 A times 10 m gives 3600 mV, which equals 3.6 V across the run.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following should be taken into consideration when calculating the voltage drop in an installation?

options.A: Current carrying capacity of the conductors
options.C: Nominal current setting of the protective device
options.D: The current that ensures effective operation of the protective device

questions.explanation: Voltage drop is calculated using the actual design current the circuit is expected to carry, since that determines the volt drop under normal operation. The protective device rating or cable capacity may be higher and would overstate the loss that occurs in service.

questions.prompt: On a mobile or transportable unit, plugs used to connect the unit to the supply shall comply with BE EN 60309-2 and:

options.A: Any plug and socket outlets shall afford a degree of protection of not less than IP44 if located inside
options.B: Appliance inlets with their enclosures shall provide a degree of protection of at least IP44
options.C: Shall be enclosed in a metal enclosure
options.D: The plug part be on the supply distribution board

questions.explanation: On mobile or transportable units, appliance inlets together with their enclosures must provide at least IP44 protection. This degree guards against ingress of solid objects and splashing water, reflecting the exposed and weather-affected environments in which such units operate.

questions.prompt: The fault current due to an earth fault of negligible impedance in a 400 V, three phase, four wire circuit having an earth fault loop impedance of 0.3 F is:
questions.explanation: Earth fault current equals the supply voltage divided by the earth fault loop impedance. For a 400 V three-phase, four-wire circuit the relevant phase voltage to earth is 230 V, so 230 divided by 0.3 ohms gives approximately 766.6 A.

questions.prompt: A 30 A protective device to BS 1361 when carrying a fault current of 200 A should operate in:
questions.explanation: The 0.4 s figure is the maximum disconnection time required for final circuits up to 32 A in a TN system, protecting against electric shock by clearing earth faults quickly. Time/current characteristics for a 30 A BS 1361 device show it operating within this limit at around 200 A.

questions.prompt: A black sleeve or disc is placed on one of the conductors of a three- core MICC cable. This indicates the:

options.B: Line 1 of a three phase a.c. circuit
options.C: Line 2 of a three phase a.c. circuit
options.D: Line 3 of a three phase a.c. circuit

questions.explanation: Standard core identification on multicore cables uses coloured sleeving or discs at terminations to mark each conductor. A black marker denotes the second line conductor of a three-phase a.c. circuit, ensuring correct phase sequence and safe connection at both ends.

questions.prompt: An unfused spur connected to a 30 A ring circuit may supply:

options.B: One twin socket-outlet or one single socket-outlet
options.D: Two twin socket-outlets or one fixed appliance

questions.explanation: An unfused spur taken from a ring final circuit has no additional overload protection, so its loading must be limited to prevent the spur cable being overstressed. It may therefore feed only one single or one twin socket-outlet, or one item of permanently connected equipment.

questions.prompt: Prior to an inspection in accordance with BS 7671, the competent person carrying out the test shall normally:

options.B: Disconnect the installation from the supply
options.C: Ensure that all switches are off
options.D: Ensure that the supply is connected

questions.explanation: Inspection involves examining the installation while it is safe to work on, so the supply is normally isolated to remove the risk of shock or arcing. Disconnecting from the supply allows close examination and dead testing without danger to the person carrying out the work.

questions.prompt: A legible diagram, chart or table relating to an installation must be provided to indicate:

options.A: Any circuit of equipment vulnerable to a typical test
options.B: Location of all portable equipment for testing purposes
options.C: That the original installation design has not changed
options.D: The location of all fixed equipment for testing purposes

questions.explanation: Recorded information must warn the person testing of anything that could be damaged by standard test procedures, such as electronic devices vulnerable to high test voltages. Identifying such circuits or equipment beforehand prevents inadvertent damage during routine verification.

questions.prompt: When carrying out an insulation resistance test on a 230 V socket- outlet circuit incorporating surge protective devices (SPD), the test voltage may be reduced to:
questions.explanation: Insulation resistance testing applies a high d.c. voltage that can damage surge protective devices connected between live conductors and earth. Reducing the test voltage to 250 V allows the circuit to be tested with the SPD in place, while a satisfactory result of at least 1 megohm still confirms adequate insulation.

questions.prompt: During an initial verification, a test result fails to comply with BS 7671 Part The procedure to be adopted is to:

options.B: Make good and complete the Electrical Installation Certificate
options.C: Make good and complete the Periodic Inspection Report
options.D: Record the fault on the Periodic Inspection Report

questions.explanation: Initial verification confirms a new installation complies before it is energised for use, so any non-compliant result must be corrected rather than simply recorded. Once the defect is rectified and the installation complies, the Electrical Installation Certificate can properly be completed.

questions.prompt: For circuits having a nominal voltage above 500 V, the minimum insulation resistance is:
questions.explanation: Minimum insulation resistance values rise with circuit voltage to ensure adequate insulation strength against the operating stress. For circuits with a nominal voltage above 500 V, a test at 1000 V d.c. must give a reading of at least 1 megohm to be acceptable.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is the required test procedure if an existing installation is extended to include extra lighting and socket outlets?

options.A: All relevant tests must be carried out
options.C: No testing is required, only visual inspection

questions.explanation: Adding lighting and socket-outlets is an addition to an existing installation, which counts as new work requiring verification before being put into service. All relevant tests appropriate to the new circuits must be carried out to confirm they are safe and compliant.

questions.prompt: It is a requirement of BS 7671 that a Schedule of Test Results should always be attached to an Electrical Installation Certificate for:

options.D: New installations, alterations or additions to existing installations

questions.explanation: Certification must record the results that demonstrate compliance, so a Schedule of Test Results accompanies the Electrical Installation Certificate as evidence of the testing performed. This applies to new installations and to any alteration or addition, since each involves work that must be verified.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 requires that the person ordering installation work must be informed of the:

options.C: Name and address of the regional electricity company

questions.explanation: Certification documentation must include a recommendation for the interval to the next inspection so the installation continues to be maintained safely. Informing the person ordering the work of the need for periodic testing ensures deterioration is identified before it becomes dangerous.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following factors does not affect the frequency of the periodic inspection?
questions.explanation: The interval between periodic inspections is determined by factors affecting the rate of deterioration and the risk involved, such as the type of installation, how it is used and operated, and the frequency of maintenance. The presence of supplies for safety services does not itself set this interval.

questions.prompt: Electric heating units embedded in the floor of a bathroom and intended for heating the location may be installed below any zone provided they are:

options.A: Covered by an earthed metallic grid
options.B: Covered with at least 50 mm of screed
options.C: Supplied from an electrically separated source

questions.explanation: In a bathroom, buried floor heating elements could become a shock hazard if a fault occurred, so an additional protective measure is required. An earthed metallic grid over the heating units, connected to protective bonding, ensures any fault is detected and disconnected safely.

questions.prompt: Electrical equipment installed in Zone 1 of a swimming pool must have a minimum degree of protection in accordance with:
questions.explanation: Equipment in the immediate splash area around a swimming pool must resist water ingress to remain safe. Zone 1 demands a minimum of IPX4, meaning protection against splashing water from any direction, since the device is exposed to water but not to immersion or jets.

questions.prompt: Construction site regulations apply to:
questions.explanation: The special requirements for construction and demolition sites address temporary installations exposed to harsh conditions and increased shock risk. Earthworks fall within this scope, whereas permanent associated buildings such as offices, canteens and toilets follow the ordinary installation rules.

questions.prompt: In agricultural premises, heating appliances shall be fixed so as to maintain an appropriate distance from livestock. In the absence of manufacturer's guidance, a radiant heater used in the vicinity of livestock should be placed at a distance of not less than:
questions.explanation: Heating appliances near livestock must be positioned to avoid burns and fire risk from animal contact or combustible bedding. Where no manufacturer figure is given, a radiant heater should be kept at least 0.5 m from livestock to maintain a safe separation.

questions.prompt: The socket outlet and its enclosure, forming part of a pitch supply equipment for a caravan park, must comply with BS EN 60309-2 and have a minimum index of protection of:
questions.explanation: Pitch supply equipment on a caravan park is exposed outdoors to rain and splashing, so its enclosure must resist water ingress. A minimum of IP44 provides protection against solid objects above one millimetre and splashing water, suiting the standard industrial socket-outlet used.

questions.prompt: Inspection and testing of a fairground installation must take place:

options.C: Only if it is fed from an a.c. supply
options.D: Only if it is fed from the public supply system

questions.explanation: Fairground and amusement installations are repeatedly dismantled, transported and reassembled, which can disturb connections and damage cables. Inspection and testing after each assembly on site confirms the installation has not been compromised in transit and is safe before public use.

questions.prompt: The first Edition of the Rules and Regulations for the prevention of Fire Risks Arising from Electrical Lighting was issued in
questions.explanation: The earliest national wiring rules grew out of fire-prevention concerns at the dawn of electric lighting. These 1882 rules from the Society of Telegraph Engineers and Electricians were the first ancestor of today's BS 7671, issued long before AC mains became widespread.

questions.prompt: Electrical installation design shall take into account
questions.explanation: Design must consider how the installation behaves within its electromagnetic environment, both the disturbances it may suffer and those it may emit. Accounting for electromagnetic compatibility protects sensitive equipment and avoids malfunction, whereas copper prices and planning approval are not electrical safety characteristics.

questions.prompt: The Regulations are designed to protect:
questions.explanation: The fundamental purpose stated at the outset is protection of people, livestock and property against the hazards electricity can create, such as shock, burns and fire. Livestock are explicitly included because animals can be more vulnerable to electric shock than people.

questions.prompt: Which Voltage range do the BS7671 Regulations include requirements for?
questions.explanation: The scope covers low-voltage installations, defined as not exceeding 1000V AC or 1500V DC between conductors. Above these thresholds the installation is treated as high voltage and falls outside the normal requirements of the Regulations.

questions.prompt: An area or temporary structure used for display, marketing or sales is defined as
questions.explanation: The defined term for a temporary structure or area used to display, market or sell goods is a stand. This precise definition matters because special location requirements apply to exhibitions, shows and stands, which carry particular risks from temporary wiring and public access.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 defines extra-low voltage a.c. as not exceeding:
questions.explanation: Extra-low voltage is bounded at 50V AC and 120V ripple-free DC between conductors or to earth. These thresholds mark the upper limit below which the shock risk is reduced, and they underpin SELV and PELV protective measures.

questions.prompt: Diversity may be taken into account when considering
questions.explanation: Diversity recognises that not all connected loads operate simultaneously at full power, so it is applied when assessing the maximum demand of an installation. Allowing for diversity gives a realistic demand figure and avoids oversizing cables, switchgear and the supply unnecessarily.

questions.prompt: With reference to the nature of the supply, which one of the following can be determined by calculation, enquiry or measurement?

options.B: The maximum demand of the installation
options.C: The prospective short-circuit current at the origin of the installation
options.D: The rating of the circuit protective device

questions.explanation: The prospective short-circuit current at the origin is a characteristic of the supply that may be established by calculation, enquiry of the distributor, or direct measurement. Knowing this value is essential so that protective devices have an adequate breaking capacity.

questions.prompt: Which of the following forms part of the assessment of general characteristics?
questions.explanation: Assessing general characteristics includes evaluating external influences such as ambient temperature, moisture, dust and mechanical stresses. These conditions determine the suitable equipment and wiring systems, whereas switchgear quantities and circuit calculations are part of detailed design rather than this assessment.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does not fall under compatibility?
questions.explanation: Compatibility concerns whether equipment characteristics could harmfully affect other equipment or the supply, covering things like starting currents, power factor and transient overvoltages. Continuity of service is a separate consideration about maintaining supply, not a compatibility issue between connected equipment.

questions.prompt: The following are all reasons for dividing a circuit except

options.A: Allow of future expansion within the electrical installation
options.B: Preventing dangers arising from nuisance tripping
options.C: Preventing the indirect energising of circuit intended to be isolated

questions.explanation: Circuits are divided to limit the consequences of a fault, reduce nuisance tripping, prevent indirect energising of isolated circuits and minimise electromagnetic interference. Allowing for future expansion is good practice but is not a stated reason for dividing the installation into separate circuits.

questions.prompt: The image represents which type of earthing system?
questions.explanation: A TN-S system has a separate protective earth conductor run all the way from the supply transformer, distinct from the neutral throughout. The drawing showing distinct neutral and earth conductors with no combined PEN section identifies this arrangement.

questions.prompt: When protecting against burns a metallic part intended to be touched but not hand held shall be limited to a maximum temperature of:
questions.explanation: To prevent burns, an accessible metallic part intended to be touched but not gripped is limited to 70 degrees Celsius. Metal conducts heat readily, so this lower limit guards against skin injury during brief contact in normal service.

questions.prompt: Table 41.1 What will be the operating time for a 60A BS 3036 protective device when the value of fault current is 205A:
questions.explanation: A BS 3036 rewireable fuse is a relatively slow device, and the time/current characteristic shows that a 60A fuse needs about 205A to reach a 5 second disconnection time. Reading the curve at that fault current gives the 5.0 second operating point.

questions.prompt: In a 230V TN system, for final circuits supplying fixed current using equipment exceeding 32A the disconnection time is limited to:
questions.explanation: For fixed equipment with a rating exceeding 32A on a 230V TN system, the maximum disconnection time is 5 seconds rather than 0.4 seconds. Larger fixed circuits are permitted the longer time because the touch-voltage risk is managed differently than for socket outlets.

questions.prompt: To meet the requirements of BS 7671, all overcurrent protective devices, without back-up protection on the supply side, must be capable of:

options.A: Not operating during a short-circuit fault
options.B: Operating at a current lower that their rated current
options.D: Withstanding the prospective short-circuit current at that point in the installation

questions.explanation: Every protective device must have a breaking capacity at least equal to the prospective fault current at its point of installation, unless backed up by another device. Otherwise it could fail to clear a fault safely and may rupture, causing fire or injury.

questions.prompt: Which is a method of fault protection
questions.explanation: Fault protection guards against contact with parts that become live under a first fault, and reinforced insulation provides this by a single insulation system equivalent to double insulation. Insulation of live parts, obstacles and placing out of reach are basic protection measures instead.

questions.prompt: An undervoltage device has operated and restoring the supply may cause danger. The reclosure of this device should be

options.A: Automatic when under the supervision of a competent person
options.D: Possible only with the use of a key or tool

questions.explanation: Where restoring supply after an undervoltage operation could create danger, such as machinery restarting unexpectedly, automatic reclosure must be prevented. Manual operation ensures a person deliberately re-energises the circuit only when it is safe to do so.

questions.prompt: A SELV source can be derived from which one of the following?
questions.explanation: A SELV system relies on electrical separation between the source and the supply mains so a fault cannot raise the low-voltage circuit to a dangerous potential. A safety isolating transformer provides that segregated double-wound construction; an autotransformer shares a common winding and cannot guarantee separation.

questions.prompt: Except where otherwise recommended by the manufacturer, spotlights and projectors rated at over 100 W and up to 300 W shall be installed at a minimum distance from combustible materials of
questions.explanation: Luminaires emit significant radiant heat that can ignite nearby materials, so minimum spacing increases with lamp rating. For spotlights and projectors rated above 100 W up to 300 W, keeping at least 0.8 m from combustible materials limits the temperature reached and reduces the fire risk.

questions.prompt: Where particular risks of fire exist, the classification for high density occupation areas with easy conditions of evacuation is
questions.explanation: Conditions of evacuation are graded by occupant density and how readily people can leave. The BD classification combining high density with easy evacuation conditions is BD3, which reflects areas crowded with people but where exit routes remain straightforward to use.

questions.prompt: Which of the following under certain conditions could be used as an earth electrode?

options.D: An underground water supply provided by the water board

questions.explanation: Underground metalwork can act as an electrode only if it stays reliably in contact with the general mass of earth and is not liable to removal. A private water supply pipe may qualify, whereas the public water board supply must never be used and gas pipes are explicitly prohibited as electrodes.

questions.prompt: The value of the external loop impedance can be found by more than one method. One of these could be taking a reading at

options.A: Both at the supply and at the furthest outlet, and subtracting one result from the other
options.B: The furthest outlet from the origin of the supply
options.D: The supply point and subtracting the value of R1+R2

questions.explanation: The external loop impedance Ze represents only the supply side back to the transformer, so it must be measured with the installation disconnected. Taking the reading at the origin of supply, with the consumer's main earth disconnected, captures that external path without including the installation's own conductors.

questions.prompt: Undervoltage protection circuit are required to stay de-energised where the restoration of power may cause

options.C: Unexpected stopping of the motor circuit

questions.explanation: Undervoltage protection holds a circuit off after a supply dip so that equipment does not restart on its own. This matters where the unexpected starting of machinery on power restoration could injure an operator who assumed the plant was safely stopped.

questions.prompt: An electric fire having an element exposed to touch would increase the risk of an electric shock by
questions.explanation: Basic protection guards against contact with parts that are live in normal service, such as an exposed heating element. An element open to touch defeats that basic protection, so the increased shock risk arises through basic contact with a normally live part.

questions.prompt: Which of the following energy sources is not suitable for a SELV supply?
questions.explanation: A SELV supply must be electrically separated from higher-voltage circuits so no fault can transfer a dangerous voltage. Batteries, independent generators and safety isolating transformers all provide this separation, but an autotransformer shares a winding with the primary and offers no isolation, making it unsuitable.

questions.prompt: A PEN Conductor must

options.A: Have a switching or isolating device
options.C: Not have a switching or isolating device

questions.explanation: A PEN conductor combines neutral and protective earth functions, so interrupting it would leave exposed metalwork without an earth reference and create a serious shock hazard. For this reason no switching or isolating device may be inserted in a PEN conductor.

questions.prompt: SPD Stands for
questions.explanation: SPD stands for Surge Protective Device, equipment fitted to limit transient overvoltages from lightning or switching events. It diverts surge energy to earth, protecting sensitive equipment and insulation from damage caused by short-duration voltage spikes.

questions.prompt: An industrial board supplies
questions.explanation: An industrial board typically distributes three-phase power to plant such as motors rather than domestic-style single-phase final circuits. Supplying four three-phase motors reflects this industrial loading, where three-phase TP supplies are needed for the rotating machinery commonly found on such installations.

questions.prompt: A cable concealed in a wall outside the prescribed zones at a depth of less than 50 mm must

options.A: Be enclosed in earthed metallic conduit

questions.explanation: Cables hidden in walls less than 50 mm deep and outside the permitted zones get no protection from a known cable route, so a penetrating screw or nail could pierce a live conductor. Enclosing them in earthed metallic conduit provides mechanical protection and a path to trip the protective device on a fault.

questions.prompt: The minimum information contained on a periodic inspection and testing notice would be the

options.A: Company's address and date of next inspection
options.B: Date of inspection and inspectors name
options.C: Date of last inspection and date of next inspection
options.D: Date of next inspection and clients name

questions.explanation: The periodic inspection notice exists so the next inspection is not overlooked once an installation is in service. As a minimum it must record the date of the last inspection and the recommended date for the next, prompting timely reassessment of the installation's condition.

questions.prompt: Fire detection and fire alarm systems for buildings shall be in accordance with?
questions.explanation: Fire detection and alarm systems are designed, installed and maintained to a dedicated standard rather than the general wiring rules. BS 5839 is the code of practice governing such systems in buildings, so installations are required to comply with it.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect:

options.A: For a fixed installation flexible conductors of csa less than 10mm2 may serve as a PEN conductor
options.B: No means of switching shall be inserted in the outer conductor of a concentric cable
options.C: The use of PEN conductors is permitted within an installation where authorisation has been obtained
options.D: The use of PEN conductors is permitted within an installation where the supply is obtained from a private generating plant

questions.explanation: A PEN conductor carries combined neutral and earth current, so it must have ample cross-sectional area and mechanical robustness; small flexible conductors cannot reliably serve this role. The statement permitting a flexible conductor below 10 mm squared as a PEN conductor is therefore the incorrect one.

questions.prompt: Under fault conditions, cables are subjected to stress and thermal effects. One item not normally encountered would be
questions.explanation: A fault current produces intense heating and strong magnetic forces, so conductors must withstand thermal damage and the electromechanical and electromagnetic stresses these generate. Electrochemical effects relate to corrosion processes rather than the brief, high-energy conditions of a fault, so they are not normally encountered here.

questions.prompt: The magnetic circuit of the transformer of an RCD shall enclose:

options.A: All line conductors of the protected circuit
options.B: All live and earth conductors of the protected circuit
options.C: All live conductors of the protected circuit
options.D: Neutral and earth conductors of the protected circuit

questions.explanation: An RCD works by sensing the small imbalance between flowing line and neutral currents, which appears only if some current escapes to earth. Its transformer core must therefore enclose all live conductors of the circuit, line and neutral, so that under healthy conditions their fluxes cancel.

questions.prompt: A permanent warning notice must be fixed at or near the point of connection of every earthing conductor to an earth electrode bearing the words:

options.C: Safety Electrical Connection  Do Not Remove
options.D: Safety Electrical Earth  Do Not Remove

questions.explanation: The connection between earthing conductor and electrode is safety-critical, and removing it would leave the installation without effective earthing. A durable notice reading Safety Electrical Connection Do Not Remove warns anyone working nearby not to disconnect it.

questions.prompt: In high rise buildings lightning conductors must be bonded to the
questions.explanation: A lightning protection system must be tied into the building's earthing arrangement so that all conductive parts share a common reference. Bonding to the installation earth prevents dangerous potential differences and side-flashing between the lightning down-conductors and the electrical installation during a strike.

questions.prompt: The symbol shown above indicates

options.A: Luminaire for use with high pressure sodium lamps that have an internal ignitor
options.B: Luminaire for use with high pressure sodium lamps that require an external ignitor
options.C: Luminaire suitable for direct mounting an normally flammable surfaces

questions.explanation: Luminaire marking symbols distinguish lamps that carry their own internal starting circuitry from those needing an external ignitor. This symbol identifies a fitting for high pressure sodium lamps with an internal ignitor, so the installer knows no separate ignitor needs to be wired into the supply.

questions.prompt: Split concentric cable could be used as a distribution cable to supply what type of earthing system
questions.explanation: Split concentric cable carries the neutral and protective functions in a combined outer conductor, which is only permissible where the supply combines PEN functions. That arrangement matches a TN-C-S system, where the combined PEN is separated into neutral and earth at the installation origin.

questions.prompt: What is particular about a FELV system in a medical location?

options.A: Associated enclosures should be non conductive
options.B: It should be fused on the supply side
options.C: It should be tested in accordance with Chapter 6
options.D: It should not be relied upon for protection against shock

questions.explanation: Functional extra-low voltage is provided for operational reasons only and does not guarantee the separation or isolation that SELV or PELV offer. In a medical location it therefore cannot be treated as a protective measure against electric shock, and additional protection must still be applied.

questions.prompt: Where a clamp is used for bonding purposes a permanent label shall be fixed in a visible position with the wording

options.A: Danger Earth Connection  Do Not Remove
options.B: Danger Electrical Connection  Do Not Remove
options.C: Safety Earth Connection Do Not Remove
options.D: Safety Electrical Connection  Do Not Remove

questions.explanation: Bonding clamps must carry durable warning labels so that anyone working nearby understands the connection is essential for safety. The required wording reads Safety Electrical Connection Do Not Remove, alerting maintainers not to disconnect a conductor that maintains equipotential bonding and shock protection.

questions.prompt: When an addition is made to an existing installation, the contractor shall record on the Electrical Installation Certificate or the Minor Electrical Installation Works Certificate any

options.C: Records of repair over the last five years
options.D: Voltage drop in the longest circuit

questions.explanation: When certifying an addition, the contractor is only responsible for the new work but must flag anything found that affects safety. Recording defects in the existing installation discharges the duty to report dangerous conditions and protects the client and contractor, even though those faults fall outside the new work.

questions.prompt: The frequency of a periodic inspection on an older installation depends upon

options.D: The type, use and operation of the installation

questions.explanation: There is no fixed universal interval for periodic inspection; the appropriate frequency is assessed for each installation. The type of premises, how it is used and how it is operated determine the wear, deterioration and risk, so these factors set how often inspection and testing should occur.

questions.prompt: A polarity test is conducted to verify that

options.A: Every fuse and single pole device is connected in the line conductor only
options.B: The circuit protection will operate within a pre-determined time
options.C: The resistance is sufficiently low to operate the protective device within the specified time
options.D: There is no breakdown of the conductor's insulation

questions.explanation: Polarity testing confirms that switching and protective devices are placed correctly so that they interrupt the live conductor rather than the neutral. Verifying every fuse and single-pole device sits in the line conductor ensures equipment cannot remain live when the device opens, which is essential for safe isolation.

questions.prompt: A periodic inspection would be carried out on

options.D: An extension of existing lighting circuit

questions.explanation: Periodic inspection and testing assesses installations already in service to confirm they remain safe for continued use. It applies to an existing property, whereas new work, refurbishments and circuit additions are verified by initial verification and certified accordingly rather than by a periodic report.

questions.prompt: On caravan sites, overhead conductors in areas subject to vehicle movement shall be placed at a minimum height above ground of:
questions.explanation: On caravan sites, overhead lines must be kept high enough to clear the tall vehicles, caravans and machinery that move around the site. A minimum height of 6.0m where vehicle movement occurs prevents contact between live conductors and passing vehicles or people on top of them.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements regarding Section 740 is incorrect:

options.A: RCDs are not required for circuits protected by electrical separation
options.B: RCDs are required to protect socket-outlets rated greater than 32A
options.C: RCDs not exceeding 300mA shall be provided at the origin of the installation
options.D: The nominal supply voltage shall not exceed 230V/400V a.c

questions.explanation: For caravan and camping installations the residual current protection requirement applies to every socket-outlet up to and including 32A, not only those rated above 32A. Stating that protection is required for outlets greater than 32A misrepresents the rule, making that the incorrect statement.

questions.prompt: In agricultural premises an RCD may be used for protection against fire. The current rating should not exceed:
questions.explanation: Agricultural premises carry a heightened fire risk, so residual current devices are used to give additional protection against fire from earth leakage. A rating not exceeding 300mA balances sensitivity to fault currents against nuisance tripping while still disconnecting before a dangerous fire can develop.

questions.prompt: Equipment on a pontoon in a marina that is subject to impact to level AG2 should have a mechanical protection code of
questions.explanation: External influence AG2 denotes medium mechanical impact, and protection against impact is rated by the IK code rather than the IP code. IK08 provides the impact resistance suited to equipment on a marina pontoon exposed to that level of mechanical stress.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum protection afforded electrical equipment if installed in a jetty in a marina?
questions.explanation: Equipment on a marina jetty is exposed to splashing water from all directions but the principal concern is moisture ingress rather than solid objects. A minimum rating of IPX4 ensures protection against splashing water, with the X indicating no specific requirement is placed on the solid-particle digit here.

questions.prompt: Zone 0 in a swimming pool installation is the

options.B: The floor or surface expected to be occupied by persons
options.C: The horizontal plane 2.5m above the floor
options.D: The interior of the pool and a vertical plane 2m above the basin

questions.explanation: Swimming pool zones are defined by proximity to water to set the protective measures required. Zone 0 is the interior of the basin itself, the most hazardous region, where only SELV at very low voltage and strictly limited equipment are permitted.

questions.prompt: External influences when designing an installation for a marina would include

options.A: Contact of the body with potential
options.B: High dust content in the atmosphere
options.C: The grouping of many cable on one tray

questions.explanation: Marina environments raise the risk of electric shock because people may be wet, immersed or in contact with water and conductive structures. Designing for contact of the body with potential addresses this reduced body resistance and the consequent need for enhanced shock protection.

questions.prompt: Heating unit design to be used underfloor have a minimum IP rating of
questions.explanation: Underfloor heating elements may be buried in screed or beneath floors where they can be subject to temporary immersion in water or moisture. A minimum rating of IPX7 ensures the unit withstands immersion, protecting it against ingress in those damp, enclosed conditions.

questions.prompt: Where conduit is to be installed installations and vehicles and machinery operate is should be afforded a protection rating to withstand
questions.explanation: Where conduit runs through areas with vehicle and machinery movement it must resist the heavier mechanical impacts likely in such locations. Specifying conduit able to withstand a 5J impact provides the robustness needed to protect the enclosed conductors from damage by passing plant.

questions.prompt: On completion of an electrical condition installation report an inspector notes C1 against an item of electrical equipment. This would indicate

options.A: Does not conform to current regulations

questions.explanation: A C1 classification on a condition report means danger is present and a risk of injury exists, so immediate remedial action is needed. It signals an existing hazard rather than a mere recommendation, and the person ordering the report must be told without delay.

questions.prompt: Busbar trunking should have an In declared by the manufacture to
questions.explanation: Busbar trunking systems are manufactured and rated to the relevant low-voltage switchgear and assembly standard, BS EN 60439-2, which is the product standard the manufacturer uses to declare the rated current In. This ensures the assembly's stated current-carrying capacity is verified to a recognised testing regime.

questions.prompt: The maximum size fuse that should be fitted within a standard fused spur connected to a ring final circuit should be
questions.explanation: A fused connection unit spurred from a ring final circuit takes a BS 1362 cartridge fuse whose maximum rating is 13A, matching the largest standard plug fuse. This limits the load drawn through the spur so the protective device and the spur cabling are not overloaded.

questions.prompt: Information regarding Energy Efficiency can be found in
questions.explanation: Energy efficiency requirements were introduced as a distinct division of the Regulations, placed in Part 8. Locating it as its own part keeps the design measures for efficient use of electrical energy separate from the protection and selection requirements in the earlier parts.

questions.prompt: BSEN 61009 30mA Rated RCBO with an instrument tripping current set to 30mA must trip within
questions.explanation: When tested at its rated residual operating current of 30mA, a general type RCD or RCBO must disconnect within 300ms. This limit ensures the device clears an earth-fault leakage current quickly enough to protect against electric shock under the additional protection provided by 30mA devices.

questions.prompt: In medical locations of Group 1 and Group 2, where RCDs are required, which protective measure shall not be used?

options.A: RCD type A according to BS EN 61008
options.B: RCD type A according to BS EN 61009
options.C: RCD type B according to BS EN 62423

questions.explanation: Medical locations can carry DC components and complex earth-fault currents that a basic type AC device cannot reliably detect, so a plain type AC RCD must not be used. Type A or type B devices are specified because they respond correctly to pulsating or smooth DC residual currents.

questions.prompt: In a bathroom area protection by electrical separation shall only be used for?

options.B: Circuits supplying one item of current-using equipment
options.C: Either of the first two answers

questions.explanation: Electrical separation in a location containing a bath or shower is restricted so that one source supplies only a single item of current-using equipment or one socket-outlet. Limiting the separated circuit this way preserves the integrity of the isolated supply and prevents a second fault creating a shock path.

questions.prompt: Which of the following factors describes the correct co-ordination between electrical equipment in order not to impair the safety of the installation requiring continuity of service?

options.A: Back-up protection in case of short-circuit between OCPD and overload relays
options.C: Protection in case of overload between OCPD and SCPD
options.D: Selectivity between OPCDs equipped with under-voltage relay

questions.explanation: To maintain continuity of service without impairing safety, devices must be coordinated so they discriminate correctly, here through selectivity between overcurrent protective devices fitted with under-voltage relays. Proper selectivity ensures only the device nearest a fault operates, leaving healthy circuits energised.

questions.prompt: The maximum Zs in a 15A/230 V TN circuit covered by 411.3.2.2 protected by a BS 3036 fuse is?
questions.explanation: For a 15A circuit on a 230V TN system protected by a semi-enclosed BS 3036 fuse, the tabulated maximum earth-fault loop impedance giving timely disconnection is 2.43Ω. The rewireable fuse's slower characteristic demands a lower Zs than cartridge devices of the same rating to achieve the required disconnection.

questions.prompt: Concerning protection against overvoltages due to earth faults, which information on the high voltage system is NOT necessary?

options.A: Maximum level of earth fault current
options.B: Maximum overvoltage the earthing system can withstand

questions.explanation: Assessing overvoltages from earth faults on the high-voltage side relies on the fault current magnitude, the quality of the system earthing and the resistance of the earthing arrangement. The maximum overvoltage the earthing system can withstand is an outcome to be checked, not input data needed for the assessment.

questions.prompt: Where it is necessary to limit the consequences of the risk of fire due to fault currents, identify which of the following RCD`s would be used?

options.A: RCD with operating current not exceeding 150mA
options.B: RCD with operating current not exceeding 30 mA
options.C: RCD with operating current not exceeding 300 mA
options.D: RCD with operating current not exceeding 500 mA

questions.explanation: Where protection against fire arising from earth-fault currents is required, an RCD with a rated operating current not exceeding 300mA is specified. This threshold is low enough to interrupt a fault current capable of igniting materials, while avoiding the nuisance tripping a 30mA device would suffer on larger installations.

questions.prompt: Which would be appropriate support for wiring systems?

options.A: Cable suspended below a cable tray
options.D: Wall-to-wall span across an access route
