questions.explanation: Zone 0 of a swimming pool is the interior of the basin, where equipment may be fully and continuously immersed. The minimum protection is therefore IPX8, the rating for continuous submersion in water, ensuring enclosures remain sealed at depth.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is the maximum number of vehicles that can be connected to a single charging socket-outlet
questions.explanation: Each charging point must serve only one vehicle at a time so that protective measures, load assessment and disconnection can be reliably applied to a single connection. Connecting more than one vehicle to a single socket-outlet is therefore not permitted, limiting the maximum to one.

questions.prompt: Within zones 0 and 1 of a swimming pool, a protective provision against electric shock should be by means of
questions.explanation: Zones 0 and 1 of a swimming pool are wet, high-risk areas where the body is immersed or in close contact with water, so the protective measure must limit voltage to a safe level. SELV at reduced voltage is required because it provides protection by both basic and fault protection at extra-low voltage.

questions.prompt: Electrical equipment installed in zones 1 and 2 of a bathroom must have a minimum index of protection (IP rating) of
questions.explanation: Zones 1 and 2 of a bathroom are exposed to splashing and spray during normal use, so enclosures must resist water ingress from any direction. A minimum rating of IPX4 ensures equipment withstands splashing water without the moisture entering and creating a shock or fault risk.

questions.prompt: For inland navigation vessels, socket outlets not exceeding 125A shall be
questions.explanation: Socket-outlets supplying inland navigation vessels must be the industrial type designed for robust, weather-exposed power connections. BS EN 60309-2 plugs and sockets up to 125A provide the keyed, IP-rated configuration suited to this demanding shore-supply environment.

questions.prompt: At what height, except in special environment conditions, should socket outlets in caravan parks be placed
questions.explanation: Socket-outlets serving caravan pitches are mounted at a height that keeps them clear of ground water and accidental damage while remaining within easy reach. A range of 0.5m to 1.5m above ground achieves this balance except where special environmental conditions dictate otherwise.

questions.prompt: Zone 3 of a sauna extends above zone 2 at a distance from the floor of
questions.explanation: Sauna zones are defined by height because temperature rises sharply toward the ceiling, so equipment in each zone must suit its thermal conditions. Zone 3 begins above zone 2 at 1.0m from the floor, separating the cooler lower region from the hotter air above.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum three-phase nominal supply voltage of a temporary electrical installation in an exhibition
questions.explanation: Temporary installations at exhibitions, shows and stands are subject to particular safety constraints, but standard low-voltage distribution is still permitted for their supply. The maximum three-phase nominal voltage is 400V AC, the usual line-to-line value for a low-voltage three-phase system.

questions.prompt: Equipment installed in zone 3 of a hot air sauna room must be able to withstand a minimum temperature of
questions.explanation: Air temperature in a sauna increases with height, so equipment located in the upper region must tolerate the greatest heat. Equipment in zone 3, the hottest zone near the ceiling, must be rated to withstand a minimum temperature of 125 degrees Celsius.

questions.prompt: Details of ring and radial arrangements can be found in
questions.explanation: Appendix 15 of BS 7671 is dedicated to ring and radial final circuit arrangements, setting out the standard layouts, conductor sizing and protective device relationships. It is the reference designers consult to confirm a given socket-outlet circuit conforms to the recognised configurations.

questions.prompt: Details on current-carrying capacity and voltage drop for busbar trunking and powertrack systems can be found in
questions.explanation: Appendix 8 deals specifically with busbar trunking and powertrack systems, giving the current-carrying capacity and voltage-drop data those prefabricated distribution systems need. Standard cable tables in Appendix 4 do not cover them, so their own appendix provides the rating information for design.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is the correct grouping factor for six circuits bunched on a surface
questions.explanation: Table 4C1 in Appendix 4 gives rating factors for groups of circuits or multicore cables bunched together. Six circuits grouped on a single surface attract a factor of 0.57, reflecting the reduced heat dissipation when conductors are clustered, so the cable current rating must be derated accordingly.

questions.prompt: A building whose structure has an external influence category CB4
questions.explanation: The external influence codes in Appendix 5 classify building construction, where category CB describes the design of the structure. CB4 denotes a building that is flexible or unstable, meaning the wiring system and its supports must accommodate the movement expected from such a structure.

questions.prompt: Which observation code should be recorded where a dangerous condition is revealed during a periodic inspection and test of an installation
questions.explanation: The classification codes in Appendix 6 rank observations by severity, and C1 signifies danger present requiring immediate remedial action. Where inspection reveals a condition that poses a real and immediate risk of injury, it must be coded C1 so the duty holder acts at once.

scoring.label: Pass — review the missed clauses and tables
Near miss — practise navigation through BS 7671
Major gaps — rebuild 18th Edition structure and lookup skills

priorities: BS 7671 scope, exclusions, definitions and the seven-part structure.
Protection for safety: ADS, RCDs, SPDs, overcurrent, thermal effects and isolation.
Selection and erection: wiring systems, current-carrying capacity, voltage drop and appendices.
Inspection, testing, certification and special installations or locations.
Use regulation-book logic; these mocks test close wording and table lookup judgement.
